ITQAN:v4p397/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p397/r7.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p397/r7.claim: Those asking what is lawful include Adi ibn Hatim, Zayd ibn al-Muhalhil al-Tai, Asim ibn Adi, Sad ibn Khaythama, and Uwaymir ibn Saidah.
ITQAN:v4p397/r7.anchor: سمي منهم عدي بن حاتم وزيد بن المهلهل الطائيان وعاصم بن عدي وسعد بن خيثمة وعويمر بن ساعدة

BURSEVI:v2p275/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p275/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p275/r1.claim: ماذا combines the interrogative ما with relative ذا and asks what foods have been made lawful.
BURSEVI:v2p275/r1.anchor: ما للاستفهام وذا بمعنى الذي والمعنى ما الذي أحل لهم من المطاعم

BURSEVI:v2p275/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p275/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p275/r2.claim: Tayyib means tasty and desired; what counts as pleasant is judged by people of honorable, fine character, while desert Arabs consider all animals good to eat.
BURSEVI:v2p275/r2.anchor: والطيب في اللغة المستلذ المشتهى فالتقدير كل ما يستلذ ويشتهي والعبرة في الاستلذاذ والاستطابة بأهل المروءة

BURSEVI:v2p275/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p275/r3.speaker: الإمام في تفسيره
BURSEVI:v2p275/r3.claim: The Imam's commentary says desert people find all animals pleasant to eat, supplying the criterion for what is tayyib.
BURSEVI:v2p275/r3.anchor: فإن أهل البادية يستطيبون أكل جميع الحيوانات كذا قال الإمام في تفسيره

BURSEVI:v2p275/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p275/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p275/r4.claim: وما علمتم is coordinated with الطيبات by supplying an implied noun meaning the game of what you have trained; ما is relative with its pronoun omitted.
BURSEVI:v2p275/r4.anchor: عطف على الطيبات بتقدير المضاف على أن ما موصولة والعائد محذوف

BURSEVI:v2p275/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p275/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p275/r5.claim: الجوارح is a circumstantial phrase and plural of جارحة, meaning an acquiring animal; it may also derive from wounding, since hunting animals often tear prey.
BURSEVI:v2p275/r5.anchor: حال من الموصول جمع جارحة بمعنى كاسبة

BURSEVI:v2p275/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p275/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p275/r6.claim: The term covers any trainable animal that catches game for its owner, including hunting mammals such as cheetahs, leopards, and dogs, and birds such as falcons and eagles; their catches are lawful.
BURSEVI:v2p275/r6.anchor: والمراد بالجوارح في الآية كل ما يكسب الصيد على أهله من سباع البهائم كالفهد والنمر والكلب

BURSEVI:v2p275/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p275/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p275/r7.claim: مكلبين means training and inciting hunting animals; it comes from dog because dogs are especially receptive to hunting instruction, and is an accusative circumstantial phrase attached to the trainer.
BURSEVI:v2p275/r7.anchor: أي معلمين لها الصيد والمكلب مؤدب الجوارح

BURSEVI:v2p275/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p275/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p275/r8.claim: Calling the trainers مكلبين stresses their expertise: the title applies only to a highly skilled trainer, so the phrase means they are adept and renowned in training.
BURSEVI:v2p275/r8.anchor: فائدتها المبالغة في التعليم لما أن اسم المكلب لا يقع إلا على النحرير في علمه

BURSEVI:v2p275/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p275/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p275/r9.claim: تعلمونهن is a second circumstantial phrase; God taught people the techniques of training, whether by inspiration, reason as a divine gift, or learned methods such as sending, calling back, stopping, and having the animal hold prey without eating it.
BURSEVI:v2p275/r9.anchor: حال ثانية {مما علمكم الله} من الحيل وطرق التعليم والتأديب

BURSEVI:v2p276/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p276/r1.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
BURSEVI:v2p276/r1.claim: Al-Kashshaf says the verse teaches that students should learn from a deeply expert master who knows a field's subtleties, even if reaching that teacher requires a long journey.
BURSEVI:v2p276/r1.anchor: قال صاحب "الكشاف" قوله تعالى : {تعلمونهن مما علمكم الله} فيه تنبيه على أن كل من يأخذ علما ينبغي أن يأخذه

BURSEVI:v2p276/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p276/r2.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
BURSEVI:v2p276/r2.claim: A Prophetic saying urges seekers to pursue knowledge even as far away as China.
BURSEVI:v2p276/r2.anchor: قال عليه السلام : "اطلبوا العلم ولو بالصين"

BURSEVI:v2p276/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p276/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p276/r3.claim: Learning from someone unqualified wastes one's days and leaves one regretting it when meeting the true experts.
BURSEVI:v2p276/r3.anchor: فكم من آخذ من غير متقن ضيع أيامه وعض عند لقاء النحارير أنامله

BURSEVI:v2p276/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p276/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p276/r4.claim: The partitive من means eat some of what the animal held, omitting inedible hides, bones, and feathers; the relative pronoun has an omitted antecedent, and على marks what was held for the hunter.
BURSEVI:v2p276/r4.anchor: من تبعيضية لما أن البعض مما لا يتعلق به الأكل كالجلود والعظام والريش

BURSEVI:v2p276/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p276/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p276/r5.claim: Eat only the prey the trained animal has not eaten; if it ate from the prey, it held it for itself, as the Prophet told ʿAdi ibn Hatim, and most jurists agree.
BURSEVI:v2p276/r5.anchor: وهو الذي لم يأكلن منه وأما ما أكلن منه فهو مما أمسكن على أنفسهن لقوله عليه السلام لعدي بن حاتم

BURSEVI:v2p276/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p276/r6.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
BURSEVI:v2p276/r6.claim: The Prophet told ʿAdi ibn Hatim not to eat prey from which the hunting animal has eaten, since it caught that prey for itself.
BURSEVI:v2p276/r6.anchor: لقوله عليه السلام لعدي بن حاتم : "وإن أكل منه فلا تأكل إنما أمسكه على نفسه"

BURSEVI:v2p276/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p276/r7.speaker: بعضهم ومنهم أبو حنيفة
BURSEVI:v2p276/r7.claim: Some jurists, including Abu Hanifa, allow the remainder of prey caught by a trained bird but not by a dog, since a dog can be trained not to eat by beating whereas a hawk cannot.
BURSEVI:v2p276/r7.anchor: وقال بعضهم ومنهم أبو حنيفة : يؤكل مما بقي من جوارح الطير ولا يؤكل مما بقي من الكلب

BURSEVI:v2p276/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p276/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p276/r8.claim: The pronoun in واذكروا اسم الله عليه may refer to what was trained, requiring invocation when releasing it, or to the prey held, requiring invocation when slaughtering it.
BURSEVI:v2p276/r8.anchor: الضمير لما في علمتم أي سموا عليه عند إرساله أو لما في ما أمسكن أي سموا عليه إذا أدركتم ذكاته

BURSEVI:v2p276/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p276/r9.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BURSEVI:v2p276/r9.claim: In Abu Thaʿlaba's report, the Prophet says to avoid the People of the Book's utensils if alternatives exist, or wash them if not; eat game taken with a bow or trained dog when God's name was invoked, and eat an untrained dog's catch only if it is found alive and slaughtered.
BURSEVI:v2p276/r9.anchor: وعن أبي ثعلبة قال : قلت يا نبي الله إنا بأرض قوم أهل كتاب أفنأكل في آنيتهم

BURSEVI:v2p276/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p276/r10.speaker: أنس رضي الله عنه
BURSEVI:v2p276/r10.claim: Anas reports that the Prophet sacrificed two white, horned rams by his own hand, saying God's name and magnifying Him.
BURSEVI:v2p276/r10.anchor: وعن أنس رضي الله عنه أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم "كان يضحي بكبشين أملحين أقرنين

BURSEVI:v2p276/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p276/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p276/r11.claim: The recommended formula is بسم الله الله أكبر without و because the conjunction would cut off the light of the basmala, according to Sharh Mukhtasar al-Wiqaya.
BURSEVI:v2p276/r11.anchor: والمستحب أن يقول بسم الله الله أكبر بلا واو لأن ذكر الواو يقطع نور التسمية

BURSEVI:v2p276/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p276/r12.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p276/r12.claim: Leaving the qibla orientation is disliked, while the sacrifice remains valid, as stated in al-Dhakhira.
BURSEVI:v2p276/r12.anchor: وكره ترك التوجه إلى القبلة وحلت كذا في "الذخيرة"

BURSEVI:v2p276/r13.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p276/r13.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p276/r13.claim: Deliberately omitting God's name makes the animal carrion and forbidden, while forgetting to invoke it leaves the meat lawful.
BURSEVI:v2p276/r13.anchor: ومتروك التسمية عمدا حرام لأنه ميتة بخلاف متروكها نسيانا فإنه حلال

BURSEVI:v2p276/r14.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p276/r14.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p276/r14.claim: Taqwa here means observing God's prohibitions; سريع الحساب means either that reckoning arrives soon or that it is completed quickly once begun, so God accounts for every small and great matter swiftly.
BURSEVI:v2p276/r14.anchor: في شأن محرماته {إن الله سريع الحساب} سريع إتيان حسابه أو سريع تمامه

BURSEVI:v2p276/r15.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p276/r15.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p276/r15.claim: The verse establishes that hunting is lawful.

BURSEVI:v2p277/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p277/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p277/r1.claim: In the inward reading, spiritual seekers ask what is lawful or forbidden to them in this world and the next.
BURSEVI:v2p277/r1.anchor: والإشارة في الآية أن أرباب الطلب وأصحاب السلوك

BURSEVI:v2p277/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p277/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BURSEVI:v2p277/r2.claim: A reported saying says the world is forbidden to the people of the hereafter, the hereafter to the people of the world, and both to God's own people.
BURSEVI:v2p277/r2.anchor: كما قال صلى الله عليه وسلم "الدنيا حرام على أهل الآخرة والآخرة حرام على أهل الدنيا

BURSEVI:v2p277/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p277/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p277/r3.claim: Inwardly, the good things are whatever do not interrupt one's way of reaching God.
BURSEVI:v2p277/r3.anchor: وهي ما لا يقطع عليكم طريق الوصول إلى الله فإن الله طيب لا يقبل إلا الطيب

BURSEVI:v2p277/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p277/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p277/r4.claim: Because God is pure and accepts only the pure, whatever one consumes, wears, says, thinks, or does from self-interest is tainted by the ego's self-directed impulse and is spiritually foul.
BURSEVI:v2p277/r4.anchor: وكل مأكول ومشروب وملبوس ومقول ومعقول ومعمول طلبتموه بحظ من الحظوظ فقد لوثتموه للوث داعي الوجود

BURSEVI:v2p277/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p277/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p277/r5.claim: What one seeks sincerely to fulfill obligations, purified by the breath of spiritual witnessing, is among the good things and suits the good.
BURSEVI:v2p277/r5.anchor: وما طلبتموه بالحق للقيام بأداء الحقوق مطيبا بنفحات الشهود فهو من الطيبات لا يصلح إلا للطيبين

BURSEVI:v2p277/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p277/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p277/r6.claim: Inwardly, God reckons people before they finish their deeds and repays them immediately: good brings intimacy, rank, and providential attraction; evil brings distance, expulsion, abasement, and abandonment.
BURSEVI:v2p277/r6.anchor: إشارة إلى أنه تعالى يحاسب العباد على أعمالهم قبل أن يفرغوا منها

BURSEVI:v2p277/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p277/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p277/r7.claim: An anonymous maxim says each person acts for himself: whoever does wrong harms himself, and whoever does good does good for himself.
BURSEVI:v2p277/r7.anchor: نعم ما قيل : (هركه كند بخود كند ورهمه نيك بد كند)

BURSEVI:v2p277/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p277/r8.speaker: الصائب
BURSEVI:v2p277/r8.claim: Al-Saʾib's couplet portrays one's own desire as the constant destroyer of one's inner home.
BURSEVI:v2p277/r8.anchor: هركه كند بخود كند ورهمه نيك بد كند) قال الصائب :

BURSEVI:v2p277#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p277#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p277#2/r1.claim: The good things are those that sound, cultivated natures do not find repugnant.
BURSEVI:v2p277#2/r1.anchor: أحل لكم الطيبات} وهي ما لم تستخبثه الطباع السليمة

BURSEVI:v2p277#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p277#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p277#2/r2.claim: Alternatively, good things are those no revealed text or juristic analogy establishes as forbidden.
BURSEVI:v2p277#2/r2.anchor: أو ما لم يدل نص شارع ولا قياس مجتهد على حرمته

ELMALILI:5:4-5/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:5:4-5/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:5:4-5/r1.claim: In his rendering of 5:4, the author calls lawful foods wholesome, describes trained hunting animals as taught from God's teaching, and says to eat what they bring and invoke God's name over it.
ELMALILI:5:4-5/r1.anchor: De ki sizin için bütün pâk nimetler helâl kılındı, alıştırarak ve Allah’ın size öğrettiğinden öğreterek yetiştirdiğiniz avcı hayvanların

ELMALILI:5:4-5/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:5:4-5/r5.speaker: İkrime ve Muhammed b. Ka‘b
ELMALILI:5:4-5/r5.claim: They report that after Gabriel said angels would not enter a house with a dog, the Prophet ordered dogs killed; after Abu Rafi killed Medina's dogs through al-ʿAwālī, three men asked what was lawful and the verse was revealed.
ELMALILI:5:4-5/r5.anchor: İkrime ve Muhammed b. Ka‘b’den nakledildiğine göre Cebrâil aleyhisselâm “biz kelb bulunan eve girmeyiz” demiş olduğundan dolayı Hazret-i Peygamber köpeklerin öldürülmesini emretmiş

ELMALILI:5:4-5/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:5:4-5/r6.speaker: Ebû Râfi‘
ELMALILI:5:4-5/r6.claim: In a report cited with its chain from al-Hākim's Ṣaḥīḥ, Abu Rafi says the Prophet ordered him to kill dogs, after which people asked what had been made lawful from the community he ordered killed and God revealed the verses.
ELMALILI:5:4-5/r6.anchor: Hâkim Ebû Abdullah’ın Sahîh’inde senediyle rivayet ettiği üzere Ebû Râfi‘demiştir ki: “Resûlullah bana köpeklerin katlini emretti

ELMALILI:5:4-5/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:5:4-5/r7.speaker: Sa‘îd b. Cübeyr
ELMALILI:5:4-5/r7.claim: He reports that ʿAdiyy b. Ḥātim and Zayd al-Khayl asked about dogs and falcons catching game, since some animals survived for slaughter while others died before it; the verse was revealed in response.
ELMALILI:5:4-5/r7.anchor: Sa‘îd b. Cübeyr demiştir ki: “Adiyy b. Hâtim ve Zeydü’l- Hayl ‘yâ Resûlallah, biz kelblerle ve doğanlarla av avlarız

ELMALILI:5:4-5/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:5:4-5/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:5:4-5/r8.claim: On the latter report, the question follows from the slaughter exception in 5:3, and the answer explains the legal meaning of ritual slaughter, fitting the context.
ELMALILI:5:4-5/r8.anchor: cevap da tezkiyenin ma‘nâ-yı şer‘îsini tafsil ve îzah sadedinde vârid olmuş demek olur ki siyâka pek münâsibdir

ELMALILI:5:4-5/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:5:4-5/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:5:4-5/r9.claim: The two reports imply different revelation sequences, one before and one after the prohibition passage, creating a chronology problem if the related 'today' statements refer to separate days.
ELMALILI:5:4-5/r9.anchor: Evvelki rivayet bu âyetlerin nüzûlü hurmet âyetinden mukaddem olduğuna, ikinci rivayet de muahhar bulunduğuna delâlet etmektedir

ELMALILI:5:4-5/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:5:4-5/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:5:4-5/r10.claim: He holds that the several 'today' statements belong to the same period, not separate days; they encompass the final years of the Prophet and make the prohibitions and permissions historically or legally connected.
ELMALILI:5:4-5/r10.anchor: bunlar mücerred yevm-i arefeyi değil, Sûre-i Mâide’nin bütün zamân-ı nüzûlünü istî‘âb eden sinîn-i ahîre-i Muhammediyeyi zamân-ı vâhid olarak ifade etmekte

ELMALILI:5:4-5/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:5:4-5/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:5:4-5/r11.claim: The phrase 'they ask you what is lawful for them' can present a general possible question, not only narrate a question that happened at one historical moment.
ELMALILI:5:4-5/r11.anchor: sual vâki‘i hikaye değil, “sorarlar” diye vâki‘ve mümkine şâmil olarak daha umûmî bir sual tasavvur edilmek lâzım gelir

ELMALILI:5:4-5/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:5:4-5/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:5:4-5/r12.claim: Tayyibāt contrasts with impure things; 7:157 says God makes wholesome things lawful and vile things forbidden, so the Muslim table should contain clean, pleasant foods.
ELMALILI:5:4-5/r12.anchor: nitekim وَيُحِلُّ لَهُمُ ٱلطَّيِّبَٰتِ وَيُحَرِّمُ عَلَيْهِمُ ٱلْخَبَٰٓئِثَ [el-A‘râf 7/157]

ELMALILI:5:4-5/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:5:4-5/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:5:4-5/r13.claim: Lexically, tayyib means something enjoyable, clean, and pleasant; by analogy, permitted food free of a presumption of prohibition is also called tayyib because it is harmless.
ELMALILI:5:4-5/r13.anchor: “tayyib” lügatta “müstelez”, yani hazzedilen temiz ve hoş şey demektir

ELMALILI:5:4-5/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:5:4-5/r14.speaker: İbn Cerîr Taberî
ELMALILI:5:4-5/r14.claim: Tabari and some exegetes gloss tayyibāt as simply lawful things, but the author rejects this as a weakly redundant reading, 'lawful things were made lawful.'
ELMALILI:5:4-5/r14.anchor: İbn Cerîr Taberî gibi bazı müfessirîn burada “tayyibât”ı helâller diye tefsir etmişlerse

ELMALILI:5:4-5/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:5:4-5/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:5:4-5/r15.claim: The majority of exegetes and jurists take tayyibāt to mean clean, pleasant things that people find appetizing, which the author adopts.
ELMALILI:5:4-5/r15.anchor: ekser müfessirîn ve müctehidîn bunun “lezzet ve iştihâ hissedilen temiz ve hoş şeyler” mânasına hamli vâcib [1574] olduğunu göstermişlerdir

ELMALILI:5:4-5/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:5:4-5/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:5:4-5/r16.claim: Not every personally liked thing is lawful: corrupted habits and morals do not count, and the criterion is what sound human nature finds clean and agreeable.
ELMALILI:5:4-5/r16.anchor: İbret, tab‘-ı selîmedir. Ve tayyibât ancak tab‘-ı selîm erbâbının tiksinmeyip hoşlandıkları şeylerdir

ELMALILI:5:4-5/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:5:4-5/r17.speaker: author
ELMALILI:5:4-5/r17.claim: Desert inhabitants and people under necessity may enjoy eating every kind of animal, but their tastes do not determine what counts as wholesome.
ELMALILI:5:4-5/r17.anchor: bâdiye halkı ve ıztırar içinde yaşayanlar her nevi hayvânâtı hoşlanıp yiyebilirler

ELMALILI:5:4-5/r18.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:5:4-5/r18.speaker: author
ELMALILI:5:4-5/r18.claim: Although 2:29 indicates original permissibility and would broadly allow benefiting from earthly things, 7:157 excludes vile things and limits lawful consumption to wholesome goods; absent specific evidence, this is the general rule for determining halal and haram.
ELMALILI:5:4-5/r18.anchor: Gerçi خَلَقَ لَكُم مَّا فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ جَمِيعًۭا [el-Bakara 2/29] medlûlünce ibâha asıldır

ELMALILI:5:4-5/r19.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:5:4-5/r19.speaker: author
ELMALILI:5:4-5/r19.claim: Pre-Islamic Arabs superstitiously prohibited some otherwise wholesome livestock as bahīra, sāʾiba, waṣīla, and ḥām; 7:32 reinforces that wholesome provision is lawful and helps explain the revelation's purpose.
ELMALILI:5:4-5/r19.anchor: tayyibâttan olan en‘âmdan bazılarını Sûre-i En‘âm’da beyan olunacağı üzere “bahîre”, “sâibe”, “vasîle”, “hâm” nâmlarıyla kendilerine tahrim ederler

ELMALILI:5:4-5/r20.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:5:4-5/r20.speaker: author
ELMALILI:5:4-5/r20.claim: Tayyibāt includes wholesome birds as well as livestock and all plants.
ELMALILI:5:4-5/r20.anchor: bu tayyibâtta behîme-i en‘âmdan başka kuşların ve hatta bütün nebâtâtın dahi hoşları dâhildir

ELMALILI:5:4-5/r21.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:5:4-5/r21.speaker: author
ELMALILI:5:4-5/r21.claim: The verse does not imply that every part of an otherwise lawful animal is lawful; impure parts remain forbidden even in animals that were properly slaughtered.
ELMALILI:5:4-5/r21.anchor: müzekkâ olan hayvânâtın eczâsı meyânında bulunan habâisin de haram olduğunu iş‘âr etmektedir

ELMALILI:5:4-5/r22.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:5:4-5/r22.speaker: author
ELMALILI:5:4-5/r22.claim: In sum, everything that sound nature and sound human disposition find wholesome is lawful.
ELMALILI:5:4-5/r22.anchor: Velhâsıl tab‘-ı selîmin ve fıtrat-ı sahîhanın hoşlandığı bütün tayyibât helâl kılındı

ELMALILI:5:4-5#2/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:5:4-5#2/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:5:4-5#2/r1.claim: Cevāriḥ is the plural of jāriḥa, from jarḥ; by association with making an impact it means earners, and can name both limbs that wound or acquire and hunting predators or birds.
ELMALILI:5:4-5#2/r1.anchor: “Cevârih”, “câriha”nın cem‘idir ki esasen “cerh”ten me’huz olup tesir mânası mülâhazasıyla kâsibe mânasına isim olmuştur

ELMALILI:5:4-5#2/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:5:4-5#2/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:5:4-5#2/r2.claim: Mukallibīn means trainers who accustom hunting animals to pursue prey and teach them hunting.
ELMALILI:5:4-5#2/r2.anchor: “Mükellib” teklîb eden, yani hayvânât-ı cârihayı ava dadandırıp alıştıran, avcılık tâlim edip öğreten demektir

ELMALILI:5:4-5#2/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:5:4-5#2/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:5:4-5#2/r3.claim: A trained dog goes when sent, answers a call, holds prey without eating it, does not flee when the owner approaches, obeys restraint, and has made this a habit through at least three repetitions.
ELMALILI:5:4-5#2/r3.anchor: bir kelb, sâhibi tarafından kışkırtıldığı yere gider, çağırılınca icâbet eder, avı tutunca hapseder yemez, sâhibi almak isteyince kaçmaz

ELMALILI:5:4-5#2/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:5:4-5#2/r4.speaker: أحمد بن حنبل
ELMALILI:5:4-5#2/r4.claim: Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal considers two successful repetitions sufficient for a hunting animal to count as trained.
ELMALILI:5:4-5#2/r4.anchor: Ahmed b. Hanbel ikiyi, Hasan-ı Basrî biri kâfi görmüştür

ELMALILI:5:4-5#2/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:5:4-5#2/r5.speaker: حسن-ı Basrî
ELMALILI:5:4-5#2/r5.claim: Ḥasan al-Baṣrī considers one successful repetition sufficient for a hunting animal to count as trained.
ELMALILI:5:4-5#2/r5.anchor: Ahmed b. Hanbel ikiyi, Hasan-ı Basrî biri kâfi görmüştür

ELMALILI:5:4-5#2/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:5:4-5#2/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:5:4-5#2/r6.claim: The term taklīb is used by predominance because dogs are the most commonly trained hunters, though kelb may refer to any predatory animal.
ELMALILI:5:4-5#2/r6.anchor: Bu tâlime “teklib” denilmesi tağlib tarîkiyledir. Zira ale’l-ekser tâlim edilen kelblerdir

ELMALILI:5:4-5#2/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:5:4-5#2/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:5:4-5#2/r7.claim: To show that kelb is not limited to dogs, he cites the Prophet's prayer that God send one of His kelbs against ʿUtba, whom a lion later ate on the road.
ELMALILI:5:4-5#2/r7.anchor: Resûlullah “اللهمّ سل ِّط عليه كلبًا من كلابك: İlâhî buna kelblerinden bir kelbi musallat et” diye dua etmiş

ELMALILI:5:4-5#2/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:5:4-5#2/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:5:4-5#2/r8.claim: The lawful trained hunters include dogs and other predators, trained through understanding God taught people; they may be kept and bought or sold, but the animals themselves are not food.
ELMALILI:5:4-5#2/r8.anchor: ava alıştırarak Allah’ın size öğrettiği idrâkâttan tâlim ederek öğrettiğiniz mu‘allem avcı hayvanlar helâl kılındı

ELMALILI:5:4-5#2/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:5:4-5#2/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:5:4-5#2/r9.claim: The syntax says eat from what hunting animals hold, not everything they hold, so one should eat the wholesome portions rather than all parts.
ELMALILI:5:4-5#2/r9.anchor: değil مِمَّآ أَمْسَكْنَ’dir. Tuttuklarının hepsini değil, bir kısmını, eczâ-yı tayyibesini yiyiniz

ELMALILI:5:4-5#2/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:5:4-5#2/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:5:4-5#2/r10.claim: The animals must hold prey for their human owner; prey held for themselves is not covered by the wording.
ELMALILI:5:4-5#2/r10.anchor: mutlaka أَمْسَكْنَ değil أَمْسَكْنَ عَلَيْكُمْ’dür, yani kendilerine değil size tutuverdiklerini yiyiniz

ELMALILI:5:4-5#2/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:5:4-5#2/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:5:4-5#2/r11.claim: If a trained dog sent by a hunter wounds and kills prey and the hunter arrives after it is dead, the game is lawful; the trained predator's wound takes the place of ritual slaughter.
ELMALILI:5:4-5#2/r11.anchor: Şu hâlde bir kelb mu‘allem olursa ve avcı tarafından sevk edilir de bir avı tutar, cerh eder, öldürür de avcı ona ölmüş olduğu hâlde yetişirse helâldir

ELMALILI:5:4-5#2/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:5:4-5#2/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:5:4-5#2/r12.claim: The same rule applies to other trained hunting animals and to arrows, spears, and guns; the hunter need not reach the animal alive, since that would erase the distinction between trained and untrained hunters.
ELMALILI:5:4-5#2/r12.anchor: Diğer cevârih ve kezâlik ok, mızrak, tüfek de böyledir. Behemehâl diri iken yetişilip zebh edilmesi şart değildir

ELMALILI:5:4-5#2/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:5:4-5#2/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:5:4-5#2/r13.claim: Wounding is required: although some permit prey killed by choking or impact based on the wording's apparent generality, the author says such prey is like strangled or struck carrion and forbidden.
ELMALILI:5:4-5#2/r13.anchor: bazıları مِمَّآ أَمْسَكْنَ عَلَيْكُمْ zâhiren mutlaktır diyerek yine yenir demiş ise de doğrusu bunun münhanika veya mevkūzeden farkı yoktur

ELMALILI:5:4-5#2/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:5:4-5#2/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:5:4-5#2/r14.claim: If a trained dog wounds and kills the prey but eats some, the animal is forbidden because it held the prey for itself rather than for its owner.
ELMALILI:5:4-5#2/r14.anchor: kelb-i mu‘allem cerh ü katletmiş olmakla beraber biraz da yemiş bulunursa bu da yenmez. Çünkü o onu kendine tutmuş demektir

ELMALILI:5:4-5#2/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:5:4-5#2/r15.speaker: سلمان-ı Fârisî، سعد ب. أبي وقاص، ابن عمر، أبو هريرة
ELMALILI:5:4-5#2/r15.claim: Salman al-Farisi, Saʿd ibn Abi Waqqas, Ibn ʿUmar, and Abu Hurayra are each reported to allow eating game that the trained dog has partly eaten.
ELMALILI:5:4-5#2/r15.anchor: Selmân-ı Fârisî’den, Sa‘d b. Ebî Vakkâs’dan, İbn Ömer’den, Ebû Hureyre’den yenir diye rivayet de edilmiştir

ELMALILI:5:4-5#2/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:5:4-5#2/r16.speaker: Mâlik ve Evzâî
ELMALILI:5:4-5#2/r16.claim: Malik and al-Awzaʿi also hold that game partly eaten by a trained dog is lawful.

ELMALILI:5:4-5#2/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:5:4-5#2/r17.speaker: author
ELMALILI:5:4-5#2/r17.claim: The issue distinguishes dogs from birds: a bird's eating part of its prey does not bar permissibility, a position held by the Hanafis.
ELMALILI:5:4-5#2/r17.anchor: kuşun yemiş olması hılline mâni‘olmayacağı gösterilmiştir ki Hanefiyye buna kāildirler

ELMALILI:5:4-5#2/r18.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:5:4-5#2/r18.speaker: author
ELMALILI:5:4-5#2/r18.claim: Remembering God's name over the catch means saying the basmala when releasing the dog or bird.
ELMALILI:5:4-5#2/r18.anchor: yani kelbi ve kuşu salarken besmele çekin

ELMALILI:5:4-5#2/r19.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:5:4-5#2/r19.speaker: author
ELMALILI:5:4-5#2/r19.claim: Because God reckons swiftly, people should guard against disobeying His commands.
ELMALILI:5:4-5#2/r19.anchor: ve her hâlde Allah serî‘u’l-hisâb olduğundan emirlerine muhalefetten sakının

ELMALILI:5:4-5#2/r20.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:5:4-5#2/r20.speaker: author
ELMALILI:5:4-5#2/r20.claim: After reinforcing the prohibitions with the statement of perfected religion in 5:3, the passage reaffirms and then generalizes lawful foods.
ELMALILI:5:4-5#2/r20.anchor: Bugün size bütün tayyibât, her nevi hoş nimetler helâl kılındı

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:4/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:4/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:4/r1.claim: After 5:3 prohibited meat from animals torn apart by predators, Muslims asked whether trained hunting dogs and birds counted as predators and whether their prey was lawful; this verse was revealed in response.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:4/r1.anchor: Önceki âyette müslümanlara birtakım hayvanların, özellikle yırtıcı olanlarının parçaladığı hayvanların etlerini yemenin haram olduğu bildirilince bazı müslümanlar av için yetiştirilmiş olan köpek ve kuşun da yırtıcılar kapsamına girip girmediğini

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:4/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:4/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:4/r2.claim: Tayyibāt means pleasant, clean, and good things.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:4/r2.anchor: “İyi ve temiz olanlar” diye tercüme edilen tayyibât sözlükte “lezzetli, temiz ve iyi şey” anlamına gelen tayyibe kelimesinin çoğuludur.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:4/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:4/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:4/r3.claim: Things are presumptively permissible absent evidence of prohibition; God created what is on earth for people, while revelation specifies forbidden items and the tayyib condition excludes filthy or harmful things.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:4/r3.anchor: İslâm’a göre eşyada aslolan mubah olmaktır. Bu genel kural, haram olduğuna dair hakkında delil bulunmayan her şey için geçerlidir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:4/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:4/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:4/r4.claim: The Prophet makes clean things lawful and impure things unlawful, and the Qur’an emphasizes that good things have not been forbidden; sound taste and the general qualities in revelation assess purity and goodness.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:4/r4.anchor: A‘râf sûresinin 157. âyetinde Hz. Peygamber’in, ümmetine temiz şeyleri helâl kıldığı, pis şeyleri ise haram kıldığı bildirilerek helâl olma hükmü temiz ve iyi şeylere tahsis edilmiştir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:4/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:4/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:4/r5.claim: Jawāriḥ literally covers predatory or tearing animals, but here means trained hunting dogs, falcons, and similar animals.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:4/r5.anchor: “Yırtıcı hayvanlar” diye tercüme edilen cevârih kelimesi cârihanın çoğuludur. Kelime bütün yırtıcı ve parçalayıcı hayvanları ifade etmekle birlikte burada av için eğitilmiş olan köpek, doğan ve benzeri yırtıcı hayvanlar kastedilmektedir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:4/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:4/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:4/r6.claim: Trained hunters do not excessively damage prey and are lawful, while untrained animals tear it; trained animals may be kept and sold, and their catch is lawful only when caught for the owner rather than for themselves.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:4/r6.anchor: Bu hayvanlar eğitildikleri takdirde yakaladıkları avı fazla hırpalamadıkları için bunlarla avlanmak meşrûdur. Eğitilmemiş hayvanlar avı hırpalayıp parçaladıklarından bunlarla avlanmak meşrû değildir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:4/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:4/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:4/r7.claim: The command to pronounce God’s name means saying the basmala when releasing a trained hunter; prey killed by it through wounding is lawful, but Hanafis forbid it if the basmala was omitted while Shafiʿis allow it even when omitted intentionally.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:4/r7.anchor: “Üzerine Allah’ın adını da anın” meâlindeki cümle, avcı hayvan av üzerine salıverilirken besmele çekilmesi yani “bismillâh” denilmesi gerektiğini ifade eder.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:4/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:4/r8.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:4/r8.claim: A trained dog’s wound substitutes for slaughter, so the prey need not be slaughtered while still alive; if another dog joined and the killer is unknown, the meat is unlawful.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:4/r8.anchor: Eğitilmiş köpeğin yaralaması kesme yerine geçtiği için avladığı hayvanın canlı iken kesilmesi şart değildir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:4/r9.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:4/r9.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:4/r9.claim: If a hunter kills prey by strangling it or striking it without wounding it, the animal is treated as strangled or struck and cannot be eaten.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:4/r9.anchor: Avcı hayvan, avı yaralamadan boğarak veya çarparak öldürürse bu av, boğulmuş veya darbe ile öldürülmüş hayvan hükmünde olduğu için yenmez

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:4/r10.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:4/r10.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:4/r10.claim: After 5:3 and 5:4 identify lawful and unlawful meats, the end of 5:4 demands reverence for God’s commands and warns that those who disobey will be held to account.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:4/r10.anchor: 3 ve 4. âyetlerde etleri helâl veya haram olan hayvanlar belirtildikten sonra 4. âyetin sonunda bu konuda Allah’ın emir ve yasaklarına saygılı davranılması istenmekte

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p87/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p87/r2.speaker: أبو رافع
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p87/r2.claim: After Gabriel said he would not enter a house containing an image or dog, a dog was found and Abu Rafi was ordered to kill the dogs in Medina; people then asked what was lawful, and the verse was revealed.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p87/r2.anchor: عن أبي رافع قال جاء جبريل إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فاستأذن عليه فأذن له فأبطأ فأخذ رداءه فخرج إليه

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p87/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p87/r3.speaker: عكرمة
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p87/r3.claim: When Abu Rafi was sent to kill dogs as far as al-ʿAwali, people asked the Prophet what was lawful for them, and the verse was revealed.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p87/r3.anchor: عن عكرمة أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بعث أبا رافع في قتل الكلاب حتى بلغ العوالي

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p87/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p87/r4.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p87/r4.claim: After the Prophet ordered dogs killed, people asked what was lawful for them, and the verse was revealed.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p87/r4.anchor: عن محمد بن كعب القرظي قال لما أمر النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بقتل الكلاب

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p87/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p87/r5.speaker: الشعبي
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p87/r5.claim: ʿAdi ibn Hatim asked about game hunted by dogs, and the Prophet did not know what to answer until the clause about teaching hunting animals was revealed.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p87/r5.anchor: من طريق الشعبي أن عدي بن حاتم الطائي قال أتى رجل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يسأله عن صيد الكلاب فلم يدر ما يقول له

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p87/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p87/r6.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p87/r6.claim: ʿAdi ibn Hatim and Zayd ibn Muhalhil asked what game was lawful when their dogs and falcons hunted cattle, donkeys and gazelles, while carrion was forbidden; the verse answered them.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p87/r6.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير أن عدي بن حاتم وزيد بن مهلهل الطائيين سألا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقالا يا رسول الله إنا قوم نصيد بالكلاب

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p190/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p190/r4.speaker: أبو رافع
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p190/r4.claim: Abu Rafi reports that after the dog-killing order, people asked what remained lawful to eat; the verse answered them, and al-Hakim included the report in his Sahih.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p190/r4.anchor: عن أبي رافع قال: أمرني رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - بقتل الكلاب، فقال الناس: يا رسول الله

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p191/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p191/r1.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p191/r1.claim: The commentators give a fuller Abu Rafi account: Gabriel would not enter because a puppy was in the house; after the order to kill dogs, people asked what they could eat.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p191/r1.anchor: وذكر المفسرون شرح هذه القصة قالوا: قال أبو رافع: جاء جبريل عليه السلام إلى النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم -

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p191/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p191/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p191/r2.claim: The Prophet permitted useful dogs, forbade keeping dogs with no benefit, and ordered harmful, biting, or rabid dogs killed while sparing harmless ones.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p191/r2.anchor: فلما نزلت أذن رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - في اقتناء الكلاب التي ينتفع بها، ونهى عن إمساك ما لا نفع فيه منها،

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p191/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p191/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p191/r3.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr says the verse concerned Adi ibn Hatim and Zayd al-Khayl, who asked about dog and hawk prey, some caught alive and some already dead.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p191/r3.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير: نزلت هذه الآية في عدي بن حاتم وزيد بن المهلهل الطائيين

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p191/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p191/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p191/r4.claim: The author glosses wholesome foods as slaughtered animals and trained hunting creatures as working dogs and birds of prey.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p191/r4.anchor: يعني الذبائح {وما علمتم من الجوارح} يعني: وصيد ما علمتم من الجوارح، وهي الكواسب من الكلاب وسباع الطير.

ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p184/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p184/r1.speaker: مجاهد
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p184/r1.claim: Mujahid says falcons, hawks, leopards, and other predatory animals used for hunting all count as trained hunting animals.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p184/r1.anchor: أخبرني ليث أنه سمع مجاهدا وسئل عن الصقر والبازي والفهد وما يصطاد به من السباع فقال هذه كلها جوارح

ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p184/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p184/r2.speaker: عدي بن حاتم
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p184/r2.claim: The Prophet told ʿAdi ibn Hatim to eat what his named hunting dog catches, even if it kills the prey; he forbade eating prey the dog ate or prey mixed with another, uninvoked dog because the killer is uncertain.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p184/r2.anchor: عن عدي بن حاتم قال قلت يا رسول الله إن أرضي أرض صيد قال إذا أرسلت كلبك وسميت فكل ما أمسك عليك كلبك وإن قتل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p158/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p158/r1.speaker: ابن شهاب
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p158/r1.claim: Ibn Shihab says the Prophet's letter to Amr ibn Hazm when sending him to Najran began with the command to fulfill contracts and continued through the statement that God is swift in reckoning.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p158/r1.anchor: وقال ابن شهاب: قرأت الكتاب الذي كتبه الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم لعمرو بن حزم حين بعثه إلى نجران

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p176#2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p176#2/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p176#2/r1.claim: Jawāriḥ are game-catching predatory animals and birds such as dogs, cheetahs, leopards, eagles, falcons, and hawks; the word refers either to wounding prey or earning a catch.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p176#2/r1.anchor: الجوارح: الكواسب من سباع البهائم والطير، كالكلب والفهد والنمر والعقاب والصقر والباز والشاهين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p176#2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p176#2/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p176#2/r2.claim: The root can mean earning, as in the saying that a woman has no earner and the verse about what people earn by day.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p176#2/r2.anchor: ومنه: ويعلم ما جرحتم بالنهار أي ما كسبتم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p176#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p176#2/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p176#2/r3.claim: The emphatic mukallib means one who trains dogs for hunting; the lighter form can mean an owner of dogs.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p176#2/r3.anchor: المكلب بالتشديد: معلم الكلاب ومضريها على الصيد، وبالتخفيف صاحب كلاب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p176#2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p176#2/r4.speaker: الزجاج
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p176#2/r4.claim: Al-Zajjaj says mukallib, mukallab, and kullāb all mean a dog owner.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p176#2/r4.anchor: وقال الزجاج: رجل مكلب ومكلب وكلاب صاحب كلاب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p178/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p178/r1.speaker: عكرمة ومحمد بن كعب
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p178/r1.claim: Ikrima and Muhammad b. Kaʿb report that Asim b. Adi, Saʿid b. Khaythama, and Uwaymir b. Saʿida asked what was lawful from the dogs after people had been ordered to kill them.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p178/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p178/r2.speaker: جبريل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p178/r2.claim: Gabriel's statement that angels do not enter a house containing a dog is given as the reason dogs were ordered killed.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p178/r2.anchor: لقول جبريل عليه السلام: «إنا لا ندخل بيتا فيه كلب»

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p178/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p178/r3.speaker: أبو رافع
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p178/r3.claim: In al-Hakim's Sahih, Abu Rafi reports that the Prophet ordered him to kill dogs; people then asked what they could lawfully take from them, and the verse was revealed.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p178/r3.anchor: بسنده إلى أبي رافع. قال: «أمرني رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بقتل الكلاب»

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p178/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p178/r4.speaker: ابن جبير
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p178/r4.claim: Ibn Jubayr gives another occasion: Adi b. Hatim and Zayd al-Khayl hunted with dogs and falcons, sometimes finding prey alive and sometimes only dead, and asked what was lawful.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p178/r4.anchor: وقال ابن جبير: نزلت في عدي بن حاتم وزيد الخيل قالا: يا رسول الله، إنا نصيد بالكلاب والبزاة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p178/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p178/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p178/r5.claim: The response exceeds the narrow question about hunted food by also giving a general answer about permissible foods.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p178/r5.anchor: وعلى اعتبار السبب يكون الجواب أكثر مما وقع السؤال عنه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p178/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p178/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p178/r6.claim: Mādhā may be parsed wholly as an interrogative followed by a predicate clause, or as interrogative mā plus predicate dhā, with the clause then a relative complement.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p178/r6.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون ماذا كلها استفهاما، والجملة خبر. ويحتمل أن يكون ما استفهاما، وذا خبرا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p178/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p178/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p178/r7.claim: The likely sense is what foods are lawful, prompted by the preceding list of forbidden carrion and other impure foods.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p178/r7.anchor: والظاهر أن المعنى: ماذا أحل لهم من المطاعم، لأنه لما ذكر ما حرم من الميتة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p178/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p178/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p178/r8.claim: Because the question uses third-person plural in يسألونك, its answer says لهم in the third person.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p178/r8.anchor: ولما كان يسألونك الفاعل فيه ضمير غائب قال لهم بضمير الغائب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p178/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p178/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p178/r9.claim: Direct wording ماذا أحل لنا is also grammatical: the first-person pronoun can quote what the questioners actually said.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p178/r9.anchor: ويجوز في الكلام ماذا أحل لنا، كما تقول: أقسم زيد ليضربن ولأضربن

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p178/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p178/r10.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p178/r10.claim: Al-Zamakhshari supplies an implicit saying verb after يسألونك; the author says this is unnecessary because the question clause is the suspended object of the verb, as in 68:40.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p178/r10.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: في السؤال معنى القول، فلذلك وقع بعده ماذا أحل لهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p178/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p178/r11.speaker: أبو عبد الله الرازي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p178/r11.claim: Al-Razi argues that this is not a verbatim quotation: questioners would say what is lawful for us, not for them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p178/r11.anchor: وقال أبو عبد الله الرازي: لو كان حكاية لكلامهم لكانوا قد قالوا: ماذا أحل لهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p178/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p178/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p178/r12.claim: The wording depicts how the event happened rather than reproducing the questioners' exact words.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p178/r12.anchor: وإنما يقولون: ماذا أحل لنا. بل الصحيح

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p178#2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p178#2/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p178#2/r1.claim: Arabs had forbidden wholesome foods such as bahīra, sāʾiba, waṣīla, and ḥām without God's warrant; the verse establishes that permitted foods are the wholesome ones.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p178#2/r1.anchor: لما كانت العرب تحرم أشياء من الطيبات كالبحيرة، والسائبة، والوصيلة، والحام، بغير إذن من الله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p178#2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p178#2/r2.speaker: الشافعي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p178#2/r2.claim: Al-Shafiʿi's interpretation that tayyibāt means tasty, pleasant things is strengthened by 7:157, which contrasts wholesome things with foul things.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p178#2/r2.anchor: ويقوي قول الشافعي: أن المعنى المستلذات

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p178#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p178#2/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p178#2/r3.claim: The author finds the interpretation tayyibāt = already lawful things weaker than the sense of pleasant foods.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p178#2/r3.anchor: ويضعف أن المعنى: قل أحل لكم المحللات

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p178#2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p178#2/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p178#2/r4.claim: In Arabic tayyib can mean either lawful or pleasant; judging taste belongs to people of good manners, though some people enjoy every animal.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p178#2/r4.anchor: والطيب في لسان العرب يستعمل للحلال وللمستلذ

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p178#2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p178#2/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p178#2/r5.claim: The reply is a verbal sentence that answers the question's meaning rather than its nominal grammatical form.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p178#2/r5.anchor: وهذه الجملة جاءت فعلية، فهي جواب لما سألوا عنه في المعنى لا على اللفظ

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p178#2/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p178#2/r6.speaker: الضحاك والسدي وابن جبير وعطاء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p178#2/r6.claim: They prioritize the explicit word mukallibīn and restrict jawāriḥ to dogs; Ibn Umar also says only dogs hunt, and he and Abu Jaʿfar reject bird-caught prey unless slaughtered while alive.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p178#2/r6.anchor: فغلب الضحاك والسدي وابن جبير وعطاء ظاهر لفظ مكلبين فقالوا: الجوارح هي الكلاب خاصة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p178#2/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p178#2/r7.speaker: قوم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p178#2/r7.claim: Some jurists permit hawks and similar birds, relying on the report of ʿAdi b. Hatim.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p178#2/r7.anchor: وجوز قوم البزاة، فجوزوا صيدها لحديث عدي بن حاتم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p178#2/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p178#2/r8.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p178#2/r8.claim: The majority prioritizes the broad wording what you have trained, reading mukallibīn as disciplining and habituating predators, and includes trainable beasts and birds.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p178#2/r8.anchor: وغلب الجمهور ظاهر: وما علمتم، وقالوا: معنى مكلبين مؤدبين ومضرين ومعودين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p178#2/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p178#2/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p178#2/r9.claim: The highest degree of training is that a predator responds when released and called, stops when rebuked after catching prey, and does not eat the catch.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p178#2/r9.anchor: وأقصى غاية التعليم أن يشلى فيستشلي، ويدعى فيجيب، ويزجر بعد الظفر فينزجر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p178#2/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p178#2/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p178#2/r10.claim: The circumstantial word mukallibīn reinforces trained, while also describing a competent trainer; the term derives from dogs because they are most often trained.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p178#2/r10.anchor: وفائدة هذه الحال وإن كانت مؤكدة لقوله: علمتم، فكان يستغنى عنها أن يكون المعلم مؤتمرا بالتعليم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p179/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p179/r1.speaker: أبو سليمان الدمشقي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p179/r1.claim: Abu Sulayman al-Dimashqi says the wording mukallibīn is used because most hunting was done with dogs.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p179/r1.anchor: قال أبو سليمان الدمشقي: وإنما قيل مكلبين، لأن الغالب من صيدهم أن يكون بالكلاب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p179/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p179/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p179/r2.claim: Taklīb derives from kalb in the sense of eagerness or habituation: one is described as a dog with respect to something when avid for it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p179/r2.anchor: واشتقت من الكلب وهي الضراوة يقال: هو كلب بكذا إذا كان ضاريا به

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p179/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p179/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p179/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhshari suggests a predator is called a dog, citing the Prophet's prayer that a dog attack a man; the author rejects the derivation because training is the trainer's act and predators are predators by nature.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p179/r3.anchor: قال الزمخشري: أو لأن السبع يسمى كلبا، ومنه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p179/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p179/r4.speaker: الحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p179/r4.claim: Hasan disliked game trained by a Jewish or Christian trainer, based on the verse's address to believers.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p179/r4.anchor: فكره الصيد به الحسن، أو مجوسيا فكره الصيد به: جابر بن عبد الله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p179/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p179/r5.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله والحسن وعطاء ومجاهد والنخعي والثوري وإسحاق
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p179/r5.claim: Jabir, Hasan, Ataa, Mujahid, al-Nakhaʿi, al-Thawri, and Ishaq disliked game trained by a Magian.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p179/r5.anchor: أو مجوسيا فكره الصيد به: جابر بن عبد الله، والحسن، وعطاء، ومجاهد، والنخعي، والثوري، وإسحاق

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p179/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p179/r6.speaker: مالك وأبو حنيفة والشافعي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p179/r6.claim: Malik, Abu Hanifa, and al-Shafiʿi permit prey caught by Jewish or Christian dogs when the hunter is Muslim, likening it to their knife.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p179/r6.anchor: وأجاز أكل صيد كلابهم: مالك، وأبو حنيفة، والشافعي إذا كان الصائد مسلما. قالوا: وذلك مثل شفرته

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p179/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p179/r7.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p179/r7.claim: The majority permits game hunted by a person of the Book; Malik rejects it and sees no distinction between such hunting and their slaughter.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p179/r7.anchor: والجمهور: على جواز ما صاد الكتابي. وقال مالك: لا يجوز فرق بين صيده وذبيحته

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p179/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p179/r8.speaker: عطاء وابن جبير والنخعي ومالك وأبو حنيفة والليث والشافعي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p179/r8.claim: The majority, including these named jurists, forbids eating game hunted by a Magian.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p179/r8.anchor: وما صاد المجوسي فالجمهور على منع أكله: عطاء، وابن جبير، والنخعي، ومالك، وأبو حنيفة، والليث، والشافعي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p179/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p179/r9.speaker: أبو ثور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p179/r9.claim: Abu Thawr reports a view that Magians count as People of the Book and their hunted game is lawful.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p179/r9.anchor: وقال أبو ثور: فيه قول أنهم أهل كتاب، وأن صيدهم جائز

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p179/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p179/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p179/r10.claim: The phrase what you trained may be coordinated with wholesome foods, requiring an omitted noun such as their game or their keeping; alternatively it is a subject with conditional mā and the answer eat, which is better because it needs no ellipsis.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p179/r10.anchor: وما علمتم موضع ما رفع على أنه معطوف على الطيبات، ويكون حذف مضاف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p179/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p179/r11.speaker: ابن عباس وابن الحنفية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p179/r11.claim: Ibn Abbas and Ibn al-Hanafiyya recite what you were taught in the passive, referring to knowledge about predators and hunting with them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p179/r11.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس وابن الحنفية: وما علمتم مبنيا للمفعول

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p179/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p179/r12.speaker: ابن عباس وابن الحنفية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p179/r12.claim: They also read mukallibīn as muklibīn from Form IV; Forms II and IV can share a meaning.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p179/r12.anchor: وقرأ: مكلبين من أكلب، وفعل وأفعل، قد يشتركان

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p179/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p179/r13.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p179/r13.claim: The apparent general wording includes wholly black dogs, so their prey is lawful according to the majority.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p179/r13.anchor: والظاهر دخول الكلب الأسود البهيم في عموم الجوارح، وأنه يجوز أكل صيده، وبه قال الجمهور

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p179/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p179/r14.speaker: أحمد وجماعة من أهل الظاهر
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p179/r14.claim: Ahmad and some literalists forbid prey caught by a solid-black dog because the law commands killing it; Ahmad knows of no one who permits it, and Ishaq agrees.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p179/r14.anchor: ومذهب أحمد وجماعة من أهل الظاهر: أنه لا يجوز أكل صيده، لأنه مأمور بقتله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p179/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p179/r15.speaker: الحسن وقتادة والنخعي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p179/r15.claim: Hasan, Qatada, and al-Nakhaʿi disliked hunting with a solid-black dog.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p179/r15.anchor: وكره الصيد به: الحسن، وقتادة، والنخعي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p179/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p179/r16.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p179/r16.claim: The passage's earlier highest standard of dog training is obedience to commands and stopping when rebuked.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p179/r16.anchor: وقد تقدم ذكر أقصى غاية التعليم في الكلب، أنه إذا أمر ائتمر، وإذا زجر انزجر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p179/r17.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p179/r17.speaker: قوم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p179/r17.claim: Some add that a trained hunting dog must not eat any of the prey; most do not impose that condition on predatory birds.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p179/r17.anchor: وزاد قوم شرطا آخر وهو أن لا يأكل مما صاد، فأما سباع الطير فلا يشترط فيها الأكل عند الجمهور

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p179/r18.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p179/r18.speaker: ربيعة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p179/r18.claim: Rabiʿa says a predatory bird is trained when it responds to a call.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p179/r18.anchor: وقال ربيعة: ما أجاب منها فهو المعلم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p179/r19.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p179/r19.speaker: ابن حبيب
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p179/r19.claim: Ibn Habib requires only obedience to the command for a bird, since birds cannot practically be made to stop when called back.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p179/r19.anchor: وقال ابن حبيب: لا يشترط فيها إلا شرط واحد: وهو أنه إذا أمرها أطاعت

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p179/r20.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p179/r20.speaker: أبو حنيفة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p179/r20.claim: Abu Hanifa sets no fixed number of successful hunts to establish training.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p179/r20.anchor: وكان أبو حنيفة لا يجد في ذلك عددا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p179/r21.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p179/r21.speaker: أصحابنا
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p179/r21.claim: The author's companions say a dog is trained after hunting and holding prey three times.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p179/r21.anchor: وقال أصحابنا: إذا صاد الكلب وأمسك ثلاث مرات فقد حصل له التعليم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p179/r22.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p179/r22.speaker: غيرهم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p179/r22.claim: Other jurists consider one successful hunt enough to count the dog as trained.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p179/r22.anchor: وقال غيرهم: إذا فعل ذلك مرة واحدة فقد صار معلما

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p180/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p180/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p180/r1.claim: Human training of predators comes from God's gift of perception and thought; predators likewise have enough awareness to accept commands and prohibitions.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p180/r1.anchor: إن تعليمكم إياهن ليس من قبل أنفسكم، إنما هو من العلم الذي علمكم الله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p180/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p180/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p180/r2.claim: Mentioning God's teaching here signals the merit and nobility of knowledge as a divine favor.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p180/r2.anchor: وفي قوله: مما علمكم الله، إشعار ودلالة على فضل العلم وشرفه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p180/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p180/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p180/r3.claim: The omitted object is teaching the animals to hunt for their owners rather than themselves; untrained prey is forbidden because permission requires training and the text says it is held for you.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p180/r3.anchor: ومفعول علم وتعلمونهن الثاني محذوف تقديره: وما علمتموه طلب الصيد لكم لا لأنفسهن

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p180/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p180/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p180/r4.claim: The phrase what God taught can mean the proper discipline of following God's commands and avoiding prohibitions, so the predator is trained when it obeys and stops.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p180/r4.anchor: ومعنى مما علمكم الله أي: من الأدب الذي أدبكم به تعالى، وهو اتباع أوامره واجتناب نواهيه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p180/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p180/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p180/r5.claim: Al-Zamakhshari interprets God's teaching as obligations revealed by God and acquired through reason.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p180/r5.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: مما علمكم الله من كلم التكليف، لأنه إلهام من الله تعالى ومكتسب بالعقل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p180/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p180/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p180/r6.claim: The clause teaching them is a second circumstantial clause; it may instead be independent if mā in the earlier phrase is not conditional, or parenthetical between condition and answer.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p180/r6.anchor: والجملة من قوله: تعلمونهن، حال ثانية. ويجوز أن تكون مستأنفة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p180/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p180/r7.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p180/r7.claim: Al-Zamakhshari advises students to learn only from deeply expert teachers and travel to them, warning that poor instruction wastes time and is regretted before masters.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p180/r7.anchor: وخطّب الزمخشري هنا فقال: وفيه فائدة جليلة وهي أن كل آخذ علما أن لا يأخذه إلا من قبل أهله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p180/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p180/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p180/r8.claim: Eat is a permissive command, and min is partitive: eat some of the prey caught for you; treating min as redundant is weak.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p180/r8.anchor: فكلوا مما أمسكن عليكم هذا أمر إباحة. ومن هنا للتبعيض والمعنى: كلوا من الصيد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p180/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p180/r9.speaker: سعد بن أبي وقاص وسلمان الفارسي وأبو هريرة وابن عمر ومالك وأصحابه
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p180/r9.claim: They allow prey held for its owner even if the predator eats from it, including the remnant, because the predator's killing is its slaughter.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p180/r9.anchor: وظاهره أنه إذا أمسك على مرسله جاز الأكل سواء أكل الجارح منه، أو لم يأكل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p180/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p180/r10.speaker: أبو هريرة وابن جبير وعطاء وقتادة وعكرمة والشافعي وأحمد وإسحاق وأبو ثور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p180/r10.claim: They forbid any remainder the predator has eaten because it held that prey for itself, not its owner.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p180/r10.anchor: وقال أبو هريرة أيضا وابن جبير، وعطاء، وقتادة، وعكرمة، والشافعي، وأحمد، وإسحاق، وأبو ثور: لا يؤكل ما بقي من أكل الكلب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p181/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p181/r1.speaker: النبي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p181/r1.claim: In the report of ʿAdi, the Prophet says not to eat if the dog eats, because it held the prey for itself.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p181/r1.anchor: في حديث عدي «وإذا أكل فلا تأكل فإنما أمسك على نفسه»

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p181/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p181/r2.speaker: علي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p181/r2.claim: Ali says that if a falcon eats from the prey, it should not be eaten.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p181/r2.anchor: وعن علي: «إذا أكل البازي فلا تأكل»

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p181/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p181/r3.speaker: ابن عباس والشعبي والنخعي وحماد بن أبي سليمان وأبو جعفر محمد بن علي الثوري وأبو حنيفة وأصحابه
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p181/r3.claim: They distinguish dogs from falcons: forbid prey partly eaten by a dog but permit falcon prey, because dogs can be trained to stop whereas falcons cannot be struck or stopped in that way.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p181/r3.anchor: وفرق قوم ما أكل منه الكلب فمنعوا من أكله، وبين ما أكل منه البازي، فرخصوا في أكله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p181/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p181/r4.speaker: سفيان الثوري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p181/r4.claim: The apparent ruling treats a predator drinking blood as having eaten from the prey; Sufyan al-Thawri disliked that case.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p181/r4.anchor: والظاهر أن الجارح إذا شرب من الدم أكل الصيد، وكره ذلك سفيان الثوري

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p181/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p181/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p181/r5.claim: The apparent ruling forbids prey caught after the predator escapes without being released by its owner.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p181/r5.anchor: والظاهر أنه إذا انفلت من صاحبه فصاد من غير إرسال أنه لا يجوز أكل ما صاد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p181/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p181/r6.speaker: علي والأوزاعي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p181/r6.claim: Ali and al-Awzaʿi allow prey if its owner had taken the animal out for hunting.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p181/r6.anchor: وقال علي، والأوزاعي: إن كان أخرجه صاحبه للصيد جاز أكل ما صاد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p181/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p181/r7.speaker: ربيعة وأبو حنيفة ومالك والشافعي وأبو ثور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p181/r7.claim: Rabiʿa, Abu Hanifa, Malik, al-Shafiʿi, and Abu Thawr forbid prey when its owner did not release the animal.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p181/r7.anchor: وممن منع من أكله إذا صاد من غير إرسال صاحبه: ربيعة، وأبو حنيفة، ومالك، والشافعي، وأبو ثور

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p181/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p181/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p181/r8.claim: The apparent general phrase permits eating prey killed in a dog's mouth without a wound; another view forbids it as carrion.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p181/r8.anchor: والظاهر جواز أكل ما قتله الكلب بفمه من غير جرح لعموم مما أمسكن

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p181/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p181/r9.speaker: بعضهم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p181/r9.claim: Some jurists forbid prey killed by a dog's mouth without a wound because it is dead carrion.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p181/r9.anchor: وقال بعضهم: لا يجوز لأنه ميت

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p181/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p181/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p181/r10.claim: The pronoun in remember God's name on it most likely returns to the implied act of eating, meaning pronounce God's name over food.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p181/r10.anchor: الظاهر عود الضمير في عليه إلى المصدر المفهوم من قوله: فكلوا، أي على الأكل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p181/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p181/r11.speaker: النبي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p181/r11.claim: A report in Sahih Muslim says to name God and eat what is beside you, supporting the reference to eating.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p181/r11.anchor: وفي الحديث في صحيح مسلم «سم الله وكل مما يليك»

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p181/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p181/r12.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p181/r12.claim: Another reading refers the pronoun to the prey, requiring God's name when it is slaughtered after being caught alive; the author finds this far-fetched.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p181/r12.anchor: وقيل: يعود على ما أمسكن، على معنى: وسموا عليه إذا أدركتم ذكاته، وهذا فيه بعد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p181/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p181/r13.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p181/r13.claim: A further reading refers it to the trained predators and requires invoking God's name when releasing them, supported by the Prophet's instruction about releasing a dog after naming God.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p181/r13.anchor: وقيل: على ما علمتم من الجوارح أي: سموا عليه عند إرساله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p181/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p181/r14.speaker: النبي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p181/r14.claim: The Prophet says prey may be eaten if one releases the dog after invoking God's name.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p181/r14.anchor: إذا أرسلت كلبك وذكرت اسم الله فكل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p181/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p181/r15.speaker: الفقهاء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p181/r15.claim: Jurists differ over whether naming God at release is obligatory or recommended; the recommended formula is In God's name, and God is greatest.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p181/r15.anchor: واختلفوا في التسمية عند الإرسال: أهي على الوجوب؟ أو على الندب؟ والمستحب أن يكون لفظها بسم الله والله أكبر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p181/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p181/r16.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p181/r16.claim: The proposed reordered syntax placing invocation before eat is weak and should be rejected.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p181/r16.anchor: وقول من زعم: أن في الكلام تقديما وتأخيرا، وأن الأصل: فاذكروا اسم الله عليه وكلوا مما أمسكن عليكم، قول مرغوب عنه لضعفه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p181/r17.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p181/r17.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p181/r17.claim: The command to fear God follows the food prohibitions because piety keeps people from the forbidden; swift reckoning threatens those who disobey and may mean the near arrival of Judgment.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p181/r17.anchor: لما تقدم ذكر ما حرم وأحل من المطاعم أمر بالتقوى، فإن التقوى بها يمسك الإنسان عن الحرام

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p181/r18.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p181/r18.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p181/r18.claim: Alternatively, reckoning means recompense that comes soon, or God's encompassing knowledge lets Him account for all creation at once without debate or counting.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p181/r18.anchor: أو يراد بالحساب المجازاة، فتوعد من لم يتق بمجازاة سريعة قريبة، أو لكونه تعالى محيطا بكل شيء

QASHANI:5:4-5/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:5:4-5/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:5:4-5/r1.claim: The permitted good things are divine realities, true knowledge, and intellectual virtues acquired through intellect, heart, and spirit.
QASHANI:5:4-5/r1.anchor: من الحقائق والمعارف الحقية والفضائل العلمية

QASHANI:5:4-5/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:5:4-5/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:5:4-5/r2.claim: Trained hunting animals symbolize outward and inward senses, other faculties, and bodily instruments used to acquire virtues and good manners.
QASHANI:5:4-5/r2.anchor: من جوارح حواسكم الظاهرة والباطنة وسائر قواكم وآلاتكم البدنية في اكتساب الفضائل والآداب

QASHANI:5:4-5/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:5:4-5/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:5:4-5/r3.claim: Training them with what God taught means using moral and legal sciences that explain how to enjoy pleasures fairly.
QASHANI:5:4-5/r3.anchor: من علوم الأخلاق والشرائع التي تبين طريق الاحتظاء من الحظوظ على وجه العدالة

QASHANI:5:4-5/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:5:4-5/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:5:4-5/r4.claim: Use what the faculties acquire through proper teaching, inward intention, and a sound aim that perfects the person or community, rather than pursuing their own pleasure and appetite.
QASHANI:5:4-5/r4.anchor: على ما ينبغي بنية وإرادة قلبية وغرض صحيح يؤدي إلى كمال الشخص أو النوع

QASHANI:5:4-5/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:5:4-5/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:5:4-5/r5.claim: Remembering God's name means inwardly recognizing that these faculties serve the complete human form, not another goal; make God a safeguard so their use is good.
QASHANI:5:4-5/r5.anchor: واحضروا بقلوبكم أنها للصورة الإنسانية الكاملة تقصد وتراد

QASHANI:5:4-5/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:5:4-5/r6.speaker: author
QASHANI:5:4-5/r6.claim: God's swift accounting is the immediate imprint of acquired dispositions in the soul when one acts, rather than an accounting stretched across periods.
QASHANI:5:4-5/r6.anchor: يحاسبكم بها في آن لا في أزمنة، كحصول هيآتها في أنفسكم عند ارتكابها

QUSHAYRI:v1p250/r7.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p250/r7.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p250/r7.claim: Lawful food is what leaves the heart wholesome; forbidden food hardens the heart and brings estrangement, while guarding against illicit and doubtful food brightens hearts and times.
QUSHAYRI:v1p250/r7.anchor: وهو الحلال الذي تحصل من تناوله طيبة القلوب فإن أكل الحرام يوجب قسوة القلب

QUSHAYRI:v1p250/r8.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p250/r8.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p250/r8.claim: The trained dog gives up its own share and keeps the catch for its master; likewise, a person whose deeds and states belong wholly to God rises in rank without self-interest.
QUSHAYRI:v1p250/r8.anchor: ولما كان الكلب المعلم ترك حظه ، وأمسك ما اصطاده على صاحبه حلت فريسته

QUSHAYRI:v1p250/r9.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p250/r9.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p250/r9.claim: Good manners can raise the lowly to the rank of the great, while bad manners can lower the noble to the state of the inferior.
QUSHAYRI:v1p250/r9.anchor: ويقال حسن الأدب يلحق الأخسة برتبة الأكابر ، وسوء الأدب يرد الأعزة إلى حالة الأصاغر

QUSHAYRI:v1p250/r10.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p250/r10.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p250/r10.claim: The command to mention God's name shows that eating in heedlessness is not pleasing in the final reckoning.
QUSHAYRI:v1p250/r10.anchor: بين أن الأكل - على الغفلة - غير مرضي عنه ( في القيمة )

QUSHAYRI:v1p250/r11.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p250/r11.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p250/r11.claim: God's swift accounting means no affair distracts Him from another; He promptly accounts for the beloved and friends, with each moment's reward or punishment multiplied.
QUSHAYRI:v1p250/r11.anchor: بحيث لا يشغله شأن عن شأن ، وسريع الحساب - اليوم - مع الأحباب والأولياء ، فهم لا يسامحون

ALUSI-FULL:v6p62#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p62#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v6p62#2/r1.claim: The passage begins detailing permitted things after the preceding account of prohibitions.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p62#2/r1.anchor: شروع فى تفصيل المحللات التى ذكر بعضها على وجه الاجمال اثر بيان المحرمات

ALUSI-FULL:v6p62#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p62#2/r2.speaker: أبو رافع
ALUSI-FULL:v6p62#2/r2.claim: Abū Rāfiʿ reports that Gabriel delayed entering because a house contained an image or dog; after a puppy was found, the Prophet ordered dogs killed in Medina, and people’s question about what remained lawful occasioned the verse.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p62#2/r2.anchor: أخرج ابن جرير والبيهقى فى سننه وغيرهما عن أبى رافع قال : جاء جبريل عليه السلام

ALUSI-FULL:v6p62#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p62#2/r3.speaker: عكرمة
ALUSI-FULL:v6p62#2/r3.claim: ʿIkrima identifies the questioners as ʿĀṣim ibn ʿAdī, Saʿd ibn Khaythama, and ʿUwaym ibn Sāʿida.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p62#2/r3.anchor: وأخرج ابن جرير عن عكرمة أن السائل عاصم بن عدى وسعد بن خيثمة وعويم بن ساعدة

ALUSI-FULL:v6p62#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p62#2/r4.speaker: ابن جبير
ALUSI-FULL:v6p62#2/r4.claim: Ibn Jubayr instead names ʿAdī ibn Ḥātim and Zayd ibn al-Muhalhil al-Ṭāʾī as the questioners.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p62#2/r4.anchor: وأخرج ابن أبى حاتم عن ابن جبير أن السائل عدى بن حاتم وزيد بن المهلهل الطائيان

ALUSI-FULL:v6p62#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p62#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v6p62#2/r5.claim: The question embeds the meaning of a statement, so its answer is quoted as a clause; the verb governs the clause because asking causes and leads to knowledge, contrary to Abū Ḥayyān.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p62#2/r5.anchor: وقد ضمن السؤال معنى القول ولذا حكيت به الجملة كما تحكى بالقول وليس معلقا

ALUSI-FULL:v6p62#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p62#2/r6.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v6p62#2/r6.claim: Abū Ḥayyān disagrees that the question verb can govern the clause; some grammarians posit an omitted noun, “the answer to what was made lawful.”
ALUSI-FULL:v6p62#2/r6.anchor: خلافا لأبى حيان فاندفع ماقيل : إن السؤال ليس مما يعمل فى الجمل

ALUSI-FULL:v6p62#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p62#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v6p62#2/r7.claim: The prior context suggests they ask which foods and meals are permitted; another view takes the question to concern game and slaughter.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p62#2/r7.anchor: المسئول نظرا للكلام السابق ماأحل من المطاعم والمآكل

ALUSI-FULL:v6p62#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p62#2/r8.speaker: البلخي
ALUSI-FULL:v6p62#2/r8.claim: Al-Balkhī defines wholesome things as those that sound human dispositions do not find disgusting or recoil from.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p62#2/r8.anchor: مالم تستخبثه الطباع السليمة ولم تنفر عنه وإلى ذلك ذهب البلخى

ALUSI-FULL:v6p62#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p62#2/r9.speaker: أبو علي الجبائي، أبو مسلم
ALUSI-FULL:v6p62#2/r9.claim: Abū ʿAlī al-Jubbāʾī and Abū Muslim define wholesome things as foods, sacrifices, and game God has authorized people to eat.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p62#2/r9.anchor: وعن أبى على الجبائى وأبى مسلم هى ماأذن سبحانه فى أكله من المأكولات والذبائح والصيد

ALUSI-FULL:v6p62#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p62#2/r10.speaker: قائلون
ALUSI-FULL:v6p62#2/r10.claim: Another definition is anything for which no text or analogy establishes a prohibition; consensus also falls within this view because it must rest on textual evidence.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p62#2/r10.anchor: مالم يرد بتحريمه نص أو قياس ويدخل فى ذلك الاجماع إذ لابد من استناده لنص

ALUSI-FULL:v6p62#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p62#2/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v6p62#2/r11.claim: On the latter two definitions “wholesome” means lawful, while on the first it means pleasant; Arabic usage supports both senses.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p62#2/r11.anchor: والطيب على هذين القولين بمعنى الحلال وعلى الأول بمعنى الحلال وعلى الأول بمعنى المستلذ وقد جاء بالمعنيين

ALUSI-FULL:v6p62#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p62#2/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v6p62#2/r12.claim: One grammatical analysis coordinates “what you train” with wholesome things as a relative clause, supplying an omitted “catch”; another treats it as the source of catching, a specific case under the general permission.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p62#2/r12.anchor: عطف على الطيبات بتقدير مضاف على أن ما موصولة والعائد محذوف أى وصيد ماعلمتموه

ALUSI-FULL:v6p62#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p62#2/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v6p62#2/r13.claim: Al-Ālūsī says the apparent reading needs no implied “catch,” because permissibility and prohibition attach to actions.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p62#2/r13.anchor: الظاهر أنه لاحاجة إلى جعل الصيد لأن الحل والحرمة مما يتعلق بالفعل

ALUSI-FULL:v6p62#2/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p62#2/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v6p62#2/r14.claim: Alternatively, “what” is conditional and the following command is its response, coordinated with the sentence “the wholesome things are made lawful for you.”
ALUSI-FULL:v6p62#2/r14.anchor: ويحتمل أن تكون ما شرطية مبتدأ والجواب فكلوا والخبر الجواب والشرط على المختار

ALUSI-FULL:v6p62#2/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p62#2/r15.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v6p62#2/r15.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī allows an implied noun even with conditional “what,” since a noun annexed to a conditional expression has the same grammatical status as the expression itself.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p62#2/r15.anchor: ونقل عن الزمخشرى أنه قال بالتقدير فيه وقال تقديره لايبطل كون ما شرطية

ALUSI-FULL:v6p62#2/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p62#2/r16.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v6p62#2/r16.claim: The implied-noun analysis is challenged because the predicate would then need an understood referent, unless “what they caught” is made to stand in place of “what you trained.”
ALUSI-FULL:v6p62#2/r16.anchor: وتعقب بأنه على ذلك التقدير يصير الخبر حاليا عن ضمير المبتدأ

ALUSI-FULL:v6p62#2/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p62#2/r17.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v6p62#2/r17.claim: A further, less apparent analysis treats “what” as a relative pronoun and “eat” as its predicate, with the prefixed faʾ inserted by analogy to a conditional clause.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p62#2/r17.anchor: وجوز كونها مبتدأ على تقدير كونها موصولة أيضا والخبر كلوا والفاء إنما دخلت تشبيها للموصول باسم الشرط

ALUSI-FULL:v6p62#2/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p62#2/r18.speaker: أبو البقاء
ALUSI-FULL:v6p62#2/r18.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ takes the hāʾ in “jawāriḥ” as an intensive feminine ending; the word is commonly used without an expressed noun.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p62#2/r18.anchor: الجوارح حمع جارحة والهاء فيها كا قال أبو البقاء للمبالغة وهى صفة غلبة

ALUSI-FULL:v6p62#2/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p62#2/r19.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v6p62#2/r19.claim: “Jawāriḥ” means acquisitive beasts of prey and birds, either because they earn for their owners or because they commonly wound prey.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p62#2/r19.anchor: الكواسب من سباع البهائم والطير وهو من قولهم

ALUSI-FULL:v6p62#2/r20.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p62#2/r20.speaker: ابن عمر، السدي، الضحاك، أئمة أهل البيت
ALUSI-FULL:v6p62#2/r20.claim: Ibn ʿUmar, al-Suddī, al-Ḍaḥḥāk, and a report ascribed to the Imams of the Prophet’s family restrict “jawāriḥ” to dogs.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p62#2/r20.anchor: وعن ابن عمر رضى الله تعالى عنهما والسدى والضحاك وهو المروى عن أئمة أهل البيت بزعم الشيعة أنها الكلاب فقط

ALUSI-FULL:v6p62#2/r21.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p62#2/r21.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v6p62#2/r21.claim: “Mukallibīn” means training the hunting animals; the term derives from the dog because it is commonly trained, or because every beast of prey may be called a dog.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p62#2/r21.anchor: أى معلمين لها الصيد والمكلب مؤدب الجوارح ومضربها بالصيد

ALUSI-FULL:v6p62#2/r22.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p62#2/r22.speaker: أبو نوفل
ALUSI-FULL:v6p62#2/r22.claim: Abū Nawfal reports that a lion killed Lahab ibn Abī Lahab after the Prophet prayed for a “dog” to be set upon him; al-Ḥākim graded the report sound in chain, though al-Ālūsī says it does not show birds are included.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p62#2/r22.anchor: صحيح الأسناد من حديث أبى نوفل قال : كان لهب بن أبى لهب يسب النبى

ALUSI-FULL:v6p63/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p63/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v6p63/r1.claim: Another etymology derives “mukallibīn” from kalb meaning avidity: someone may be called avid for something, and the participle describes the trainer.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p63/r1.anchor: من الكلب الذى هو بمعنى الضرواة يقال : هو كلب بكذا إذا ضاربا به

ALUSI-FULL:v6p63/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p63/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v6p63/r2.claim: The circumstantial “mukallibīn” emphasizes the intensity of training, since only an expert at the craft is called a trainer.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p63/r2.anchor: وانتصابه على الحالية من فاعل علمتم وفائدتها المبالغة فى التعليم لما أن الملكب لايقع إلا على النحرير فى علمه

ALUSI-FULL:v6p63/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p63/r3.speaker: ابن عباس، ابن مسعود، الحسن
