ALUSI-FULL:v6p63/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, Ibn Masʿūd, and al-Ḥasan read “mukallibīn” with a light consonant from “aklaba”; the forms faʿʿala and afʿala can share a meaning.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p63/r3.anchor: وعن ابن عباس وابن مسعود والحسن رضى الله تعالى عنهم أنهم قرأوا مكلبين بالتخفيف من أكلب وفعل وأفعل قد يستعملان بمعنى واحد

ALUSI-FULL:v6p63/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p63/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v6p63/r4.claim: “Teaching them” may be circumstantial from the pronoun in “trainers,” an independent sentence if “what” is not conditional, or a second circumstance from “you trained”; Abū al-Baqāʾ’s objection to two circumstances from one governor is questioned.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p63/r4.anchor: حال من ضمير مكلبين أو استئنافية إن لم تكن ما شرطية وإلا فهى معترضة

ALUSI-FULL:v6p63/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p63/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v6p63/r5.claim: “From what God taught you” refers to techniques and methods of training, given either by divine inspiration or by the intellect God created in the animals.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p63/r5.anchor: من الحيل وطرق التعليم والتأديب وذلك إما بالالهام منه سبحاته أو بالعقل الذى خلقه فيهم

ALUSI-FULL:v6p63/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p63/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v6p63/r6.claim: Another explanation is that God taught people the signs of trained prey: the animal responds to release and command, returns when called, and holds prey without eating it.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p63/r6.anchor: المراد مما عرفكم سبحانه أن تعلموه من اتباع الصيد بأن يسترسل بارسال صاحبه وينزجر

ALUSI-FULL:v6p63#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p63#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v6p63#2/r1.claim: In “from what God taught you,” the preposition may indicate cause or mean “some of what God taught you.”
ALUSI-FULL:v6p63#2/r1.anchor: من أجلية وقيل : تبعيضية أى بعض ما علمكم الله

ALUSI-FULL:v6p63#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p63#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v6p63#2/r2.claim: “Eat what they catch for you” follows from the permission for trained animals, makes explicit the result of training, or serves as a conditional response or predicate.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p63#2/r2.anchor: جملة متفرعة على بيان حل صيد الجوارح المعلمة مبنية للمضاف المقدر

ALUSI-FULL:v6p63#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p63#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v6p63#2/r3.claim: The preposition in “from what they caught” is partitive because hides, bones, and other parts of a catch are not eaten; al-Akhfash instead treats it as extra.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p63#2/r3.anchor: من تبعيضية إذ من الممسك مالا يؤكل كالجلد والعظم وغير ذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v6p63#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p63#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v6p63#2/r4.claim: “What” is relative or descriptive with an omitted object, and the feminine pronoun refers to the trained animals; “for you” is figuratively an expression of superiority.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p63#2/r4.anchor: ما موصولة أو موصوفة والعائد محذوف أى أمسكنه وضمير الؤنث للجوارح

ALUSI-FULL:v6p63#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p63#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v6p63#2/r5.claim: The restriction “for you” excludes prey the animals catch for themselves, signaled by their eating from it.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p63#2/r5.anchor: والتقييد بذلك لاخراج ماأمسكنه على أنفسهن وعلامته أن يأكلن منه

ALUSI-FULL:v6p63#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p63#2/r6.speaker: عدي بن حاتم
ALUSI-FULL:v6p63#2/r6.claim: A report from ʿAdī ibn Ḥātim says that if a trained dog was released in God’s name, one may eat what it catches for its owner, but not if it eats, since then it caught the prey for itself; most jurists follow this.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p63#2/r6.anchor: روى أصحاب السنن عن عدى بن حاتم

ALUSI-FULL:v6p63#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p63#2/r7.speaker: علي، الشعبي، عكرمة
ALUSI-FULL:v6p63#2/r7.claim: ʿAlī, al-Shaʿbī, and ʿIkrima are also reported to hold that prey from a dog that eats must not be eaten.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p63#2/r7.anchor: روى عن على كرم الله تعالى وجهه والشعبى وعكرمة

ALUSI-FULL:v6p63#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p63#2/r8.speaker: أبو حنيفة وأصحابه
ALUSI-FULL:v6p63#2/r8.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa and his followers say a dog that eats its catch is untrained and its prey is unlawful, but prey from a falcon or similar bird remains lawful even if it eats because such birds cannot be trained not to eat.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p63#2/r8.anchor: وقال أبو حنيفة رضى الله تعالى عنه وأصحابه إذا أكل الكلب من الصيد فهو غير معلم لايؤكل صيده ويؤكل صيد البازى ونحوه

ALUSI-FULL:v6p63#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p63#2/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v6p63#2/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās is reported to distinguish dogs from falcons: do not eat prey if the dog eats, but eat prey if the falcon eats, since the dog can be beaten and the falcon cannot.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p63#2/r9.anchor: إذا أكل الكلب فلا تأكل وإذا أكل الصقر فكل لأن الكلب تستطيع أن تضربه

ALUSI-FULL:v6p63#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p63#2/r10.speaker: إمام الحرمين
ALUSI-FULL:v6p63#2/r10.claim: Imām al-Ḥaramayn, a Shāfiʿī, follows the distinction that tolerates a hunting bird’s eating its prey.

ALUSI-FULL:v6p63#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p63#2/r11.speaker: مالك، الليث
ALUSI-FULL:v6p63#2/r11.claim: Mālik and al-Layth permit eating the catch even when the dog has eaten from it.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p63#2/r11.anchor: يؤكل وان أكل الكلب منه وقد روى عن سلمان

ALUSI-FULL:v6p63#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p63#2/r12.speaker: سلمان، سعد بن أبي وقاص، أبو هريرة
ALUSI-FULL:v6p63#2/r12.claim: Salman, Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ, and Abū Hurayra are reported to permit the catch if the dog ate two-thirds, a third remains, and God’s name was invoked.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p63#2/r12.anchor: وقد روى عن سلمان وسعد بن أبى وقاص وأبى هريرة رضى الله تعالى عنهم أنه إذا أكل الكلب ثلثيه وبقى ثلثه

ALUSI-FULL:v6p63#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p63#2/r13.speaker: ابن عباس، الحسن، السدي
ALUSI-FULL:v6p63#2/r13.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Ḥasan, and al-Suddī take “invoke God’s name over it” to mean saying the name when releasing the trained animal.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p63#2/r13.anchor: الضمير لما علمتم كما يدل عليه الخبر السابق والمعنى سموا عليه عند إرساله وروى ذلك ابن عباس والحسن والسدى

ALUSI-FULL:v6p63#2/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p63#2/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v6p63#2/r14.claim: Others refer the pronoun to the caught animal and say the name if it is found alive and slaughtered; a further, less likely view refers it to the act of eating, as Abū Ḥayyān prefers.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p63#2/r14.anchor: لما أمسكن أى سموا عليه إذا أدركتم ذكائه

ALUSI-FULL:v6p63#2/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p63#2/r15.speaker: أبو حنيفة، الشافعي
ALUSI-FULL:v6p63#2/r15.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa regards invoking God’s name as obligatory, while al-Shāfiʿī regards it as recommended; on the eating-time interpretation, it is recommended by agreement.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p63#2/r15.anchor: والأمر للوجوب عند أبى حنيفة رضى الله تعالى عنه وللندب عند الشافعى وهو على القول الأخير للندب بالاتفاق

ALUSI-FULL:v6p63#2/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p63#2/r16.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v6p63#2/r16.claim: The command to fear God concerns His prohibitions, including eating prey caught by untrained animals; “swift in reckoning” means that His accounting comes or is completed swiftly.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p63#2/r16.anchor: فى شأن محرماته ومنها أكل صيد الجوارح الغير المعلمة

ALUSI-FULL:v6p63#2/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p63#2/r17.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v6p63#2/r17.claim: Whether the reckoning begins quickly or is completed quickly, God takes account of every deed, small and great; the explicit divine name builds awe and explains the rule.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p63#2/r17.anchor: والمراد على التقديرين أنه جل شأنه يؤاخذكم على جميع الأفعال حقيرها وجليلها وإظهار الاسم الجليل

ALUSI-FULL:v6p63#2/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p63#2/r18.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v6p63#2/r18.claim: The warning after hunting encourages vigilance because hunting often distracts people from prayer and purity; hunters who guard their religion are rarer than a white crow and are rewarded.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p63#2/r18.anchor: ذكر هذا إثر بيان حكم الصيد لحث متعاطيه على التقوى لما أنه مظنة التهاون والغفلة

ALUSI-FULL:v6p63#2/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p63#2/r19.speaker: صفوان بن أمية
ALUSI-FULL:v6p63#2/r19.claim: In a report from Ṣafwān ibn Umayya, ʿUrfuṭa ibn Nāhik asks whether hunting is lawful for a family dependent on it despite its distraction from remembrance and congregational prayer; the Prophet permits it, calls lawful provision a form of striving, and urges love of the congregation and remembrance.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p63#2/r19.anchor: الطبرانى عن صفوان بن أمية أن عرفطة بن نهيك التميمى

ALUSI-FULL:v6p63#2/r20.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p63#2/r20.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v6p63#2/r20.claim: The verse supports teaching animals and striking them when useful, as well as keeping dogs for hunting; guard dogs are included by analogy.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p63#2/r20.anchor: واستدل بالآية على جواز تعليم الحيوان وضربه للمصلحة لأن التعليم قد يحتاج لذلك وعلى إباحة اتخاذ الكلب للصيد

ALUSI-FULL:v6p63#2/r21.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p63#2/r21.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v6p63#2/r21.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says game caught by a Magian’s trained dog, hawk, falcon, or eagle is not lawful even with invocation, because the animal was trained by a Magian rather than through God’s teaching.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p63#2/r21.anchor: إلى هذا ذهب ابن عباس رضى الله تعالى عنهما فقد روى عنه فى المسلم يأخذ كلب المجوسى

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p5#3/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p5#3/r2.speaker: أبو ميسرة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p5#3/r2.claim: Abū Maysara says this sura contains eighteen rulings not revealed together elsewhere, including forbidden carrion, trained hunting animals, food and marriage with People of the Book, purification, theft, hunting in consecration, and testimony at death.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p5#3/r2.anchor: روي عن أبي ميسرة قال: أنزل الله تعالى في هذه السورة ثمانية عشر حكما لم ينزلها في غيرها،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p15/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p15/r1.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p15/r1.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr says the verse was revealed about ʿAdī ibn Ḥātim and Zayd al-Muhalhil al-Ṭāʾī, known as Zayd al-Khayl and renamed Zayd al-Khayr, who asked about hunting with dogs and falcons.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p15/r1.anchor: قال سعيد بن جبير: نزلت هذه الآية في عدي بن حاتم وزيد بن المهلهل الطائيين وهو زيد الخيل

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p15/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p15/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p15/r2.claim: Another account says the verse answered people who asked what could be used from the dogs the Prophet had ordered killed; he then allowed keeping useful dogs and forbade keeping useless ones.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p15/r2.anchor: وقيل: سبب نزولها أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لما أمر بقتل الكلاب قالوا: يا رسول الله ماذا يحل لنا من هذه الأمة التي أمرت بقتلها؟

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p15/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p15/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p15/r3.claim: Abū Hurayra reports that keeping a dog except for livestock, hunting, or crops diminishes one's reward by a qīrāṭ each day.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p15/r3.anchor: عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "من اتخذ كلبا إلا كلب ماشية أو صيد أو زرع انتقص من أجره كل يوم قيراط"

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p15/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p15/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p15/r4.claim: The first account is the sounder explanation for the verse's occasion of revelation.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p15/r4.anchor: والأول أصح في سبب نزول هذه الآية

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p15#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p15#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p15#2/r1.claim: One view defines the lawful good things as slaughtered animals over which God's name was pronounced; another includes anything Arabs find pleasant unless Qurʾān or Sunna forbids it.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p15#2/r1.anchor: يعني: الذبائح على اسم الله تعالى، وقيل: كل ما تستطيبه العرب وتستلذه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p15#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p15#2/r2.speaker: الضحاك والسدي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p15#2/r2.claim: They restrict hunting beasts to dogs and require ritual slaughter for prey caught by other animals; the author says this view is not followed.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p15#2/r2.anchor: فقال الضحاك والسدي: هي الكلاب دون غيرها، ولا يحل ما صاده غير الكلب إلا أن يدرك ذكاته،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p15#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p15#2/r3.speaker: جمهور أهل العلم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p15#2/r3.claim: The majority take jawāriḥ as trainable hunting predators, including beasts such as cheetahs, leopards, and dogs and birds such as hawks, eagles, and falcons; prey from all is lawful.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p15#2/r3.anchor: بل عامة أهل العلم على أن المراد من الجوارح والكواسب من سباع البهائم كالفهد والنمر والكلب

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p15#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p15#2/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p15#2/r4.claim: Jawāriḥ are so called because they earn their owners' sustenance from hunting; the root can mean to earn, as in calling a family's breadwinner its jāriḥa.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p15#2/r4.anchor: سميت جارحة: لجرحها لأربابها أقواتهم من الصيد، أي: كسبها،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p15#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p15#2/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p15#2/r5.claim: Mukallib is one who incites dogs to hunt or trains them; kilāb can mean dog-owner or a hunter using dogs.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p15#2/r5.anchor: ، {مكلبين} والمكلب الذي يغري الكلاب على الصيد، ويقال للذي يعلمها أيضا: مكلب،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p15#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p15#2/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p15#2/r6.claim: Mukallibīn is accusative as a circumstantial phrase, describing the handlers as they set the beasts onto prey; dogs are named because they are most common, though all hunting animals are meant.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p15#2/r6.anchor: ، ونصب مكلبين على الحال، أي: في حال تكليبكم هذه الجوارح أي إغرائكم إياها على الصيد،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p15#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p15#2/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p15#2/r7.claim: Training means teaching the beasts the etiquette of taking prey.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p15#2/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p15#2/r8.speaker: السدي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p15#2/r8.claim: Al-Suddī interprets the phrase as meaning as God taught you, with min functioning like the particle kāf.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p15#2/r8.anchor: ، وقال السدي: أي كما علمكم الله، "من" بمعنى الكاف،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p15#2/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p15#2/r9.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p15#2/r9.claim: A trained animal's catch is lawful if it goes out when released by its owner and catches and kills the prey.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p15#2/r9.anchor: أراد أن الجارحة المعلمة إذا خرجت بإرسال صاحبها فأخذت الصيد وقتلته كان حلالا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p15#2/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p15#2/r10.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p15#2/r10.claim: A beast counts as trained when it responds to release and restraint and holds rather than eats prey; after this is observed repeatedly, at least three times, its catch is lawful when sent by its owner.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p15#2/r10.anchor: وإذا وجد ذلك منه مرارا وأقله ثلاث مرات كانت معلمة، يحل قتلها إذا خرجت بإرسال صاحبها.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p15#2/r11.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p15#2/r11.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p15#2/r11.claim: ʿAdī ibn Ḥātim reports: eat prey killed by a named, trained dog; refuse prey it eats or that is caught with uninvoked dogs, and avoid game found in water, while a wound from one's arrow alone remains lawful even if found later.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p15#2/r11.anchor: عن عدي بن حاتم عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p17/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p17/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p17/r1.claim: Pronouncing God's name is required over slaughter at the time of slaughter and in hunting when releasing the animal or shooting the arrow.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p17/r1.anchor: ففيه بيان أن ذكر اسم الله عز وجل على الذبيحة شرط حالة ما يذبح، وفي الصيد حالة ما يرسل الجارحة أو السهم.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p17/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p17/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p17/r2.claim: Anas reports that the Prophet sacrificed two speckled, horned rams with his own hand, saying God's name and the takbīr while placing his foot on their sides.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p17/r2.anchor: عن قتادة عن أنس قال: "ضحى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بكبشين أملحين أقرنين ذبحهما بيده

BAYDAWI-FULL:5:3-5/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:3-5/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:3-5/r2.claim: Because the question contains the sense of saying, mādhā takes a full clause as its complement; the word mādhā has been discussed earlier.
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:3-5/r2.anchor: لما تضمن السؤال معنى القول أوقع على الجملة، وقد سبق الكلام في

BAYDAWI-FULL:5:3-5/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:3-5/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:3-5/r3.claim: The wording says alayhim rather than ʿalaynā to preserve the indirect third-person form of yasʾalūnaka, though either wording is idiomatic.
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:3-5/r3.anchor: وإنما قال لهم ولم يقل لنا على الحكاية، لأن

BAYDAWI-FULL:5:3-5/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:3-5/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:3-5/r4.claim: They ask about permitted foods because, after hearing what was forbidden, they wanted to know what was allowed.
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:3-5/r4.anchor: والمسؤول ما أحل لهم من المطاعم كأنهم لما تلي عليهم ما حرم عليهم سألوا عما أحل لهم

BAYDAWI-FULL:5:3-5/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:3-5/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:3-5/r5.claim: The wholesome are things that sound natures do not find repugnant.
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:3-5/r5.anchor: ما لم تستخبثه الطباع السليمة ولم تنفر عنه

BAYDAWI-FULL:5:3-5/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:3-5/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:3-5/r6.claim: One implication is that whatever Arabs consider repulsive is prohibited.

BAYDAWI-FULL:5:3-5/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:3-5/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:3-5/r7.claim: Alternatively, wholesome means foods for which neither a text nor an analogy establishes prohibition.
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:3-5/r7.anchor: أو ما لم يدل نص ولا قياس على حرمته

BAYDAWI-FULL:5:3-5/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:3-5/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:3-5/r8.claim: The phrase about what you have trained can be a relative clause coordinated with wholesome foods, implying game caught by what you trained, or a conditional clause whose answer is eat.
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:3-5/r8.anchor: عطف على { الطيبات } إن جعلت { ما } موصولة على تقدير

BAYDAWI-FULL:5:3-5/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:3-5/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:3-5/r9.claim: Jawāriḥ are animals that catch prey for their owners, including predatory quadrupeds and birds.
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:3-5/r9.anchor: كواسب الصيد على أهلها من سباع ذوات الأربع والطير

BAYDAWI-FULL:5:3-5/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:3-5/r10.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:3-5/r10.claim: Mukallibīn means trainers who discipline hunting animals; the term derives from dogs because they are commonly trained this way or because every predator is called a dog, and it is circumstantial to stress training.
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:3-5/r10.anchor: مكلبين } معلمين إياه الصيد، والمكلب مؤدب الجوارح

BAYDAWI-FULL:5:3-5/r11.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:3-5/r11.speaker: رسول الله
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:3-5/r11.claim: The Prophet's supplication that God set one of His dogs on a man supports calling every predator a dog.
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:3-5/r11.anchor: " اللهم سلط عليه كلبا من كلابك "

BAYDAWI-FULL:5:3-5/r12.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:3-5/r12.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:3-5/r12.claim: What God taught includes hunting tricks and training methods, whether inspired by God, acquired through God-given reason, or taught as God's rules for how the animal follows, responds, returns, and holds prey for its owner.
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:3-5/r12.anchor: من الحيل وطرق التأديب، فإن العلم بها إلهام من الله تعالى

BAYDAWI-FULL:5:3-5/r13.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:3-5/r13.speaker: رسول الله
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:3-5/r13.claim: The Prophet told ʿAdi ibn Hatim not to eat prey if the hunting animal ate from it, because it caught that prey for itself.
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:3-5/r13.anchor:
لقوله عليه الصلاة والسلام لعدي بن حاتم
" وإن أكل منه فلا تأكل

BAYDAWI-FULL:5:3-5/r14.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:3-5/r14.speaker: أكثر الفقهاء
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:3-5/r14.claim: Most jurists hold that one may eat only what the trained animal did not eat.

BAYDAWI-FULL:5:3-5/r15.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:3-5/r15.speaker: بعض الفقهاء
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:3-5/r15.claim: Some jurists do not require this condition for predatory birds because they cannot realistically be trained to that degree.
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:3-5/r15.anchor: وقال بعضهم: لا يشترط ذلك في سباع الطير لأن

BAYDAWI-FULL:5:3-5/r16.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:3-5/r16.speaker: آخرون
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:3-5/r16.claim: Other jurists do not require the condition at all.

BAYDAWI-FULL:5:3-5/r17.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:3-5/r17.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:3-5/r17.claim: The pronoun in remembering God's name may refer to the trained animal, with invocation at release, or to the prey, with invocation when slaughtering it after capture.
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:3-5/r17.anchor: الضمير لما علمتم والمعنى: سموا عليه عند إرساله

BAYDAWI-FULL:5:3-5/r18.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:3-5/r18.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:3-5/r18.claim: God-consciousness here means observing God's prohibitions; He quickly reckons and holds people to account for both major and minor matters.
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:3-5/r18.anchor: واتقوا الله } في محرماته. { إن الله سريع الحساب } فيؤاخذكم

SULAMI:v1p171/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p171/r1.speaker: سهل
SULAMI:v1p171/r1.claim: Sahl defines good things as lawful provision.
SULAMI:v1p171/r1.anchor: قال سهل : الطيبات : الرزق من الحلال .

SULAMI:v1p171/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p171/r2.speaker: يوسف بن الحسين
SULAMI:v1p171/r2.claim: Yusuf ibn al-Husayn says good provision comes without strenuous effort or greedy expectation.
SULAMI:v1p171/r2.anchor: وقال يوسف بن الحسين : الطيب من الرزق ما يبدو لك من غير تكلف ولا إشراف نفس .

SULAMI:v1p171/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p171/r3.speaker: الروذباري
SULAMI:v1p171/r3.claim: Al-Rudhbari says the best provision for people of gnosis is divine aid.
SULAMI:v1p171/r3.anchor: وقال الروذباري : أطيب أرزاق العارفين المعونات .

BIQAI-FULL:v2p394/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p394/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p394/r1.claim: Because dogs had been ordered killed and game could die before ritual slaughter, people asked which dogs or dead game were permitted; the preceding context made this question natural.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p394/r1.anchor: وكان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قد أمر بقتل الكلاب

BIQAI-FULL:v2p394/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p394/r2.speaker: أبو رافع
BIQAI-FULL:v2p394/r2.claim: Al-Wahidi transmits from Abu Rafi that after the Prophet ordered dogs killed, people asked what was lawful from a species they had been ordered to kill, and this verse was revealed.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p394/r2.anchor: روى الواحدي في أسباب النزول بسنده عن أبي رافع رضي الله عنه

BIQAI-FULL:v2p394/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p394/r3.speaker: الواحدي
BIQAI-FULL:v2p394/r3.claim: Al-Wahidi says al-Hakim also narrated this report in his Sahih.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p394/r3.anchor: رواه الحاكم أبو عبد الله في صحيحه

BIQAI-FULL:v2p394/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p394/r4.speaker: أبو رافع
BIQAI-FULL:v2p394/r4.claim: In the fuller account, Gabriel would not enter a house containing an image or dog; Abu Rafi was ordered to kill the city's dogs, spared a guard dog out of pity, then killed it on the Prophet's order.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p394/r4.anchor: جاء جبريل إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فاستأذن عليه

BIQAI-FULL:v2p394/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p394/r5.speaker: أبو رافع
BIQAI-FULL:v2p394/r5.claim: After the verse, the Prophet permitted keeping dogs with a useful purpose, prohibited useless ones, ordered harmful black or biting dogs killed, and spared harmless dogs.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p394/r5.anchor: فلما نزلت أذن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في اقتناء الكلاب التي ينتفع بها

BIQAI-FULL:v2p394/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p394/r6.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
BIQAI-FULL:v2p394/r6.claim: Said b. Jubayr says the verse concerned Adi b. Hatim and Zayd b. al-Muhalhil, whom the Prophet renamed Zayd al-Khayr, after they asked about dogs and falcons catching game that sometimes died before slaughter.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p394/r6.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير : نزلت هذه الآية في عدي بن حاتم

BIQAI-FULL:v2p394/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p394/r7.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
BIQAI-FULL:v2p394/r7.claim: The two hunters asked because their dogs and falcons caught cattle, donkeys, gazelles, and monitor lizards; some prey could be slaughtered in time, while other prey died first, although carrion was forbidden.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p394/r7.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير : نزلت هذه الآية في عدي بن حاتم وزيد بن المهلهل

BIQAI-FULL:v2p394/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p394/r8.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
BIQAI-FULL:v2p394/r8.claim: Said b. Jubayr glosses the wholesome things as slaughtered animals and the hunting animals as catching dogs and predatory birds.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p394/r8.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير : نزلت هذه الآية في عدي بن حاتم وزيد بن المهلهل

BIQAI-FULL:v2p394/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p394/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p394/r9.claim: The wording answers about food generally, rather than asking what God made lawful for us, and covers keeping dogs, game, and other foods.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p394/r9.anchor: ولما كان هذا إخبارا عن غائب قال

BIQAI-FULL:v2p394/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p394/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p394/r10.claim: Wholesome foods are those sound natures regard as pure, with no prohibited impurity or disgust; this includes lawful slaughter, animals once forbidden as sa'iba, seafood, and other permitted non-food benefits.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p394/r10.anchor: فلا خبث فيها بنوع تحريم ولا تقذر

BIQAI-FULL:v2p394/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p394/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p394/r11.claim: Hunting animals are called jawāriḥ because they wound or cause slaughter, or because the root also means earning.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p394/r11.anchor: أي التي من شأنها أن تجرح

BIQAI-FULL:v2p396/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p396/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p396/r1.claim: The term jawāriḥ also means earners, as in 6:60; here it refers to hunting predators and birds, whose keeping and hunting are permitted when trained.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p396/r1.anchor: وهو كواسب الصيد من السباع والطير

BIQAI-FULL:v2p396/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p396/r2.speaker: الشافعي
BIQAI-FULL:v2p396/r2.claim: Al-Shafi'i says a dog is trained when it responds to a hunting signal, stops when restrained and does not eat the catch, answers when called, and does not flee when approached; this must happen repeatedly.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p396/r2.anchor: قال الشافعي : والكلب لا يصير معلما إلا عند أمور

BIQAI-FULL:v2p396/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p396/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p396/r3.claim: No fixed count is specified for these trained behaviors because, absent a revealed text or consensus, the judgment returns to customary usage.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p396/r3.anchor: ولم يذكر حدا لأن الاسم إذا لم يكن معلوما من نص ولا إجماع وجب الرجوع فيه إلى العرف

BIQAI-FULL:v2p396/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p396/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p396/r4.claim: The training clause is phrased around dogs although it covers all hunting animals because dogs require more training; it implies strenuous, careful instruction.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p396/r4.anchor: وبنى الحال من الكلاب وإن كان المراد العموم

BIQAI-FULL:v2p396/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p396/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p396/r5.claim: Commentators say the circumstantial clause means the trainer must be highly skilled and precise in the training.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p396/r5.anchor: وفائدة هذه الحال أن يكون المعلم نحريرا في علمه

BIQAI-FULL:v2p396/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p396/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p396/r6.claim: The further clause about teaching the animals can be another circumstantial phrase or a resumption, covering wild animals and birds and crediting God as the source of this knowledge.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p396/r6.anchor: وأكد ذلك بحال أخرى أو استئناف فقال

BIQAI-FULL:v2p396/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p396/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p396/r7.claim: The verse teaches every seeker to learn from the most knowledgeable and expert specialists, even if the journey is arduous.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p396/r7.anchor: فأفاد ذلك أن على كل طالب لشيء أن لا يأخذه إلا من أجل العلماء به وأشدهم دراية له

BIQAI-FULL:v2p396/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p396/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p396/r8.claim: Only game held for the hunter by trained instruction is lawful, including prey that dies before slaughter; prey held through the animal's own instinct and appetite is not lawful.

BIQAI-FULL:v2p396/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p396/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p396/r9.claim: God's name is spoken when releasing the hunting animal or when slaughtering prey reached alive, in contrast with pre-Islamic practice.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p396/r9.anchor: أي على ما أمسكن عند إرسال الجارح

BIQAI-FULL:v2p396/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p396/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p396/r10.claim: The phrase about naming God relates to the exception from the prohibition of carrion in 5:3 and explains the rule against hunting while in ihram.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p396/r10.anchor: وقد صارت نسبة هذه الجملة . كما ترى . إلى

BIQAI-FULL:v2p396#2/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p396#2/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p396#2/r1.claim: Training hunting animals is unusual despite its familiarity, and hunting with them is wondrous in its method; this leads to a warning about God's swift reckoning and exact knowledge of deserved reward and punishment.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p396#2/r1.anchor: ولما كان تعليم الجوارح أمرا خارجا عن العادة في نفسه

BIQAI-FULL:v2p396#2/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p396#2/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p396#2/r2.claim: Believers must account for themselves and fear God concerning whether prey was properly slaughtered and whether the animal held it for them or for itself.

BIQAI-FULL:v2p396#2/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p396#2/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p396#2/r3.claim: Only one overcome by awe of God attends to all the fine distinctions of hunting law, fearing Him in what is permitted and forbidden.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p396#2/r3.anchor: لا يقف عندها إلا من غلبت عليه مهابة اله واستشعره خوفه

BIQAI-FULL:v2p396#2/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p396#2/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p396#2/r4.claim: God is swift to reckon because He knows everything and can act at any time, able to recompense as He wills without one person or affair distracting Him from another.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p396#2/r4.anchor: أي عالم بكل شيء وقادر عليه في كل وقت

DURR-FULL:v3p21/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p21/r1.speaker: الفجيع العامري
DURR-FULL:v3p21/r1.claim: The Prophet permitted carrion to people in severe need, after learning that their ordinary food was only a morning and evening drink of milk; the source says hunger led to this allowance.
DURR-FULL:v3p21/r1.anchor: عن الفجيع العامري أنه قال يارسول الله مايحل لنا من الميتة فقال: ماطعامكم قلنا: نغتبق ونصطبح

DURR-FULL:v3p21/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p21/r2.speaker: عقبة
DURR-FULL:v3p21/r2.claim: ʿUqba clarifies that their food portions were a cup in the morning and a cup in the evening.
DURR-FULL:v3p21/r2.anchor: قال عقبة: قدح غدوة وقدح عشية

DURR-FULL:v3p21/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p21/r3.speaker: سمرة بن جندب
DURR-FULL:v3p21/r3.claim: Samura reports that once a household has enough milk for its evening drink, it must avoid forbidden carrion; al-Hakim grades the report sound.
DURR-FULL:v3p21/r3.anchor: عن سمرة بن جندب أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال إذا رويت أهلك من اللبن غبوقا فاجتنب مانهى الله عنه من ميتة

DURR-FULL:v3p21/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p21/r4.speaker: أبو رافع
DURR-FULL:v3p21/r4.claim: After Gabriel delayed because of a dog or image and a puppy was found, the Prophet ordered dogs killed; when people asked what they could eat, the verse was revealed, and he permitted game held by a named, dispatched dog if it had not eaten it.
DURR-FULL:v3p21/r4.anchor: عن أبي رافع قال: جاء جبريل إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فاستأذن عليه فأذن له فأبطأ فأخذ رداءه فخرج

DURR-FULL:v3p21/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p21/r5.speaker: عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v3p21/r5.claim: After Abu Rafiʿ's dog-killing mission reached al-ʿAwālī, several men asked what was lawful, and the verse was revealed.
DURR-FULL:v3p21/r5.anchor: عن عكرمة أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بعث أبا رافع في قتل الكلاب فقتل حتى بلغ العوالي

DURR-FULL:v3p21/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p21/r6.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
DURR-FULL:v3p21/r6.claim: Muhammad ibn Kaʿb says people asked what they could lawfully eat after the Prophet ordered dogs killed, and the verse was revealed.
DURR-FULL:v3p21/r6.anchor: عن محمد بن كعب القرظي قال لما أمر النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بقتل الكلاب قالوا: يارسول الله ماذا أحل لنا

DURR-FULL:v3p22/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p22/r1.speaker: الطائيين
DURR-FULL:v3p22/r1.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr says ʿAdi ibn Hatim and Zayd al-Muhalhil al-Ṭāʾī asked what was lawful after carrion had been forbidden, and the verse was revealed.
DURR-FULL:v3p22/r1.anchor: الطائيين سألا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقالا: يارسول الله قد حرم اللخ الميتة

DURR-FULL:v3p22/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p22/r2.speaker: عامر
DURR-FULL:v3p22/r2.claim: ʿĀmir says ʿAdi asked the Prophet about game caught by dogs, and the hunting-animal verse was revealed after the Prophet did not know what to answer.
DURR-FULL:v3p22/r2.anchor: عن عامر أن عدي بن حاتم الطائي أتى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فسأله عن صيد الكلاب فلم يدر مايقول له

DURR-FULL:v3p22/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p22/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v3p22/r3.claim: The Prophet said good foods are lawful and foul foods forbidden; a person in need may eat forbidden food until able to stop, with need measured by sustaining a household until expected offspring or gain arrives.
DURR-FULL:v3p22/r3.anchor: فقال له النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: يحل لك الطيبات ويحرم عليك الخبائث إلا ان تفتقرالى طعام لك

DURR-FULL:v3p22/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p22/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v3p22/r4.claim: The Prophet tells the Bedouin that after his family has had its evening milk, he should avoid prohibited food, and that his property is all accessible and contains nothing forbidden.
DURR-FULL:v3p22/r4.anchor: فقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: إذا أرويت أهلك غبوقا من الليل فاجتنب ماحرم الله عليك من طعام

DURR-FULL:v3p22/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p22/r5.speaker: عرفطة بن نهيك التميمي
DURR-FULL:v3p22/r5.claim: The Prophet allowed ʿArfaṭa and his family to hunt for their livelihood, noting that earlier messengers hunted; love of the congregation can accompany absence for work, and earning lawful provision for one's dependents is jihad.
DURR-FULL:v3p22/r5.anchor: عن صفوان بن أمية أن عرفطة بن نهيك التميمي قال: يارسول الله إني وأهل بيتي يرزقون من هذا الصيد

DURR-FULL:v3p22/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p22/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v3p22/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the trained hunting animals as dogs and hawks, with the continuation adding panthers, falcons, and comparable animals.
DURR-FULL:v3p22/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {وما علمتم من الجوارح مكلبين} قال: هي الكلاب المعلمة والبازي يعلم الصيد

DURR-FULL:v3p22/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p22/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v3p22/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas says game caught by a trained animal may be eaten if killed for the hunter, but not if the animal eats the prey itself; God's name is said when releasing it, and forgetting to do so carries no blame.
DURR-FULL:v3p22/r7.anchor: {فكلوا مما أمسكن عليكم} يقول: كلوا مما قتلن فإن قتل وأكل فلا تأكل

DURR-FULL:v3p23/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p23/r1.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v3p23/r1.claim: Mujahid identifies the hunting animals as birds and dogs.
DURR-FULL:v3p23/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله {من الجوارح مكلبين} قال: الطير والكلاب

DURR-FULL:v3p23/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p23/r2.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v3p23/r2.claim: Qatada says trained animals hunt prey; game held or killed by a dispatched dog, bird, or arrow is edible when God's name was invoked.
DURR-FULL:v3p23/r2.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله {من الجوارح مكلبين} قال: يكالبن الصيد {فكلوا مما أمسكن عليكم} قال: إذا أرسلت كلبك

DURR-FULL:v3p23/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p23/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v3p23/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says a Muslim may not eat game caught by a trained Magian's dog, hawk, or falcon even after invoking God, because the Magian trained it.
DURR-FULL:v3p23/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس: في المسلم يأخذ كلب المجوسي المعلم أو بازه أو صقره مما علمه المجوسي فيرسله فيأخذه

DURR-FULL:v3p23/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p23/r4.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v3p23/r4.claim: Al-Hasan interprets trained hunting animals broadly and says teaching them means teaching them to pursue, as God taught people.
DURR-FULL:v3p23/r4.anchor: عن الحسن في قوله {وما علمتم من الجوارح} قال: كل ما {تعلمونهن مما علمكم الله} قال: تعلمونهن من الطلب

DURR-FULL:v3p23/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p23/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v3p23/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas says a trained dog is one that holds its prey and does not eat it before its owner arrives.
DURR-FULL:v3p23/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: إنما المعلم من الكلاب أن يمسك صيده فلايأكل كل منه حتى يأتيه صاحبه

DURR-FULL:v3p23/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p23/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v3p23/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas says game is not edible if the dog eats it, since the dog caught it for itself.
DURR-FULL:v3p23/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: إذا أكل الكلب فلاتأكل فإنما أمسك على نفسه

DURR-FULL:v3p23/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p23/r7.speaker: عدي بن حاتم
DURR-FULL:v3p23/r7.claim: The Prophet permits eating game that a hawk catches for the hunter.
DURR-FULL:v3p23/r7.anchor: عن عدي بن حاتم قال: سألت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن صيد البازي قال: ماأمسك عليك فكل

DURR-FULL:v3p23/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p23/r8.speaker: عدي بن حاتم
DURR-FULL:v3p23/r8.claim: The Prophet permits game held or killed by the hunter's named, trained dog, unless another dog joined it, because God's name was invoked only over the hunter's own dog.
DURR-FULL:v3p23/r8.anchor: عن عدي بن حاتم قال قلت: يارسول الله إني أرسل الكلاب المعلمة واذكر اسم الله فقال: إذا أرسلت كلبك المعلم

DURR-FULL:v3p23/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p23/r9.speaker: عدي بن حاتم
DURR-FULL:v3p23/r9.claim: The Prophet says one may eat game held by a named dog if it does not eat the prey; game pierced by an arrow is also lawful when God's name was invoked.
DURR-FULL:v3p23/r9.anchor: عن عدي بن حاتم قال: قلت يارسول الله إنا قوم نصيد بالكلاب والبزاة فما يحل لنا منها

AKHFASH:v1p275/r5.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p275/r5.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p275/r5.claim: In ماذا أحل, ذا may be treated as a relative pronoun meaning الذي.
AKHFASH:v1p275/r5.anchor: وقال {ماذا أحل} فان شئت جعلت "ذا" بمنزلة "الذي"

AKHFASH:v1p275/r6.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p275/r6.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p275/r6.claim: Alternatively, ذا in ماذا may be extra, as the cited verse's ماذا cannot mean ما الذي without making the sentence ungrammatical.
AKHFASH:v1p275/r6.anchor: وان شئت جعلتها زائدة كما قال الشاعر

AKHFASH:v1p275/r7.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p275/r7.speaker: الشاعر
AKHFASH:v1p275/r7.claim: An unidentified poet's ماذا بال نسوتكم is cited to show ذا must be extra there: substituting ما الذي would not make sense.
AKHFASH:v1p275/r7.anchor: يا خزر تغلب ماذا بال نسوتكم * لا يستفقن الى الديرين تحنانا

AKHFASH:v1p275/r8.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p275/r8.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p275/r8.claim: الجوارح means earners or catchers; Arab usage calls a person's dependents or property جارحة, meaning servants or owned workers.
AKHFASH:v1p275/r8.anchor: [و] قال {الجوارح} وهي الكواسب كما تقول: "فلان جارحة أهله" و"مالهم جارحة" أي: مالهم مماليك "ولا حافرة".

AKHFASH:v1p275/r9.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p275/r9.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p275/r9.claim: He notes the preposition من in مما أمسكن and parallels its use in ordinary expressions such as كان من حديث and قد كان من مطر.

AKHFASH:v1p275/r10.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p275/r10.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p275/r10.claim: In وينزل من السماء من جبال فيها من برد, the phrase is interpreted as God sending down mountains of hail from the sky.
AKHFASH:v1p275/r10.anchor: وهو فيما فسر "ينزل من السماء جبالا فيها برد"

AKHFASH:v1p275/r11.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p275/r11.speaker: بعضهم
AKHFASH:v1p275/r11.claim: Some take the mountains of hail to be in the sky: God makes mountains of hail there and sends the hail down from them.
AKHFASH:v1p275/r11.anchor: وقال بعضهم {وينزل من السمآء من جبال فيها من برد}

IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p72/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p72/r5.speaker: القرطبي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p72/r5.claim: Al-Qurtubi counts nineteen obligations unique to this surah, including rules on forbidden foods, trained hunting animals, scripture food and spouses, purification, theft, hunting while consecrated, pre-Islamic livestock customs, and testimony at death.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p72/r5.anchor: وذكر القرطبي أن فيها تسع عشرة فريضة ليست في غيرها ، وهي سبع في قوله : { والمنخنقة ، والموقوذة ، والمتردية ، والنطيحة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p110/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p110/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p110/r1.claim: If people had asked about lawful foods after hearing the prohibitions, يسألونك is present tense for a repeated or expected question; the clause may be explanatory after 5:3 or a new transition from forbidden foods to inherent permissions.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p110/r1.anchor: إن كان الناس قد سألوا عما أحل لهم من المطعومات بعد أن سمعوا ما حرم عليهم في الآية السابقة ، أو قبل أن يسمعوا ذلك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p110/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p110/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p110/r2.claim: If no question had yet occurred, the present tense anticipates one because people want a comprehensive account of permitted food and possible further prohibitions; Qur'anic يسألونك can carry either sense.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p110/r2.anchor: وعليه فوجه فصل جملة { يسألونك } أنها استئناف بياني ناشىء عن جملة { حرمت عليكم الميتة }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p110/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p110/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p110/r3.claim: With an actual earlier question, the answer can follow the prohibitions with the lawful foods, or state only the lawful foods if the prohibitions had already been explained; anticipated questioning makes the verse foreground the halal comprehensively.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p110/r3.anchor: فعلى الوجه الأول يكون الجواب قد حصل ببيان المحرمات أولا ثم ببيان الحلال ، أو ببيان الحلال فقط

IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p110/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p110/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p110/r4.claim: الطيبات abbreviates good foods; طيب conveys purity, growth, and a pleasing outcome now and later. A harmful pleasure is not truly good, so the best kind is beneficial as well as pleasant.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p110/r4.anchor: و { الطيبات } صفة لمحذوف معلوم من السياق ، أي الأطعمة الطيبة ، وهي الموصوفة بالطيب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p110/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p110/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p110/r5.claim: Ṭayyib can also denote what the law permits, since permission signals goodness and safety from harm; here the linguistic sense is intended so that أحل can be predicated of it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p110/r5.anchor: والمراد بالطيبات في قوله : { أحل لكم الطيبات } معناها اللغوي ليصح إسناد فعل { أحل } إليها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p111/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p111/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p111/r1.claim: Calling foods طيبات and then declaring them lawful makes goodness the reason for permission and implies that the forbidden opposite consists of خبائث.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p111/r1.anchor: والطيبات } وصف للأطعمة قرن به حكم التحليل ، فدل على أن الطيب علة التحليل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p111/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p111/r2.speaker: مالك
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p111/r2.claim: Mālik identifies الطيبات as lawful foods; Ibn ʿĀshūr explains that permission is a practical sign of goodness, not a definition of it, because goodness can be hard to delimit.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p111/r2.anchor: فعن مالك : الطيبات الحلال ، ويتعين أن يكون مراده أن الحل هو المؤذن بتحقق وصف الطيب في الطعام المباح

IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p111/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p111/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p111/r3.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr reads the verse as gratitude and correction of pagan food taboos: whatever God permits is good, overturning their bans without cause and permission for vile foods.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p111/r3.anchor: بل أريد به الامتنان والإعلام بأن ما أحله الله لهم فهو طيب ، إبطالا لما اعتقدوه في زمن الشرك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p111/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p111/r4.speaker: الشافعي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p111/r4.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī defines good foods as lawful and palatable; things people find repugnant, such as geckos, belong to the forbidden خبائث.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p111/r4.anchor: وعن الشافعي : الطيبات : الحلال المستلذ ، فكل مستقذر كالوزغ فهو من الخبائث حرام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p111/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p111/r5.speaker: فخر الدين
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p111/r5.claim: Fakhr al-Dīn says palatability is judged by people of honor and good character, since Bedouins find all animals palatable.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p111/r5.anchor: قال فخر الدين : العبرة في الاستلذاذ والاستطابة بأهل المروءة والأخلاق الجميلة ، فإن أهل البادية يستطيبون أكل جميع الحيوانات

IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p111/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p111/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p111/r6.claim: The creation of everything on earth for humanity implies broad permission to benefit from it, restricted by the prohibition of vile things; Ibn ʿĀshūr calls this a major principle for food rulings.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p111/r6.anchor: وتتأكد دلالة هذه الآيات بقوله تعالى : خلق لكم ما في الأرض جميعا } ( البقرة : 29 ) فهذا يقتضي التمكن من الانتفاع بكل ما في الأرض

IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p111/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p111/r7.speaker: الشافعي وأبو حنيفة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p111/r7.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī permits horse meat because it is self-evidently pleasant and therefore lawful under this verse; Abū Ḥanīfa does not permit it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p111/r7.anchor: منها أن لحم الخيل مباح عند الشافعي . وقال أبو حنيفة : ليس بمباح . حجة الشافعي أنه مستلذ مستطاب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p111/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p111/r8.speaker: محمد الكاكي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p111/r8.claim: In the Hanafi Sharḥ al-Hidāya, Muḥammad al-Kākī reports the rule that what Arabs find pleasant is lawful and what they find repugnant is forbidden.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p111/r8.anchor: وفي ( شرح الهداية ) في الفقه الحنفي لمحمد الكاكي ( أن ما استطابه العرب حلال ، لقوله تعالى : { ويحل لهم الطيبات }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p111/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p111/r9.speaker: محمد الكاكي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p111/r9.claim: The stated taste standard uses urban Hijazis because revelation addressed them, excludes Bedouins whose diet reflects necessity, and compares unfamiliar Muslim-city foods with the nearest Hijazi equivalent.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p111/r9.anchor: والذين تعتبر استطابتهم أهل الحجاز من أهل الأمصار ، لأن القرآن أنزل عليهم وخوطبوا به

IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p111/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p111/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p111/r10.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr objects that making some Muslims' customs control a universal law is unsuitable; Hijazis disliked monitor lizard, yet the Prophet did not forbid it to Khālid.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p111/r10.anchor: وفيه من التحكم في تحكيم عوائد بعض الأمة دون بعض ما لا يناسب التشريع العام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p111/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p111/r11.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p111/r11.claim: In a report from Khālid ibn al-Walīd, the Prophet said the monitor lizard was not from his people's land and that he disliked it, but did not prohibit it for Khālid.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p111/r11.anchor: بشهادة قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم في حديث خالد بن الوليد : ( ليس هو من أرض قومي فأجدني أعافه ) ومع ذلك لم يحرمه على خالد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p113/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p113/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p113/r1.claim: وما علمتم may coordinate with الطيبات as an implied noun, prey of trained animals, with فكلوا as the result; alternatively it begins a sentence with conditional ما and فكلوا as its answer.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p113/r1.anchor: يجوز أن يكون عطفا على { الطيبات } عطف المفرد ، على نية مضاف محذوف ، والتقدير : وصيد ما علمتم من الجوارح

IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p113/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p113/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p113/r2.claim: Trained game is singled out because its goodness may be unclear when a predator's wound raises doubt about ritual slaughter; the verse addresses this case, while weapons hunting comes at 5:94.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p113/r2.anchor: وخص بالبيان من بين الطيبات لأن طيبه قد يخفى من جهة خفاء معنى الذكاة في جرح الصيد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p113/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p113/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p113/r3.claim: The phrase means prey caught for the hunter by animals he has trained, as the following command confirms; it does not permit eating the trained dogs or birds themselves.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p113/r3.anchor: والمعنى : وما أمسك عليكم ما علمتم بقرينة قوله بعد { فكلوا مما أمسكن عليكم }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p113/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p113/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p113/r4.claim: Jawāriḥ is plural of jāriḥ or jāriḥa; animals are treated as a feminine collective, as Arabs call predators الكواسب, a usage illustrated by Labīd's verse.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p113/r4.anchor: والجوارح : جمع الجارح ، أو الجارحة ، جرى على صيغة جمع فاعلة ، لأن الدواب مراعى فيها تأنيث جمعها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p113/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p113/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p113/r5.claim: Labīd's line غبس كواسب ما يمن طعامها supplies poetic evidence for the feminine collective form used for predators.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p113/r5.anchor: كما قالت العرب للسباع : الكواسب ، قال لبيد : غبس كواسب ما يمن طعامها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p114/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p114/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p114/r1.claim: مكلبين is a circumstantial qualifier of علمتم, describing dog training; mukallib is an active participle from the noun dog, following the common method of hunting.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p114/r1.anchor: { ومكلبين } حال من ضمير { علمتم } مبينة لنوع التعليم وهو تعليم المكلب ، والمكلب بكسر اللام بصيغة اسم الفاعل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p114/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p114/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p114/r2.claim: Because dog training was the common case, مكلبين does not restrict the general permission to dogs; the wording also includes trained cheetahs and falcons.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p114/r2.anchor: ولذلك فوقوعه حالا من ضمير { علمتم } ليس مخصصا للعموم الذي أفاده قوله : { وما علمتم } فهذا العموم يشمل غير الكلاب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p114/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p114/r3.speaker: ابن عمر
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p114/r3.claim: Ibn ʿUmar, as quoted by Ibn al-Mundhir, restricts edible prey killed by a trained hunter to dogs; birds of prey must be recovered alive and slaughtered. Al-Ḍaḥḥāk and al-Suddī also held this.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p114/r3.anchor: وخالف في ذلك ابن عمر ، حكى عنه ابن المنذر أنه قصر إباحة أكل ما قتله الجارح على صيد الكلاب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p114/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p114/r4.speaker: الحسن وقتادة والنخعي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p114/r4.claim: Al-Ḥasan, Qatāda, and al-Nakhaʿī disliked prey from a wholly black dog, citing the Prophetic statement that a black dog is a devil; Ibn ʿĀshūr calls this proof weak.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p114/r4.anchor: إلا ما شذ من قول الحسن وقتادة والنخعي بكراهة صيد الكلب الأسود البهيم ، أي عام السواد ، محتجين بقول النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ( الكلب الأسود شيطان ) أخرجه مسلم ، وهو احتجاج ضعيف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p114/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p114/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p114/r5.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr says the devil description means the dog is prone to biting and bad temperament; the report concerns a dog crossing before a worshipper and can be interpreted figuratively.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p114/r5.anchor: وهل يشك أحد أن معنى كونه شيطانا أنه مظنة للعقر وسوء الطبع . على أن مورد الحديث في أنه يقطع الصلاة إذا مر بين يدي المصلي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p114/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p114/r6.speaker: أحمد بن حنبل وإسحاق بن راهويه
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p114/r6.claim: Aḥmad says he knows no one who permits eating prey from a wholly black dog, and Isḥāq agrees; Ibn ʿĀshūr challenges this position against the majority of jurists.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p114/r6.anchor: وعن أحمد بن حنبل : ما أعرف أحدا يرخص فيه ( أي في أكل صيده ) إذا كان بهيما ، وبه قال إسحاق بن راهويه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p115/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p115/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p115/r1.claim: The second circumstantial clause teaches that humans are endowed to teach, from Adam's naming, and some animals can learn; it both confirms the training and expresses divine grace.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p115/r1.anchor: وقوله : { تعلمونهن مما علمكم الله } حال ثانية ، قصد بها الامتنان والعبرة والمواهب التي أودعها الله في الإنسان

IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p115/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p115/r2.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p115/r2.claim: Al-Kashshāf advises learners to take knowledge from the most expert and discerning teachers, traveling far if needed; an inept teacher wastes the student's time and invites later regret.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p115/r2.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) ( وفي تكرير الحال فائدة أن على كل آخذ علما

IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p115/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p115/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p115/r3.claim: The ف in فكلوا is explanatory-result when ما is relative, and links a conditional answer when ما is conditional.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p115/r3.anchor: والفاء في قوله : ( فكلوا مما أمسكن عليكم ) فاء الفصيحة في قوله : { وما علمتم من الجوارح } إن جعلت ( ما ) من قوله { وما علمتم } موصولة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p115/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p115/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p115/r4.claim: من in مما أمسكن is a common partitive used with things consumed, as in eating fruit; it neither forbids the whole catch nor guards against imagined objections about bones, feathers, skin, or horns.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p115/r4.anchor: وحرف ( من ) في قوله { مما أمسكن عليكم } للتبعيض ، وهذا تبعيض شائع الاستعمال في كلام العرب عند ذكر المتناولات

IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p115/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p115/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p115/r5.claim: على means for the hunter's benefit, like imprisonment for assault or striking a child for lying; ʿAlqama's poem says the fighters act to defend truth, supporting this causal sense.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p115/r5.anchor: وحرف ( على ) في قوله { مما أمسكن عليكم } بمعنى لام التعليل ، كما تقول : سجن على الاعتداء ، وضرب الصبي على الكذب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p115/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p115/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p115/r6.claim: The author reinforces this causal reading with ʿAlqama ibn Shaybān's verse, then compares the phrase with God's instruction to retain one's wife and a Prophetic saying about retaining some wealth.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p115/r6.anchor: وقول علقمة بن شيبان : ونطاعن الأعداء عن أبنائنا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p115/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p115/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p115/r7.claim: The verse permits prey caught by trained dogs, cheetahs, and birds of prey such as falcons and hawks after the hunter releases them; scholars agree on this baseline and differ over its conditions.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p115/r7.anchor: ومعنى الآية إباحة أكل ما صاده الجوارح : من كلاب ، وفهود ، وسباع طير : كالبزاة ، والصقور ، إذا كانت معلمة وأمسكت بعد إرسال الصائد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p116/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p116/r1.speaker: العلماء
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p116/r1.claim: Jurists recognize training when a land animal pursues after release, comes when called, stops when rebuked, and returns with prey; birds require only obedience to a command.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p116/r1.anchor: فأما شرط التعليم فاتفقوا على أنه إذا أشلي ، فانشلى ، فاشتد وراء الصيد ، وإذا دعي فأقبل ، وإذا زجر فانزجر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p116/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p116/r2.speaker: مالك وأبو حنيفة والشافعي وأحمد وأبو يوسف ومحمد
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p116/r2.claim: Mālik, Abū Ḥanīfa, and al-Shāfiʿī judge training by hunters' custom without a fixed repetition count; Aḥmad, Abū Yūsuf, and Muḥammad require two or three repetitions.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p116/r2.anchor: وصفات التعليم راجعة إلى عرف أهل الصيد ، وأنه صار له معرفة ، وبذلك قال مالك ، وأبو حنيفة ، والشافعي : ولا حاجة إلى ضبط ذلك بمرتين أو ثلاث ، خلافا لأحمد ، وأبي يوسف ، ومحمد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p116/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p116/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p116/r3.claim: A hunter's release is shown when the animal captures after being sent by hand or by a command it understands, such as this is yours; release stands in for intention to slaughter, and it remains sent until returning with prey.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p116/r3.anchor: وأما شرط الإمساك لأجل الصائد : فهو يعرف بإمساكها الصيد بعد إشلاء الصائد إياها ، وهو الإرسال من يده

IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p116/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p116/r4.speaker: جماعة من الصحابة والتابعين
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p116/r4.claim: A group of Companions and Successors says that if the hunting animal eats, the remainder cannot be eaten because it caught for itself; al-Shāfiʿī, Aḥmad, Abū Thawr, and Isḥāq follow this view.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p116/r4.anchor: فقال جماعة من الصحابة والتابعين : إذا أكل الجارح من الصيد لم تؤكل البقية ؛ لأنه إنما أمسك على نفسه ، لا على ربه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p116/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p116/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p116/r5.claim: In the sound report of ʿAdī ibn Ḥātim, the Prophet says not to eat when the dog eats, because it caught the prey for itself.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p116/r5.anchor: وفي هذا المعنى حديث عدي بن حاتم في الصحيح : أنه سأل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن الكلب ، فقال : ( وإذا أكل فلا تأكل فإنما أمسك على نفسه )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p116/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p116/r6.speaker: جماعة من الصحابة ومالك وأصحابه
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p116/r6.claim: Another group of Companions, followed by Mālik and his school, permits the uneaten remainder even if the hunting animal ate; they cite Abū Thaʿlaba al-Khushanī's report asking the Prophet about this case.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p116/r6.anchor: وقال جماعة من الصحابة : إذا أكل الجارح لم يضر أكله ، ويؤكل ما بقي . وهو قول مالك وأصحابه : لحديث أبي ثعلبة الخشني

IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p116/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p116/r7.speaker: أبو ثعلبة الخشني
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p116/r7.claim: Abū Thaʿlaba al-Khushanī asks the Prophet whether the catch remains lawful if the animal ate from it; the source locates this report in Abū Dāwūd's collection.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p116/r7.anchor: لحديث أبي ثعلبة الخشني ، في ( كتاب أبي داوود ) : أنه سأل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال : ( وإن أكل منه )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p116/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p116/r8.speaker: بعض أصحابنا
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p116/r8.claim: Some of Ibn ʿĀshūr's colleagues use the partitive من in the verse to argue that what remains may be eaten; he rejects this, since من commonly precedes objects without implying partial consumption.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p116/r8.anchor: ورام بعض أصحابنا أن يحتج لهذا بقوله تعالى : { مما أمسكن عليكم } حيث جاء بمن المفيدة للتبعيض

IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p116/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p116/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p116/r9.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr holds that a released animal which returns with prey caught it for its owner even if it ate some, perhaps from hunger or forgetfulness.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p116/r9.anchor: والكلب أو الجارح ، إذا أشلاه القناص فانشلى ، وجاء بالصيد إلى ربه . فهو قد أمسكه عليه وإن كان قد أكل منه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p116/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p116/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p116/r10.claim: Eating from prey does not invalidate an animal's training when its overall behavior follows hunting practice; the lapse is an aberration or impetuousness.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p116/r10.anchor: والصواب أن ذلك لا يقدح في تعليمه ، إذا كانت أفعاله جارية على وفق أفعال الصيد ، وإنما هذا من الفلتة أو من التهور

IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p116/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p116/r11.speaker: ابن عباس وحماد والنخعي وأبو حنيفة وأبو ثور
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p116/r11.claim: Some permit eating prey from a bird of prey that ate, reasoning that birds understand training less fully than dogs; the view is reported from Ibn ʿAbbās, Ḥammād, al-Nakhaʿī, Abū Ḥanīfa, and Abū Thawr.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p116/r11.anchor: ومال جماعة إلى الترخيص في ذلك في سباع الطير خاصة ، لأنها لا تفقه من التعليم ما يفقه الكلب ، وروي هذا عن ابن عباس ، وحماد ، والنخعي ، وأبي حنيفة ، وأبي ثور

IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p117/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p117/r1.speaker: مالك وبعض أصحابه
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p117/r1.claim: If a hunter did not see the animal catch prey and later finds it where the animal ranged, Mālik says not to eat it while some of his companions allow it; a fatal arrow wound makes the catch edible.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p117/r1.anchor: فعن مالك : لا يؤكل ، وعن بعض أصحابه : يؤكل . وأما إذا وجد الصائد سهمه في مقاتل الصيد فإنه يؤكل لا محالة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p117/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p117/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p117/r2.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr reads مما أمسكن عليكم as excluding game the person neither hunted nor saw caught, since it may have died by an irregular cause rather than valid slaughter.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p117/r2.anchor: وأحسب أن قوله تعالى : { مما أمسكن عليكم } احتراز عن أن يجد أحد صيدا لم يصده هو ، ولا رأى الجارح حين أمسكه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p117/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p117/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p117/r3.claim: The verse does not bar another person from eating prey caught by someone else's dog if the catch was witnessed and the hunter is absent, or if the prey is bought from or requested of its hunter.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p117/r3.anchor: وأنه لا يحرم على من لم يتصد للصيد أن يأكل صيدا رأى كلب غيره حين صاده إذا لم يجد الصائد قريبا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p117/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p117/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p117/r4.claim: Mention God's name at release because the animal may kill by its wound; if it brings prey alive, slaughter it and mention God then. The compact word عليه covers both cases.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p117/r4.anchor: وقوله : { واذكروا اسم الله عليه } أمر بذكر الله على الصيد ، ومعناه أن يذكره عند الإرسال لأنه قد يموت بجرح الجارح

IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p117/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p117/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p117/r5.claim: The rules for forgetting the invocation and deliberately omitting it are treated in legal manuals; Ibn ʿĀshūr closes the point by saying religion is easy.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p117/r5.anchor: وحكم نسيان التسمية وتعمد تركها معلوم من كتب الفقه والخلاف ، والدين يسر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p117/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p117/r6.speaker: الجمهور
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p117/r6.claim: The majority treat hunting as a form or quality of ritual slaughter, which Ibn ʿĀshūr prefers; on this basis, they allow game caught by a scripturalist but not by a Zoroastrian.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p117/r6.anchor: فالجمهور ألحقوه بالذكاة ، وهو الراجح ، ولذلك أجازوا أكل صيد الكتابي دون المجوسي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p117/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p117/r7.speaker: مالك
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p117/r7.claim: Mālik treats hunting as a concession for Muslims, so rejects game caught by either a scripturalist or a Zoroastrian; Ibn ʿĀshūr calls his proof from 5:94 weak because that verse concerns sanctuary restrictions, not hunting law.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p117/r7.anchor: وقال مالك : هو رخصة للمسلمين فلا يؤكل صيد الكتابي ولا المجوسي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p117/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p117/r8.speaker: أشهب وابن وهب
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p117/r8.claim: Ashhab and Ibn Wahb disagree with Mālik's position; jurists otherwise agree that Zoroastrian game is not eaten, except for a report from Abū Thawr that includes them among the People of the Book.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p117/r8.anchor: وخالفه أشهب ، وابن وهب ، من أصحابه . ولا خلاف في عدم أكل صيد المجوسي إلا رواية عن أبي ثور إذ ألحقهم بأهل الكتاب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p117/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p117/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p117/r9.claim: The disagreement over Zoroastrian game reflects differing principles about the legal status of hunting, not disagreement over a subsidiary application.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p117/r9.anchor: فهو اختلاف في الأصل لا في الفرع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p118/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p118/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p118/r1.claim: The command to fear God is a general conclusion that closes the hunting ruling and suits its subject broadly.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p118/r1.anchor: { واتقوا الله } الآية تذييل عام ختمت به آية الصيد

FARRA:v1p301/r5.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p301/r5.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p301/r5.claim: الجوارح means dogs; مكلبين is a circumstantial accusative describing the people who own or train dogs, and ما is nominative.
FARRA:v1p301/r5.anchor: يعنى الكلاب. ومكلبين نصب على الحال خارجة من (لكم) ، يعني بمكلبين

FARRA:v1p302/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p302/r1.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p302/r1.claim: تعلمونهن means training the dogs not to eat their prey.

FARRA:v1p302/r2.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p302/r2.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p302/r2.claim: Only prey held for the owner and not eaten is lawful; if the dog eats it, it held it for itself.
FARRA:v1p302/r2.anchor: فكلوا مما أمسكن عليكم مما لم يأكلن منه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p156/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p156/r1.speaker: أبو رافع
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p156/r1.claim: The occasion was Gabriel's refusal to enter a house with a dog, the Prophet's order to kill dogs as far as al-ʿAwālī, and the three Companions' question about which dogs could be used; ʿIkrima and Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb also report it as a Companion-level account.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p156/r1.anchor: وروى هذا السبب أبو رافع مولى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو كان المتولي لقتل الكلاب، وحكاه أيضا عكرمة ومحمد بن كعب القرظي موقوفا عليهما

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p156/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p156/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p156/r2.claim: The apparent question concerns permitted foods, not keeping dogs; the answer may address more than asked, as the Prophet often expanded instruction while clarifying the law.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p156/r2.anchor: وظاهر الآية أن سائلا سأل عما أحل للناس من المطاعم لأن قوله تعالى: قل أحل لكم الطيبات ليس الجواب على ما يحل لنا من اتخاذ الكلاب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p156/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p156/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p156/r3.claim: For Mālik and others, al-ṭayyibāt means lawful foods, whether or not they are pleasurable to eat.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p156/r3.anchor: والطيبات الحلال هذا هو المعنى عند مالك وغيره ولا يراغى مستلذا كان أم لا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p156/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p156/r4.speaker: الشافعي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p156/r4.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī takes al-ṭayyibāt to mean lawful and pleasurable foods, and treats repulsive animals such as geckos and beetles as forbidden filth.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p156/r4.anchor: وقال الشافعي: الطيبات الحلال المستلذ وكل مستقذر كالوزغ والخنافس وغيرها فهي من الخبائث حرام

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p156/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p156/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p156/r5.claim: The highest training is for the dog to go when sent, return when called, stop after seizing prey when checked, and not eat the catch; a trained non-black dog used by a Muslim hunter and trained by a Muslim is agreed to be valid, while defects open disagreement.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p156/r5.anchor: وأعلى مراتب التعليم أن يشلى الحيوان فينشلي ويدعى فيجيب ويزجر بعد ظفره بالصيد فينزجر وأن يكون لا يأكل من صيده

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p156/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p156/r6.speaker: جمهور الأمة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p156/r6.claim: The majority count any trained hunting animal, including a cheetah or a bird such as a falcon, as a jawāriḥ; Ibn ʿAṭiyya connects the term with earning or acquiring, as in 6:60.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p156/r6.anchor: فجمهور الأمة على أن كل ما صاد بعد تعليم فهو جارح أي كاسب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p156/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p156/r7.speaker: ابن عمر
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p156/r7.claim: Ibn ʿUmar says hunting is only by dogs; a bird's catch is lawful only if its ritual slaughter is caught in time, a restriction also related from Abū Jaʿfar.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p156/r7.anchor: وكان ابن عمر يقول إنما يصاد بالكلاب فأما ما صيد به من البزاة وغيرها من الطير فما أدركت ذكاته فذكه فهو حلال لك وإلا فلا تطعمه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p156/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p156/r8.speaker: قوم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p156/r8.claim: Some permit falcons because of ʿAdī ibn Ḥātim's report that the Prophet said to eat what a falcon holds for the hunter.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p156/r8.anchor: واستثنى قوم البزاة فجوزوا صيدها لحديث عدي بن حاتم قال: سألت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن صيد البازي فقال إذا أمسك عليك فكل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p156/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p156/r9.speaker: الضحاك والسدي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p156/r9.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk and al-Suddī restrict “jawāriḥ mukallibīn” to dogs.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p156/r9.anchor: وقال الضحاك والسدي: وما علمتم من الجوارح مكلبين هي الكلاب خاصة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p156/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p156/r10.speaker: الحسن وقتادة وإبراهيم النخعي وأحمد بن حنبل وابن راهويه
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p156/r10.claim: They disapprove of hunting with a solid-black dog; Aḥmad says he knows no one who permits it, while ordinary scholars in Medina and Kufa allow any trained dog.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p156/r10.anchor: وقال أحمد بن حنبل ما أعرف أحدا يرخص فيه إذا كان بهيما

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p156#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p156#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس وأبو هريرة والشعبي وإبراهيم النخعي وسعيد بن جبير وعطاء بن أبي رباح وقتادة وعكرمة والشافعي وأحمد وإسحاق وأبو ثور والنعمان وأصحابه
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p156#2/r1.claim: These authorities prohibit eating what remains when a dog eats the prey, because it held the prey for itself; they interpret “what they hold for you” as complete restraint and cite the Prophet's instruction to ʿAdī ibn Ḥātim.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p156#2/r1.anchor: وإذا أكل فلا تأكل فإنما أمسك على نفسه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p156#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p156#2/r2.speaker: سعد بن أبي وقاص وعبد الله ابن عمر وأبو هريرة وسلمان الفارسي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p156#2/r2.claim: These authorities allow the remainder even if only a piece is left; Mālik and his followers read “what they hold for you” generally, so any amount of restraint suffices.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p156#2/r2.anchor: إذا أكل الجارح أكل ما بقي وإن لم تبق إلا بضعة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p156#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p156#2/r3.speaker: النخعي وأصحاب الرأي والثوري وحماد بن أبي سليمان
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p156#2/r3.claim: They allow eating what a falcon has eaten from its catch, limiting this concession to falcons.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p156#2/r3.anchor: رخصوا فيما أكل البازي منه خاصة في البازي

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p156#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p156#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p156#2/r4.claim: For a bird of prey, no more demanding training can be required than responding when called and going when sent.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p156#2/r4.anchor: كأنه لا يمكن فيه أكثر من ذلك لأن حد تعليمه أن يدعى فيجيب، وأن يشلى فينشلي

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p156#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p156#2/r5.speaker: جمهور الناس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p156#2/r5.claim: Most scholars allow the prey if the hunting animal drinks its blood; ʿAṭāʾ says drinking blood is not eating, while al-Shaʿbī and Sufyān al-Thawrī disapprove of that prey.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p156#2/r5.anchor: وإذا كان الجارح يشرب من دم الصيد فجمهور الناس على أن ذلك الصيد يؤكل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p156#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p156#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p156#2/r6.claim: Only a dog can be fully trained, and most animals eat their catch, so Mālik did not make abstaining from prey a condition of training.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p156#2/r6.anchor: وليس في الحيوان شيء يقبل التعليم التام إلا الكلب شاذا وأكثرها يأكل من الصيد ولذلك لم ير مالك ذلك من شروط التعليم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p156#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p156#2/r7.speaker: ربيعة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p156#2/r7.claim: Rabīʿa says a bird is trained and predatory when it responds to being called.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p156#2/r7.anchor: وأما الطير فقال ربيعة: ما أجاب منها إذا دعي فهو المعلم الضاري.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p157/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p157/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p157/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya explains Rabīʿa's criterion by noting that most animals naturally go when sent.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p157/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p157/r2.speaker: أصحاب أبي حنيفة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p157/r2.claim: The Ḥanafī authorities count a dog as trained after it hunts and holds prey three times consecutively; al-Nuʿmān sets no number, while others require only one successful instance.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p157/r2.anchor: إذا صاد الكلب وأمسك ثلاث مرات ولاء فقد حصل منه التعليم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p157/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p157/r3.speaker: الحسن البصري
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p157/r3.claim: Al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī disapproves of hunting with a dog trained by a Jew or Christian.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p157/r3.anchor: وإذا كان الكلب تعليم يهودي أو نصراني فكره الصيد به الحسن البصري

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p157/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p157/r4.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله والحسن وعطاء ومجاهد وإبراهيم النخعي والثوري وإسحاق بن راهويه
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p157/r4.claim: They disapprove of hunting with a Zoroastrian's trained dog, falcon, or hawk.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p157/r4.anchor: فأما كلب المجوسي وبازه وصقره فكره الصيد بها جابر بن عبد الله والحسن وعطاء ومجاهد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p157/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p157/r5.speaker: مالك والشافعي وأبو حنيفة وأصحابهم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p157/r5.claim: They allow a Muslim to hunt with a Zoroastrian's trained animal, treating it like the hunter's knife.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p157/r5.anchor: ومالك رحمه الله والشافعي وأبو حنيفة وأصحابهم على إباحة الصيد بكلابهم إذا كان الصائد مسلما قالوا: وذلك مثل شفرته

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p157/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p157/r6.speaker: جمهور الأمة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p157/r6.claim: Most authorities permit a People of the Book hunter, but Mālik forbids it, distinguishing hunting from slaughter and citing 5:94; Ibn Wahb and Ashhab allow it like their slaughter.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p157/r6.anchor: فجمهور الأمة على جواز صيده غير مالك رحمه الله فإنه لم يجوز صيد اليهودي والنصراني وفرق بين ذلك وبين ذبيحته

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p157/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p157/r7.speaker: محمد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p157/r7.claim: The Book of Muḥammad forbids the hunt and slaughter of Sabians, whom it describes as people between Jews and Christians with no religion.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p157/r7.anchor: وفي كتاب محمد لا يجوز صيد الصابىء ولا ذبيحته وهم قوم بين اليهود والنصارى لا دين لهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p157/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p157/r8.speaker: مالك والشافعي وأبو حنيفة وأصحابهم وعطاء وابن جبير والنخعي والليث بن سعد وجمهور الناس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p157/r8.claim: They forbid eating a Zoroastrian's catch; Abū Thawr gives two positions, one agreeing and another treating Zoroastrians as People of the Book and permitting it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p157/r8.anchor: فمنع من أكل صيده مالك والشافعي وأبو حنيفة وأصحابهم وعطاء وابن جبير والنخعي والليث بن سعد وجمهور الناس

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p157/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p157/r9.speaker: ابن عباس ومحمد بن الحنفية
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p157/r9.claim: They read “ʿallamtum” with ḍamma on the ʿayn and kasra on the lām, meaning the animals' hunting was taught or directed.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p157/r9.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس ومحمد بن الحنفية «علمتم» بضم العين وكسر اللام أي أمر الجوارح والصيد بها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p157/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p157/r10.speaker: قوم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p157/r10.claim: Some derive jawāriḥ from an animal with a fang, claw, or talon that wounds its prey; Ibn ʿAṭiyya rejects this as weak and says the linguists disagree.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p157/r10.anchor: وحكى ابن المنذر عن قوم أنهم قالوا الجوارح مأخوذ من الجارح أي الحيوان الذي له ناب وظفر أو مخلب يجرح به صيده

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p157/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p157/r11.speaker: جمهور الناس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p157/r11.claim: The majority read mukallibīn with a doubled lām, meaning a trainer or instigator of dogs; the term can also describe someone training another animal by making it like a dog.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p157/r11.anchor: وقرأ جمهور الناس «مكلبين» بفتح الكاف وشد اللام والمكلب معلم الكلاب ومضريها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p157/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p157/r12.speaker: الحسن وأبو زيد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p157/r12.claim: They read with a still kāf and light lām, meaning owners of dogs, formed like a word for someone who has many of something.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p157/r12.anchor: وقرأ الحسن وأبو زيد «مكلبين» بسكون الكاف وتخفيف اللام ومعناه أصحاب كلاب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p157/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p157/r13.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p157/r13.claim: Some commentators take the doubled-lām reading to mean a person who owns dogs.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p157/r13.anchor: وقال بعض المفسرين: المكلب بفتح الكاف وشد اللام صاحب الكلاب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p157#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p157#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p157#2/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says the preceding explanation of mukallib is not precise.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p157#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p157#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p157#2/r2.claim: “What you have taught” has an implied noun: the game or the keeping of the animals taught; their instruction includes hunting techniques and securing prey, and min can mean either a part or a point of origin.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p157#2/r2.anchor: أي يعلمونهن من الحيلة في الاصطياد والتأتي لتحصيل الحيوان وهذا جزء مما علمه الله الإنسان

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p157#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p157#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p157#2/r3.claim: The feminine pronoun in “you teach them” follows the grammatical gender of jawāriḥ, the plural of jāriḥa.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p157#2/r3.anchor: وأنث الضمير في تعلمونهن مراعاة للفظ الجوارح إذ هو جمع جارحة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p157#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p157#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p157#2/r4.claim: “Eat what they hold for you” may mean prey from which they ate nothing, or any prey they held even if they ate some; this underlies the juristic disagreement.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p157#2/r4.anchor: فكلوا مما أمسكن عليكم يحتمل أن يريد مما أمسكن فلم يأكلن منه شيئا.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p157#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p157#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p157#2/r5.claim: The command to name God applies when releasing the animal, under the same legal rules as naming God at slaughter.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p157#2/r5.anchor: واذكروا اسم الله عليه أمر بالتسمية عند الإرسال على الصيد وفقه الصيد والذبح في معنى التسمية واحد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p157#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p157#2/r6.speaker: الشعبي وابن سيرين ونافع وأبو ثور
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p157#2/r6.claim: They dislike meat when God's name was omitted forgetfully, representing the strict view that omission prevents eating.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p157#2/r6.anchor: ممن رويت عنه كراهية ما لم يسم عليه الله نسيانا الشعبي وابن سيرين ونافع وأبو ثور

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p157#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p157#2/r7.speaker: أشهب
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p157#2/r7.claim: Ashhab treats naming as recommended: meat is forbidden if the omission shows contempt, but allowed when someone intentionally omitted it without knowing the rule and without neglecting the law.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p157#2/r7.anchor: وإلى ذلك ينحو أشهب في قوله إن ترك التسمية مستخفا لم تؤكل وإن تركها عامدا لا يدري قدر ذلك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p157#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p157#2/r8.speaker: مالك وجمهور أهل العلم
