IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p157#2/r8.claim: They require naming when one remembers but excuse forgetfulness; deliberate omission invalidates prey or slaughter, while one who forgot names God at eating and the meat remains lawful.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p157#2/r8.anchor: ومذهب مالك وجمهور أهل العلم: أن التسمية واجبة مع الذكر ساقطة مع النسيان

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p157#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p157#2/r9.speaker: أكثر أهل العلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p157#2/r9.claim: Most scholars prefer that the formula name God alone and say “In God's name, God is greatest”; some permit adding a blessing on the Prophet.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p157#2/r9.anchor: واستحب أكثر أهل العلم أن لا يذكر في التسمية غير الله تعالى وأن لفظها بسم الله والله كبر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p157#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p157#2/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p157#2/r10.claim: The general command to fear God points to all the commands contained in these verses.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p157#2/r10.anchor: ثم أمر تعالى بالتقوى على الجملة والإشارة الغريبة هي إلى ما تضمنته هذه الآيات من الأوامر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p157#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p157#2/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p157#2/r11.claim: God's reckoning is swift because He knows everything, needs no counting, and can reckon with all creatures at once.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p157#2/r11.anchor: وسرعة الحساب هي من أنه تبارك وتعالى قد أحاط بكل شيء علما فلا يحتاج إلى محاولة عد ويحاسب جميع الخلائق دفعة واحدة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p157#2/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p157#2/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p157#2/r12.claim: Alternatively, the verse warns that the Day of Judgment will arrive soon.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p157#2/r12.anchor: وتحتمل الآية أن تكون وعيدا بيوم القيامة كأنه قال إن حساب الله لكم سريع إتيانه إذ يوم القيامة قريب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p157#2/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p157#2/r13.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p157#2/r13.claim: Alternatively, swift reckoning means prompt retribution in this world if people fail to fear God.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p157#2/r13.anchor: ويحتمل أن يريد ب الحساب المجازاة فكأنه توعد في الدنيا بمجازاة سريعة قريبة إن لم يتق الله.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p141#2/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p141#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p141#2/r1.claim: Jawāriḥ are hunting dogs; the root ijti rāḥ means earning or acquiring, as in a woman having no provider and what you acquire.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p141#2/r1.anchor: كلاب الصيد. وأصل الاجتراح: الاكتساب. يقال: امرأة لا جارح لها، أي: لا كاسب.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p141#2/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p141#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p141#2/r2.claim: Mukallibīn means people who own or handle dogs.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p290/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p290/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p290/r1.claim: One occasion report says the verse came after people asked what from the dogs they had been ordered to kill remained lawful; al-Hakim included it in his Sahih from Abu Rafiʿ, from the Prophet.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p290/r1.anchor: أخرجه أبو عبد الله الحاكم في صحيحه من حديث أبي رافع عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p290/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p290/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p290/r2.claim: The dog-killing order followed Gabriel's refusal to enter because a house contained a dog or image; they then found a puppy in one of their houses.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p290/r2.anchor: إنا لا ندخل بيتا فيه كلب ولا صورة فنظروا فاذا في بعض بيوتهم جرو

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p290/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p290/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p290/r3.claim: A second occasion report says ʿAdi ibn Hatim and Zayd al-Khayl, whom the Prophet renamed Zayd al-Khayr, asked about their dog and falcon catches: some could be ritually slaughtered, others not, while carrion was forbidden.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p290/r3.anchor: قاله سعيد بن جبير قال الزجاج ومعنى الكلام يسألونك أي شيء أحل لهم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p290/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p290/r4.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p290/r4.claim: The question asks what is lawful; the answer supplies good things and the game caught by trained animals, with the latter phrase omitted because the context makes it clear.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p290/r4.anchor: وأحل لكم صيد ما علمتم من الجوارح والتأويل أنهم سألوا عنه ولكن حذف ذكر صيد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p290/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p290/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p290/r5.claim: The two explanations of good things are permitted slaughtered animals, or what Arabs find good and palatable so long as it is not forbidden.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p290/r5.anchor: أحدهما أنها المباح من الذبائح والثاني أنها ما استطابه العرب مما لم يحرم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p290/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p290/r6.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p290/r6.claim: Jawarih are predatory land animals or birds used for hunting, such as dogs, cheetahs, falcons and hawks, that accept training; Ibn ʿAbbas says every hunting animal is a jarih.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p290/r6.anchor: كالكلب والفهد والصقر والبازي ونحو ذلك مما يقبل التعليم قال ابن عباس كل شيء صاد فهو جارح

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p290/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p290/r7.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p290/r7.claim: One etymology of jawarih derives it from acquisition: the animals earn their owners a livelihood, just as a woman with no breadwinner is called one with no jarih.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p290/r7.anchor: أصل الاجتراح الاكتساب يقال امرأة لا جارح لها أي لا كاسب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p290/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p290/r8.speaker: الماوردي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p290/r8.claim: An alternative etymology calls them jawarih because they usually wound what they hunt.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p290/r8.anchor: لأنها تجرح ما تصيد في الغالب ذكره الماوردي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p290/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p290/r9.speaker: أبو سليمان الدمشقي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p290/r9.claim: A trained beast answers when called, goes out when sent to hunt, and holds the catch for its owner rather than itself; not eating the catch is a sign of this.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p290/r9.anchor: إذا دعوته أجاب وإذا أسدته استأسد ومضى في طلبه وإذا أمسك أمسك عليك لا على نفسه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p290/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p290/r10.speaker: أبو سليمان الدمشقي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p290/r10.claim: Birds are trained differently from land predators: hunting birds are trained by eating, while dogs and cheetahs are trained by leaving the catch uneaten.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p290/r10.anchor: الطائر إنما يعلم الصيد بالأكل والفهد والكلب وما أشبههما يعلمون بترك الأكل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p292/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p292/r1.speaker: أبو صالح، ابن عمر، سعيد بن جبير، عطاء، الضحاك، السدي، الفراء، الزجاج، ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p292/r1.claim: Mukkalibin can mean owners of dogs; al-Zajjaj glosses mukallib or kilabi as a person who hunts with dogs.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p292/r1.anchor: أصحاب الكلاب رواه أبو صالح عن ابن عباس وهو قول ابن عمر وسعيد بن جبير وعطاء والضحاك والسدي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p292/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p292/r2.speaker: ابن عباس، الحسن، مجاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p292/r2.claim: A second explanation of mukkalibin is that the hunters persist in hunting.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p292/r2.anchor: أن معنى مكلبين مصرين على الصيد وهذا مروي عن ابن عباس والحسن ومجاهد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p292/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p292/r3.speaker: أبو سليمان الدمشقي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p292/r3.claim: A third explanation is trainers; they are called mukallibin because most hunting was done with dogs.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p292/r3.anchor: أن مكلبين بمعنى معلمين قال أبو سليمان الدمشقي وإنما قيل لهم مكلبين لأن الغالب من صيدهم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p292/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p292/r4.speaker: الحسن، أبو رزين، ثعلب
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p292/r4.claim: Al-Hasan and Abu Razin read mukallibin with a still kaf; Thaʿlab explains aklaba as having many dogs and says Arabs call the hunter mukallib.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p292/r4.anchor: وقرأ الحسن وأبو رزين مكلبين بسكون الكاف يقال أكلب الرجل إذا كثرت كلابه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p292/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p292/r5.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p292/r5.claim: Teaching the animals means disciplining them to seek game.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p292/r5.anchor: قال سعيد بن جبير تؤدبونهن لطلب الصيد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p292/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p292/r6.speaker: الفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p292/r6.claim: Teaching the animals means disciplining them not to eat their catch.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p292/r6.anchor: وقال الفراء تؤدبونهن أن لا يأكلن صيدهن

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p292/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p292/r7.speaker: ابن عباس، عطاء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p292/r7.claim: One legal view makes not eating a condition for training every hunting animal, so a catch it eats cannot be eaten by people.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p292/r7.anchor: أنه شرط في كل الجوارح فان أكلت لم يؤكل روي عن ابن عباس وعطاء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p292/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p292/r8.speaker: سعد بن أبي وقاص، ابن عمر، أبو هريرة، سلمان الفارسي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p292/r8.claim: A second legal view says abstaining from the catch is not a condition for any kind of trained animal; its catch is lawful even if it eats.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p292/r8.anchor: أنه ليس بشرط في الكل ويؤكل وإن أكلت روي عن سعد ابن أبي وقاص وابن عمر وأبي هريرة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p292/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p292/r9.speaker: الشعبي، النخعي، السدي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p292/r9.claim: The preferred view requires abstention from land predators, but not birds: birds are trained to eat and their catches are permitted, whereas land predators are trained not to eat.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p292/r9.anchor: أنه شرط في جوارح البهائم وليس بشرط في جوارح الطير وبه قال الشعبي والنخعي والسدي وهو أصح

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p292/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p292/r10.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p292/r10.claim: On the preferred distinction, a dog or cheetah eating its catch makes it unlawful, while a falcon or hawk eating its catch remains lawful; Abu Hanifa and his school agree.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p292/r10.anchor: إذا أكل الكلب والفهد من الصيد لم يبح أكله فأما ما أكل منه الصقر والبازي فمباح وبه قال أبو حنيفة وأصحابه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p292/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p292/r11.speaker: مالك
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p292/r11.claim: Malik permits a catch eaten by a dog, cheetah or falcon, and permits a dog-killed catch if the dog did not eat it.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p292/r11.anchor: وقال مالك يباح أكل ما أكل منه الكلب والفهد والصقر فان قتل الكلب ولم يأكل أبيح

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p292/r12.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p292/r12.speaker: أبو حنيفة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p292/r12.claim: Abu Hanifa does not permit a dog-killed catch merely because the dog did not eat it; if live game dies before one can slaughter it, it is permitted, but if slaughter was possible it is not.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p292/r12.anchor: وقال أبو حنيفة لا يباح فان أدرك الصيد وفيه حياة فمات قبل أن يذكيه فان كل ذلك قبل القدرة على ذكاته أبيح

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p292/r13.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p292/r13.speaker: مالك، الشافعي، أبو حنيفة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p292/r13.claim: Malik and al-Shafiʿi permit game that dies after being caught alive when slaughter was not possible, but not when it was possible; Abu Hanifa permits neither case.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p292/r13.anchor: وإن أمكنه فلم يذكه لم يبح وبه قال مالك والشافعي وقال أبو حنيفة لا يباح في الموضعين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p292/r14.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p292/r14.speaker: أحمد، الجمهور، الثوري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p292/r14.claim: Ahmad has one report that hunting with a Magian's dog is not disliked, as most authorities hold, and another report of dislike, as al-Thawri holds.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p292/r14.anchor: فأما الصيد بكلب المجوسي فروي عن أحمد أنه لا يكره وهو قول الأكثرين وروي عنه الكراهة وهو قول الثوري

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p292/r15.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p292/r15.speaker: الثوري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p292/r15.claim: Al-Thawri objects to hunting with a Magian's dog because the address about trained game is directed to believers.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p292/r15.anchor: لقوله تعالى ﴿ وما علمتم من الجوارح ﴾ وهذا خطاب للمؤمنين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p292/r16.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p292/r16.speaker: القاضي أبو يعلى
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p292/r16.claim: The Hanbalis forbid hunting with a trained black dog: the Prophet's command to kill it prevents lawful possession and makes its action legally void.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p292/r16.anchor: منع أصحابنا الصيد بالكلب الأسود وإن كان معلما لأن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أمر بقتله

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p294/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p294/r1.speaker: الأخفش
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p294/r1.claim: Al-Akhfash treats min in the command to eat from what the animals catch as an extra particle, as in the cited expression in 24:43.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p294/r1.anchor: قال الأخفش من زائدة كقوله ﴿ فيها من برد ﴾ النور 43

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p294/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p294/r2.speaker: ابن عباس، السدي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p294/r2.claim: The pronoun in the command to mention God's name refers to the act of releasing the hunting animal; on the author's view, naming God is a condition for lawful game.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p294/r2.anchor: أحدهما أنها ترجع إلى الإرسال قاله ابن عباس والسدي وعندنا أن التسمية شرط في إباحة الصيد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p294/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p294/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p294/r3.claim: The other interpretation refers the pronoun to eating, making the invocation recommended rather than a condition.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p294/r3.anchor: والثاني ترجع إلى الأكل فتكون التسمية مستحبة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p294/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p294/r4.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p294/r4.claim: The command to fear God means not deeming lawful game over which God's name was not mentioned.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p294/r4.anchor: قال سعيد بن جبير لا تستحلوا ما لم يذكر اسم الله عليه

MAJAZ:v1p154/r1.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p154/r1.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p154/r1.claim: Jawāriḥ are hunting animals; jāriḥat ahlihi can also mean the family’s breadwinner, while ijtaraha and jaraḥa mean to earn or acquire.
MAJAZ:v1p154/r1.anchor: «وما علمتم من الجوارح» (4) أي الصوائد، ويقال: فلان جارحة أهله أي كاسبهم،

MAJAZ:v1p154/r2.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p154/r2.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p154/r2.claim: The source cites further Qurʾanic usages of ijtaraha and jaraḥa for earning, including “what you have earned.”
MAJAZ:v1p154/r2.anchor:
«اجترحوا السيئات»
(45/ 20) كسبوا، «وما جرحتم» (6/ 60) أي ما كسبتم.

MAJAZ:v1p154/r3.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p154/r3.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p154/r3.claim: Mukallibīn means owners or trainers of dogs.

MAJAZ:v1p154/r4.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p154/r4.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p154/r4.claim: Ṭufayl al-Ghanawī’s line uses mukallib for a dog handler who notices a faint sound.
MAJAZ:v1p154/r4.anchor: تبارى مراخيها الزجاج كأنها ... ضراه أحست نبأة من مكلب

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p18/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p18/r1.speaker: الشافعي، النووي، الرافعي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p18/r1.claim: One view permits prey killed by a hunting dog's impact without a wound, relying on the general wording of 5:4 and reports from Adi; companions attribute this view to Shafi'i, and later jurists such as Nawawi and Rafi'i endorse it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p18/r1.anchor: وهذا قول حكاه الأصحاب عن الشافعي، رحمه الله، وصححه بعض المتأخرين [منهم] (5) كالنووي والرافعي.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p18/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p18/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p18/r2.claim: Ibn Kathir says this permissive position is not clear from Shafi'i's al-Umm and al-Mukhtasar, where Shafi'i presented two possible readings without committing, although his discussion slightly favors permissibility.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p18/r2.anchor: قلت: وليس ذلك بظاهر من كلام الشافعي في الأم والمختصر، فإنه قال في كلا الموضعين: "يحتمل معنيين".

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p18/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p18/r3.speaker: أبو حنيفة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p18/r3.claim: Ibn al-Sabbagh transmits permissibility from Abu Hanifa through the narration of al-Hasan ibn Ziyad.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p18/r3.anchor: نقله ابن الصباغ عن أبي حنيفة، من رواية الحسن بن زياد، عنه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p18/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p18/r4.speaker: ابن جرير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p18/r4.claim: Ibn Jarir attributes permissibility to Salman, Abu Hurayra, Sa'd, and Ibn Umar, but Ibn Kathir calls this very strange and says no explicit report from them is known; it appears to be Ibn Jarir's inference.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p18/r4.anchor: فحكاه في تفسيره عن سلمان الفارسي، وأبي هريرة، وسعد بن أبي وقاص، وابن عمر. وهذا غريب جدا، وليس يوجد ذلك مصرحا به عنهم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p18/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p18/r5.speaker: الشافعي، المزني، ابن الصباغ، أبو يوسف، محمد، أحمد بن حنبل
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p18/r5.claim: The second view forbids prey killed by impact without a wound: it is one Shafi'i position, chosen by Muzani, favored by Ibn al-Sabbagh's wording, reported from Abu Hanifa by Abu Yusuf and Muhammad, and famous from Ahmad.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p18/r5.anchor: والقول الثاني: أن ذلك لا يحل، وهو أحد القولين عن الشافعي، رحمه الله، واختاره المزني

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p18/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p18/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p18/r6.claim: Ibn Kathir prefers the prohibition as more consistent with legal principles and the foundations of the law.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p18/r6.anchor: وهذا القول أشبه بالصواب، والله أعلم، لأنه أجرى عن (2) القواعد الأصولية، وأمس بالأصول (3) الشرعية.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p18/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p18/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم (حديث رافع بن خديج)
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p18/r7.claim: The Prophet says to eat what causes blood to flow when God's name is pronounced, in response to Rafi ibn Khadij's question about slaughtering with reeds; the report is in both Sahih collections.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p18/r7.anchor: قلت: يا رسول الله، إنا لاقو العدو غدا وليس معنا مدى، أفنذبح بالقصب؟ قال: (4) "ما أنهر الدم وذكر اسم الله عليه فكلوه".

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p18/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p18/r8.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p18/r8.claim: Though prompted by a specific case, the majority of legal theorists apply the hadith's general wording; the Prophet's ruling that every intoxicating drink is forbidden illustrates the rule beyond honey wine alone.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p18/r8.anchor: العبرة بعموم اللفظ عند جمهور من العلماء في الأصول والفروع

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p19/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p19/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p19/r1.claim: Against the objection that Rafi's report concerned slaughtering tools, Ibn Kathir argues that its wording commands eating whatever makes blood flow and names God, so it governs both the tool and the animal slaughtered.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p19/r1.anchor: هذا يؤخذ منه الحكمان معا، يؤخذ حكم الآلة التي يذكى بها، وحكم المذكى

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p19/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p19/r2.speaker: المزني
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p19/r2.claim: Muzani's method restricts the unrestricted dog report by the arrow report: an arrow that kills by its flat side is not edible, while one that penetrates is; both are hunting means and the prey dies from impact.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p19/r2.anchor: طريقة المزني، وهي أن السهم جاء التصريح فيه بأنه إن قتل بعرضه فلا تأكل، وإن خزق فكل.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p19/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p19/r3.speaker: المزني
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p19/r3.claim: Muzani's analogy parallels restricting unqualified emancipation in expiation for ẓihār by the requirement of faith in homicide expiation; the analogy takes precedence over general wording for those who accept the principle.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p19/r3.anchor: كما وجب حمل مطلق الإعتاق في الظهار على تقييده بالإيمان في القتل، بل هذا أولى.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p19/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p19/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p19/r4.claim: On the analogy, a dog that kills by its weight is unlawful like an arrow that kills by its flat side, because both are hunting tools and the prey dies from blunt force; analogy takes precedence over generality according to the four imams and majority.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p19/r4.anchor: والجامع أن كلا منهما آلة للصيد، وقد مات بثقله فيهما. ولا يعارض ذلك بعموم الآية؛ لأن القياس مقدم على العموم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p20/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p20/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p20/r1.claim: The lawgiver applies the category of beaten prey during hunting: when a dog strikes with its flat side, the Prophet calls it wakidh and forbids eating; no scholar distinguishes this while exempting prey killed by impact, so that permissive claim would violate consensus.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p20/r1.anchor: وإن أصابه بعرضه (3) فإنما هو وقيذ فلا تأكله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p20/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p20/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p20/r2.claim: The general permission for trained hunting animals is already limited by consensus to edible species, so a preserved general text outweighs one whose generality has exceptions.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p20/r2.anchor: ليست على عمومها بالإجماع، بل مخصوصة بما صدن من الحيوان المأكول

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p20/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p20/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p20/r3.claim: Prey killed by blunt impact retains blood and associated fluids and is therefore like carrion, making it unlawful by analogy.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p20/r3.anchor: هذا الصيد والحالة هذه في حكم الميتة سواء؛ لأنه قد احتقن فيه الدماء وما يتبعها من الرطوبات

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p20/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p20/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p20/r4.claim: The prohibition and permission verses should both remain operative, with the Sunna explaining them: a penetrating arrow or wounded prey falls under permission, while bluntly struck prey is beaten or gored and falls under prohibition.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p20/r4.anchor: وكذا ينبغي أن تكون آية التحليل محكمة، أعني قوله: {يسألونك ماذا أحل لهم قل أحل لكم الطيبات [وما علمتم من الجوارح مكلبين] }

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p20/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p20/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p20/r5.claim: The dog rule was not spelled out because dogs ordinarily kill with claw or fang and blunt collisions are rare, while arrows often miss or strike with the flat side and therefore needed both cases stated.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p20/r5.anchor: أن من شأن الكلب أن يقتل بظفره أو نابه أو بهما معا، وأما اصطدامه هو والصيد فنادر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p20/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p20/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p20/r6.claim: A sound report in both Sahih collections says not to eat prey when the dog has eaten from it, because it may have caught the prey for itself.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p20/r6.anchor: إن أكل فلا تأكل، فإني أخاف أن يكون أمسك على نفسه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p20/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p20/r7.speaker: أبو هريرة، ابن عباس، الحسن، الشعبي، النخعي، أبو حنيفة، صاحباه، أحمد، الشافعي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p20/r7.claim: Many authorities hold that prey eaten from by the dog is unlawful, following the report as a specification of the verse's general permission; this is Shafi'i's famous position.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p20/r7.anchor: فقالوا: لا يحل ما أكل منه الكلب، حكي ذلك عن أبي هريرة، وابن عباس. وبه قال الحسن، والشعبي، والنخعي.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p20/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p20/r8.speaker: علي، سعد، سلمان، أبو هريرة، ابن عمر، ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p20/r8.claim: Ibn Jarir transmits the contrary view from these Companions: prey remains edible even if the dog ate from it, down to a final morsel; Malik and Shafi'i's old position agree, while Shafi'i's new position leaves two views.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p20/r8.anchor: وروى ابن جرير في تفسيره عن علي، وسعد، وسلمان، وأبي هريرة، وابن عمر، وابن عباس: أن الصيد يؤكل وإن أكل منه الكلب

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p31#3/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p31#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p31#3/r1.claim: After the preceding verse forbids harmful filthy things to body, religion, or both and allows necessity, this verse permits wholesome things, as does 7:157's description of Muhammad.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p31#3/r1.anchor: لما ذكر تعالى ما حرمه في الآية المتقدمة من الخبائث الضارة لمتناولها، إما في بدنه، أو في دينه، أو فيهما

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p31#3/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p31#3/r2.speaker: عدي بن حاتم، زيد بن المهلهل الطائي، سعيد بن جبير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p31#3/r2.claim: Adi ibn Hatim and Zayd ibn al-Muhalhil asked the Prophet what was lawful after carrion was forbidden, and the verse was revealed; Sa'id ibn Jubayr explains wholesome things here as lawful slaughtered animals.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p31#3/r2.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير، عن عدي بن حاتم، وزيد بن المهلهل الطائيين (1) سألا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، فقالا يا رسول الله، قد حرم الله الميتة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p31#3/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p31#3/r3.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p31#3/r3.claim: Muqatil ibn Hayyan defines wholesome things as anything people may lawfully obtain, meaning lawful provision.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p31#3/r3.anchor: ما أحل لهم من كل شيء أن يصيبوه (5) وهو الحلال من الرزق.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p31#3/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p31#3/r4.speaker: الزهري
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p31#3/r4.claim: When asked about drinking urine as a treatment, al-Zuhri said it is not among wholesome things.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p31#3/r4.anchor: وقد سئل الزهري عن شرب البول للتداوي فقال: ليس هو من الطيبات.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p31#3/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p31#3/r5.speaker: مالك
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p31#3/r5.claim: Malik said that selling clay eaten by people is not among wholesome things.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p31#3/r5.anchor: سئل مالك عن بيع الطين الذي يأكله الناس. فقال: ليس هو من الطيبات.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p32/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p32/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p32/r1.claim: The permitted game includes prey taken by trained dogs, cheetahs, falcons, and similar hunting animals, following the majority of early authorities and imams.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p32/r1.anchor: وهي من الكلاب والفهود والصقور وأشباه ذلك، كما هو مذهب الجمهور من الصحابة والتابعين والأئمة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p32/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p32/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p32/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas defines the trained jawarih as trained dogs, falcons, and any bird trained to hunt.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p32/r2.anchor: علي بن أبي طلحة، عن ابن عباس في قوله: {وما علمتم من الجوارح مكلبين} وهن (8) الكلاب المعلمة (9) والبازي

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p32/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p32/r3.speaker: خيثمة، طاوس، مجاهد، مكحول، يحيى بن أبي كثير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p32/r3.claim: These authorities are reported to give the same broad account of hunting animals as the preceding view.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p32/r3.anchor: وروي عن خيثمة، وطاوس، ومجاهد، ومكحول، ويحيى بن أبي كثير، نحو ذلك.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p32/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p32/r4.speaker: الحسن
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p32/r4.claim: Al-Hasan counts buzzards and falcons among the hunting animals.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p32/r4.anchor: وروي عن الحسن أنه قال: الباز والصقر من الجوارح.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p32/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p32/r5.speaker: علي بن الحسين
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p32/r5.claim: Ali ibn al-Husayn is reported to hold the same view that buzzards and falcons are jawarih.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p32/r5.anchor: وروي عن علي بن الحسين مثله.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p32/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p32/r6.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p32/r6.claim: Mujahid disliked game caught by any bird and cited the verse's wording about trained hunting animals.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p32/r6.anchor: ثم روي عن مجاهد أنه كره صيد الطير كله، وقرأ قول الله [عز وجل] (11) {وما علمتم من الجوارح مكلبين}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p32/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p32/r7.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p32/r7.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr is reported to share Mujahid's disapproval of bird game.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p32/r7.anchor: وروي عن سعيد بن جبير نحو ذلك.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p32/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p32/r8.speaker: الضحاك، السدي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p32/r8.claim: Ibn Jarir also transmits the preceding restrictive view about bird game from al-Dahhak and al-Suddi.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p32/r8.anchor: ونقله ابن جرير عن الضحاك والسدي

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p32/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p32/r9.speaker: ابن عمر
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p32/r9.claim: Ibn Umar says a bird's catch is lawful if recovered alive; if the bird has already killed it, do not eat it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p32/r9.anchor: عن ابن عمر قال: أما ما صاد من الطير البزاة وغيرها من الطير، فما أدركت فهو لك، وإلا فلا تطعمه.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p32/r10.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p32/r10.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p32/r10.claim: Ibn Kathir prefers the majority view that bird game is like dog-caught game because birds seize prey with their talons just as dogs seize it with teeth.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p32/r10.anchor: قلت: والمحكي عن الجمهور أن صيد الطيور كصيد الكلاب (12) ؛ لأنها تكلب الصيد بمخالبها (13) كما تكلبه الكلاب، فلا فرق.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p32/r11.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p32/r11.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p32/r11.claim: The four imams and others, including Ibn Jarir, adopt the majority position that bird and dog game are alike.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p32/r11.anchor: وهذا (14) مذهب الأئمة الأربعة وغيرهم، واختاره ابن جرير

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p32/r12.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p32/r12.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p32/r12.claim: In a report from Adi ibn Hatim, the Prophet permits eating whatever a falcon holds for its owner.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p32/r12.anchor: عن عدي بن حاتم قال: سألت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن صيد البازي، فقال: "ما أمسك عليك فكل".

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p32/r13.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p32/r13.speaker: الإمام أحمد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p32/r13.claim: Ahmad excludes game caught by a black dog because he considers black dogs obligatory to kill and unlawful to keep.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p32/r13.anchor: واستثنى الإمام أحمد صيد الكلب الأسود؛ لأنه عنده مما يجب قتله ولا يحل اقتناؤه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p32/r14.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p32/r14.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p32/r14.claim: A report from Abu Dharr says a black dog interrupts prayer and the Prophet calls it a devil, explaining Ahmad's exception.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p32/r14.anchor: عن أبي ذر؛ أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "يقطع الصلاة الحمار والمرأة والكلب الأسود"

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p32/r15.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p32/r15.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p32/r15.claim: A separate report says the Prophet ordered dogs to be killed.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p32/r15.anchor: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أمر بقتل الكلاب

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p33/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p33/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p33/r1.claim: Jawarih is derived from jarh, meaning acquisition; Arabic speakers use jaraha for earning, including earning good for one's family.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p33/r1.anchor: وسميت هذه الحيوانات التي يصطاد بهن: جوارح، من الجرح، وهو: الكسب. كما تقول (5) العرب: فلان جرح أهله خيرا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p33/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p33/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p33/r2.claim: The verse at 6:60 uses jarah for what people earn, whether good or evil, during the day.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p33/r2.anchor: وقال الله تعالى: {وهو الذي يتوفاكم بالليل ويعلم ما جرحتم بالنهار} [الأنعام: 60] أي: ما كسبتم من خير وشر.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p33/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p33/r3.speaker: أبو رافع مولى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p33/r3.claim: Abu Rafi reports that after the Prophet ordered dogs killed, people asked what from the creatures they could eat; revelation answered with the allowance for good foods and trained catches, and the Prophet permitted a named dog's catch unless it ate it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p33/r3.anchor: عن أبي رافع مولى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم؛ أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أمر بقتل الكلاب، فقتلت، فجاء الناس فقالوا: يا رسول الله، ما يحل لنا من هذه الأمة التي أمرت (6) بقتلها؟

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p33/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p33/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p33/r4.claim: After the revelation, the Prophet says to eat what a named dog catches for its sender, provided the dog has not eaten from the prey.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p33/r4.anchor: فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "إذا أرسل الرجل كلبه وسمى، فأمسك عليه، فليأكل ما لم يأكل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p33/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p33/r5.speaker: أبو رافع مولى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p33/r5.claim: A second account says Gabriel would not enter a house containing a dog, so Abu Rafi was ordered to kill Medina's dogs; he spared a woman's barking dog out of pity, then returned and killed it before the people asked what remained lawful.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p33/r5.anchor: جاء جبريل إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ليستأذن (7) عليه، فأذن له فقال: قد أذنا لك يا رسول الله. قال: أجل، ولكنا لا ندخل بيتا فيه كلب

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p33/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p33/r6.speaker: الحاكم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p33/r6.claim: Al-Hakim transmits the Abu Rafi account through Ibn Ishaq and Aبان ibn Salih and grades it sound, while noting al-Bukhari and Muslim did not include it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p33/r6.anchor: عن أبان بن صالح، به. وقال: صحيح ولم يخرجاه.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p34/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p34/r1.speaker: عكرمة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p34/r1.claim: Ikrima reports that after Abu Rafi was sent to kill dogs through al-Awali, Asim ibn Adi, Sa'd ibn Khaythama, and Uwaym ibn Saida asked what was lawful, and the verse was revealed.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p34/r1.anchor: عن ابن جريج، عن عكرمة؛ أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بعث أبا (1) رافع في قتل الكلاب

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p34/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p34/r2.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p34/r2.claim: Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi also identifies the killing of dogs as the occasion for this verse's revelation.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p34/r2.anchor: وهكذا قال محمد بن كعب القرظي في سبب نزول هذه الآية: إنه في قتل الكلاب.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p34/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p34/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p34/r3.claim: Grammatically, mukallibin may describe the subject who trained the animals or the jawarih as trained for hunting.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p34/r3.anchor: يحتمل أن يكون حالا من الضمير في {علمتم} فيكون حالا من الفاعل، ويحتمل أن يكون حالا من المفعول وهو {الجوارح}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p34/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p34/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p34/r4.claim: If a hunting animal kills prey by striking or clawing it, that prey is unlawful according to one of al-Shafi'i's two positions and a group of scholars.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p34/r4.anchor: على أن الجارحة إذا قتل الصيد بصدمته أو بمخلابه وظفره أنه لا يحل، كما هو أحد قولي الشافعي وطائفة من العلماء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p34/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p34/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p34/r5.claim: Training means the animal obeys when released or incited and holds its catch for its owner until he arrives instead of keeping it for itself.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p34/r5.anchor: وإذا أشلاه استشلى (8) وإذا أخذ الصيد أمسكه على صاحبه حتى يجيء إليه ولا يمسكه لنفسه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p34/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p34/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p34/r6.claim: A trained animal's catch is lawful if it holds prey for its owner and God's name was invoked at release, even if it kills the prey; this is agreed upon.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p34/r6.anchor: وأمسك على صاحبه، وكان قد ذكر اسم الله عند إرساله حل الصيد، وإن قتله بالإجماع.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p34/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p34/r7.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p34/r7.claim: The Prophet tells Adi ibn Hatim to eat what a trained dog catches when God's name was said at release, even if it kills, unless a different dog joins the catch.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p34/r7.anchor: قلت: وإن قتلن؟ قال: "وإن قتلن ما لم يشركها كلب (11) ليس منها

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p34/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p34/r8.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p34/r8.claim: For prey struck with a mi'rad, eat it if the shaft pierces through; if its broad side only strikes and kills it, it is blunt-force prey and must not be eaten.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p34/r8.anchor: وإن أصابه بعرض فإنه وقيذ، فلا تأكله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p34/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p34/r9.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p34/r9.claim: If the prey is found alive, slaughter it; if found dead and the dog did not eat it, eat it because the dog's catch counts as slaughter.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p34/r9.anchor: إذا أرسلت كلبك فاذكر اسم الله، فإن أمسك عليك فأدركته حيا فاذبحه، وإن أدركته قد قتل ولم يأكل منه فكله، فإن أخذ الكلب ذكاته

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p34/r10.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p34/r10.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p34/r10.claim: The Prophet forbids eating prey if the dog has eaten from it, explaining that it may have caught the prey for itself.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p34/r10.anchor: فإن أكل فلا تأكل، فإني أخاف أن يكون أمسك على نفسه.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p34/r11.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p34/r11.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p34/r11.claim: Ibn Kathir says this is the majority view and the correct Shafi'i position: dog-eaten prey is categorically unlawful; a group of early authorities held it never becomes unlawful for that reason.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p34/r11.anchor: فهذا دليل للجمهور (14) وهو الصحيح من مذهب الشافعي، وهو أنه إذا أكل الكلب من الصيد يحرم مطلقا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p35/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p35/r1.speaker: سلمان الفارسي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p35/r1.claim: Salman says one may eat the hunt even when the dog has eaten two thirds of it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p35/r1.anchor: عن سعيد بن المسيب قال: قال سلمان الفارسي: كل وإن أكل ثلثيه (1) -يعني الصيد-إذا أكل منه الكلب.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p35/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p35/r2.speaker: سعد بن أبي وقاص
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p35/r2.claim: Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas says to eat the catch even if only a small piece remains after the dog has eaten.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p35/r2.anchor: أنه سأل سعد بن أبي وقاص عن الصيد يأكل منه الكلب، فقال: كل، وإن لم يبق منه إلا حذية

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p35/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p35/r3.speaker: سعد بن أبي وقاص
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p35/r3.claim: A second report from Sa'd says to eat even if the dog has eaten two thirds of the catch.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p35/r3.anchor: عن سعيد بن المسيب، عن سعد بن أبي وقاص قال: كل وإن أكل ثلثيه.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p35/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p35/r4.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p35/r4.claim: Abu Hurayra permits eating if the dog consumed two thirds and one third remains.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p35/r4.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: لو أرسلت كلبك فأكل منه، فإن أكل ثلثيه وبقي ثلثه فكل.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p35/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p35/r5.speaker: ابن عمر
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p35/r5.claim: Ibn Umar permits eating whatever a named, trained dog catches whether it eats from the prey or not.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p35/r5.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عمر قال: إذا أرسلت كلبك المعلم وذكرت اسم الله (13) فكل ما أمسك عليك، أكل أو لم يأكل.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p35/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p35/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p35/r6.claim: Ibn Kathir says these reports are established from Salman, Sa'd, Abu Hurayra, and Ibn Umar, attributed also to Ali and Ibn Abbas; the question is disputed from Ata and al-Hasan, and the allowance is held by al-Zuhri, Rabi'a, and Malik and was al-Shafi'i's older view and suggested in his later view.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p35/r6.anchor: فهذه الآثار ثابتة عن سلمان، وسعد بن أبي وقاص، وأبي هريرة، وابن عمر. وهو محكي عن علي، وابن عباس. واختلف فيه عن عطاء، والحسن البصري. وهو قول الزهري، وربيعة، ومالك. وإليه ذهب الشافعي في القديم، وأومأ إليه في الجديد.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p35/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p35/r7.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p35/r7.claim: A report attributed to Salman from the Prophet says that if the dog has eaten by the time the hunter finds the catch, the hunter may eat what remains.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p35/r7.anchor: عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "إذا أرسل الرجل كلبه على الصيد فأدركه، وقد أكل منه، فليأكل ما بقي

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p35#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p35#2/r1.speaker: ابن جرير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p35#2/r1.claim: Ibn Jarir questions the marfu report's chain: Sa'id's hearing from Salman is unknown, and reliable transmitters report the statement as Salman's own.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p35#2/r1.anchor: وفي إسناد هذا الحديث نظر، وسعيد غير معلوم له سماع من سلمان، والثقات يروونه من كلام سلمان غير مرفوع.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p35#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p35#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p35#2/r2.claim: Ibn Kathir agrees with Ibn Jarir's chain criticism but says the same ruling is soundly transmitted as a prophetic report through other routes.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p35#2/r2.anchor: وهذا الذي قاله ابن جرير صحيح، لكن قد روي هذا المعنى مرفوعا من وجوه أخر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p35#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p35#2/r3.speaker: أبو ثعلبة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p35#2/r3.claim: Abu Tha'labah's report permits game caught by trained dogs whether alive or dead, including when the dog ate, and also answers questions about bow-shot game and using Magian vessels after washing them in necessity.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p35#2/r3.anchor: أن أعرابيا -يقال له: أبو ثعلبة-قال: يا رسول الله، إن لي كلابا مكلبة، فأفتني في صيدها.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p35#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p35#2/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p35#2/r4.claim: In Abu Tha'labah's report, the Prophet says dog-caught game remains lawful even if the dog eats from it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p35#2/r4.anchor: قال: وإن أكل منه؟ قال: "نعم، وإن أكل منه".

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p35#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p35#2/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p35#2/r5.claim: The Prophet says to eat what an arrow returns unless it has entered water or another arrow's mark is found on it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p35#2/r5.anchor: قال: "كل ما ردت عليك قوسك" قال: ذكيا وغير ذكي؟ قال: "وإن تغيب عنك ما لم يصل، أو تجد فيه أثر غير سهمك".

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p35#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p35#2/r6.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p35#2/r6.claim: When necessity requires using Magian vessels, the Prophet says to wash them and eat from them.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p35#2/r6.anchor: قال: أفتني في آنية المجوس إذا اضطررنا إليها. قال: "اغسلها وكل فيها".

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p35#2/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p35#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p35#2/r7.claim: Ibn Kathir calls the two Abu Tha'labah chains good and records another wording allowing a named dog's catch even if it ate and whatever one's hand returns.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p35#2/r7.anchor: وهذان إسنادان جيدان، وقد روى الثوري، عن سماك بن حرب، عن عدي قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "ما كان من كلب ضار أمسك عليك، فكل". قلت: وإن أكل؟ قال: "نعم".

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p35#2/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p35#2/r8.speaker: عبد الملك بن حبيب
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p35#2/r8.claim: Abd al-Malik ibn Habib transmits through al-Sha'bi from Adi a version permitting a predatory dog's catch even if it ate.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p35#2/r8.anchor: وروى عبد الملك بن حبيب: حدثنا أسد بن موسى، عن ابن أبي زائدة، عن الشعبي، عن عدي مثله.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p35#2/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p35#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p35#2/r9.claim: These reports support allowing prey eaten by a dog; some authorities therefore do not prohibit it at all.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p35#2/r9.anchor: فهذه آثار دالة على أنه يغتفر إن أكل منه الكلب. وقد احتج بها من لم يحرم الصيد بأكل الكلب

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p35#2/r10.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p35#2/r10.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p35#2/r10.claim: A conciliatory view forbids prey when the dog eats immediately, as it may have caught it for itself, but allows it if the dog first held it for its owner and ate later from hunger; Ibn Kathir calls this a good reconciliation of the reports.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p35#2/r10.anchor: إن أكل عقب ما أمسكه فإنه يحرم لحديث عدي بن حاتم.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p35#2/r11.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p35#2/r11.speaker: الأستاذ أبو المعالي الجويني
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p35#2/r11.claim: Al-Juwayni had wished someone would clearly distinguish the circumstances in which dog-eaten game is forbidden, and Ibn Kathir says God fulfilled that wish through this distinction.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p35#2/r11.anchor: وقد تمنى الأستاذ أبو المعالي الجويني في كتابه "النهاية" أن لو فصل مفصل هذا التفصيل، وقد حقق الله أمنيته

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p35#2/r12.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p35#2/r12.speaker: طائفة من الأصحاب
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p35#2/r12.claim: A group of Shafi'i school colleagues adopts the distinction between immediate eating and eating after the dog waits and becomes hungry.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p35#2/r12.anchor: وقال بهذا القول والتفريق طائفة من الأصحاب

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p35#2/r13.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p35#2/r13.speaker: طائفة من العلماء
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p35#2/r13.claim: A fourth view forbids dog-eaten prey under Adi's report but allows prey eaten by falcons and similar birds because they can only be trained by eating.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p35#2/r13.anchor: وقال آخرون قولا رابعا في المسألة، وهو التفرقة بين أكل الكلب فيحرم لحديث عدي، وبين أكل الصقور ونحوها فلا يحرم؛ لأنه لا يقبل التعليم إلا بالأكل.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p37/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p37/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p37/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas permits bird-caught prey even if the bird kills it or eats and plucks it: birds return to their owners when trained, unlike dogs that do not return after being struck.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p37/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس؛ أنه قال في الطير: إذا أرسلته فقتل فكل، فإن الكلب إذا ضربته لم يعد، وإن تعلم الطير أن يرجع إلى صاحبه وليس يضرب، فإذا أكل من الصيد ونتف الريش فكل.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p37/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p37/r2.speaker: إبراهيم النخعي، الشعبي، حماد بن أبي سليمان
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p37/r2.claim: Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, al-Sha'bi, and Hammad ibn Abi Sulayman hold the same permissive view about bird-caught prey even if eaten.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p37/r2.anchor: وكذا قال إبراهيم النخعي، والشعبي، وحماد بن أبي سليمان.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p37/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p37/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p37/r3.claim: The Adi ibn Hatim report supports distinguishing dogs from falcons: it conditions dog-caught prey on the dog not eating, while stating no such condition for falcons.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p37/r3.anchor: فوجه الدلالة لهم أنه اشترط في الكلب ألا يأكل، ولم يشترط ذلك في البزاة، فدل على التفرقة بينهما في الحكم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p37#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p37#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p37#2/r1.claim: The command to remember God's name over the catch means invoking it when releasing the hunting animal.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p37#2/r1.anchor: وقوله: {فكلوا مما أمسكن عليكم واذكروا اسم الله عليه} أي: عند الإرسال

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p37#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p37#2/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p37#2/r2.claim: The Prophet tells Adi ibn Hatim to say God's name when releasing the trained dog and then eat what it catches.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p37#2/r2.anchor: كما قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لعدي بن حاتم: "إذا أرسلت كلبك المعلم (3) وذكرت اسم الله، فكل ما أمسك عليك".

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p37#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p37#2/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p37#2/r3.claim: In Abu Tha'labah's report, the Prophet commands saying God's name when releasing a dog or shooting an arrow.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p37#2/r3.anchor: وفي حديث أبي ثعلبة المخرج في الصحيحين أيضا: "إذا أرسلت كلبك، فاذكر اسم الله، وإذا رميت بسهمك فاذكر اسم الله"

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p37#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p37#2/r4.speaker: أحمد بن حنبل
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p37#2/r4.claim: Ahmad's well-known position requires saying God's name both when releasing a dog and when shooting an arrow, based on the verse and hadith.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p37#2/r4.anchor: اشترط من اشترط من الأئمة كأحمد [بن حنبل] (4) -في المشهور عنه (5) -التسمية -عند إرسال الكلب والرمي بالسهم لهذه الآية وهذا الحديث

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p37#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p37#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p37#2/r5.claim: The majority, including al-Suddi and others, understand this verse as commanding invocation at release.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p37#2/r5.anchor: وهذا القول هو المشهور عن (6) الجمهور، أن (7) المراد بهذه الآية الأمر بالتسمية عند الإرسال، كما قال (8) السدي وغير واحد.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p37#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p37#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p37#2/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas says to say 'in God's name' when releasing the hunting animal, but sees no harm if one forgets.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p37#2/r6.anchor: وقال علي بن أبي طلحة، عن ابن عباس في قوله: {واذكروا اسم الله عليه} يقول: إذا أرسلت جارحك فقل: باسم الله، وإن نسيت فلا حرج.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p37#2/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p37#2/r7.speaker: بعض الناس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p37#2/r7.claim: Some interpret the command as saying God's name when eating, citing the Prophet's instruction to his stepson to name God, eat with the right hand, and eat what is near.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p37#2/r7.anchor: وقال بعض الناس: المراد بهذه الآية الأمر بالتسمية عند الأكل كما ثبت في الصحيح: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم علم ربيبه عمر بن أبي سلمة فقال: "سم الله، وكل بيمينك، وكل مما يليك".

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p37#2/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p37#2/r8.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p37#2/r8.claim: When asked about meat from recent converts whose invocation was uncertain, the Prophet tells the questioners to say God's name themselves and eat.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p37#2/r8.anchor: عن عائشة أنهم قالوا: يا رسول الله، إن قوما يأتوننا -حديث عهدهم بكفر-بلحمان لا ندري أذكر اسم الله عليها (10)

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p37#2/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p37#2/r9.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p37#2/r9.claim: A report from Aisha says the Prophet taught that naming God at the start of a meal suffices; if forgotten, one should say it at the beginning and end when remembering.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p37#2/r9.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عبيد بن عمير، عن عائشة؛ أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يأكل الطعام في ستة نفر من أصحابه، فجاء أعرابي فأكله بلقمتين، فقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: "أما إنه لو (1) كان ذكر اسم الله لكفاكم، فإذا أكل أحدكم فليذكر اسم الله، فإن نسي أن يذكر اسم الله أوله فليقل: باسم الله (2) أوله وآخره

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p37#2/r10.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p37#2/r10.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p37#2/r10.claim: Ibn Kathir notes that the first chain for Aisha's meal report is disconnected because Abdullah ibn Ubayd ibn Umayr did not hear this report from her.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p37#2/r10.anchor: وهذا منقطع بين عبد الله (4) بن عبيد بن عمير وعائشة، فإنه لم يسمع منها هذا الحديث

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p38/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p38/r1.speaker: أم كلثوم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p38/r1.claim: A second chain for the meal report has a woman called Umm Kulthum transmit it from Aisha; Ahmad, Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, and al-Nasa'i record it, and al-Tirmidhi grades it hasan sahih.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p38/r1.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عبيد بن عمير؛ أن امرأة منهم -يقال لها: أم كلثوم- حدثته، عن عائشة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p38/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p38/r2.speaker: الترمذي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p38/r2.claim: Al-Tirmidhi grades the alternate Aisha chain for the meal report hasan sahih.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p38/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p38/r3.speaker: أمية بن مخشي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p38/r3.claim: Umayya ibn Makhshi, a Companion, reports that a man who named God only at his last bite was told that Satan had eaten with him until the invocation, after which the food was vomited.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p38/r3.anchor: إن جدي أمية بن مخشى (10) -وكان من أصحاب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم-سمعته يقول

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p38/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p38/r4.speaker: ابن معين، النسائي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p38/r4.claim: Ibn Ma'in and al-Nasa'i regard Jabir ibn Subh as reliable, while Abu al-Fath al-Azdi says his report is not strong enough as proof.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p38/r4.anchor: ووثقه ابن معين والنسائي، وقال أبو الفتح الأزدي: لا تقوم به الحجة.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p38/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p38/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p38/r5.claim: The Prophet says Satan shares a meal when God's name is not invoked; a girl and a Bedouin tried to begin eating without invocation, so he took their hands and stopped them.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p38/r5.anchor: فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "إن الشيطان يستحل الطعام إذا لم يذكر اسم الله عليه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p39/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p39/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p39/r1.claim: The Prophet says that naming God upon entering one's home and at meals prevents Satan from claiming lodging or supper; omitting either invocation allows him to claim it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p39/r1.anchor: عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "إذا دخل الرجل بيته، فذكر الله (8) عند دخوله وعند طعامه، قال الشيطان: لا مبيت لكم ولا عشاء، وإذا دخل فلم (9) يذكر اسم الله عند دخوله قال الشيطان: أدركتم (10) المبيت

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p39/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p39/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p39/r2.claim: When people say they eat without becoming full, the Prophet suggests they may eat separately and instructs them to gather and name God so their food will be blessed.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p39/r2.anchor: أن رجلا قال للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: إنا نأكل وما نشبع؟ قال: "فلعلكم (12) تأكلون متفرقين، اجتمعوا على طعامكم واذكروا اسم الله، يبارك لكم فيه ".

NAHHAS:v2p7/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p7/r4.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p7/r4.claim: In ماذا, ما is a nominative subject and أحل لهم is its predicate; ذا may be extra, or mean الذي with قل أحل لكم الطيبات as predicate.
NAHHAS:v2p7/r4.anchor: ( ما ) في موضع رفع بالابتداء والخبر ( أحل لهم ) ( وذا ) زائدة وإن شئت كان بمعنى الذي

NAHHAS:v2p7/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p7/r5.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p7/r5.claim: الطيبات means lawful things; anything forbidden is not wholesome.
NAHHAS:v2p7/r5.anchor: وهو الحلال وكل حرام فليس بطيب

NAHHAS:v2p7/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p7/r6.speaker: قيل
NAHHAS:v2p7/r6.claim: An alternative defines wholesome food as what its eater or drinker enjoys without harm in this life or the next.
NAHHAS:v2p7/r6.anchor: وقيل الطيب ما التذه آكله وشاربه ولم يكن عليه منه ضرر في الدنيا ولا في الآخرة

NAHHAS:v2p7/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p7/r7.speaker: الأخفش
NAHHAS:v2p7/r7.claim: Al-Akhfash gives جارحة as the singular of الجوارح.

NAHHAS:v2p7/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p7/r8.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p7/r8.claim: مكلبين is accusative as a circumstantial phrase.

NAHHAS:v2p7/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p7/r9.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p7/r9.claim: The underlying form of أمسكن عليكم is أمسكنه; the pronoun هاء is omitted because the intervening noun phrase is long.
NAHHAS:v2p7/r9.anchor: الأصل أمسكنه وحذفت الهاء لطول الاسم

NAHHAS:v2p7/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p7/r10.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p7/r10.claim: This verse together with the preceding one indicates that a catch is not eaten if the trained hunting animal has eaten from it.
NAHHAS:v2p7/r10.anchor: وفي هذا وفيما قبله دليل على أنه إن أكل الجارحة لم يؤكل منه

NAHHAS:v2p7/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p7/r11.speaker: قيل
NAHHAS:v2p7/r11.claim: Some say remembering God's name is by the heart.

NAHHAS:v2p7/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p7/r12.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p7/r12.claim: Language makes the spoken tongue the literal sense of remembering God's name and remembrance by the heart metaphorical.
NAHHAS:v2p7/r12.anchor: والذي توجبه اللغة أن يكون باللسان حقيقة وبالقلب مجازا

JISHUMI:v3p1873/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p1873/r1.speaker: ابن مسعود والحسن
JISHUMI:v3p1873/r1.claim: The common reading has mُkallibīn with a doubled lām; Ibn Masʿūd and al-Ḥasan read it without doubling, which may mean the same thing or refer to someone with many dogs.
JISHUMI:v3p1873/r1.anchor: قراءة العامة مكلبين بالتشديد، وعن ابن مسعود والحسن مكلبين بالتخفيف

JISHUMI:v3p1873/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p1873/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v3p1873/r2.claim: Ṭayyib means the opposite of foul, lawful and wholesome, or pleasant; ḥalāl, ṭayyib, ṭalq, and mubāḥ are near-synonyms, though mubāḥ implies an authorizer.
JISHUMI:v3p1873/r2.anchor: الطيب: ضد الخبيث، والطيب: الحلال الطيب، والطيب: المستلذ

JISHUMI:v3p1873/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p1873/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v3p1873/r3.claim: Jawāriḥ are hunting earners among predatory birds and other animals; the singular is jāriḥ.
JISHUMI:v3p1873/r3.anchor: الجوارح: الكواسب للصيد من سباع الطير وغيرها واحدها جارح

JISHUMI:v3p1873/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p1873/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v3p1873/r4.claim: The word for limbs is related to earning because limbs are used to acquire misdeeds; ijti rāḥ means work or acquisition, linked to 45:21.
JISHUMI:v3p1873/r4.anchor: ومنه الجارحة لأنه يكسب بها اجتراح السيئات، ومنه: (أم حسب الذين اجترحوا السيئات)

JISHUMI:v3p1873/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p1873/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v3p1873/r5.claim: A mukallib is one who trains dogs for hunting, analogous to a teacher or educator.
JISHUMI:v3p1873/r5.anchor: والكلاب والمكلب الذي يعلم الكلاب الصيد فمكلب صاحب الكلاب كمعلم صاحب التعليم

JISHUMI:v3p1873/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p1873/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v3p1873/r6.claim: A rabid dog has a madness-like disease; a bitten human can also be called kalb, and kalab describes hardship by comparison with the dog's severity.
JISHUMI:v3p1873/r6.anchor: والكلب الكلب هو الذي يأخذه شبه الجنون فيكلب لحوم الناس، فإذا عقر إنسانا قيل: إنسان كلب

JISHUMI:v3p1873/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p1873/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v3p1873/r7.claim: One parsing makes mā the subject and dhā its predicate, meaning “what is the thing that was made lawful for them?”
JISHUMI:v3p1873/r7.anchor: الأول: موضعه رفع بالابتداء، وخبره (ذا)، وتقديره: أي شيء الذي أحل لهم؟

JISHUMI:v3p1873/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p1873/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v3p1873/r8.claim: Another parsing treats mādhā as one nominative noun, with uḥilla as its predicate: “what was made lawful for you?”
JISHUMI:v3p1873/r8.anchor: الثاني: (ماذا) اسم واحد ومحله رفع و(أحل) خبره تقديره: أي شيء أحل لكم

JISHUMI:v3p1873/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p1873/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v3p1873/r9.claim: Mukallibīn is an accusative circumstantial phrase: the addressees are in the state of becoming owners of trained dogs.
JISHUMI:v3p1873/r9.anchor: مكلبين: نصب على الحال تقديره: وما علمتم من الجوارح في حال مصيركم أصحاب كلاب

JISHUMI:v3p1873/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p1873/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v3p1873/r10.claim: Al-ṭayyibāt is nominative as the passive verb's subject; with the active reading aḥalla, it would be accusative as the object.
JISHUMI:v3p1873/r10.anchor: أحل لكم الطيبات رفع (الطيبات)؛ لأنه اسم ما لم يسم فاعله

JISHUMI:v3p1873/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p1873/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v3p1873/r11.claim: Min in mimma amsakna is partitive because only some of the prey is lawful, not its entrails and blood.
JISHUMI:v3p1873/r11.anchor: و (من) في قوله: مما أمسكن عليكم للتبعيض لأنه أحل بعضا، ولم يحل الفرث والدم

JISHUMI:v3p1873/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p1873/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v3p1873/r12.claim: Another grammatical view takes min as an emphatic extra particle, with a parallel phrase at 39:7.
JISHUMI:v3p1873/r12.anchor: وقيل: زائدة للتوكيد (يغفر لكم من ذنوبكم)

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p640/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p640/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p640/r1.claim: The indirect question means ‘they say to you, what has been made lawful for them’; the shift to third person follows the wording ‘they ask you,’ though first person would also be correct.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p640/r1.anchor: في السؤال معنى القول فلذلك وقع بعده ﴿ ماذا أحل لهم ﴾ كأنه قيل يقولون لك ماذا احل لهم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p640/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p640/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p640/r2.claim: ‘What’ is the subject and ‘has been made lawful for them’ its predicate; the question concerns foods after prohibited foods were recited to them.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p640/r2.anchor: و ( ماذا ) مبتدأ وأحل لهم ) خبره كقولك أي شيء احل لهم ومعناه ماذا احل لهم من المطاعم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p640/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p640/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p640/r3.claim: ‘Good things’ means what is not foul: anything not prohibited by scripture, the Sunna, or a jurist’s analogy.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p640/r3.anchor: أي ما ليس بخبيث منها وهو كل ما لم يات تحريمه في كتاب أو سنة أو قياس مجتهد

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p640/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p640/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p640/r4.claim: The trained hunting animals may coordinate with ‘good things’ with an omitted word, meaning lawful food and game caught by your trained animals; alternatively, ‘what’ is conditional and ‘eat’ is its answer.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p640/r4.anchor: عطف على الطيبات أي أحل لكم الطيبات وصيد ما علمتم فحذف المضاف أو تجعل ( ما ) شرطية وجوابها ( فكلوا )

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p640/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p640/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p640/r5.claim: Jawāriḥ are hunting predators among beasts and birds, including dogs, leopards, tigers, eagles, falcons, and hawks.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p640/r5.anchor: والجوارح الكواسب من سباع البهائم والطير كالكلب والفهد والنمر والعقاب والصقر والبازي والشاهين

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p640/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p640/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p640/r6.claim: Mukallib is the person who trains and disciplines hunting animals for their owner; the word derives from dogs because dogs are the most common, or because predators are called dogs.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p640/r6.anchor: والمكلب مؤدب الجوارح ومضربها بالصيد لصاحبها ورائضها لذلك بما علم من الحيل

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p640/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p640/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p640/r7.claim: The term can also derive from a predator being called a dog, or from keliba, ‘to be keenly attached’ to something.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p640/r7.anchor: أو لأن السبع يسمى كلبا ومنه قوله عليه السلام

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p640/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p640/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p640/r8.claim: To show that a predator is called a dog, the author cites a Prophetic supplication for God to set one of His dogs on a man; the animal was a lion.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p640/r8.anchor: اللهم سلط عليه كلبا من كلابك ) + + فأكله الأسد

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p640/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p640/r9.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p640/r9.claim: The word can also mean keenly attached to something, as in describing someone as ‘a dog’ for it.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p640/r9.anchor: أو من الكلب الذي هو بمعنى الضراوة يقال هو كلب بكذا اذا كان ضاريا به

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p640#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p640#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p640#2/r1.claim: ‘Trainers’ is a circumstantial accusative modifying ‘you have trained’; it indicates a highly skilled expert in training hunting animals.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p640#2/r1.anchor: فائدتها ان يكون من يعلم الجوارح نحريرا في علمه مدربا فيه موصوفا بالتكليب

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p640#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p640#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p640#2/r2.claim: ‘Teaching them’ is either a second circumstantial clause or a new sentence; the verse teaches that learners should seek knowledge from the most expert and discerning teachers, even over long journeys.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p640#2/r2.anchor: و ﴿ تعلمونهن ﴾ حال ثانية أو استئناف وفيه فائدة جليلة وهي ان على كل آخذ علما ان لا يأخذه الا من أقتل اهله علما

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p640#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p640#2/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p640#2/r3.claim: What God taught means the knowledge of training, divinely inspired yet acquired through reason; alternatively it is what God showed people about sending, recalling, stopping, and retaining the catch for its owner.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p640#2/r3.anchor: ﴿ مما علمكم الله ﴾ من علم التكليب لأنه الهام من الله ومكتسب بالعقل أو مما عرفكم ان تعلموه من اتباع الصيد

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p640#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p640#2/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p640#2/r4.claim: A variant reads mukallibīn with a lighter form; afʿala and faʿʿala often share a meaning.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p640#2/r4.anchor: وقرىء ( مكلبين ) بالتخفيف وأفعل وفعل يشتركان كثيرا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p640#2/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p640#2/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p640#2/r5.claim: In a sound report to ʿAdi ibn Hatim, the Prophet says not to eat the catch if the dog ate it, since it caught for itself.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p640#2/r5.anchor: لقوله عليه الصلاة والسلام لعدي بن حاتم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p640#2/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p640#2/r6.speaker: علي
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p640#2/r6.claim: Ali said not to eat the catch if a falcon ate from it.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p640#2/r6.anchor: وعن علي رضي الله عنه إذا اكل البازي فلا تاكل

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p640#2/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p640#2/r7.speaker: العلماء
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p640#2/r7.claim: Scholars differed: some require predatory beasts to refrain from eating because they can be trained by beating, but do not impose the condition on predatory birds.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p640#2/r7.anchor: وفرق العلماء فاشترطوا في سباع البهائم ترك الأكل لأنها تؤدب بالضرب ولم يشترطوه في سباع الطير

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p640#2/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p640#2/r8.speaker: بعض العلماء
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p640#2/r8.claim: Some scholars do not treat eating as relevant and do not distinguish an animal holding all of the prey from holding only part.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p640#2/r8.anchor: ومنهم من لم يعتبر ترك الأكل أصلا ولم يفرق بين إمساك الكل والبعض

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p640#2/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p640#2/r9.speaker: سلمان وسعد بن أبي وقاص وأبو هريرة
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p640#2/r9.claim: Salman, Saʿd ibn Abi Waqqas, and Abu Hurayra allowed eating when a dog consumed two-thirds, left one-third, and God’s name had been invoked.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p640#2/r9.anchor: وعن سلمان وسعد بن أبي وقاص وأبي هريرة رضي الله عنهم اذا اكل الكلب ثلثيه وبقي ثلثه وذكرت اسم الله عليه فكل

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p641/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p641/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p641/r1.claim: The pronoun in ‘mention God’s name over it’ can refer to the catch: invoke God when you find it alive and slaughter it.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p641/r1.anchor: قلت إما ان يرجع إلى ما أمسكن على معنى وسموا عليه إذا ادركتم ذكاته

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p641/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p641/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p641/r2.claim: Alternatively, the pronoun refers to the trained animal, so God’s name is invoked when it is sent out.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p641/r2.anchor: أو إلى ما علمتم من الجوارح أي سموا عليه عند إرساله

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p14/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p14/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p14/r1.claim: Al-tayyibat means lawful things; lawful things are called good even when not pleasurable, by analogy with what people enjoy.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p14/r1.anchor: يعني بالطيبات الحلال , وإنما سمي الحلال طيبا , وإن لم يكن مستلذا تشبيها بما يستلذ .

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p14/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p14/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p14/r2.claim: Jawarih are hunting animals, beasts or birds, that earn prey for their owners; the word derives from earning, as in the cited line by al-A'sha of Banu Tha'laba, where ajtaraḥ means “acquired.”
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p14/r2.anchor: سميت جوارح لكسب أهلها بها من قولهم : فلان جارحة أهله أي كاسبهم

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p14/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p14/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p14/r3.claim: Al-A'sha of Banu Tha'laba's cited word ajtaraḥ is evidence for the sense “acquired.”
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p14/r3.anchor: ذا جبار منضجا ميسمه … يذكر الجارح ما كان اجترح … أي ما اكتسب

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p14/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p14/r4.speaker: ابن عمر
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p14/r4.claim: Ibn Umar, al-Dahhak, and al-Suddi restrict mukallibin to dogs, making only dog-caught game lawful.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p14/r4.anchor: يعني من الكلاب دون غيرها , وأنه لا يحل إلا صيد الكلاب وحدها , وهذا قول ابن عمر

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p14/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p14/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p14/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas, Ali ibn al-Husayn, al-Hasan, and Mujahid say taklib describes trained hunting predators, including non-dogs, made eager for the hunt like dogs.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p14/r5.anchor: أن التكليب من صفات الجوارح من كلب وغيره , ومعناه مضرين على الصيد كما تضري الكلاب , وهو قول ابن عباس

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p14/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p14/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p14/r6.claim: A third view treats taklib as an attribute of the predator meaning that it has been trained.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p14/r6.anchor: أن معنى التكليب من صفات الجارح : التعليم .

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p14/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p14/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p14/r7.claim: Training means teaching predators to seek game for people through the discipline and training methods God has taught.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p14/r7.anchor: أى تعلمونهن من طلب الصيد لكم مما علمكم الله من التأديب الذي أدبكم وصفات التعليم

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p14/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p14/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p14/r8.claim: A trained predator is released when sent, responds when called, and holds its prey when it catches it.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p14/r8.anchor: فهو أن يشلى إذا أشلي , ويجيب إذا دعي ويمسك إذا أخذ .

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p14/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p14/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p14/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas and Ata say refraining from eating the catch is required for every hunting animal; if it eats, the catch is not lawful.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p14/r9.anchor: أنه شرط في كل الجوارح , فإن أكلت لم تؤكل , وهذا قول ابن عباس , وعطاء .

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p14/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p14/r10.speaker: ابن عمر
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p14/r10.claim: Ibn Umar, Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, Abu Hurayra, and Salman say refraining from eating is not required for any hunting animal, and its catch remains lawful if eaten.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p14/r10.anchor: أنه ليس بشرط فى كل الجوارح ويؤكل وإن أكلت , وهذا قول ابن عمر

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p14/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p14/r11.speaker: الشعبي
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p14/r11.claim: Al-Sha'bi, al-Nakha'i, and al-Suddi require non-eating for mammalian predators but not birds, so a bird's catch is lawful even if the bird eats.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p14/r11.anchor: أنه شرط في جوارح البهائم فلا يؤكل ما أكلت , وليس بشرط في جوارح الطير , فيؤكل وإن أكلت

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p14/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p14/r12.speaker: أبو رافع
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p14/r12.claim: Abu Rafi' reports that Gabriel refused to enter a house with a dog; after the Prophet ordered dogs killed, a woman kept one barking by her, and Abu Rafi' killed it on the Prophet's renewed order. People then asked what was lawful to them from the kind of animal they had been ordered to kill, and the verse was revealed.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p14/r12.anchor: عن أبي رافع قال : جاء جبريل

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p14/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p14/r13.speaker: زيد الخير
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p14/r13.claim: A second account says Zayd al-Khayl, renamed Zayd al-Khayr by the Prophet, asked about Dureih and Abu Dujana, whose five dogs hunted gazelles; the verse was revealed in response.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p14/r13.anchor: ما حكي أن زيد الخيل لما وفد على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال فيه من الخير ما قال فسماه زيد الخير

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p14/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p14/r14.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p14/r14.claim: Ibn Abbas, as related by Hisham, names the five dogs al-Mukhtalis, Ghallab, al-Ghanim, Sahlib, and al-Muta'ati.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p14/r14.anchor: وحكى هشام عن ابن عباس أن أسماء هذه الكلاب الخمسة التي لدريح وأبي دجانة : المختلس وغلاب والغنيم وسهلب والمتعاطي

MUJAHID:v1p185#2/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p185#2/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p185#2/r1.claim: The trained hunting animals called jawāriḥ include birds and dogs.
MUJAHID:v1p185#2/r1.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد قال ﴿ الجوارح ﴾ الطير والكلاب

MUQATIL:5:4-5/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:5:4-5/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:5:4-5/r1.claim: Zayd al-Khayr and ʿAdi ibn Hatim asked what hunting dogs make lawful.
MUQATIL:5:4-5/r1.anchor: وذلك أن زيد الخير، وهو من بنى المهلهل، وعدى بن حاتم الطائيان، سألا النبى صلى الله عليه وسلم

MUQATIL:5:4-5/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:5:4-5/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:5:4-5/r2.claim: Their question concerned dogs that caught gazelles, cattle, and wild donkeys, some of which were found alive but died before being slaughtered; they asked because carrion is forbidden.
MUQATIL:5:4-5/r2.anchor: كلاب آل درع وآل حورية يصدن الظباء والبقر والحمر، فمنها ما تدرك ذكاته فيموت، وقد حرم الله عز وجل الميتة

MUQATIL:5:4-5/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:5:4-5/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:5:4-5/r3.claim: The pure things mean lawful food, including hunted game that can be ritually slaughtered before it dies.
MUQATIL:5:4-5/r3.anchor: يعنى الحلال، وذبح ما أحل الله لهم من الصيد مما أدركت ذكاته

MUQATIL:5:4-5/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:5:4-5/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:5:4-5/r4.claim: The trained hunting animals are dogs; training means disciplining them as God taught, so they learn good and evil.
MUQATIL:5:4-5/r4.anchor: يعنى الكلاب معلمين للصيد، { تعلمونهن مما علمكم الله } ، يقول: تؤدبوهن كما أدبكم الله، فيعرفون الخير والشر

MUQATIL:5:4-5/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:5:4-5/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:5:4-5/r5.claim: They may eat the prey that trained dogs hold for them.
MUQATIL:5:4-5/r5.anchor: يقول: فكلوا مما أمسكن، يعنى حبس عليكم الكلاب المعلمة

MUQATIL:5:4-5/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:5:4-5/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:5:4-5/r6.claim: They should mention God's name over the prey when releasing the dog after it has held the prey for them.
MUQATIL:5:4-5/r6.anchor: واذكروا اسم الله عليه } إذا أرسلتم بعد أن أمسك عليكم

MUQATIL:5:4-5/r7.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:5:4-5/r7.speaker: author
MUQATIL:5:4-5/r7.claim: They must not eat game that died as carrion, except game killed by a trained dog.
MUQATIL:5:4-5/r7.anchor: فلا تستحلوا أكل الصيد من الميتة، إلا ما ذكى من صيد الكلب المعلم

MUQATIL:5:4-5/r8.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:5:4-5/r8.speaker: author
MUQATIL:5:4-5/r8.claim: God's account is swift for anyone who deems dead game lawful, except in necessity.
MUQATIL:5:4-5/r8.anchor: إن الله سريع الحساب } [آية: 4] لمن يستحل أكل الميتة من الصيد إلا من اضطر

NASAFI-FULL:v1p269#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p269#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p269#2/r1.claim: Although the question is phrased as asking, it has the sense of reported speech; asking what is lawful for them matches the third-person wording, while asking what is lawful for us would also be correct.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p269#2/r1.anchor: ﴿ يسألونك ﴾ فى السؤال معنى القول فلذا وقع بعده

NASAFI-FULL:v1p269#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p269#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p269#2/r2.claim: Mādhā is the subject and aḥalla is its predicate; the question concerns permitted foods after they heard the prohibited impure foods recited.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p269#2/r2.anchor: وماذا متبدا وأحل لهم خبره كقولك أى شيء احل لهم

NASAFI-FULL:v1p269#2/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p269#2/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p269#2/r3.claim: The wholesome things mean either everything not impure or anything not prohibited by scripture, Sunna, consensus, or analogy.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p269#2/r3.anchor: ﴿ قل أحل لكم الطيبات ﴾ أى ماليس بخبيث منها

NASAFI-FULL:v1p269#2/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p269#2/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p269#2/r4.claim: What you have trained may coordinate with wholesome foods, with the implied phrase prey of trained animals; alternatively, mā is conditional and eat is its answer.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p269#2/r4.anchor: ﴿ وما علمتم ﴾ عطف على الطيبات أى احل لكم الطيبات

NASAFI-FULL:v1p269#2/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p269#2/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p269#2/r5.claim: Jawāriḥ are hunting beasts and birds such as dogs, cheetahs, eagles, falcons, and hawks; another derivation from wounding requires the prey to be wounded to be lawful.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p269#2/r5.anchor: ﴿ من الجوارح ﴾ أى الكواسب للصيد من سباع البهائم والطير

NASAFI-FULL:v1p269#2/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p269#2/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p269#2/r6.claim: The circumstantial phrase mukallibīn is not redundant with you have trained: it specifies that people training the animals are themselves skilled trainers, a word derived from dogs because dogs are most often trained or because predators are called dogs.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p269#2/r6.anchor: ﴿ مكلبين ﴾ حال من علمتم وفائدة هذه الحال مع أنه استغنى عنها بعلمتم

NASAFI-FULL:v1p269#2/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p269#2/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p269#2/r7.claim: A Prophetic report asks God to set one of His dogs on a man, whom a lion then ate; this supports using dog for a predator.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p269#2/r7.anchor: ومنه الحديث اللهم سلط عليه كلبا من كلابك فأكله الأسد

NASAFI-FULL:v1p269#2/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p269#2/r8.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p269#2/r8.claim: Learning them may be a circumstantial clause or a new sentence; either way it implies taking knowledge from the most expert teacher, not an unskilled one, lest one waste time and regret it before experts.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p269#2/r8.anchor: ﴿ تعلمونهن ﴾ حال أو استئناف ولا موضع له وفيه دليل على أن كل آخذ علما

NASAFI-FULL:v1p269#2/r9.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p269#2/r9.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p269#2/r9.claim: The training is from what God taught people.

NASAFI-FULL:v1p269#2/r10.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p269#2/r10.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p269#2/r10.claim: Eat only what the hunting animal catches for its owner; a dog-like animal's eating from the prey makes it unlawful, while a falcon-like bird's eating does not.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p269#2/r10.anchor: ﴿ فكلوا مما أمسكن عليكم ﴾ الامساك على صاحبه أن لا يأكل منه

NASAFI-FULL:v1p269#2/r11.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p269#2/r11.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p269#2/r11.claim: The pronoun in invoking God's name can refer to the prey, with the invocation at slaughter if found alive, or to the trained animal, with the invocation when it is released.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p269#2/r11.anchor: ﴿ واذكروا اسم الله عليه ﴾ يرجع إلى ما أمسكن على معنى وسموا عليه

NASAFI-FULL:v1p269#2/r12.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p269#2/r12.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p269#2/r12.claim: The warning to fear God means avoid disobeying His command throughout these matters; He accounts for people's actions swiftly, without delay.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p269#2/r12.anchor: ﴿ واتقوا الله ﴾ واحذروا مخالفة أمره فى هذا كله

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4/r1.speaker: عدي بن حاتم
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4/r1.claim: The occasion of revelation is a question from ʿAdi b. Hatim and Zayd b. Muhalhil, whom the Prophet renamed Zayd al-Khayr, about hunting with dogs and falcons when some prey died before they could slaughter it.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4/r1.anchor: نزلت بسبب عدي بن حاتم وزيد بن مهلهل وهو زيد الخيل الذي سماه رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم زيد الخير

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4/r2.claim: In “what has been made lawful to them,” “ma” may be the subject with “has been made lawful to them” as predicate, and “dha” is extra; alternatively “ma-dha” is a relative pronoun with the answer as predicate.
