QURTUBI-FULL:5:4/r2.anchor: «ما» في موضع رفع بالابتداء، والخبر أحل لهم وذا زائدة وإن شئت كانت بمعنى الذي

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4/r3.claim: Tayyibat means lawful things, since anything forbidden is not wholesome; other glosses define them as harmless pleasant food and drink or properly slaughtered animals.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4/r3.anchor: وهو الحلال، وكل حرام فليس بطيب.

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4/r4.claim: “What you have trained” ellipses “the game of”: otherwise the wording would seem to permit eating the trained predators themselves, a view no one holds.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4/r4.anchor: أي وصيد ما علمتم ففي الكلام إضمار لا بد منه

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4/r5.claim: Some legal writers infer that the verse permits benefits from trained dogs and birds of prey, including selling them and using them in other ways, while excluding eating the predators themselves.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4/r5.anchor: وذلك يوجب إباحة سائر وجوه الانتفاع فدل على جواز بيع الكلب والجوارح

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4/r6.speaker: السهيلي
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4/r6.claim: ʿAdi reportedly had five named hunting dogs: Salhab, Ghallab, al-Mukhtalis, and al-Mutanaʿis; al-Suhayli is unsure whether the fifth was Akhtab or Waththab.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4/r6.anchor: وكان أسماء أكلبه سلهب وغلاب والمختلس والمتناعس قال السهيلي وخامس أشك

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4/r7.claim: The community agrees on the conditions for a trained nonblack dog: it responds to release and call, stops when rebuked after catching prey, does not eat the prey, wounds it, and is released by a Muslim invoking God’s name.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4/r7.anchor: أجمعت الأمة على أن الكلب إذا لم يكن أسود وعلمه مسلم فينشلي إذا أشلي ويجيب إذا دعي

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4/r8.claim: If a required hunting condition is missing, the ruling becomes disputed.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4/r8.anchor: فإن انخرم شرط من هذه الشروط دخل الخلاف.

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4/r9.speaker: جمهور الأمة
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4/r9.claim: Most scholars allow prey taken by any trained predator, such as a cheetah, falcon, or hawk; the word denotes an animal that earns or acquires.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4/r9.anchor: فجمهور الأمة على أن كل ما صاد بعد التعليم فهو جارح كاسب.

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4/r10.claim: The root “jaraḥa” means to acquire, as in the verse about what people earn by day and the verse about those who have earned sins.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4/r10.anchor: ومنه الجارحة لأنها يكتسب بها ومنه اجتراح السيئات

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#2/r1.claim: Al-Aʿsha’s verse uses “jaraha” to refer to what the hunter acquired, supporting the sense of jawāriḥ as earners.

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#2/r2.speaker: الرماني
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#2/r2.claim: “Mukallibin” can mean dog owners or trainers, as a teacher is the owner of training; it may also mean people who intensively train animals for hunting.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#2/r2.anchor: وقيل: معناه مضرين على الصيد كما تضرى الكلاب قال الرماني: وكلا القولين محتمل.

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#2/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#2/r3.claim: Al-Qurtubi says “mukallibin” does not restrict the lawful predators to dogs; exclusivists’ argument from the word is not decisive.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#2/r3.anchor: وليس في «مكلبين» دليل على أنه إنما أبيح صيد الكلاب خاصة

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#2/r4.speaker: ابن عمر
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#2/r4.claim: Ibn Umar says prey caught by falcons or other birds must be properly slaughtered if reached alive; otherwise it is not eaten.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#2/r4.anchor: روي عن ابن عمر فيما حكى ابن المنذر عنه قال: وأما ما يصاد به من البزاة وغيرها من الطير

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#2/r5.speaker: أبو جعفر
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#2/r5.claim: Abu Jaʿfar likewise says a falcon’s prey is not lawful unless the hunter can reach it alive for slaughter.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#2/r5.anchor: وسأل أبو جعفر عن البازي يحل صيده قال: لا إلا أن تدرك ذكاته.

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#2/r6.speaker: الضحاك
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#2/r6.claim: Al-Dahhak and al-Suddi take trained “jawāriḥ mukallibin” to mean dogs specifically.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#2/r6.anchor: وقال الضحاك والسدي: «وما علمتم من الجوارح مكلبين» هي الكلاب خاصة

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#2/r7.speaker: أحمد
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#2/r7.claim: Al-Hasan, Qatada, and al-Nakhaʿi disliked prey from an entirely black dog; Ahmad knew of no one who permitted it, and Ishaq shared that view.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#2/r7.anchor: فكره صيده الحسن وقتادة والنخعي. وقال أحمد: ما أعرف أحدا يرخص فيه إذا كان بهيما وبه قال إسحق بن راهويه

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#2/r8.speaker: عوام أهل العلم
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#2/r8.claim: Ordinary scholars of Medina and Kufa permit hunting with any trained dog.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#2/r8.anchor: فأما عوام أهل العلم بالمدينة والكوفة فيرون جواز صيد كل كلب معلم

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#2/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#2/r9.speaker: النبي
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#2/r9.claim: Those who bar black dogs cite the Prophetic report “the black dog is a devil,” transmitted by Muslim.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#2/r9.anchor: أما من منع صيد الكلب الأسود فلقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم:

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#2/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#2/r10.speaker: جمهور الأمة
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#2/r10.claim: The majority answer that the verse is general and that the occasion of revelation and a report from ʿAdi support falcon hunting; al-Tirmidhi’s report says to eat what the falcon holds, but its sole transmitter Mujalid is weak.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#2/r10.anchor: احتج الجمهور بعموم الآية، واحتجوا أيضا في جواز صيد البازي بما ذكر من سبب النزول

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#2/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#2/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#2/r11.claim: The same ruling is supported by analogy: what a dog can do, a cheetah can do, with no relevant difference; the comparison is likened to sword and dagger.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#2/r11.anchor: وبالمعنى وهو أن كل ما يتأتى من الكلب يتأتى من الفهد مثلا فلا فارق إلا فيما لا مدخل له في التأثير

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#3/r1.speaker: الليث
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#3/r1.claim: Al-Layth criticizes hunting as something that can seem like falsehood despite being treated as legitimate.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#3/r1.anchor: وهو ظاهر قول الليث: ما رأيت حقا أشبه بباطل منه، يعني الصيد

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#3/r2.speaker: النبي
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#3/r2.claim: The Prophetic instruction to release the dog and invoke God’s name entails intention and the basmala.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#3/r2.anchor: إذا أرسلت كلبك وذكرت اسم الله عليه فكل

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#3/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#3/r3.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#3/r3.claim: Malik disliked hunting when done partly for sport, Ibn Abd al-Hakam allowed it, and al-Layth voiced a maxim criticizing how hunting resembles falsehood.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#3/r3.anchor: فلو قصد مع ذلك اللهو فكرهه مالك وأجازه ابن عبد الحكم

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#3/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#3/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#3/r4.claim: Hunting without intending lawful slaughter is forbidden because it needlessly destroys an animal; the Prophet prohibited killing animals except for food.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#3/r4.anchor: فأما لو فعله بغير نية التذكية فهو حرام لأنه من باب الفساد وإتلاف حيوان لغير منفعة

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#3/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#3/r5.speaker: جمهور العلماء
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#3/r5.claim: Most scholars, the Zahiris, and some hadith scholars require verbal invocation of God at release; without it the prey is not eaten.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#3/r5.anchor: وقد ذهب الجمهور من العلماء إلى أن التسمية لا بد منها بالقول عند الإرسال

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#3/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#3/r6.speaker: جماعة من أصحابنا
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#3/r6.claim: Other scholars in the Maliki school and elsewhere allow eating the Muslim’s hunted or slaughtered animal even if the basmala was deliberately omitted, treating the command as recommendation.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#3/r6.anchor: وذهبت جماعة من أصحابنا وغيرهم إلى أنه يجوز أكل ما صاده المسلم وذبحه وإن ترك التسمية عمدا

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#3/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#3/r7.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#3/r7.claim: Malik’s well-known view distinguishes deliberate omission, which bars eating, from forgetfulness, which does not; this is also the position of the regional jurists and one Shafii opinion.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#3/r7.anchor: وذهب مالك في المشهور إلى الفرق بين ترك التسمية عمدا أو سهوا

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#3/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#3/r8.speaker: جمهور العلماء
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#3/r8.claim: The hunter must release or urge the predator; an animal that starts hunting on its own without release or encouragement is not lawful to eat according to the majority and named schools.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#3/r8.anchor: فأما لو انبعث الجارح من تلقاء نفسه من غير إرسال ولا إغراء فلا يجوز صيده

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#3/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#3/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#3/r9.claim: The reason is that a self-starting predator hunts and holds the prey for itself, so the hunt cannot be attributed to the hunter’s release.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#3/r9.anchor: لأنه إنما صاد لنفسه من غير إرسال وأمسك عليها، ولا صنع للصائد فيه

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#3/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#3/r10.speaker: عطاء
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#3/r10.claim: Ata and al-Awzai allow the prey if the hunter had taken the animal out for hunting.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#3/r10.anchor: وقال عطاء بن أبي رباح والأوزاعي: يؤكل صيده إذا كان أخرجه للصيد.

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#3/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#3/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#3/r11.claim: Most readers read “ʿallamtum” with fatḥa; Ibn Abbas and Muhammad b. al-Hanafiyya read “ʿullimtum” with a ḍamma on ʿayn and kasra on lām, meaning instruction about predators and hunting.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#3/r11.anchor: وابن عباس ومحمد بن الحنفية بضم العين وكسر اللام، أي من أمر الجوارح والصيد بها

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#3/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#3/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#3/r12.claim: Jawāriḥ means earners; the view that it means animals that wound and bleed is weak and contrary to the linguists, though Ibn al-Mundhir attributes it to some.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#3/r12.anchor: وقيل: سميت جوارح لأنها تجرح وتسيل الدم، فهو مأخوذ من الجراح وهذا ضعيف

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#3/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#3/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#3/r13.claim: Most readers say “mukallibin” with an open kāf and doubled lām, for dog trainers; the term can also describe trainers of other animals, hunters, or dog owners.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#3/r13.anchor: و «مكلبين» قراءة الجمهور بفتح الكاف وشد اللام، والمكلب معلم الكلاب ومضريها.

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#3/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#3/r14.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#3/r14.claim: Al-Hasan reads “muklibin” with a quiescent kāf and light lām, meaning owners of dogs; “aklaba” means that a person’s dogs increased.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#3/r14.anchor: وقرأ الحسن «مكلبين» بسكون الكاف وتخفيف اللام، ومعناه أصحاب كلاب

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#3/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#3/r15.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#3/r15.claim: The verb aklaba means a persons dogs multiplied, illustrating the reading as dog owners.

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#4/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#4/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#4/r1.claim: The feminine pronoun in “you teach them” agrees with jawāriḥ, a feminine plural noun.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#4/r1.anchor: أنث الضمير مراعاة للفظ الجوارح إذ هو جمع جارحة

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#4/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#4/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#4/r2.claim: Scholars agree that trained dogs and analogous land predators must obey when commanded and stop when rebuked.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#4/r2.anchor: ولا خلاف بين العلماء في شرطين في التعليم وهما: أن يأتمر إذا أمر وينزجر إذا زجر

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#4/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#4/r3.speaker: ابن حبيب
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#4/r3.claim: Most scholars require the same obedience from trained birds, but Ibn Habib says birds need only obey a command because they rarely stop when rebuked.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#4/r3.anchor: وذكر ابن حبيب أنه لا يشترط فيها أن تنزجر إذا زجرت فإنه لا يتأتى ذلك فيها غالبا

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#4/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#4/r4.speaker: ربيعة
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#4/r4.claim: Rabiʿa considers a bird trained if it answers when called, since most animals naturally respond to being released.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#4/r4.anchor: وقال ربيعة: ما أجاب منها إذا دعي فهو المعلم الضاري

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#4/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#4/r5.speaker: الشافعي
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#4/r5.claim: Al-Shafii and most scholars require the animal to hold prey for its owner; Malik’s well-known view does not require this.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#4/r5.anchor: وقد شرط الشافعي وجمهور من العلماء في التعليم أن يمسك على صاحبه، ولم يشترطه مالك في المشهور عنه.

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#4/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#4/r6.speaker: الشافعي
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#4/r6.claim: Al-Shafii defines a trained animal as one that responds to release, returns when called, holds prey for its owner without eating it, and has done so repeatedly enough to be considered trained by custom.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#4/r6.anchor: وقال الشافعي: المعلم هو الذي إذا أشلاه صاحبه انشلى وإذا دعاه إلى الرجوع رجع إليه

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#4/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#4/r7.speaker: الشافعي
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#4/r7.claim: Al-Shafii and the Kufans say an animal that repeatedly obeys and holds prey becomes trained on its third performance; others say after three performances it is trained and prey is lawful on the fourth, while another view counts one performance and permits the second catch.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#4/r7.anchor: وعن الشافعي أيضا والكوفيين: إذا أشلي فانشلى وإذا أخذ حبس وفعل ذلك مرة بعد مرة أكل صيده في الثالثة.

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#4/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#4/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#4/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas, Abu Hurayra, al-Nakhaʿi, Qatada, Ibn Jubayr, Ata, Ikrima, al-Shafii, Ahmad, Ishaq, Abu Thawr, al-Nuʿman, and his companions say prey is lawful only if the predator did not eat any of it.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#4/r8.anchor: فقال ابن عباس وأبو هريرة والنخعي وقتادة وابن جبير وعطاء بن أبي رباح وعكرمة والشافعي وأحمد وإسحاق وأبو ثور

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#4/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#4/r9.speaker: النعمان
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#4/r9.claim: This first view says an animal that eats has held the prey for itself rather than its owner; Abu Hanifa applies the no-eating condition to dogs and cheetahs, but not birds.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#4/r9.anchor: لأنه أمسك على نفسه ولم يمسك على ربه. والفهد عند أبي حنيفة وأصحابه كالكلب ولم يشترطوا ذلك في الطيور

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#4/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#4/r10.speaker: سعد بن أبي وقاص
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#4/r10.claim: Saʿd b. Abi Waqqas, Ibn Umar, Salman, and Abu Hurayra also hold that prey remains lawful even if the predator ate some, including when only a piece remains.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#4/r10.anchor: وقال سعد بن أبي وقاص وعبد الله بن عمر وسلمان الفارسي وأبو هريرة أيضا: المعنى وإن أكل

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#4/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#4/r11.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#4/r11.claim: Malik and his school, along with one Shafii opinion, accept the second view; al-Qurtubi calls it analogical.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#4/r11.anchor: وهذا قول مالك وجميع أصحابه، وهو القول الثاني للشافعي، وهو القياس.

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#5/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#5/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#5/r1.claim: He cites Muslim’s report forbidding the prey if the dog has eaten from it, setting up the contrary report below.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#5/r1.anchor: إذا أكل فلا تأكل فإنما أمسك على نفسه

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#5/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#5/r2.speaker: أبو ثعلبة الخشني
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#5/r2.claim: The Prophet permits game caught by a dog released in God’s name, even if the dog ate some, and what the hunter’s hand brings back; the report is in Abu Dawud.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#5/r2.anchor: أبي ثعلبة الخشني قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في صيد الكلب: «إذا أرسلت كلبك وذكرت اسم الله عليه فكل وإن أكل منه

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#5/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#5/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#5/r3.claim: A version attributed to ʿAdi is unsound; the sound report from him is the Muslim narration.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#5/r3.anchor: أخرجه أبو داود وروي عن عدي ولا يصح والصحيح عنه حديث مسلم

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#5/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#5/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#5/r4.claim: He prefers reconciling the reports: treat the prohibition as scrupulous caution and the permission as legal allowance; the Prophet advised ʿAdi, who had means, to abstain and needy Abu Thaʿlaba that he could eat.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#5/r4.anchor: قالوا: إن عديا كان موسعا عليه فأفتاه النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بالكف ورعا، وأبا ثعلبة كان محتاجا فأفتاه بالجواز والله أعلم.

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#5/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#5/r5.speaker: أبو عمر
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#5/r5.claim: Abu ʿUmar holds that Abu Thaʿlaba’s report abrogates ʿAdi’s, since the Prophet answered that the hunter could eat even when the dog ate.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#5/r5.anchor: وقال أبو عمر في كتاب «الاستذكار»: وقد عارض حديث عدي هذا حديث أبي ثعلبة، والظاهر أن حديث أبي ثعلبة ناسخ له

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#5/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#5/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#5/r6.claim: He questions abrogation because the chronology is unknown and prefers reconciling both reports unless their dates are known.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#5/r6.anchor: قلت: هذا فيه نظر لأن التاريخ مجهول والجمع بين الحديثين أولى ما لم يعلم التاريخ والله أعلم.

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#5/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#5/r7.speaker: أصحاب الشافعي
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#5/r7.claim: They allow eating when the dog ate from extreme hunger; otherwise they disallow it as evidence of deficient training.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#5/r7.anchor: وأما أصحاب الشافعي فقالوا: إن كان الأكل عن فرط جوع من الكلب أكل وإلا لم يؤكل فإن ذلك من سوء تعليمه.

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#5/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#5/r8.speaker: النخعي والثوري وأصحاب الرأي وحماد بن أبي سليمان وابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#5/r8.claim: Some early authorities distinguish dogs and cheetahs, whose eating from prey bars it, from falcons, whose eating does not bar it.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#5/r8.anchor: وقد روي عن قوم من السلف التفرقة بين ما أكل منه الكلب والفهد فمنعوه، وبين ما أكل منه البازي فأجازوه قاله النخعي والثوري وأصحاب الرأي وحماد بن أبي سليمان، وحكى عن ابن عباس

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#5/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#5/r9.speaker: النخعي والثوري وأصحاب الرأي وحماد بن أبي سليمان وابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#5/r9.claim: Their rationale is that dogs and cheetahs can be struck and rebuked, whereas birds cannot; training a bird is limited to answering a call and coming when urged, since beating harms it.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#5/r9.anchor: وقالوا: الكلب والفهد يمكن ضربه وزجره، والطير لا يمكن ذلك فيه، وحد تعليمه أن يدعى فيجيب، وأن يشلى فينشلي لا يمكن فيه أكثر من ذلك، والضرب يؤذيه.

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#5/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#5/r10.speaker: الجمهور من العلماء
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#5/r10.claim: Most scholars hold that prey remains edible when the hunting animal drank its blood.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#5/r10.anchor: والجمهور من العلماء على أن الجارح إذا شرب من دم الصيد أن الصيد يؤكل

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#5/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#5/r11.speaker: عطاء
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#5/r11.claim: ʿAta says that drinking blood does not count as eating from the prey.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#5/r11.anchor: قال عطاء: ليس شرب الدم بأكل

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#5/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#5/r12.speaker: الشعبي وسفيان الثوري
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#5/r12.claim: Al-Shaʿbi and Sufyan al-Thawri disliked eating prey from which the animal drank blood.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#5/r12.anchor: وكره أكل ذلك الصيد الشعبي وسفيان الثوري

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#5/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#5/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#5/r13.claim: There is no disagreement that the injury causing permissibility must be established with certainty; doubt bars eating.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#5/r13.anchor: ولا خلاف بينهم أن سبب إباحة الصيد الذي هو عقر الجارح له لا بد أن يكون متحققا غير مشكوك فيه، ومع الشك لا يجوز الأكل

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#5/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#5/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#5/r14.claim: If another dog is found with the hunter’s dog, it is presumed to have joined on its own rather than being released by another hunter; scholars do not differ on this presumption.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#5/r14.anchor: فإن وجد الصائد مع كلبه كلبا آخر فهو محمول على أنه غير مرسل من صائد آخر، وأنه إنما انبعث في طلب الصيد بطبعه ونفسه، ولا يختلف في هذا

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#6/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#6/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#6/r1.claim: Do not eat prey mixed with dogs other than the one named over, because the hunter named only his own dog.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#6/r1.anchor: وإن خالطها كلاب من غيرها فلا تأكل

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#6/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#6/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#6/r2.claim: If another hunter released a dog that jointly caught the prey, the two hunters share it.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#6/r2.anchor: فأما لو أرسله صائد آخر فاشترك الكلبان فيه فإنه للصائدين يكونان شريكين فيه.

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#6/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#6/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#6/r3.claim: If one dog inflicted the mortal wound before the other arrived, the prey belongs to that dog’s hunter.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#6/r3.anchor: فلو أنفذ أحد الكلبين مقاتله ثم جاء الآخر فهو للذي أنفذ مقاتله

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#6/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#6/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#6/r4.claim: Do not eat a shot animal found drowned, since it is uncertain whether the water or the arrow killed it; the cited report allows eating after a day only when the arrow’s mark alone is found.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#6/r4.anchor: وإن رميت بسهمك فاذكر اسم الله فإن غاب عنك يوما فلم تجد فيه إلا أثر سهمك فكل وإن وجدته غريقا في الماء فلا تأكل فإنك لا تدري الماء قتله أو سهمك

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#6/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#6/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#6/r5.claim: If prey dies in the dogs’ mouths without being wounded, it is not edible because it was strangled, like an animal killed by a blunt knife before its throat was cut.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#6/r5.anchor: لو مات الصيد في أفواه الكلاب من غير بضع لم يؤكل لأنه مات خنقا فأشبه أن يذبح بسكين كالة فيموت في الذبح قبل أن يفرى حلقه.

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#6/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#6/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#6/r6.claim: If the hunter could seize and slaughter the prey but lets it die, it is not edible; once accessible, he was negligent in performing the required slaughter.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#6/r6.anchor: ولو أمكنه أخذه من الجوارح وذبحه فلم يفعل حتى مات لم يؤكل، وكان مقصرا في الذكاة لأنه قد صار مقدورا على ذبحه

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#6/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#6/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#6/r7.claim: If he catches it and it dies while he reaches for a knife already with him, it is edible; if he must leave to fetch a knife, it is not.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#6/r7.anchor: ولو أخذه ثم مات قبل أن يخرج السكين، أو تناولها وهي معه جاز أكله ولو لم تكن السكين معه فتشاغل بطلبها لم تؤكل.

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#6/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#6/r8.speaker: الشافعي وابن القاسم
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#6/r8.claim: One Shafiʿi position requires a wound before prey caught by a hunting animal is edible, citing the verse’s phrase “trained hunters.”
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#6/r8.anchor: وقال الشافعي: فيما نالته الجوارح ولم تدمه قولان أحدهما ألا يؤكل حتى يجرح لقوله تعالى: { من الجوارح } وهو قول ابن القاسم

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#6/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#6/r9.speaker: أشهب
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#6/r9.claim: Ashhab’s other Shafiʿi-cited position allows prey that died from the dog’s impact, even without a wound.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#6/r9.anchor: والآخر أنه حل وهو قول أشهب، قال أشهب: إن مات من صدمة الكلب أكل.

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#6/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#6/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#6/r10.claim: A report permits eating an animal found after being absent for a day with only the arrow mark.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#6/r10.anchor: فإن غاب عنك يوما فلم تجد فيه إلا أثر سهمك فكل

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#6/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#6/r11.speaker: أبو ثعلبة
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#6/r11.claim: Abu Thaʿlaba’s Abu Dawud version adds that the prey may be eaten after three days unless it has begun to stink.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#6/r11.anchor:
ونحوه في حديث أبي ثعلبة الذي خرجه أبو داود، غير أنه زاد
" فكله بعد ثلاث ما لم ينتن "

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#6/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#6/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#6/r12.claim: That report conflicts with the instruction to eat what was killed in view and leave what died unseen.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#6/r12.anchor: كل ما أصميت ودع ما أنميت

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#6/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#6/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#6/r13.claim: Ismaʿ is killing quickly while the hunter sees it; inmaʿ is when the shot animal disappears and dies unseen, with the verb describing a shot that vanishes and then dies.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#6/r13.anchor: فالإصماء ما قتل مسرعا وأنت تراه، والإنماء أن ترمي الصيد فيغيب عنك فيموت وأنت لا تراه يقال: قد أنميت الرمية فنمت تنمى إذا غابت ثم ماتت

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#6/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#6/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#6/r14.claim: Imruʾ al-Qays’s line illustrates the verb for a shot that disappears from view.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#6/r14.anchor: قال امرؤ القيس: فهو لا تنمي رميته ماله لا عد من نفره

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#6/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#6/r15.speaker: علماؤنا
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#6/r15.claim: One reported position allows unseen prey whether it was killed by arrow or dog.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#6/r15.anchor: وقد اختلف العلماء في أكل الصيد الغائب على ثلاثة أقوال: يؤكل، وسواء قتله السهم أو الكلب.

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#6/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#6/r16.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#6/r16.claim: A second position bars any prey that disappeared from view.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#6/r16.anchor: الثاني لا يؤكل شيء من ذلك إذا غاب لقوله:

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#7/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#7/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#7/r1.claim: The second position bars unseen prey for fear another creature may have helped kill it.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#7/r1.anchor: وإنما لم يؤكل مخافة أن يكون قد أعان على قتله غير السهم من الهوام.

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#7/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#7/r2.speaker: علماؤنا
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#7/r2.claim: A third reported position allows unseen prey killed by arrow but not by dog, since an arrow has one clear cause while a hunting animal may kill in several ways.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#7/r2.anchor: الفرق بين السهم فيؤكل وبين الكلب فلا يؤكل ووجهه أن السهم يقتل على جهة واحدة فلا يشكل والجارح على جهات متعددة فيشكل والثلاثة الأقوال لعلمائنا.

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#7/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#7/r3.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#7/r3.claim: In a report outside the Muwatta, Malik says not to eat prey found dead after the night if the arrow, hawk, or dog had not inflicted the mortal wound.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#7/r3.anchor: وقال مالك في غير الموطأ: إذا بات الصيد ثم أصابه ميتا لم ينفذ البازي أو الكلب أو السهم مقاتله لم يأكله

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#7/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#7/r4.speaker: أبو عمر
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#7/r4.claim: Abu ʿUmar infers that Malik allows prey whose mortal wound was inflicted even if it spent the night, though Malik dislikes it because of Ibn ʿAbbas’s report.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#7/r4.anchor: قال أبو عمر: فهذا يدلك على أنه إذا بلغ مقاتله كان حلالا عنده أكله وإن بات، إلا أنه يكرهه إذا بات لما جاء عن ابن عباس

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#7/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#7/r5.speaker: ابن عباس والثوري
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#7/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas reports, and al-Thawri similarly says, that prey absent overnight or for a day should not be eaten or is disliked.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#7/r5.anchor: لما جاء عن ابن عباس: «وإن غاب عنك ليلة فلا تأكل» ونحوه عن الثوري قال: إذا غاب عنك يوما كرهت أكله.

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#7/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#7/r6.speaker: الشافعي
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#7/r6.claim: Al-Shafiʿi’s analogical reasoning is that prey should not be eaten if the hunter lost sight of where it fell.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#7/r6.anchor: وقال الشافعي: القياس ألا يأكله إذا غاب عنه مصرعه.

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#7/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#7/r7.speaker: الأوزاعي وأشهب وعبد الملك وأصبغ
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#7/r7.claim: They allow prey found dead the next day with the hunter’s arrow or dog mark when the wound was mortal, even if it spent the night.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#7/r7.anchor: وقال الأوزاعي: إن وجده من الغد ميتا ووجد فيه سهمه أو أثرا من كلبه فليأكله ونحوه قال أشهب وعبد الملك وأصبغ قالوا: جائز أكل الصيد وإن بات إذا نفذت مقاتله

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#7/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#7/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#7/r8.claim: “Unless it stinks” explains the dislike: stench makes food repulsive by ordinary nature, so eating is disliked but remains lawful, as the Prophet ate rancid fat.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#7/r8.anchor: تعليل لأنه إذا أنتن لحق بالمستقذرات التي تمجها الطباع فيكره أكلها فلو أكلها لجاز، كما: أكل النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم الإهالة السنخة وهي المنتنة.

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#7/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#7/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#7/r9.claim: Another explanation is fear of harm to the eater; on this rationale eating is forbidden when the danger is certain.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#7/r9.anchor: وقيل: هو معلل بما يخاف منه الضرر على آكله وعلى هذا التعليل يكون أكله محرما إن كان الخوف محققا، والله أعلم.

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#7/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#7/r10.speaker: الحسن البصري
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#7/r10.claim: Al-Hasan al-Basri disliked hunting with a trained dog owned by a Jew or Christian.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#7/r10.anchor: واختلف العلماء من هذا الباب في الصيد بكلب اليهودي والنصراني إذا كان معلما فكرهه الحسن البصري

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#7/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#7/r11.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله والحسن وعطاء ومجاهد والنخعي والثوري وإسحاق
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#7/r11.claim: These authorities disliked hunting with a Magian’s dog, hawk, or falcon.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#7/r11.anchor: وأما كلب المجوسي وبازه وصقره فكره الصيد بها جابر بن عبد الله والحسن وعطاء ومجاهد والنخعي والثوري وإسحاق

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#7/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#7/r12.speaker: مالك والشافعي وأبو حنيفة
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#7/r12.claim: They allow a Muslim to hunt with a Magian’s dog, treating it like the Magian’s knife.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#7/r12.anchor: وأجاز الصيد بكلابهم مالك والشافعي وأبو حنيفة إذا كان الصائد مسلما قالوا: وذلك مثل شفرته.

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#7/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#7/r13.speaker: جمهور الأمة
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#7/r13.claim: Most scholars allow hunting by a Jew or Christian, while Malik distinguishes their hunting from their slaughter and rejects it.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#7/r13.anchor: وأما إن كان الصائد من أهل الكتاب فجمهور الأمة على جواز صيده غير مالك، وفرق بين ذلك وبين ذبيحته

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#7/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#7/r14.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#7/r14.claim: Malik cites the verse about game within reach of hands and spears because it does not name Jews or Christians among permitted hunters.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#7/r14.anchor: وتلا يأيها الذين آمنوا ليبلونكم الله بشيء من الصيد تناله أيديكم ورماحكم [المائدة: 94] قال: فلم يذكر الله في هذا اليهود ولا النصارى.

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#7/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#7/r15.speaker: ابن وهب وأشهب
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#7/r15.claim: Ibn Wahb and Ashhab hold that a Jew’s or Christian’s hunted game is lawful just like their slaughtered meat.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#7/r15.anchor: وقال ابن وهب وأشهب: صيد اليهودي والنصراني حلال كذبيحته

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#7/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#7/r16.speaker: كتاب محمد
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#7/r16.claim: Muhammad’s legal text disallows hunting or slaughter by a Sabian, described as people between Jews and Christians with no religion.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#7/r16.anchor: وفي كتاب محمد لا يجوز صيد الصابىء ولا ذبحه وهم قوم بين اليهود والنصارى ولا دين لهم.

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#8/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#8/r1.speaker: مالك والشافعي وأبو حنيفة وأصحابهم وجمهور الناس
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#8/r1.claim: The majority, including Malik, al-Shafiʿi, and Abu Hanifa, prohibit eating game hunted by a Magian.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#8/r1.anchor: وأما إن كان الصائد مجوسيا فمنع من أكله مالك والشافعي وأبو حنيفة وأصحابهم وجمهور الناس.

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#8/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#8/r2.speaker: أبو ثور
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#8/r2.claim: Abu Thawr gives two positions: the majority’s prohibition, or permission because Magians count as People of the Book.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#8/r2.anchor: وقال أبو ثور فيها قولان: أحدهما كقول هؤلاء، والآخر أن المجوس من أهل الكتاب وأن صيدهم جائز.

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#8/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#8/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#8/r3.claim: Game hunted or slaughtered by a drunk person is not edible because valid slaughter requires intention, which the intoxicated person lacks.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#8/r3.anchor: ولو اصطاد السكران أو ذبح لم يؤكل صيده ولا ذبيحته لأن الذكاة تحتاج إلى قصد، والسكران لا قصد له.

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#8/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#8/r4.speaker: الأخفش
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#8/r4.claim: Al-Akhfash treats the preposition min in “what they held” as extra, comparing it with the wording in 6:141.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#8/r4.anchor: فقال الأخفش هي زائدة كقوله: كلوا من ثمره [الأنعام: 141].

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#8/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#8/r5.speaker: البصريون
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#8/r5.claim: The Basrans reject an added min in affirmative statements, allowing it only with negation or questions; they read the cited examples partitivally.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#8/r5.anchor: وخطأه البصريون وقالوا: «من» لا تزاد في الإثبات وإنما تزاد في النفي والاستفهام

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#8/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#8/r6.speaker: الأخفش
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#8/r6.claim: Al-Akhfash argues that min must be extra because the Qur’an elsewhere says “forgive your sins” without it; the counterargument reads min as partitive.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#8/r6.anchor: فدل على زيادتها في الإيجاب أجيب بأن «من» ههنا للتبعيض

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#8/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#8/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#8/r7.claim: He says the partitive explanation that only meat rather than offal or blood is permitted is not intended or customary in speaking of eating, undermining that account.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#8/r7.anchor: أجيب بأن «من» ههنا للتبعيض لأنه إنما يحل من الصيد اللحم دون الفرث والدم. قلت: هذا ليس بمراد ولا معهود في الأكل

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#8/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#8/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#8/r8.claim: An alternative reading is “what the hunting animals left for you”; this fits the view that their eating from prey does not invalidate it and explains the juristic dispute.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#8/r8.anchor: ويحتمل أن يريد «مما أمسكن» أي مما أبقته الجوارح لكم وهذا على قول من قال: لو أكل الكلب الفريسة لم يضر

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#8/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#8/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#8/r9.claim: The verse permits keeping dogs for hunting; authentic Sunna also permits them for crops and livestock, despite an early order to kill dogs.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#8/r9.anchor: ودلت الآية على جواز اتخاذ الكلاب واقتنائها للصيد، وثبت ذلك في صحيح السنة وزادت الحرث والماشية وقد كان أول الإسلام أمر بقتل الكلاب

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#8/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#8/r10.speaker: ابن عمر
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#8/r10.claim: Ibn ʿUmar reports the Prophet’s rule that keeping a dog outside hunting or livestock costs two qirats from one’s reward each day.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#8/r10.anchor:
عن ابن عمر عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال:
" من اقتنى كلبا إلا كلب صيد أو ماشية نقص من أجره كل يوم قيراطان "

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#8/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#8/r11.speaker: أبو هريرة
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#8/r11.claim: Abu Hurayra reports a version that also exempts a crop dog and gives a one-qirat daily reduction.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#8/r11.anchor:
هريرة قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:
" من اتخذ كلبا إلا كلب ماشية أو صيد أو زرع انتقص من أجره كل يوم قيراط "

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#8/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#8/r12.speaker: الزهري وابن عمر
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#8/r12.claim: When al-Zuhri told Ibn ʿUmar Abu Hurayra’s wording, Ibn ʿUmar replied that Abu Hurayra had crops; the Sunna confirms the stated exemptions.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#8/r12.anchor: قال الزهري: وذكر لابن عمر قول أبي هريرة فقال: يرحم الله أبا هريرة، كان صاحب زرع فقد دلت السنة على ما ذكرنا

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#9/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#9/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#9/r1.claim: The reward reduction for other dogs may deter their barking, which can alarm and disturb Muslims; a Basran poet illustrates the nuisance.

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#9/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#9/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#9/r2.claim: Other suggested reasons are that dogs keep angels from the house, are impure according to al-Shafiʿi, or represent keeping something with no benefit.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#9/r2.anchor: أو لمنع دخول الملائكة البيت، أو لنجاسته على ما يراه الشافعي، أو لاقتحام النهي عن اتخاذ ما لا منفعة فيه

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#9/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#9/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#9/r3.claim: The one- and two-qirat versions may refer to two kinds of dogs, one more harmful than the other, such as the intensely black dog singled out for killing.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#9/r3.anchor: وقال في إحدى الروايتين: «قيراطان» وفي الأخرى «قيراط» وذلك يحتمل أن يكون في نوعين من الكلاب أحدهما أشد أذى من الآخر كالأسود الذي أمر عليه الصلاة والسلام بقتله

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#9/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#9/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#9/r4.claim: Alternatively, the reduction may vary by location: two qirats in Medina or Mecca and one elsewhere.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#9/r4.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون ذلك لاختلاف المواضع، فيكون ممسكه بالمدينة مثلا أو بمكة ينقص قيراطان، وبغيرهما قيراط والله أعلم.

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#9/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#9/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#9/r5.claim: Keeping a permitted dog does not reduce reward, as with horses and cats; such a dog may be bought and sold, and Sahnun even permits pilgrimage with its sale price.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#9/r5.anchor: وأما المباح اتخاذه فلا ينقص أجر متخذه كالفرس والهر، ويجوز بيعه وشراؤه، حتى قال سحنون: ويحج بثمنه.

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#9/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#9/r6.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#9/r6.claim: Malik’s permitted livestock dog accompanies the animals to pasture, rather than guarding the house against thieves; a crop dog guards against wild animals day and night.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#9/r6.anchor: وكلب الماشية المباح اتخاذه عند مالك هو الذي يسرح معها لا الذي يحفظها في الدار من السراق. وكلب الزرع هو الذي يحفظه من الوحوش بالليل والنهار لا من السراق.

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#9/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#9/r7.speaker: غير مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#9/r7.claim: Other jurists permit rural dogs that guard livestock, crops, and houses against thieves.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#9/r7.anchor: وقد أجاز غير مالك اتخاذها لسراق الماشية والزرع والدار في البادية.

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#9/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#9/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#9/r8.claim: The verse shows that knowledge gives distinction: a trained dog is superior to other dogs, so a knowledgeable person—especially one who practices—has greater merit than others.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#9/r8.anchor: وفي هذه الآية دليل على أن العالم له من الفضيلة ما ليس للجاهل لأن الكلب إذا علم يكون له فضيلة على سائر الكلاب

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#9/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#9/r9.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#9/r9.claim: ʿAli is quoted saying that everything has a value and a person’s value lies in what he knows well.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#9/r9.anchor: كما روى عن علي بن أبي طالب كرم الله وجهه أنه قال: لكل شيء قيمة وقيمة المرء ما يحسنه.

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#9/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#9/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#9/r10.claim: The command to invoke God’s name may refer to releasing the hunting animal; hunting and slaughter use the same rule of naming, explained under al-Anʿam.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#9/r10.anchor: أمر بالتسمية قيل: عند الإرسال على الصيد، وفقه الصيد والذبح في معنى التسمية واحد، يأتي بيانه في «الأنعام»

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#9/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#9/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#9/r11.claim: He prefers interpreting the command as saying God’s name when eating.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#9/r11.anchor: وقيل: المراد بالتسمية هنا التسمية عند الأكل، وهو الأظهر.

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#9/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#9/r12.speaker: عمر بن أبي سلمة
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#9/r12.claim: In Muslim’s report, the Prophet tells the boy to say God’s name, eat with his right hand, and eat from what is before him.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#9/r12.anchor:
وفي صحيح مسلم أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال لعمر بن أبي سلمة:
" يا غلام سم الله وكل بيمينك وكل مما يليك "

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#10/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#10/r1.speaker: حذيفة
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#10/r1.claim: Hudhayfa reports the Prophet’s warning that Satan treats food as lawful when God’s name is not mentioned over it.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#10/r1.anchor:
وروي من حديث حذيفة قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:
" إن الشيطان ليستحل الطعام ألا يذكر اسم الله عليه "

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#10/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#10/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#10/r2.claim: If someone forgets the invocation at the start of eating, he should say it at the end; Umayya b. Makhshi reports the Prophet affirmed the formula and said Satan vomited the food after God was named.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#10/r2.anchor: فإن نسي التسمية أول الأكل فليسم آخره وروى النسائي عن أمية بن مخشي وكان من أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#10/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#10/r3.speaker: أمية بن مخشي
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#10/r3.claim: Umayya reports that a man invoked God’s name only at his last bite, saying “In God’s name at its beginning and end”; the Prophet said Satan vomited what he had eaten.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#10/r3.anchor:
أمية بن مخشي وكان من أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
" أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم رأى رجلا يأكل ولم يسم الله،

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#10/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#10/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#10/r4.claim: The command to fear God is general, with nearby reference to the commands contained in these verses.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#10/r4.anchor: أمر بالتقوى على الجملة، والإشارة القريبة هي ما تضمنته هذه الآيات من الأوامر.

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#10/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#10/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#10/r5.claim: God’s accounting is swift because He knows and has counted everything without needing to calculate; He reckons all creatures at once, as in 21:47.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#10/r5.anchor: من حيث كونه تعالى قد أحاط بكل شيء علما وأحصى كل شيء عددا فلا يحتاج إلى محاولة عد ولا عقد كما يفعله الحساب ولهذا قال: وكفى بنا حاسبين [الأنبياء: 47]

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#10/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#10/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#10/r6.claim: Alternatively, the phrase warns that Judgment Day is near and its accounting will arrive quickly.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#10/r6.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون وعيدا بيوم القيامة كأنه قال: إن حساب الله لكم سريع إتيانه إذ يوم القيامة قريب

QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#10/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#10/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#10/r7.claim: A further possibility is that “accounting” means requital: God threatens swift punishment in this world if people do not fear Him.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:4#10/r7.anchor: ويحتمل أن يريد بالحساب المجازاة فكأنه توعد في الدنيا بمجازاة سريعة قريبة إن لم يتقوا الله.

RAZI-FULL:v11p112/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v11p112/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v11p112/r1.claim: This verse continues the preceding discussion of foods and what may be eaten.
RAZI-FULL:v11p112/r1.anchor: وهذا أيضا متصل بما تقدم من ذكر المطاعم والمآكل

RAZI-FULL:v11p112/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v11p112/r2.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
RAZI-FULL:v11p112/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī treats the question as carrying the meaning of a statement: as though people asked, What has been made lawful for them?
RAZI-FULL:v11p112/r2.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) في السؤال معنى القول ، فلذلك وقع بعده { ماذا أحل لهم } كأنه قيل : يقولون لك ماذا أحل لهم

RAZI-FULL:v11p112/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v11p112/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v11p112/r3.claim: Al-Rāzī rejects that as a literal quotation: people would ask what is lawful for us, so the wording instead describes how the event occurred.
RAZI-FULL:v11p112/r3.anchor: واعلم أن هذا ضعيف لأنه لو كان هذا حكاية لكلامهم لكانوا قد قالوا ماذا أحل لهم

RAZI-FULL:v11p112/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v11p112/r4.speaker: الواحدي
RAZI-FULL:v11p112/r4.claim: Al-Wāḥidī offers two parses: mādhā as one noun with aḥilla as its predicate, or mā as subject and dhā as predicate with aḥilla modifying dhā.
RAZI-FULL:v11p112/r4.anchor: قال الواحدي : { ماذا } إن جعلته اسما واحدا فهو رفع بالابتداء ، وخبره { أحل } وإن شئت جعلت { ما } وحدها اسما

RAZI-FULL:v11p112/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v11p112/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v11p112/r5.claim: Pre-Islamic Arabs forbade some wholesome foods such as baḥīra, sāʾiba, waṣīla, and ḥām on weak grounds; the verse declares wholesome things lawful.
RAZI-FULL:v11p112/r5.anchor: أن العرب في الجاهلية كانوا يحرمون أشياء من الطيبات كالبحيرة والسائبة والوصيلة والحام

RAZI-FULL:v11p112/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v11p112/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v11p112/r6.claim: Ṭayyib means pleasant or appetizing; lawful is also called good by analogy because both are free of harm, so here it means what is relished, not merely what is permitted.
RAZI-FULL:v11p112/r6.anchor: واعلم أن الطيب في اللغة هو المستلذ ، والحلال المأذون فيه يسمى أيضا طيبا تشبيها بما هو مستلذ

RAZI-FULL:v11p112#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v11p112#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v11p112#2/r1.claim: Pleasantness is judged by people of good character, not by Bedouins who relish every animal; the permission of earthly benefits is qualified by the prohibition of foul things, making these verses a general food-law principle.
RAZI-FULL:v11p112#2/r1.anchor: ثم اعلم أن العبرة في الاستلذاذ والاستطابة بأهل المروءة والأخلاق الجميلة ، فإن أهل البادية يستطيبون أكل جميع الحيوانات

RAZI-FULL:v11p112#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v11p112#2/r2.speaker: الشافعي
RAZI-FULL:v11p112#2/r2.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī permits horse meat because it is plainly pleasant and wholesome, relying on the verse's general permission.
RAZI-FULL:v11p112#2/r2.anchor: منها أن لحم الخيل مباح عند الشافعي رحمه الله . وقال أبو حنيفة رحمه الله ليس بمباح . حجة الشافعي رحمه الله أنه مستلذ مستطاب

RAZI-FULL:v11p112#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v11p112#2/r3.speaker: أبو حنيفة
RAZI-FULL:v11p112#2/r3.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa holds horse meat impermissible, in contrast with al-Shāfiʿī's ruling.
RAZI-FULL:v11p112#2/r3.anchor: ومنها أن متروك التسمية عند الشافعي رحمه الله مباح ، وعند أبي حنيفة حرام ، حجة الشافعي رحمه الله أنه مستطاب مستلذ

RAZI-FULL:v11p112#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v11p112#2/r4.speaker: الشافعي
RAZI-FULL:v11p112#2/r4.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī permits meat slaughtered without pronouncing God's name; Abū Ḥanīfa forbids it, while al-Shāfiʿī invokes the general lawfulness of pleasant foods.
RAZI-FULL:v11p112#2/r4.anchor: أن متروك التسمية عند الشافعي رحمه الله مباح ، وعند أبي حنيفة حرام ، حجة الشافعي رحمه الله أنه مستطاب مستلذ

RAZI-FULL:v11p112#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v11p112#2/r7.speaker: مالك
RAZI-FULL:v11p112#2/r7.claim: Mālik and Bishr al-Marīsī permit domestic donkey meat based on these verses; al-Rāzī relies on the Prophet's prohibition of donkey meat at Khaybar.
RAZI-FULL:v11p112#2/r7.anchor: أن لحم الحمر الأهلية مباح عند مالك وعند بشر المريسي وقد احتجا بهايتن الآيتين ، إلا أنا نعتمد في تحريم ذلك

RAZI-FULL:v11p112#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v11p112#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v11p112#2/r8.claim: The Prophet prohibited domestic donkey meat on the day of Khaybar; al-Rāzī relies on that report to rule against its permissibility.
RAZI-FULL:v11p112#2/r8.anchor: ما روي عن الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه حرم لحوم الحمر الأهلية يوم خيبر

RAZI-FULL:v11p113/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v11p113/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v11p113/r1.claim: One syntactic analysis supplies an omitted word: lawful foods and the catch of trained hunting animals; the following command to eat what they catch signals the omission.
RAZI-FULL:v11p113/r1.anchor: أن فيها إضمارا ، والتقدير أحل لكم الطيبات وصيد ما علمتم من الجوارح مكلبين

RAZI-FULL:v11p113/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v11p113/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v11p113/r2.claim: An alternative analysis takes the hunting-animal clause as a new sentence whose predicate is the command to eat what the animals catch, requiring no ellipsis.
RAZI-FULL:v11p113/r2.anchor: أن يقال إن قوله { وما علمتم من الجوارح مكلبين } ابتداء كلام ، وخبره هو قوله { فكلوا مما أمسكن عليكم }

RAZI-FULL:v11p113/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v11p113/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v11p113/r3.claim: Jawāriḥ may mean animals that acquire prey, from the verb for earning or acquiring, as in the cited Qur'anic usages.
RAZI-FULL:v11p113/r3.anchor: أنها الكواسب من الطير والسباع ، واحدها جارحة ، سميت جوارح لأنها كواسب من جرح واجترح إذا اكتسب

RAZI-FULL:v11p113/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v11p113/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v11p113/r4.claim: Another lexical view derives jawāriḥ from wounding; on that view, prey taken without drawing blood is not lawful.
RAZI-FULL:v11p113/r4.anchor: أن الجوارح هي التي تجرح ، وقالوا : أن ما أخذ من الصيد فلم يسل منه دم لم يحل

RAZI-FULL:v11p113/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v11p113/r5.speaker: ابن عمر
RAZI-FULL:v11p113/r5.claim: Ibn ʿUmar, al-Ḍaḥḥāk, and al-Suddī are reported to disallow prey caught by a non-dog predator if the hunter does not reach it in time to slaughter it.
RAZI-FULL:v11p113/r5.anchor: نقل عن ابن عمر والضحاك والسدي ، أن ما صاده غير الكلاب فلم يدرك ذكاته لم يجز أكله

RAZI-FULL:v11p113/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v11p113/r6.speaker: الليث
RAZI-FULL:v11p113/r6.claim: Al-Layth reports Mujāhid's view that falcons, hawks, eagles, leopards, and other hunting predators all count as jawāriḥ.
RAZI-FULL:v11p113/r6.anchor: قال الليث : سئل مجاهد عن الصقر والبازي والعقاب والفهد وما يصطاد به من السباع ، فقال : هذه كلها جوارح

RAZI-FULL:v11p113/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v11p113/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v11p113/r7.claim: Defenders of non-dog hunting answer that mukallibīn can mean training all hunting animals, a term derived from dogs because dogs are commonly trained.
RAZI-FULL:v11p113/r7.anchor: أن المكلب هو مؤدب الجوارح ومعلمها أن تصطاد لصاحبها ، وإنما اشتق هذا الاسم من الكلب

RAZI-FULL:v11p113/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v11p113/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v11p113/r8.claim: They also argue that every predatory animal may be called a dog, citing the Prophet's prayer that a dog among God's dogs be sent against a man, whom a lion then killed.
RAZI-FULL:v11p113/r8.anchor: أن كل سبع فإنه يسمى كلبا ، ومنه قوله عليه الصلاة والسلام : ( اللهم سلط عليه كلبا من كلابك فأكله الأسد )

RAZI-FULL:v11p113/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v11p113/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v11p113/r9.claim: A third answer derives kalb from the sense of eagerness: someone intensely desirous of something is described as kalib for it.
RAZI-FULL:v11p113/r9.anchor: أنه مأخوذ من الكلب الذي هو بمعنى الضراوة ، يقال فلان : كلب بكذا إذا كان حريصا عليه

RAZI-FULL:v11p113/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v11p113/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v11p113/r10.claim: Finally, mentioning dogs does not exclude other means of hunting; hunting with a projectile or net is permitted though not named in the verse.
RAZI-FULL:v11p113/r10.anchor: تخصيصه بالذكر لا ينفي حل غيره ، بدليل أن الاصطياد بالرمي ووضع الشبكة جائز

RAZI-FULL:v11p113#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v11p113#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v11p113#2/r1.claim: The verse requires hunting animals to be trained; the Prophet told ʿAdī ibn Ḥātim to eat from prey caught by a trained dog after pronouncing God's name.
RAZI-FULL:v11p113#2/r1.anchor: دلت الآية على أن الاصطياد بالجوارح إنما يحل إذا كانت الجوارح معلمة ، لأنه تعالى قال : { وما علمتم من الجوارح مكلبين تعلمونهن مما علمكم الله }

RAZI-FULL:v11p113#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v11p113#2/r2.speaker: الشافعي
RAZI-FULL:v11p113#2/r2.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī says a dog is trained when it follows on release, holds prey without eating, answers its handler, and does not flee; repeated performance suffices, with custom determining the threshold and prevailing Abū Ḥanīfa opinion agreeing.
RAZI-FULL:v11p113#2/r2.anchor: إذا أرسل استرسل ، وإذا أخذ حبس ولا يأكل ، وإذا دعاه أجابه ، وإذا أراده لم يفر منه

RAZI-FULL:v11p113#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v11p113#2/r3.speaker: الحسن البصري
RAZI-FULL:v11p113#2/r3.claim: Al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī says a hunting animal becomes trained after one successful instance.
RAZI-FULL:v11p113#2/r3.anchor: وقال الحسن البصري رحمه الله : يصير معلما بمرة واحدة

RAZI-FULL:v11p113#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v11p113#2/r4.speaker: أبو حنيفة
RAZI-FULL:v11p113#2/r4.claim: In another report from Abū Ḥanīfa, an animal is trained after two repetitions; Aḥmad also holds this view.
RAZI-FULL:v11p113#2/r4.anchor: وعن أبي حنيفة رحمه الله في رواية أخرى أنه يصير معلما بتكرير ذلك مرتين ، وهو قول أحمد

RAZI-FULL:v11p113#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v11p113#2/r5.speaker: أبو يوسف ومحمد
RAZI-FULL:v11p113#2/r5.claim: Abū Yūsuf and Muḥammad require three repetitions for training.
RAZI-FULL:v11p113#2/r5.anchor: وعن أبي يوسف ومحمد رحمهما الله : أنه يصير معلما بثلاث مرات

RAZI-FULL:v11p113#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v11p113#2/r6.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
RAZI-FULL:v11p113#2/r6.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī reports a lightened reading of mukallibīn and notes that the forms afʿala and faʿʿala often share a meaning.
RAZI-FULL:v11p113#2/r6.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) وقرىء مكلبين بالتخفيف ، وأفعل وفعل يشتركان كثيرا

RAZI-FULL:v11p113#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v11p113#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v11p113#2/r7.claim: Mukallibīn is an accusative circumstantial qualifier of taught; it describes an expert, practiced trainer, while teach them is either a second circumstantial clause or a new sentence emphasizing the training requirement.
RAZI-FULL:v11p113#2/r7.anchor: انتصاب مكلبين على الحال من { علمتم } . فإن قيل :

RAZI-FULL:v11p114/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v11p114/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v11p114/r1.claim: If a trained dog wounds and kills prey found dead by the hunter, it is lawful; the animal's wound counts as slaughter, as with other trained predators, arrows, and spears.
RAZI-FULL:v11p114/r1.anchor: إذا كان الكلب معلما ثم صاد صيدا وجرحه وقتله وأدركه الصائد ميتا فهو حلال

RAZI-FULL:v11p114/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v11p114/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v11p114/r2.claim: If a dog kills by crushing without wounding, some call the prey carrion, while others permit it under the rule allowing what hunting animals catch for their owner.
RAZI-FULL:v11p114/r2.anchor: فقال بعضهم : لا يجوز أكله لأنه ميتة . وقال آخرون : يحل لدخوله تحت قوله { فكلوا مما أمسكن عليكم }

RAZI-FULL:v11p114/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v11p114/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v11p114/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, Ṭāwūs, al-Shaʿbī, ʿAṭāʾ, al-Suddī, and the predominant Shāfiʿī view forbid prey partly eaten by the hunting animal because it caught the prey for itself, not its owner.
RAZI-FULL:v11p114/r3.anchor: فعند ابن عباس وطاوس والشعبي وعطاء والسدي أنه لا يحل ، وهو أظهر أقوال الشافعي

RAZI-FULL:v11p114/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v11p114/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v11p114/r4.claim: The Prophet told ʿAdī: if prey is found dead and uneaten, eat it because the dog held it for you; if the dog ate from it, do not eat because it held it for itself.
RAZI-FULL:v11p114/r4.anchor: وإن أدركته وقد قتل ولم يأكل فكل فقد أمسك عليك ، وإن وجدته قد أكل فلا تطعم منه شيئا

RAZI-FULL:v11p114/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v11p114/r5.speaker: سلمان الفارسي
RAZI-FULL:v11p114/r5.claim: Salman, Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ, Ibn ʿUmar, and Abū Hurayra permit the prey even if the animal ate; this is al-Shāfiʿī's second view.
RAZI-FULL:v11p114/r5.anchor: وقال سلمان الفارسي وسعد بن أبي وقاص وابن عمر وأبو هريرة رضي الله عنهم : إنه يحل وإن أكل

RAZI-FULL:v11p114/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v11p114/r6.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
RAZI-FULL:v11p114/r6.claim: One view, transmitted from ʿAlī, treats a hawk like a dog: if it eats any of the prey, the prey may not be eaten.
RAZI-FULL:v11p114/r6.anchor: فقال قائلون : إنه لا فرق بينه وبين الكلب ، فإن أكل شيئا من الصيد لم يؤكل ذلك الصيد وهو مروي عن علي بن أبي طالب

RAZI-FULL:v11p114/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v11p114/r7.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
RAZI-FULL:v11p114/r7.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, Abū Ḥanīfa, and al-Muzanī allow what remains after a bird predator eats, but forbid what remains after a dog eats because a dog can be trained against eating by beating, unlike a hawk.
RAZI-FULL:v11p114/r7.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير وأبو حنيفة والمزني : يؤكل ما بقي من جوارح الطير ولا يؤكل ما بقي من الكلب

SAMIN-DURR:5:4/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:5:4/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:5:4/r1.claim: لهم is third person in keeping with the earlier third-person framing; saying لنا would quote the questioners' actual wording, as first-person forms do in quoted speech.
SAMIN-DURR:5:4/r1.anchor: وقوله: " لهم " بلفظ الغيبة لتقدم ضمير الغيبة في قوله تعالى: يسألونك

SAMIN-DURR:5:4/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:5:4/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:5:4/r2.claim: The interrogative ماذا suspends the question verb because asking causes knowledge, and verbs that cause knowledge can take an interrogative complement even when they are not verbs of the heart.
SAMIN-DURR:5:4/r2.anchor: و " ماذا أحل " هذا الاستفهام معلق للسؤال وإن لم يكن السؤال من أفعال القلوب،

SAMIN-DURR:5:4/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:5:4/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:5:4/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says the question contains the sense of القول, so ماذا أحل لهم follows it.
SAMIN-DURR:5:4/r3.anchor: وقال الزمخشري هنا: " في السؤال معنى القول، فلذلك وقع بعده " ماذا أحل لهم

SAMIN-DURR:5:4/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:5:4/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:5:4/r4.claim: The author says no embedded sense of القول is needed because the interrogative itself can suspend السؤال.
SAMIN-DURR:5:4/r4.anchor: ولا حاجة إلى تضمين السؤال معنى القول لما تقدم

SAMIN-DURR:5:4/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:5:4/r5.speaker: ابن الخطيب
SAMIN-DURR:5:4/r5.claim: Ibn al-Khaṭīb says this is not a direct quotation: the questioners would say ماذا أحل لنا, so the verse describes the situation rather than reproducing their words.
SAMIN-DURR:5:4/r5.anchor: بل الصحيح أنه ليس حكاية لكلامهم بعبارتهم، بل هو بيان كيفية الواقعة

SAMIN-DURR:5:4#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:5:4#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:5:4#2/r1.claim: ما may be a relative pronoun with an omitted resumptive pronoun, coordinated in the nominative with the passive subject; this requires an omitted noun such as “prey” or “taking.”
SAMIN-DURR:5:4#2/r1.anchor: في " ما " هذه ثلاثة أوجه، أحدها: أنها موصولة بمعنى الذي، العائد محذوف أي: ما علمتموه، ومحلها الرفع عطفا

SAMIN-DURR:5:4#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:5:4#2/r2.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:5:4#2/r2.claim: Alternatively ما is conditional, nominative as subject, with فكلوا as its answer; the Shaykh prefers this because it requires no ellipsis.
SAMIN-DURR:5:4#2/r2.anchor: والثاني: أنها شرطية فمحلها رفع بالابتداء، والجواب قوله: " فكلوا " قال الشيخ: " وهذا أظهر لأنه لا إضمار فيه "

SAMIN-DURR:5:4#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:5:4#2/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:5:4#2/r3.claim: ما may also be relative and nominative as subject, with فكلوا as its predicate; the فاء is used because the relative resembles a conditional noun.
SAMIN-DURR:5:4#2/r3.anchor: والثالث: أنها موصولة أيضا ومحلها الرفع بالابتداء، والخبر قوله: " فكلوا، وإنما دخلت الفاء تشبيها للموصول باسم الشرط.

SAMIN-DURR:5:4#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:5:4#2/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:5:4#2/r4.claim: من الجوارح is a circumstantial phrase whose صاحب is either the relative ما or its resumptive pronoun, with the same sense either way.
SAMIN-DURR:5:4#2/r4.anchor: وقوله: { من الجوارح } في محل نصب على الحال / وفي صاحبها وجهان

SAMIN-DURR:5:4#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:5:4#2/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:5:4#2/r5.claim: جوارح is the plural of جارحة: the term derives either from wounding prey or from earning, since جرح can mean كسب.
SAMIN-DURR:5:4#2/r5.anchor: والجوارح: جمع " جارحة " ، والهاء للمبالغة سميت بذلك لأنها تجرح الصيد غالبا أو لأنها تكسب، والجرح: الكسب

SAMIN-DURR:5:4#2/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:5:4#2/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:5:4#2/r6.claim: جارحة functions as an adjective used like a noun because its qualified noun is usually omitted.
SAMIN-DURR:5:4#2/r6.anchor: والجارحة: صفة جارية مجرى الأسماء لأنها لم يذكر موصوفها غالبا.

SAMIN-DURR:5:4#2/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:5:4#2/r7.speaker: ابن عباس وابن الحنفية
SAMIN-DURR:5:4#2/r7.claim: They read علمتم in the passive, understood as “what God taught you” about hunting animals, with الله omitted.
SAMIN-DURR:5:4#2/r7.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله بن عباس وابن الحنفية: " علمتم " مبنيا للمفعول

SAMIN-DURR:5:4#2/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:5:4#2/r8.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:5:4#2/r8.claim: مكلبين is a circumstantial phrase describing the subject of علمتم and means training, disciplining, or habituating the animals; the Shaykh says it identifies a skilled, expert trainer.
SAMIN-DURR:5:4#2/r8.anchor: " مكلبين " حال من فاعل " علمتم " ، ومعنى " مكلبين " مؤدبين ومضرين ومعودين قال الشيخ

SAMIN-DURR:5:4#2/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:5:4#2/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:5:4#2/r9.claim: The author rejects calling مكلبين redundant: despite its relation to علمتم, it establishes a distinct qualification of skilled training.
SAMIN-DURR:5:4#2/r9.anchor: وفي جعله هذه الحال مؤكدة نظر، بل هي مؤسسة.

SAMIN-DURR:5:4#2/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:5:4#2/r10.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:5:4#2/r10.claim: مكلبين may derive from the animal dog, since Arabs most often hunted with dogs, although other predators including birds are included; or from kalb meaning eagerness, itself perhaps from the dog's avidity.
SAMIN-DURR:5:4#2/r10.anchor: واشتقت هذه الحال من لفظ " الكلب " هذا الحيوان المعروف وإن كانت الجوارح يندرج فيها غيره

SAMIN-DURR:5:4#3/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:5:4#3/r1.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:5:4#3/r1.claim: The Shaykh rejects deriving the word from eagerness or predation: the lion's being called a dog describes the animal, whereas training is the teacher's act and predators are predators by nature; the author calls this objection pointless.
SAMIN-DURR:5:4#3/r1.anchor: قال الشيخ: وهذا الاشتقاق لا يصح لأن كون الأسد كلبا هو وصف فيه، والتكليب من صفة المعلم

SAMIN-DURR:5:4#3/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:5:4#3/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:5:4#3/r2.claim: A light-lām reading مكلبين is also transmitted; فعل and أفعل can overlap, though كلب means trained and made eager while أكلب means acquiring dogs, and الزجاج distinguishes dog trainer from dog owner.
SAMIN-DURR:5:4#3/r2.anchor: وقرئ: " مكلبين " بتخفيف اللام، وفعل وأفعل قد يشتركان في معنى واحد

SAMIN-DURR:5:4#3/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:5:4#3/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:5:4#3/r3.claim: The question is nominal and its answer is verbal; the answer matches it in meaning but not grammatical form.
SAMIN-DURR:5:4#3/r3.anchor: وجاءت جملة الجواب هنا فعلية وجملة السؤال اسمية

SAMIN-DURR:5:4#3/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:5:4#3/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:5:4#3/r4.claim: تعلمونهن may be an independent sentence.
SAMIN-DURR:5:4#3/r4.anchor: قوله: { تعلمونهن } فيه أربعة أوجه، أحدها: أنها جملة مستأنفة.

SAMIN-DURR:5:4#3/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:5:4#3/r5.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:5:4#3/r5.claim: It may be an accusative circumstantial clause from the subject of علمتم; Abu al-Baqāʾ disallows this because one governing verb cannot govern two circumstantials.
SAMIN-DURR:5:4#3/r5.anchor: الثاني: أنها جملة في محل نصب على أنها حال ثانية من فاعل " علمتم " ومنع أبو البقاء ذلك

SAMIN-DURR:5:4#3/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:5:4#3/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:5:4#3/r6.claim: It may instead be circumstantial to the hidden pronoun in مكلبين, a nested حال; on either circumstantial parsing it is emphatic because the teaching is already implied.
SAMIN-DURR:5:4#3/r6.anchor: الثالث: أنها حال من الضمير المستتر في " مكلبين " فتكون حالا من حال

SAMIN-DURR:5:4#3/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:5:4#3/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:5:4#3/r7.claim: It may be parenthetical if ما is conditional or a relative whose predicate is فكلوا, interrupting the protasis and answer or subject and predicate.
SAMIN-DURR:5:4#3/r7.anchor: والرابع: أن تكون جملة اعتراضية، وهذا على جعل " ما " شرطية

SAMIN-DURR:5:4#3/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:5:4#3/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:5:4#3/r8.claim: It cannot be circumstantial to الجوارح, because the unrelated circumstantial مكلبين would separate تعلمونهن from its صاحب.
SAMIN-DURR:5:4#3/r8.anchor: فالجواب أن ذلك لا يجوز، لأن ذلك يؤدي إلى الفصل بين هذه الحال وبين صاحبها بأجنبي وهو " مكلبين "

SAMIN-DURR:5:4#4/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:5:4#4/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:5:4#4/r1.claim: For مِنْ in مما أمسكن, the preferred parse is partitive with an omitted object of eating; al-Akhfash’s alternative treats it as redundant.
SAMIN-DURR:5:4#4/r1.anchor: أظهرهما: أنها تبغيضية، وهي صفة لموصوف محذوف، هو مفعول الأكل،

SAMIN-DURR:5:4#4/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:5:4#4/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:5:4#4/r2.claim: ما may be a relative pronoun or an indefinite noun qualified by a clause; its resumptive pronoun is omitted, and the construction is otherwise equivalent in either parse.
SAMIN-DURR:5:4#4/r2.anchor: و " ما " موصولة أو نكرة موصوفة، والعائد محذوف، وعلى كلا التقديرين

SAMIN-DURR:5:4#4/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:5:4#4/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:5:4#4/r3.claim: The nūn in أمسكن marks the hunting animals.

SAMIN-DURR:5:4#4/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:5:4#4/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:5:4#4/r4.claim: عليكم is governed by أمسكن, with the notion of being over or upon them used figuratively.
SAMIN-DURR:5:4#4/r4.anchor: و " عليكم " متعلق ب " أمسكن " والاستعلاء هنا مجاز.

SAMIN-DURR:5:4#4/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:5:4#4/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:5:4#4/r5.claim: The pronoun in عليه may refer to eating; a hadith telling diners to name God and eat what is nearest supports this reading.
SAMIN-DURR:5:4#4/r5.anchor: أحدها: أنها تعود على المصدر المفهوم من الفعل وهو الأكل كأنه قيل:

SAMIN-DURR:5:4#4/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:5:4#4/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:5:4#4/r6.claim: The pronoun in عليه may refer to the trained animals, meaning God’s name is invoked when releasing them to hunt; a hadith supports this.
SAMIN-DURR:5:4#4/r6.anchor: والثاني: أنه يعود على " ما علمتم " أي: اذكروا اسم الله على الجوارح

SAMIN-DURR:5:4#4/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:5:4#4/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:5:4#4/r7.claim: The pronoun in عليه may refer to the catch: invoke God’s name on game that the animals held until you reach it for slaughter.
SAMIN-DURR:5:4#4/r7.anchor: والثالث: أنها تعود على " ما أمسكن " أي: اذكروا اسم الله ما أدركتم ذكاته

STUDYQURAN:5:intro/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:5:intro/r9.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:5:intro/r9.claim: The opening verses prescribe pilgrimage, lawful foods, intermarriage, and ritual purity.
STUDYQURAN:5:intro/r9.anchor: pilgrimage, lawful foods, intermarriage, and ritual purity

STUDYQURAN:5:intro/r10.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:5:intro/r10.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:5:intro/r10.claim: These opening rulings are interspersed with reminders of God’s blessings on the Muslim community and the need to fulfill the covenant with Him.
STUDYQURAN:5:intro/r10.anchor: interspersed with reminders of God’s blessings upon the Muslim community and of the necessity of fulfilling the covenant with Him.

STUDYQURAN:5:intro/r11.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:5:intro/r11.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:5:intro/r11.claim: The opening lines have a triumphant, hopeful tone and, through their emphasis on blessings and covenant, recall Moses’ final sermon in Deuteronomy.
STUDYQURAN:5:intro/r11.anchor: tone of these opening lines is religiously triumphant and hopeful

STUDYQURAN:5:intro/r12.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:5:intro/r12.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:5:intro/r12.claim: The opening’s repeated emphasis on blessings and covenant is compared with Moses’ final sermon as recounted in Deuteronomy.
STUDYQURAN:5:intro/r12.anchor: bears some comparison with Moses’ final sermon as recounted in the Biblical book of Deuteronomy.

STUDYQURAN:5:intro/r19.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:5:intro/r19.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:5:intro/r19.claim: Its rulings include dietary law in 5:3–5 and 5:87–88.

STUDYQURAN:5:4/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:5:4/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:5:4/r1.claim: The good things, especially food, are Divine provisions believers may enjoy and should receive with gratitude.
STUDYQURAN:5:4/r1.anchor: Here and in v. 5, the Quran mentions the lawfulness of the many good

STUDYQURAN:5:4/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:5:4/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:5:4/r2.claim: Enjoying good things is linked throughout the Quran to Divine favor and a community’s spiritual purity.
STUDYQURAN:5:4/r2.anchor: The freedom to enjoy all good things, however, is tied to notions of Divine favor and the spiritual purity of a religious community throughout the Quran.

STUDYQURAN:5:4/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:5:4/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:5:4/r3.claim: After manna and quails, Israelites were told to eat the provided good things; 3:93 says all food was lawful before the Torah except what Israel self-forbade.
STUDYQURAN:5:4/r3.anchor: After the manna and quails were sent to Moses and the Israelites in the desert, they were instructed

STUDYQURAN:5:4/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:5:4/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:5:4/r4.claim: Because of Israelite wrongdoing, some previously lawful foods were later prohibited.
STUDYQURAN:5:4/r4.anchor: As a response to the “wrongdoing” of the Israelites, however, this changed

STUDYQURAN:5:4/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:5:4/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:5:4/r5.claim: Jesus brought spiritual renewal, confirmed the Torah, and made some formerly forbidden things lawful for Israelites.
STUDYQURAN:5:4/r5.anchor: Jesus, who is said by the Quran to have brought a message of spiritual renewal for the Israelites and to have confirmed the Torah

STUDYQURAN:5:4/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:5:4/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:5:4/r6.claim: Muhammad likewise made good things lawful for “them,” apparently the Jews in context, while the teaching also applies to Muslims.
STUDYQURAN:5:4/r6.anchor: which, in context, seems to refer to the Jews, although it also applies to Muslims.

STUDYQURAN:5:4/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:5:4/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:5:4/r7.claim: The Quran criticizes both consuming unlawful things and arbitrarily declaring lawful provisions unlawful; such restrictions attributed to Arabian idolaters signal spiritual decadence.
STUDYQURAN:5:4/r7.anchor: it also criticizes those who deem “unlawful”what God has made lawful

STUDYQURAN:5:4/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:5:4/r8.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:5:4/r8.claim: The verse permits hunting licit game with trained dogs, other animals, and birds such as falcons.
STUDYQURAN:5:4/r8.anchor: This verse allows the use of dogs or other animals and birds, such as falcons, in hunting licit game.

STUDYQURAN:5:4/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:5:4/r9.speaker: Ṭ and W
STUDYQURAN:5:4/r9.claim: Although some traditions deem dogs unclean, this verse permits trained hunting dogs and by extension dogs used for protection or other valuable services; their impurity does not apply in such cases.
STUDYQURAN:5:4/r9.anchor: it is thus understood that in such cases their unclean status does not apply (Ṭ, W).

STUDYQURAN:5:4/r10.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:5:4/r10.speaker: JJ and Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:5:4/r10.claim: They explain teaching hunting animals as training them to obey human commands and catch prey without eating it.
STUDYQURAN:5:4/r10.anchor: Teaching them from that which God has taught you refers to teaching them to obey human command and to catch prey without eating from it (JJ, Ṭ).

STUDYQURAN:5:4/r11.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:5:4/r11.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:5:4/r11.claim: Caught prey is lawful if God’s name is spoken before releasing the hunting animal or over prey that remains alive.
STUDYQURAN:5:4/r11.anchor: so long as one has pronounced the Name of God before releasing the hunting animal or over the prey that has been caught, if it is still alive.

STUDYQURAN:5:4/r12.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:5:4/r12.speaker: Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:5:4/r12.claim: Prey caught by an untrained wild or unknown animal, or partly eaten by the hunting animal, is unlawful because it shows inadequate training.
STUDYQURAN:5:4/r12.anchor: because it indicates that the animal has not been properly trained (Ṭ)

STUDYQURAN:5:4/r13.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:5:4/r13.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:5:4/r13.claim: Alternatively, an animal eating part of the prey can indicate that it caught the prey for itself, making it unlawful to eat.
STUDYQURAN:5:4/r13.anchor: because it indicates that the animal is considered to have caught it for itself.

STUDYQURAN:5:4/r14.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:5:4/r14.speaker: Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:5:4/r14.claim: Ṭ allows prey partly eaten by the hunting animal if the hunter reaches it alive, pronounces God’s name, and properly slaughters it under the exception in 5:3.
STUDYQURAN:5:4/r14.anchor: then it is licit according to the exception established in v. 3 (Ṭ).

TAB-FULL:v8p99#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p99#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v8p99#2/r1.claim: The answer permits wholesome lawful food and game caught for people by trained hunting beasts, including predatory animals and birds.
TAB-FULL:v8p99#2/r1.anchor: أحل منها الطيبات، وهي الحلال الذي أذن لكم ربكم في أكله من الذبائح، وأحل لكم أيضا مع ذلك صيد ما علمتم من الجوارح

TAB-FULL:v8p99#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p99#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v8p99#2/r2.claim: Jawarih are named for wounding and earning their owners sustenance through the game they catch; the root can mean earning good for one's family.
TAB-FULL:v8p99#2/r2.anchor: سميت جوارح لجرحها لأربابها وكسبها إياهم أقواتهم من الصيد، يقال منه: جرح فلان لأهله خيرا: إذا أكسبهم خيرا

TAB-FULL:v8p99#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p99#2/r3.speaker: الأعشى
TAB-FULL:v8p99#2/r3.claim: Al-A'sha's verse uses the root in the sense of acquiring or earning.
TAB-FULL:v8p99#2/r3.anchor: ومنه قول أعشى بني ثعلبة: [البحر المتقارب] ذات خد منضج ميسمه … يذكر الجارح ما كان اجترح يعني: اكتسب.

TAB-FULL:v8p99#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p99#2/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v8p99#2/r4.claim: After “what you have trained,” the text omits “of the game” because the context makes the omitted words clear.
TAB-FULL:v8p99#2/r4.anchor: وترك من قوله: {وما علمتم} [المائدة: 4] وصيد ما علمتم من الجوارح اكتفاء بدلالة ما ذكر من الكلام على ما ترك ذكره.

TAB-FULL:v8p99#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p99#2/r5.speaker: أبو رافع
TAB-FULL:v8p99#2/r5.claim: Abu Rafi reports that Gabriel would not enter a house containing a dog, so the Prophet ordered all dogs in Medina killed; after people asked what dogs could be kept, the verse was revealed.
TAB-FULL:v8p99#2/r5.anchor: عن سلمى أم رافع، عن أبي رافع، قال: جاء جبريل إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يستأذن عليه، فأذن له، فقال: «قد أذنا لك يا رسول الله» قال: أجل، ولكنا لا ندخل بيتا فيه كلب.

TAB-FULL:v8p99#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p99#2/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v8p99#2/r6.claim: The verse exempts hunting dogs, livestock dogs, and field dogs from the order to kill dogs and permits keeping them.
TAB-FULL:v8p99#2/r6.anchor: فاستثنى مما كان حرم اتخاذه منها، وأمر بقنية كلاب الصيد وكلاب الماشية وكلاب الحرث، وأذن لهم باتخاذ ذلك.

TAB-FULL:v8p102/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p102/r1.speaker: عكرمة
TAB-FULL:v8p102/r1.claim: Ikrima says the Prophet sent Abu Rafi to kill dogs; after the order reached al-Awali, several men asked what was permitted, and the verse was revealed.
TAB-FULL:v8p102/r1.anchor: عن ابن جريج، عن عكرمة: أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بعث أبا رافع في قتل الكلاب، فقتل حتى بلغ العوالي

TAB-FULL:v8p102/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p102/r2.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
TAB-FULL:v8p102/r2.claim: Muhammad b. Ka'b al-Qurazi says that when the people asked what they could eat after dogs were ordered killed, this verse was revealed.
TAB-FULL:v8p102/r2.anchor: عن محمد بن كعب القرظي، قال: لما أمر النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بقتل الكلاب، قالوا: يا رسول الله، فماذا يحل لنا من هذه الأمة؟ فنزلت

TAB-FULL:v8p102/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p102/r3.speaker: الحسن
