TAB-FULL:v8p102/r3.claim: Al-Hasan takes jawarih to include every trained creature that hunts, such as dogs, falcons, cheetahs, and other animals.
TAB-FULL:v8p102/r3.anchor: عن الحسن، في قوله: {وما علمتم من الجوارح مكلبين} [المائدة: 4] قال: " كل ما علم فصاد: من كلب، أو صقر، أو فهد، أو غيره "

TAB-FULL:v8p102/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p102/r4.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v8p102/r4.claim: Mujahid says the cheetah is one of the hunting beasts included in jawarih.
TAB-FULL:v8p102/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد، في صيد الفهد، قال: «هو من الجوارح»

TAB-FULL:v8p102/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p102/r5.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v8p102/r5.claim: Mujahid also identifies birds and dogs as jawarih covered by the verse.
TAB-FULL:v8p102/r5.anchor: عن مجاهد، في قوله: {وما علمتم من الجوارح مكلبين} [المائدة: 4] قال: «الطير، والكلاب»

TAB-FULL:v8p104/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p104/r1.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v8p104/r1.claim: Mujahid says jawarih include birds and dogs.
TAB-FULL:v8p104/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد في قول الله: {من الجوارح مكلبين} [المائدة: 4] قال: «من الطير والكلاب»

TAB-FULL:v8p104/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p104/r2.speaker: خيثمة
TAB-FULL:v8p104/r2.claim: Khaythama says falcons, hawks, and dogs are included among jawarih.
TAB-FULL:v8p104/r2.anchor: عن طلحة الإيامي، عن خيثمة، قال: " أنبئت أن الصقر , والباز، والكلب: من الجوارح "

TAB-FULL:v8p104/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p104/r3.speaker: علي بن حسين
TAB-FULL:v8p104/r3.claim: Ali b. Husayn says the hawk and falcon are jawarih.
TAB-FULL:v8p104/r3.anchor: عن نافع، عن علي بن حسين، قال: «الباز الصقر من الجوارح»

TAB-FULL:v8p104/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p104/r4.speaker: أبو جعفر
TAB-FULL:v8p104/r4.claim: Abu Ja'far likewise includes the hawk and falcon among trained jawarih.
TAB-FULL:v8p104/r4.anchor: عن شريك، عن جابر، عن أبي جعفر، قال: «الباز والصقر من الجوارح المكلبين»

TAB-FULL:v8p104/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p104/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v8p104/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies trained hunting dogs, cheetahs, falcons, and similar animals as jawarih.
TAB-FULL:v8p104/r5.anchor: عن علي، عن ابن عباس، قوله: {وما علمتم من الجوارح مكلبين} [المائدة: 4] يعني بالجوارح: الكلاب الضواري والفهود والصقور وأشباهها

TAB-FULL:v8p104/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p104/r6.speaker: طاوس
TAB-FULL:v8p104/r6.claim: Tawus says jawarih include dogs and other trained hunters, such as falcons and hawks.
TAB-FULL:v8p104/r6.anchor: عن ابن طاوس، عن أبيه: {وما علمتم من الجوارح مكلبين} [المائدة: 4] قال: «من الكلاب وغيرها، من الصقور والبيزان وأشباه ذلك مما يعلم»

TAB-FULL:v8p104/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p104/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v8p104/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas describes jawarih as trained dogs and falcons.
TAB-FULL:v8p104/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس قوله: {وما علمتم من الجوارح مكلبين} [المائدة: 4] الجوارح: الكلاب والصقور المعلمة

TAB-FULL:v8p104/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p104/r8.speaker: عبيد بن عمير
TAB-FULL:v8p104/r8.claim: Ubayd b. Umayr says jawarih are dogs and birds.
TAB-FULL:v8p104/r8.anchor: سمع عبيد بن عمير، يقول في قوله: {من الجوارح مكلبين} [المائدة: 4] قال: «الكلاب والطير»

TAB-FULL:v8p106/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p106/r1.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v8p106/r1.claim: Al-Dahhak restricts the jawarih to dogs.
TAB-FULL:v8p106/r1.anchor: عن الضحاك: {وما علمتم من الجوارح مكلبين} [المائدة: 4] قال: «هي الكلاب»

TAB-FULL:v8p106/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p106/r2.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v8p106/r2.claim: Al-Suddi says the verse permits game caught by trained dogs.
TAB-FULL:v8p106/r2.anchor: عن السدي، قوله: {وما علمتم من الجوارح مكلبين} [المائدة: 4] يقول: «أحل لكم صيد الكلاب التي علمتموهن»

TAB-FULL:v8p106/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p106/r3.speaker: ابن عمر
TAB-FULL:v8p106/r3.claim: Ibn Umar says that game taken by birds or hawks is edible if reached alive, but should not be eaten if found dead.
TAB-FULL:v8p106/r3.anchor: عن نافع , عن ابن عمر، قال: «أما ما صاد من الطير والبزاة من الطير، فما أدركت فهو لك، وإلا فلا تطعمه»

TAB-FULL:v8p106/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p106/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v8p106/r4.claim: Al-Tabari prefers including every trained bird and predatory animal, since the verse generalizes without excluding any kind of hunting beast.
TAB-FULL:v8p106/r4.anchor: وأولى القولين بتأويل الآية، قول من قال: كل ما صاد من الطير والسباع فمن الجوارح، وإن صيد جميع ذلك حلال إذا صاد بعد التعليم

TAB-FULL:v8p106/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p106/r5.speaker: عدي بن حاتم
TAB-FULL:v8p106/r5.claim: The Prophet told Adi b. Hatim that game caught by a falcon may be eaten, supporting its inclusion among jawarih and refuting the dog-only view.
TAB-FULL:v8p106/r5.anchor: عن عدي بن حاتم، قال: سألت رسول الله عن صيد البازي، فقال: «ما أمسك عليك فكل»

TAB-FULL:v8p106/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p106/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v8p106/r6.claim: Al-Tabari rejects the argument that mukallibin confines jawarih to dogs: it describes the hunter as trained or skilled, whether his game is caught by dogs or other animals.
TAB-FULL:v8p106/r6.anchor: فإن ظن ظان أن في قوله {مكلبين} [المائدة: 4] دلالة على أن الجوارح التي ذكرت في قوله: {وما علمتم من الجوارح} [المائدة: 4] هي الكلاب خاصة، فقد ظن غير الصواب

TAB-FULL:v8p106/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p106/r7.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v8p106/r7.claim: Mukallibin describes the people who hunt; it does not say that only dogs may catch the game, just as “believers” can describe people in a broader instruction.
TAB-FULL:v8p106/r7.anchor: فقوله: {مكلبين} [المائدة: 4] صفة للقانص، وإن صاد بغير الكلاب في بعض أحيانه

TAB-FULL:v8p108/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p108/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v8p108/r1.claim: “You train them” means disciplining hunting animals to seek game for people, using the instruction and knowledge God gave them.
TAB-FULL:v8p108/r1.anchor: بقوله: {تعلمونهن} [المائدة: 4] تؤدبون الجوارح، فتعلمونهن طلب الصيد لكم مما علمكم الله

TAB-FULL:v8p108/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p108/r2.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v8p108/r2.claim: Al-Suddi interprets “from what God taught you” as “as God taught you.”
TAB-FULL:v8p108/r2.anchor: عن السدي: {تعلمونهن مما علمكم الله} [المائدة: 4] يقول: «تعلمونهن من الطلب كما علمكم الله»

TAB-FULL:v8p108/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p108/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v8p108/r3.claim: Al-Tabari rejects taking min to mean “as”: in Arabic min is partitive and kaf marks comparison, and unlike meanings are not substituted; scripture is especially eloquent.
TAB-FULL:v8p108/r3.anchor: ولسنا نعرف في كلام العرب من بمعنى الكاف، لأن من تدخل في كلامهم بمعنى التبعيض، والكاف بمعنى التشبيه.

TAB-FULL:v8p108/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p108/r4.speaker: عدي بن حاتم
TAB-FULL:v8p108/r4.claim: Adi b. Hatim relates that a man asked the Prophet about dog game, and the answer came when this verse was revealed.
TAB-FULL:v8p108/r4.anchor: عن أبي بشر، قال: ثنا عامر، أن عدي بن حاتم الطائي، قال: أتى رجل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يسأله عن صيد الكلاب

TAB-FULL:v8p108/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p108/r5.speaker: عطاء
TAB-FULL:v8p108/r5.claim: Ata says a catch killed before the hunting animal is trained to hold and hunt is carrion; after it is trained, its killing counts as slaughter.
TAB-FULL:v8p108/r5.anchor: قال عطاء: «كل شيء قتله صائدك قبل أن يعلم ويمسك ويصيد فهو ميتة، ولا يكون قتله إياه ذكاة حتى يعلم ويمسك ويصيد

TAB-FULL:v8p108/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p108/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v8p108/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas says a trained dog holds its catch without eating until its owner arrives; if it eats and the owner can still slaughter the catch, it may not be eaten.
TAB-FULL:v8p108/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قال: «المعلم من الكلاب أن يمسك صيده فلا يأكل منه حتى يأتيه صاحبه، فإن أكل من صيده قبل أن يأتيه صاحبه فيدرك ذكاته، فلا يأكل من صيده»

TAB-FULL:v8p110/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p110/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v8p110/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas, through Tawus, says not to eat game when the dog eats, because it held the prey for itself.
TAB-FULL:v8p110/r1.anchor: عن طاوس، عن ابن عباس , قال: «إذا أكل الكلب فلا تأكل، فإنما أمسك على نفسه»

TAB-FULL:v8p110/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p110/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v8p110/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas, through Sa'id b. Jubayr, says a dog that eats its catch has spoiled it even if God's name was spoken; it is not trained until taught to stop.
TAB-FULL:v8p110/r2.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير، قال: قال ابن عباس: " إذا أرسل الرجل الكلب فأكل من صيده فقد أفسده، وإن كان ذكر اسم الله حين أرسله

TAB-FULL:v8p110/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p110/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v8p110/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says a dog that catches, kills, and eats the prey is a predatory beast.
TAB-FULL:v8p110/r3.anchor: عن عطاء، عن ابن عباس , قال: «إذا أخذ الكلب فقتل فأكل، فهو سبع»

TAB-FULL:v8p110/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p110/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v8p110/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says not to eat the catch because a trained dog would not eat it and would hold it for the hunter rather than itself.
TAB-FULL:v8p110/r4.anchor: عن عامر، عن ابن عباس، قال: «لا يأكل منه، فإنه لو كان معلما لم يأكل منه ولم يتعلم ما علمته، إنما أمسك على نفسه ولم يمسك عليك»

TAB-FULL:v8p110/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p110/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v8p110/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas also says that game caught by dogs that eat their prey is not to be eaten.
TAB-FULL:v8p110/r5.anchor: عن إبراهيم، عن ابن عباس، قال: «إذا أكلت الكلاب فلا تأكل»

TAB-FULL:v8p110/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p110/r6.speaker: الشعبي
TAB-FULL:v8p110/r6.claim: Al-Sha'bi says a dog that eats its catch has not learned the training given to it.
TAB-FULL:v8p110/r6.anchor: قلت لعامر الشعبي: الرجل يرسل كلبه فيأكل منه، أنأكل منه؟ قال: «لا، لم يتعلم الذي علمته»

TAB-FULL:v8p110/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p110/r7.speaker: ابن عمر
TAB-FULL:v8p110/r7.claim: Ibn Umar says to strike a dog that eats from a catch, since it is not trained.
TAB-FULL:v8p110/r7.anchor: عن مجاهد، عن ابن عمر , قال: «إذا أكل الكلب من صيد فاضربه، فإنه ليس بمعلم»

TAB-FULL:v8p110/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p110/r8.speaker: طاوس
TAB-FULL:v8p110/r8.claim: Tawus says a dog's catch is carrion if the dog ate from it.
TAB-FULL:v8p110/r8.anchor: عن ابن طاوس، عن أبيه، قال: «إذا أكل الكلب فهو ميتة، فلا تأكله»

TAB-FULL:v8p111/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p111/r1.speaker: سعيد بن جبير، الشعبي، إبراهيم
TAB-FULL:v8p111/r1.claim: Sa'id b. Jubayr, al-Sha'bi, and Ibrahim say not to eat the prey if a dog ate it, because it held the prey for itself.
TAB-FULL:v8p111/r1.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير , وسيار، عن الشعبي، ومغيرة، عن إبراهيم، أنهم قالوا: في الكلب إذا أكل من صيده فلا تأكل، فإنما أمسك على نفسه

TAB-FULL:v8p111/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p111/r2.speaker: عطاء
TAB-FULL:v8p111/r2.claim: Ata says a dead catch found after the dog ate is not prey held for the hunter but a beast's own catch, even if the dog was trained.
TAB-FULL:v8p111/r2.anchor: قال عطاء: «إن وجدت الكلب قد أكل من الصيد، فما وجدته ميتا فدعه، فإنه مما لم يمسك عليك صيدا، إنما هو سبع أمسك على نفسه ولم يمسك عليك، وإن كان قد علم»

TAB-FULL:v8p111/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p111/r3.speaker: أبو يوسف ومحمد بن الحسن
TAB-FULL:v8p111/r3.claim: A view attributed to Abu Yusuf and Muhammad b. al-Hasan requires the dog to demonstrate the training behavior three times before its catch is lawful.
TAB-FULL:v8p111/r3.anchor: وهذا قول محكي عن أبي يوسف ومحمد بن الحسن

TAB-FULL:v8p111/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p111/r4.speaker: بعض المتأخرين
TAB-FULL:v8p111/r4.claim: Some later interpreters set no numerical threshold: once a dog displays the described training behavior, it is trained and its catch is lawful.
TAB-FULL:v8p111/r4.anchor: قالوا: فإذا فعل ذلك فقد صار معلما حلالا صيده. وهذا قول بعض المتأخرين.

TAB-FULL:v8p111/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p111/r5.speaker: بعض قائلي هذه المقالة
TAB-FULL:v8p111/r5.claim: Some interpreters distinguish birds from dogs and other predatory beasts: a bird is trained by flying when released, answering a call, and not fleeing capture; it need not refrain from eating prey.
TAB-FULL:v8p111/r5.anchor: وفرق بعض قائلي هذه المقالة بين تعليم البازي وسائر الطيور الجارحة، وتعليم الكلب وضاري السباع الجارحة

TAB-FULL:v8p111/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p111/r6.speaker: إبراهيم وعطاء
TAB-FULL:v8p111/r6.claim: Ibrahim and Ata say it is permissible to eat game caught by a falcon even if the bird ate some.
TAB-FULL:v8p111/r6.anchor: عن مغيرة، عن إبراهيم، وحجاج، عن عطاء، قال: «لا بأس بصيد البازي وإن أكل منه»

TAB-FULL:v8p111/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p111/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v8p111/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas says a trained bird returns to its owner, unlike a dog that must be struck; even if the bird eats the catch or plucks feathers, it may be eaten.
TAB-FULL:v8p111/r7.anchor: عن حماد، عن إبراهيم، عن ابن عباس، أنه قال في الطير: " إذا أرسلته فقتل فكل، فإن الكلب إذا ضربته لم يعد، وإن تعليم الطير: أن يرجع إلى صاحبه

TAB-FULL:v8p111/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p111/r8.speaker: الشعبي
TAB-FULL:v8p111/r8.claim: Al-Sha'bi says falcons and hawks differ from dogs: if they catch, eat, and return when called, their catch is lawful.
TAB-FULL:v8p111/r8.anchor: عن جابر , عن الشعبي، قال: «ليس البازي والصقر كالكلب، فإذا أرسلتهما فأمسكا فأكلا فدعوتهما فأتياك، فكل منه»

TAB-FULL:v8p114/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p114/r1.speaker: إبراهيم
TAB-FULL:v8p114/r1.claim: Ibrahim permits eating prey caught by a falcon even when the falcon ate from it.
TAB-FULL:v8p114/r1.anchor: قال إبراهيم: «كل صيد البازي وإن أكل منه»

TAB-FULL:v8p114/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p114/r2.speaker: الشعبي
TAB-FULL:v8p114/r2.claim: Al-Shaʿbī, together with Ibrahim in this report, permits eating falcon prey even if it ate from the catch.
TAB-FULL:v8p114/r2.anchor: عن الشعبي، قالا: «كل من صيد البازي وإن أكل»

TAB-FULL:v8p114/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p114/r3.speaker: آخرون
TAB-FULL:v8p114/r3.claim: Some authorities require every trained predator to hold prey for its owner without eating; prey it ate is unlawful, whatever the predator species.
TAB-FULL:v8p114/r3.anchor: لا يحل أكل شيء من الصيد الذي صادته جارحة فأكلت منه

TAB-FULL:v8p114/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p114/r4.speaker: علي
TAB-FULL:v8p114/r4.claim: Ali says not to eat a falcon's catch if the falcon ate from it.
TAB-FULL:v8p114/r4.anchor: قال علي: «إذا أكل البازي من صيده فلا تأكل»

TAB-FULL:v8p114/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p114/r5.speaker: الشعبي
TAB-FULL:v8p114/r5.claim: Al-Shaʿbī says not to eat prey if the falcon ate from it.
TAB-FULL:v8p114/r5.anchor: قال: «إذا أكل البازي منه فلا تأكل»

TAB-FULL:v8p114/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p114/r6.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
TAB-FULL:v8p114/r6.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr says not to eat prey if the falcon ate from it.
TAB-FULL:v8p114/r6.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير , قال: «إذا أكل البازي فلا تأكل»

TAB-FULL:v8p114/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p114/r7.speaker: عكرمة
TAB-FULL:v8p114/r7.claim: ʿIkrima says not to eat prey if the falcon ate from it.
TAB-FULL:v8p114/r7.anchor: سمعت عكرمة، قال: «إذا أكل البازي فلا تأكل»

TAB-FULL:v8p114/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p114/r8.speaker: عطاء
TAB-FULL:v8p114/r8.claim: ʿAṭāʾ treats dog and falcon alike: do not eat prey they ate unless it is slaughtered; a falcon's catch remains lawful if it only plucked feathers and did not eat.
TAB-FULL:v8p114/r8.anchor: قال عطاء: «الكلب والبازي كله واحد، لا تأكل ما أكل منه من الصيد إلا أن تدرك ذكاته فتذكيه»

TAB-FULL:v8p114/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p114/r9.speaker: عطاء
TAB-FULL:v8p114/r9.claim: ʿAṭāʾ permits a falcon's catch when it plucked feathers but did not eat the prey.
TAB-FULL:v8p114/r9.anchor: البازي ينتف الريش؟ قال: فما أدركته ولم يأكل، فكل

TAB-FULL:v8p114/r10.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p114/r10.speaker: آخرون
TAB-FULL:v8p114/r10.claim: Other authorities define training as lunging after release, taking the prey, responding when called or not fleeing; this standard applies alike to birds and beasts.
TAB-FULL:v8p114/r10.anchor: وتعليمه الذي يحل به صيده أن يشلى على الصيد فيستشلي ويأخذ الصيد، ويدعوه صاحبه فيجيب

TAB-FULL:v8p114/r11.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p114/r11.speaker: آخرون
TAB-FULL:v8p114/r11.claim: They reject non-eating as a training condition, reasoning that a predator is trained through eating as part of its discipline.
TAB-FULL:v8p114/r11.anchor: وليس من شرط تعليم ذلك أن لا يأكل من الصيد، قالوا: وكيف يجوز أن يكون ذلك من شرطه وهو يؤدب بأكله

TAB-FULL:v8p116/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p116/r1.speaker: سلمان
TAB-FULL:v8p116/r1.claim: Reports from Salman permit eating the remainder when a trained dog ate two thirds of the prey and one third remained.
TAB-FULL:v8p116/r1.anchor: عن سلمان، قال: «إذا أرسلت كلبك على صيد، وذكرت اسم الله فأكل ثلثيه وبقي ثلثه، فكل ما بقي»

TAB-FULL:v8p116/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p116/r2.speaker: سلمان
TAB-FULL:v8p116/r2.claim: Another report from Salman permits the remainder when a named, trained dog or falcon ate half or two thirds of the prey.
TAB-FULL:v8p116/r2.anchor: عن سعيد بن المسيب، قال: قال سلمان: «إذا أرسلت كلبك المعلم أو بازك، فسميت، فأكل نصفه أو ثلثيه، فكل بقيته»

TAB-FULL:v8p116/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p116/r3.speaker: سعد بن أبي وقاص
TAB-FULL:v8p116/r3.claim: Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ permits eating the prey even when the dog left only a small piece.
TAB-FULL:v8p116/r3.anchor: سأل سعد بن أبي وقاص عن الصيد، يأكل منه الكلب، فقال: «كل وإن لم يبق منه إلا حذية , يعني بضعة»

TAB-FULL:v8p118/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p118/r1.speaker: سعد
TAB-FULL:v8p118/r1.claim: Saʿd says the prey remains lawful even when the dog ate two thirds of it.
TAB-FULL:v8p118/r1.anchor: عن سعد، قال: «كل وإن أكل ثلثيه»

TAB-FULL:v8p118/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p118/r2.speaker: أبو هريرة
TAB-FULL:v8p118/r2.claim: Abū Hurayra permits eating what remains when the dog ate two thirds and left one third.
TAB-FULL:v8p118/r2.anchor: عن أبي هريرة، قال: «إذا أرسلت كلبك فأكل منه، فإن أكل ثلثيه وبقي ثلثه فكل»

TAB-FULL:v8p118/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p118/r3.speaker: سلمان
TAB-FULL:v8p118/r3.claim: Salman permits eating a catch killed by a trained dog even if the dog ate two thirds.
TAB-FULL:v8p118/r3.anchor: عن سلمان، قال: «إذا أرسلت كلبك المعلم فأخذ فقتل، فكل وإن أكل ثلثيه»

TAB-FULL:v8p118/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p118/r4.speaker: عبد الله بن عمر
TAB-FULL:v8p118/r4.claim: Ibn ʿUmar permits all prey held by a trained dog sent with God's name, whether or not the dog ate from it.
TAB-FULL:v8p118/r4.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عمر، قال: «إذا أرسلت كلبك المعلم وذكرت اسم الله فكل ما أمسك عليك، أكل أو لم يأكل»

TAB-FULL:v8p118/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p118/r5.speaker: عبد الله بن عمر
TAB-FULL:v8p118/r5.claim: Ibn ʿUmar also saw no objection to eating prey eaten by a predatory dog.
TAB-FULL:v8p118/r5.anchor: عن ابن عمر: «أنه كان لا يرى بأسا بما أكل الكلب الضاري»

TAB-FULL:v8p121/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p121/r1.speaker: سعد
TAB-FULL:v8p121/r1.claim: Saʿd permits eating prey caught by dogs that eat from it, even if only a small piece remains.
TAB-FULL:v8p121/r1.anchor: عن سعد، قال: قلت: لنا كلاب ضوار يأكلن ويبقين؟ قال: «كل وإن لم يبق إلا بضعة»

TAB-FULL:v8p121/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p121/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v8p121/r2.claim: Al-Ṭabarī defines training as teaching a predator to pursue on release, seek and hold prey for its owner, answer its call, and not flee; eating any of the prey means it is untrained.
TAB-FULL:v8p121/r2.anchor: أن يعلم الرجل جارحه الاستشلاء إذا أشلي على الصيد , وطلبه إياه إذا أغري

TAB-FULL:v8p121/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p121/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v8p121/r3.claim: If the predator ate from its catch, the catch is unlawful unless the owner finds it alive and slaughters it; a dead catch is what the beast ate, which 5:3 forbids.
TAB-FULL:v8p121/r3.anchor: لأنه مما أكله السبع الذي حرمه الله تعالى بقوله: {وما أكل السبع} [المائدة: 3]

TAB-FULL:v8p121/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p121/r4.speaker: عدي بن حاتم
TAB-FULL:v8p121/r4.claim: The Prophet tells ʿAdī that prey eaten by the hunting dog is not to be eaten because the dog held it for itself.
TAB-FULL:v8p121/r4.anchor: عن عدي بن حاتم، أنه سأل النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عن الصيد

TAB-FULL:v8p121#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p121#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v8p121#2/r1.claim: Al-Ṭabarī rejects raising the report permitting the remainder to the Prophet: Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib's hearing from Salmān is unestablished, while reliable transmitters stop it at Salmān.
TAB-FULL:v8p121#2/r1.anchor: هذا خبر في إسناده نظر، فإن سعيدا غير معلوم له سماع من سلمان، والثقات من أهل الآثار يقفون هذا الكلام على سلمان

TAB-FULL:v8p121#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p121#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v8p121#2/r2.claim: Al-Ṭabarī extends the ruling to every hunting predator: if it ate from the prey it was untrained, so its catch is lawful only if the owner slaughtered it.
TAB-FULL:v8p121#2/r2.anchor: فكذلك حكم كل جارحة في أن ما أكل منها من الصيد فغير معلم، لا يحل له أكل صيده إلا أن يدرك ذكاته

TAB-FULL:v8p122/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p122/r1.speaker: بعضهم
TAB-FULL:v8p122/r1.claim: One group reads the command generally: all prey caught by trained dogs and other predators is lawful, whether the animal ate, the prey was slaughtered, or the predator killed it.
TAB-FULL:v8p122/r1.anchor: المعلمة من الصيد الحلال أكله، أكل منه الجارح والكلاب أو لم يأكل

TAB-FULL:v8p122/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p122/r2.speaker: آخرون
TAB-FULL:v8p122/r2.claim: Another group reads the command narrowly: only the portion held for the owner is lawful; what remains after the predator ate part was held for itself.
TAB-FULL:v8p122/r2.anchor: فإن أكلت الجوارح منه بعضا وأمسكت بعضا، فالذي أمسكت منه غير جائز أكله

TAB-FULL:v8p122/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p122/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v8p122/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says to eat what the predators killed, but not prey they both killed and ate; if they held it alive, slaughter it.
TAB-FULL:v8p122/r3.anchor: وكان ابن عباس يقول: إن قتل وأكل فلا تأكل، وإن أمسك فأدركته حيا فذكه

TAB-FULL:v8p122/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p122/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v8p122/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says not to eat a trained dog's prey if the dog ate before its owner arrived to slaughter it.
TAB-FULL:v8p122/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قال: «إن أكل المعلم من الكلاب من صيده قبل أن يأتيه صاحبه فيدرك ذكاته، فلا يأكل من صيده»

TAB-FULL:v8p122/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p122/r5.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v8p122/r5.claim: Al-Suddī says a dog-caught animal is lawful if killed without being eaten; if the dog ate, it held the prey for itself and was not trained.

TAB-FULL:v8p125/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p125/r1.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v8p125/r1.claim: Qatāda says game caught or killed by a trained dog, bird, or arrow is lawful when God's name was spoken at release.

TAB-FULL:v8p125/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p125/r2.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v8p125/r2.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says a named, trained dog's catch is lawful whether it held or killed the prey, but not if it ate, since it held it for itself.
TAB-FULL:v8p125/r2.anchor: سمعت الضحاك، يقول: «إذا أرسلت كلبك المعلم فذكرت اسم الله حين ترسله فأمسك أو قتل فهو حلال

TAB-FULL:v8p126/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p126/r1.speaker: عدي
TAB-FULL:v8p126/r1.claim: ʿAdī reports the Prophet's instruction to name God when releasing a dog and not to eat a catch the dog ate, because it held it for itself.
TAB-FULL:v8p126/r1.anchor: عن عدي، قوله: {فكلوا مما أمسكن عليكم} [المائدة: 4]

TAB-FULL:v8p126/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p126/r2.speaker: نحويي البصرة
TAB-FULL:v8p126/r2.claim: Some Basran grammarians hold that min in the phrase is inserted without meaning, as in idioms such as ‘there was some rain’; they compare 2:271 and 24:43.
TAB-FULL:v8p126/r2.anchor: قال بعض نحويي البصرة حين دخلت من في هذا الموضع لغير معنى، كما تدخله العرب في قولهم: كان من مطر، وكان من حديث

TAB-FULL:v8p126/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p126/r3.speaker: بعض أهل العربية
TAB-FULL:v8p126/r3.claim: Other grammarians reject meaningless min: it marks partitive meaning; they read 2:271 as forgiving some sins and 24:43 as sending hail like mountains, with min omitted before the explanatory ‘hail.’
TAB-FULL:v8p126/r3.anchor: وكان غيره من أهل العربية ينكر ذلك ويقول: لم تدخل من إلا لمعنى مفهوم لا يجوز الكلام ولا يصلح إلا به، وذلك أنها دالة على التبعيض

TAB-FULL:v8p126/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p126/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v8p126/r4.claim: Al-Ṭabarī says min always contributes meaning, though context can license its omission; here it is partitive, distinguishing lawful flesh from forbidden entrails, blood, and similar impurities.
TAB-FULL:v8p126/r4.anchor: ومعنى دخولها في قوله: {فكلوا مما أمسكن عليكم} [المائدة: 4] للتبعيض

TAB-FULL:v8p128/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p128/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v8p128/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says to say ‘In God's name’ when releasing the hunting animal; forgetting causes no blame.
TAB-FULL:v8p128/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {واذكروا اسم الله عليه} [المائدة: 4]

TAB-FULL:v8p128/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p128/r2.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v8p128/r2.claim: Al-Suddī says to pronounce God's name as the hunting animal is released toward prey.
TAB-FULL:v8p128/r2.anchor: عن السدي، قوله: {واذكروا اسم الله عليه} [المائدة: 4]

TAB-FULL:v8p128#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p128#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v8p128#2/r1.claim: Al-Ṭabarī warns against eating game or meat hunted or slaughtered by idolaters, idol worshipers, and people who do not affirm God's unity.
TAB-FULL:v8p128#2/r1.anchor: مما صاده أهل الأوثان وعبدة الأصنام ومن لم يوحد الله من خلقه

TAB-FULL:v8p128#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p128#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v8p128#2/r2.claim: God's accounting is swift because he preserves every deed and knows nothing is hidden; he repays each person for obedience or disobedience.
TAB-FULL:v8p128#2/r2.anchor: اعلموا أن الله سريع حسابه لمن حاسبه على نعمته عليه منكم وشكر الشاكر منكم ربه

TABATABAI:5:4-5/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:4-5/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:4-5/r1.claim: The open-ended question receives a general criterion: anything ordinary understanding regards as wholesome is lawful, since unrestricted wording is read according to familiar usage.
TABATABAI:5:4-5/r1.anchor: سؤال مطلق أجيب عنه بجواب عام مطلق فيه إعطاء الضابط الكلي الذي يميز الحلال من الحرام

TABATABAI:5:4-5/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:4-5/r2.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:5:4-5/r2.claim: One parsing treats the trained-predator phrase as coordinated with the syntactic position of wholesome foods, with an omitted word meaning the game of trained predators.
TABATABAI:5:4-5/r2.anchor: قيل إن الكلام معطوف على موضع الطيبات أي وأحل لكم ما علمتم من الجوارح أي صيد ما علمتم من الجوارح

TABATABAI:5:4-5/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:4-5/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:4-5/r3.claim: The apparent syntax coordinates the whole clause with the first clause; ما is conditional and the command to eat what the animals catch is its result, requiring no ellipsis.
TABATABAI:5:4-5/r3.anchor: والظاهر أن الجملة معطوفة على موضع الجملة الأولى. و { ما } في قوله { وما علمتم } شرطية وجزاؤها قوله

TABATABAI:5:4-5/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:4-5/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:4-5/r4.claim: Jawāriḥ are hunting birds and beasts, including falcons, hawks, dogs, and cheetahs.
TABATABAI:5:4-5/r4.anchor: والجوارح جمع جارحة وهي التي تكسب الصيد من الطير والسباع كالصقر والبازي والكلاب والفهود

TABATABAI:5:4-5/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:4-5/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:4-5/r5.claim: Mukallibīn refers to training or keeping dogs for hunting and sending them after prey; the qualifier points to a rule specific to hunting dogs, not other predators.
TABATABAI:5:4-5/r5.anchor: وأصل التكليب تعليم الكلاب وتربيتها للصيد أو اتخاذ كلاب الصيد وإرسالها لذلك

TABATABAI:5:4-5/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:4-5/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:4-5/r6.claim: The phrase about what the animals catch for you limits permissibility to prey caught for its owner, rather than for the animal itself.
TABATABAI:5:4-5/r6.anchor: التقييد بالظرف للدلالة على أن الحل محدود بصورة صيدها لصاحبها لا لنفسها

TABATABAI:5:4-5/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:4-5/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:4-5/r7.claim: Naming God over the prey completes the conditions for lawful game alongside trained dogs and a catch made for the hunter.
TABATABAI:5:4-5/r7.anchor: تتميم لشرائط الحل وأن يكون الصيد مع كونه مصطادا بالجوارح ومن طريق التكليب

TABATABAI:5:4-5/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:4-5/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:4-5/r8.claim: If a trained hunting dog kills lawful wild game for its owner before the hunter reaches it, the prey is lawful and the dog's kill counts as ritual slaughter.
TABATABAI:5:4-5/r8.anchor: إذا كانت معلمة واصطادت لكم شيئا من الوحش الذي يحل أكله بالتذكية وقد سميتم عليه فكلوا منه إذا قتلته

TABATABAI:5:4-5/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:4-5/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:4-5/r9.claim: When the dog has not killed the prey, ordinary slaughter with God's name suffices instead of the rule for game killed by the dog.
TABATABAI:5:4-5/r9.anchor: وأما دون القتل فالتذكية بالذبح والإهلال به لله يغني عن هذا الحكم

TABATABAI:5:4-5/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:4-5/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:4-5/r10.claim: The warning to fear God cautions against excessive killing or hunting for amusement and arrogance; God swiftly requites injustice, including cruelty to animals.
TABATABAI:5:4-5/r10.anchor: حتى لا يكون الاصطياد إسرافا في القتل، ولا عن تله وتجبر كما في صيد اللهو ونحوه فإن الله سريع الحساب

TABATABAI:5:4-5#7/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:4-5#7/r7.speaker: عكرمة
TABATABAI:5:4-5#7/r7.claim: ʿIkrima reports that when the Prophet sent Rāfiʿ to kill dogs, men came and asked what was lawful for them, prompting the revelation of 5:4.
TABATABAI:5:4-5#7/r7.anchor: أخرج ابن جرير عن عكرمة إن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بعث رافع في قتل الكلاب

TABATABAI:5:4-5#7/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:4-5#7/r8.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
TABATABAI:5:4-5#7/r8.claim: Muḥammad b. Kaʿb al-Quraẓī reports that after the Prophet ordered dogs killed, people asked what was lawful from this kind of animal and 5:4 was revealed.
TABATABAI:5:4-5#7/r8.anchor: أخرج ابن جرير عن محمد بن كعب القرظي قال لما أمر النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بقتل الكلاب

TABATABAI:5:4-5#7/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:4-5#7/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:4-5#7/r9.claim: The author says the two reports explain one another but do not fit the verse's broad question and answer; the people likely asked about uses of dogs such as hunting, then received a general criterion and a specific ruling.
TABATABAI:5:4-5#7/r9.anchor: الروايتان يشرح بعضهما بعضا، فالمراد السؤال عما يحل لهم من الكلاب من حيث اتخاذها واستعمالها في مآرب مختلفة كالصيد ونحوه

TABATABAI:5:4-5#8/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:4-5#8/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:4-5#8/r1.claim: In the dog reports, “this kind” means the species of dogs, as the accompanying narration explains.
TABATABAI:5:4-5#8/r1.anchor: والمراد بالأمة المسؤول عنها في الرواية نوع الكلاب على ما تفسره الرواية الآية

TABATABAI:5:4-5#8/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:4-5#8/r2.speaker: أبو رافع
TABATABAI:5:4-5#8/r2.claim: Abū Rāfiʿ reports the story of Gabriel delaying entry because of a puppy, the order to kill dogs in Medina, and the people's question that led to the verse; al-Ḥākim authenticated the report.
TABATABAI:5:4-5#8/r2.anchor: وفيه أخرج الفارابي وابن جرير وابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم والطبراني والحاكم - وصححه - والبيهقي في سننه عن أبي رافع قال جاء جبرئيل

TABATABAI:5:4-5#8/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:4-5#8/r3.speaker: رسول الله
TABATABAI:5:4-5#8/r3.claim: The Prophet says game caught for its owner by a released dog is edible when God's name was invoked, provided the dog did not eat from it.
TABATABAI:5:4-5#8/r3.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

TABATABAI:5:4-5#8/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:4-5#8/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:4-5#8/r4.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī calls the Gabriel story strange and the report confused: it claims Gabriel refused entry because of a puppy, conflicts with the verse's broad wording and syntax, and seems fabricated.
TABATABAI:5:4-5#8/r4.anchor: على أنها لا تنطبق على ظاهر الآية من إطلاق السؤال والجواب، والعطف الذي في قوله { وما علمتم من الجوارح }

TABATABAI:5:4-5#8/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:4-5#8/r5.speaker: عامر
TABATABAI:5:4-5#8/r5.claim: ʿĀmir reports that ʿAdī b. Ḥātim asked the Prophet about dog hunting and that the verse's training instruction was revealed after the Prophet could not answer.
TABATABAI:5:4-5#8/r5.anchor: عن عامر إن عدي بن حاتم الطائي أتى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فسأله عن صيد الكلاب

TABATABAI:5:4-5#8/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:4-5#8/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:4-5#8/r6.claim: The author reads these reports as imperfect applications: people discussed hunting dogs, then asked for a general distinction between lawful and unlawful, answered first by the general wholesome-food rule and then specifically.
TABATABAI:5:4-5#8/r6.anchor: الظاهر أنهم ذكروا له صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم صيد الكلاب ثم سألوه عن ضابط كلي في تمييز الحلال من الحرام

TABATABAI:5:4-5#8/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:4-5#8/r7.speaker: أبو عبد الله
TABATABAI:5:4-5#8/r7.claim: Abū ʿAbd Allāh says that in ʿAlī's book, the trained jawāriḥ in 5:4 are dogs; al-ʿAyyāshī transmits the same explanation from Samāʿa b. Mihrān.
TABATABAI:5:4-5#8/r7.anchor: عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام قال في كتاب علي عليه السلام في قوله عز وجل { وما علمتم من الجوارح مكلبين } قال هي الكلاب

TABATABAI:5:4-5#9/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:4-5#9/r1.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
TABATABAI:5:4-5#9/r1.claim: He says his father issued rulings cautiously and feared judgments about hawk and falcon prey.
TABATABAI:5:4-5#9/r1.anchor: قال أبو عبد الله عليه السلام كان أبي يفتي وكان يتقي ونحن نخاف في صيد البزاة والصقور

TABATABAI:5:4-5#9/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:4-5#9/r2.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
TABATABAI:5:4-5#9/r2.claim: He says hawk and falcon prey is now lawful only if its ritual slaughter is reached, since the verse's trained game animals are dogs.
TABATABAI:5:4-5#9/r2.anchor: فأما الآن فإنا لا نخاف ولا يحل صيدها إلا أن تدرك ذكاته

TABATABAI:5:4-5#9/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:4-5#9/r3.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
TABATABAI:5:4-5#9/r3.claim: Asked about hawks, falcons, cheetahs, and dogs, he allows eating only what is ritually slaughtered, except a dog’s catch, which may be eaten even if it killed the prey.
TABATABAI:5:4-5#9/r3.anchor: عن أبي بكر الحضرمي عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام، قال سألته عن صيد البزاة والصقور والفهود والكلاب

TABATABAI:5:4-5#9/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:4-5#9/r4.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
TABATABAI:5:4-5#9/r4.claim: Other predatory animals hold prey for themselves, whereas a trained dog holds it for its owner.
TABATABAI:5:4-5#9/r4.anchor: كل شيء من السباع يمسك الصيد على نفسها إلا الكلاب معلمة؟ فإنها تمسك على صاحبها

TABATABAI:5:4-5#9/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:4-5#9/r5.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
TABATABAI:5:4-5#9/r5.claim: When releasing the dog, one should pronounce God's name; that invocation serves as its ritual slaughter.
TABATABAI:5:4-5#9/r5.anchor: وإذا أرسلت الكلب فاذكر اسم الله عليه فهو ذكاته

TABATABAI:5:4-5#9/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:4-5#9/r6.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
TABATABAI:5:4-5#9/r6.claim: Abu ʿUbayda reports that a trained dog released with God's name may be eaten from even if it kills before the hunter reaches it.
TABATABAI:5:4-5#9/r6.anchor: عن أبي عبيدة عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام عن الرجل سرح الكلب المعلم، ويسمي إذا سرحه، قال يأكل مما أمسكن عليه وإن أدركه وقتله

TABATABAI:5:4-5#9/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:4-5#9/r7.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
TABATABAI:5:4-5#9/r7.claim: The same report forbids eating when an untrained dog joined the trained dog's catch.
TABATABAI:5:4-5#9/r7.anchor: وإن وجد معه كلب غير معلم فلا تأكل منه

TABATABAI:5:4-5#9/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:4-5#9/r8.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
TABATABAI:5:4-5#9/r8.claim: Hawk, falcon, and eagle prey is edible only if ritual slaughter is reached; a cheetah is not like a dog, and only dogs count as trained hunting animals here.
TABATABAI:5:4-5#9/r8.anchor: قلت فالصقور والعقاب والبازي؟ قال إن أدركت ذكاته فكل منه

TABATABAI:5:4-5#9/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:4-5#9/r9.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
TABATABAI:5:4-5#9/r9.claim: One may eat a dog's catch if the dog did not eat from it; if the dog ate before the hunter reached it, the catch is forbidden.
TABATABAI:5:4-5#9/r9.anchor: قال لا بأس بأكل ما أمسك الكلب مما لم يأكل الكلب منه

TABATABAI:5:4-5#9/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:4-5#9/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:4-5#9/r10.claim: The verse itself supports limiting lawful prey killed before the hunter arrives to dogs and excluding a catch shared with an untrained dog.
TABATABAI:5:4-5#9/r10.anchor: والخصوصيات المأخوذة في الروايات كاختصاص الحل عند القتل بصيد الكلب لقوله تعالى { مكلبين } وقوله { مما أمسكن عليكم }

TABATABAI:5:4-5#9/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:4-5#9/r11.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
TABATABAI:5:4-5#9/r11.claim: A Muslim may train and release a Magian's dog while invoking God's name; its catch is permitted because it is trained.
TABATABAI:5:4-5#9/r11.anchor: عن حريز عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام قال سئل عن كلب المجوس يكلبه المسلم ويسمي ويرسله قال نعم إنه مكلب إذا ذكر اسم الله عليه فلا بأس

TABATABAI:5:4-5#9/r12.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:4-5#9/r12.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:4-5#9/r12.claim: The report applies the verse's unrestricted wording about trained hunting animals.
TABATABAI:5:4-5#9/r12.anchor: أقول وفيه الأخذ باطلاق قوله { مكلبين }

TABATABAI:5:4-5#9/r13.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:4-5#9/r13.speaker: ابن عباس
TABATABAI:5:4-5#9/r13.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says not to eat prey from an animal trained by a Magian, even if a Muslim releases it and invokes God's name, because the training came from a Magian.
TABATABAI:5:4-5#9/r13.anchor: عن ابن عباس في المسلم يأخذ كلب المجوسي المعلم أو بازه أو صقره مما علمه المجوسي فيرسله فيأخذه قال لا تأكله وإن سميت

TABATABAI:5:4-5#9/r14.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:4-5#9/r14.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:4-5#9/r14.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī calls Ibn ʿAbbās's inference weak: God's teaching of animal training is not exclusive to Muslims.
TABATABAI:5:4-5#9/r14.anchor: وضعفه ظاهر، فإن الخطاب في قوله { مما علمكم الله } وإن كان متوجها إلى المؤمنين ظاهرا

TABATABAI:5:4-5#10/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:4-5#10/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:4-5#10/r1.claim: Training by a Muslim has no special status: a trained dog may belong to a Muslim or non-Muslim, just as its trainer may be either.
TABATABAI:5:4-5#10/r1.anchor: فلا فرق في الكلب المعلم بين أن يكون معلمه مسلما أو غير مسلم كما لا فرق من جهة الملك بين كونه مملوكا لمسلم ومملوكا لغيره

ZAJJAJ:v2p149/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p149/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p149/r1.claim: One parse treats ما as an interrogative noun and ذا as its predicate, with أحل modifying ما: 'what thing was made lawful for them?'
ZAJJAJ:v2p149/r1.anchor: موضع " ما " رفع، إن شئت جعلتها وحدها اسما، ويكون خبرها قوله:

ZAJJAJ:v2p149/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p149/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p149/r2.claim: Alternatively, ما and ذا form one interrogative noun in the nominative, with أحل لهم as its predicate; it has the same meaning.
ZAJJAJ:v2p149/r2.anchor: وجائز أن تكون " ما "، و " ذا "، اسما واحدا، وهي أيضا رفع بالابتداء

ZAJJAJ:v2p149/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p149/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p149/r3.claim: The pure things are everything whose prohibition is not found in the Book or Sunna.
ZAJJAJ:v2p149/r3.anchor: فالطيبات كل شيء لم يأت تحريمه في كتاب ولا سنة،

ZAJJAJ:v2p149/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p149/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p149/r4.claim: The question concerned game, though the word صيد is omitted before 'what you trained' because the context supplies it; similarly, 'ask the town' means ask its people.
ZAJJAJ:v2p149/r4.anchor: والكلام يدل على أنهم سألوا عن الصيد فيما سألوا عنه، ولكن حذف ذكر صيد

ZAJJAJ:v2p149/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p149/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p149/r5.claim: مكلبين means in a state of hunting with dogs; مُكَلِّب and كِلَاب describe a person who hunts with dogs.
ZAJJAJ:v2p149/r5.anchor: أي في هذه الحال يقال رجل مكلب، وكلاب، أي صاحب صيد

ZAJJAJ:v2p149/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p149/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p149/r6.claim: A trained dog's kill is lawful without slaughter if the hunter sent it and pronounced God's name over the prey; Zajjaj says people agree on this.
ZAJJAJ:v2p149/r6.anchor: فإذا أرسل المرسل كلب الصيد فصاد فقتل صيده، وقد ذكر الصائد اسم الله على الصيد

ZAJJAJ:v2p150/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p150/r1.speaker: بعضهم
ZAJJAJ:v2p150/r1.claim: Some jurists permit eating the prey when the trained animal has eaten from it.
ZAJJAJ:v2p150/r1.anchor:
فاختلف الفقهاء فيه إذا أكل من الصيد، فقال بعضهم يؤكل (منه) وإن
أكل منه

ZAJJAJ:v2p150/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p150/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p150/r2.claim: Arabic usage allows both cases: a hunting animal may hold prey without eating it, or may eat from it.
ZAJJAJ:v2p150/r2.anchor:
وكل ذلك في اللغة غير ممتنع لأنه قد يمسك الصيد إذا قتله ولم
يأكل منه، وقد يمسك وقد أكل منه

ZAJJAJ:v2p150/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p150/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p150/r3.claim: Training the hunting animals means disciplining them to hold prey for their owners.
ZAJJAJ:v2p150/r3.anchor: أي تؤدبونهن أن يمسكن الصيد عليكم

ZAJJAJ:v2p150/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p150/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p150/r4.claim: Prey that disappears and is later found dead does not count as held; the hadith says to eat what you saw killed and leave what disappeared.
ZAJJAJ:v2p150/r4.anchor:
فإن غاب الصيد فمات فإنه
غير ممسك. وفي الحديث: " كل ما أصميت ودع ما أنميت

ZAJJAJ:v2p150/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p150/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p150/r5.claim: The lexical root of aṣmā derives from speed and lightness.
ZAJJAJ:v2p150/r5.anchor: وأصل الصميان في اللغة السرعة والخفة

ZAJJAJ:v2p150/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p150/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p150/r6.claim: Aṣmā is prey killed by one's hunt while visible, so the hunter knows it died from that strike.
ZAJJAJ:v2p150/r6.anchor:
كل ما أصميت أي ما قتلته بصيدك وأنت تراه أسرع في
الموت

ZAJJAJ:v2p150/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p150/r7.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p150/r7.claim: Anmā is prey that goes out of sight and dies, leaving uncertainty whether the hunt or another cause killed it.
ZAJJAJ:v2p150/r7.anchor: ما غاب عنك فمات ولم تره، فلست تدري أمات بصيدك أم عرض له عارض آخر فقتله

ZAJJAJ:v2p150/r8.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p150/r8.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p150/r8.claim: The verbs distinguish an arrow that has gone on with its shaft in the quarry from one shot and then gone on with its shaft.
ZAJJAJ:v2p150/r8.anchor: يقال نمت الرمية إذا مضت والسهم فيها، وأنميت الرمية إذا رميتها فمضت والسهم فيها

ZAJJAJ:v2p150/r9.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p150/r9.speaker: امرؤ القيس
ZAJJAJ:v2p150/r9.claim: The phrase تنمي occurs in Imruʾ al-Qays's poetic example in the discussion of the hunting verb.
ZAJJAJ:v2p150/r9.anchor:
قال امرؤ القيس:
فهو لا تنمي رميته. . . ما له لا عد من نفره

ZAJJAJ:v2p150/r10.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p150/r10.speaker: الحرث بن وعلة الشيباني
ZAJJAJ:v2p150/r10.claim: Al-Ḥārith ibn Waʿla's line uses تصمي and تنمي together as hunting terms.
ZAJJAJ:v2p150/r10.anchor:
وقال الحرث بن وعلة الشيباني: (
قالت سليمى قد غنيت فتى. . . فالآن لا تصمي ولا تنمي

TABRISI:5:4/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:4/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:5:4/r1.claim: The common reading is mukallibīn with a doubled lām; Ibn Masʿud and al-Hasan are reported to read it with a light lām.
TABRISI:5:4/r1.anchor: المشهور في القراءة مكلبين بالتشديد وروي عن ابن مسعود والحسن مكلبين بالتخفيف

TABRISI:5:4/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:4/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:5:4/r2.claim: Iklāb means inciting a dog to hunt and training it; mukallib can mean someone with many dogs or a dog hunter and trainer.
TABRISI:5:4/r2.anchor: إكلاب الكلب هو إغراؤه بالصيد وإيساده

TABRISI:5:4/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:4/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:5:4/r3.claim: Al-ṭayyibāt means lawful things, though it is also glossed as pleasurable; jawāriḥ are hunting birds and predators that earn food for their owners.
TABRISI:5:4/r3.anchor: الطيب: هو الحلال وقيل: هو المستلذ والجوارح الكواسب من الطير والسباع

TABRISI:5:4/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:4/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:5:4/r4.claim: A line by al-Aʿshā uses jāriḥ for one who acquires; the poet’s line explains the word as earning.
TABRISI:5:4/r4.anchor: تذكر الجارح ما كان اجترح أي: اكتسب

TABRISI:5:4/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:4/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:5:4/r5.claim: Mādhā aḥilla lahum has two parses: mā alone may be a noun with dhā as its predicate, or mādhā may be one subject with aḥilla as its predicate.
TABRISI:5:4/r5.anchor: { ماذا أحل لهم } يحتمل أن يكون ما وحدها اسما وخبرها قوله ذا

TABRISI:5:4/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:4/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:5:4/r6.claim: Mukallibīn is circumstantial, and tuʿallimūnahunna is another circumstantial phrase attached to it.
TABRISI:5:4/r6.anchor: { ومكلبين } نصب على الحال أي وما علمتم من الجوارح

TABRISI:5:4/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:4/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:5:4/r7.claim: One grammatical view treats min in “what they catch for you” as extra, making all their catch permitted, as in the cited verse.
TABRISI:5:4/r7.anchor: قيل: إن من هنا زائدة لأن جميع ما يمسكه مباح كقوله:

TABRISI:5:4/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:4/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:5:4/r8.claim: Another view treats min as partitive: only the permitted portion is eaten, since a catch includes forbidden blood, offal, and glands.
TABRISI:5:4/r8.anchor: وقيل إن من للتبعيض لأنه لا يجوز أن يؤكل جميع ما يمسكه الكلب

TABRISI:5:4/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:4/r9.speaker: أبو رافع
TABRISI:5:4/r9.claim: Abu Rafiʿ reports that Gabriel would not enter a house with a dog; after the Prophet ordered Medina’s dogs killed, a woman’s dog was first spared, then killed on the Prophet’s order.
TABRISI:5:4/r9.anchor: عن أبي رافع قال: جاء جبرائيل إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يستأذن عليه فأذن له

TABRISI:5:4/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:4/r10.speaker: أبو رافع
TABRISI:5:4/r10.claim: When people asked what was lawful from the animals whose dogs they had been ordered to kill, the Prophet was silent and this verse was revealed; useful dogs were then permitted, while harmful or useless dogs were forbidden or killed.
TABRISI:5:4/r10.anchor: ماذا يحل لنا من هذه الأمة التي أمرت بقتل كلبها فسكت رسول الله فأنزل الآية

TABRISI:5:4/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:4/r11.speaker: أبو حمزة الثمالي، الحكم بن ظهيرة
TABRISI:5:4/r11.claim: Abu Hamza al-Thumali and al-Hakam ibn Zahir report that Zayd al-Khayl and ʿAdi ibn Hatim asked about six dogs that caught wild cattle and gazelles, some alive and some dead; the verse allowed eating what they caught.
TABRISI:5:4/r11.anchor: إن فينا رجلين لهما ستة أكلب تأخذ بقرة الوحش والظباء فمنها ما يدرك ذكاته ومنها ما يموت

TABRISI:5:4#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:4#2/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:5:4#2/r1.claim: The question asks what foods and meals, or according to another view what game and slaughtered animals, are lawful.
TABRISI:5:4#2/r1.anchor: معناه أي شيء أحل لهم أي يستخبرك المؤمنون ما الذي أحل لهم من المطاعم والمآكل

TABRISI:5:4#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:4#2/r2.speaker: أبو علي الجبائي، أبو مسلم
TABRISI:5:4#2/r2.claim: Al-Jubba’i and Abu Muslim say the good things are those God has permitted among foods, slaughter, and game.
TABRISI:5:4#2/r2.anchor: وهي الحلال الذي أذن لكم ربكم في أكله من المأكولات والذبائح والصيد عن أبي علي الجبائي وأبي مسلم

TABRISI:5:4#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:4#2/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:5:4#2/r3.claim: The author prefers defining good things as anything neither scripture nor Sunna has forbidden, since things remain permitted until a legal prohibition appears.
TABRISI:5:4#2/r3.anchor: مما لم يرد بتحريمه كتاب ولا سنة وهذا أولى لما ورد أن الأشياء كلها على الإطلاق والإباحة حتى يرد الشرع بالتحريم

TABRISI:5:4#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:4#2/r4.speaker: البلخي
TABRISI:5:4#2/r4.claim: Al-Balkhi interprets the good things as whatever people find pleasurable.

TABRISI:5:4#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:4#2/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:5:4#2/r5.claim: The phrase also makes the catch of trained hunting birds and beasts lawful, with “catch” supplying the omitted noun.
TABRISI:5:4#2/r5.anchor: أي وأحل لكم أيضا مع ذلك صيد ما علمتم من الجوارح أي الكواسب من سباع الطير والبهائم

TABRISI:5:4#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:4#2/r6.speaker: ابن عمر، الضحاك، السدي
TABRISI:5:4#2/r6.claim: Ibn Umar, al-Dahhak, and al-Suddi restrict jawāriḥ here to dogs; this is also the view transmitted from the Imams.
TABRISI:5:4#2/r6.anchor: وقيل: الجوارح هي الكلاب فقط عن ابن عمر والضحاك والسدي وهو المروي عن أئمتنا ع

TABRISI:5:4#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:4#2/r7.speaker: أبو عبد الله
TABRISI:5:4#2/r7.claim: Abu Abdillah rules that game caught by falcons, hawks, and leopards must be ritually slaughtered, while a dog’s kill may be eaten because trained dogs hold prey for their owners.
TABRISI:5:4#2/r7.anchor: سألته عن صيد البزاة والصقور والفهود والكلاب فقال: لا تأكل إلا ما ذكيت إلا الكلاب

TABRISI:5:4#2/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:4#2/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:5:4#2/r8.claim: The dog-only interpretation is supported by mukallibīn: it means dog hunters or those who train dogs.
TABRISI:5:4#2/r8.anchor: ويؤيد هذا المذهب ما يأتي بعد من قوله { مكلبين } أي أصحاب الصيد بالكلاب

TABRISI:5:4#2/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:4#2/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:5:4#2/r9.claim: Training hunting animals teaches them through God-given reason to distinguish trained from untrained; game caught by an untrained dog is unlawful unless slaughtered while alive.
TABRISI:5:4#2/r9.anchor: حتى يصرن معلمة مما ألهمكم الله بعقولكم حتى ميزتم بين المعلم وغير المعلم

TABRISI:5:4#2/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:4#2/r10.speaker: السدي
TABRISI:5:4#2/r10.claim: Al-Suddi glosses “teach them from what God taught you” as “teach them as God taught you”; the author rejects this because min does not mean kāf and the meanings are not close.
TABRISI:5:4#2/r10.anchor: وقيل: معناه { تعلمونهن } كما علمكم الله عن السدي وهذا بعيد لأن من بمعنى الكاف لا يعرف في اللغة

TABRISI:5:4#2/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:4#2/r11.speaker: سعد بن أبي وقاص، سليمان، ابن عمر
TABRISI:5:4#2/r11.claim: A trained dog rushes after prey when released, holds it for its owner, answers when called, and does not flee; repeated performance makes it trained.
TABRISI:5:4#2/r11.anchor: فإذا توالى منه ذلك كان معلما عن سعد بن أبي وقاص وسليمان وابن عمر

TABRISI:5:4#3/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:4#3/r1.speaker: ابن عباس، عدي بن حاتم، عطاء، الشعبي، طاوس، السدي
TABRISI:5:4#3/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas, ʿAdi ibn Hatim, Ata, al-Shaʿbi, Tawus, and al-Suddi add that a trained dog must not eat the prey.
TABRISI:5:4#3/r1.anchor: وقيل: هو ما ذكرناه كله وإن لا يأكل منه عن ابن عباس وعدي بن حاتم وعطاء والشعبي وطاوس والسدي

TABRISI:5:4#3/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:4#3/r2.speaker: عدي بن حاتم
TABRISI:5:4#3/r2.claim: ʿAdi ibn Hatim transmits the Prophet’s instruction not to eat game a dog has eaten, because it caught it for itself.
TABRISI:5:4#3/r2.anchor: فروى عدي بن حاتم عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال:

TABRISI:5:4#3/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:4#3/r3.speaker: أبو يوسف، محمد
TABRISI:5:4#3/r3.claim: Abu Yusuf and Muhammad set three successful instances as the threshold for a dog to count as trained.
TABRISI:5:4#3/r3.anchor: وقيل: حد التعليم أن يفعل ذلك ثلاث مرات عن أبي يوسف ومحمد

TABRISI:5:4#3/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:4#3/r4.speaker: أصحابنا
TABRISI:5:4#3/r4.claim: The author’s school gives no fixed count: a dog is trained once it displays the stated qualities; a Magian’s dog may be taught and used immediately.
TABRISI:5:4#3/r4.anchor: وقيل: لا حد لتعليم الكلاب وإذا فعل ما قلناه فهو معلم ويدل على ذلك ما رواه أصحابنا أنه إذا أخذ كلب المجوسي فعلمه في الحال فاصطاد به جاز أكل ما يقتله

TABRISI:5:4#3/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:4#3/r5.speaker: أهل البيت
TABRISI:5:4#3/r5.claim: According to the author’s report from the Prophet’s family, only a dog’s catch is lawful without slaughter; other predators must be ritually slaughtered.
TABRISI:5:4#3/r5.anchor: عند أهل البيت لا يحل أكل صيد غير الكلب إلا ما أدرك ذكاته

TABRISI:5:4#3/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:4#3/r6.speaker: سلمان، سعد بن أبي وقاص، ابن عمر
TABRISI:5:4#3/r6.claim: Those allowing other trained predators say an animal is trained by returning to its handler, chasing and catching prey, and answering the call; it remains trained whether or not it eats.
TABRISI:5:4#3/r6.anchor: فإذا كان كذلك كان معملا أكل منه أو لم يأكل روي ذلك عن سلمان وسعد بن أبي وقاص وابن عمر

TABRISI:5:4#3/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:4#3/r7.speaker: علي، الشعبي، عكرمة
TABRISI:5:4#3/r7.claim: Ali, al-Shaʿbi, and ʿIkrima are reported to hold that prey eaten by the hunting animal is not lawful.
TABRISI:5:4#3/r7.anchor: وقال آخرون ما أكل منه فلا يؤكل رووه عن علي ع والشعبي وعكرمة

TABRISI:5:4#3/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:4#3/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:5:4#3/r8.claim: “Eat what they caught for you” supports the view that a dog-eaten catch is unlawful, because the dog caught that prey for itself.
TABRISI:5:4#3/r8.anchor: وهذا يقوي قول من قال: ما أكل منه الكلب لا يجوز أكله لأنه أمسك على نفسه

TABRISI:5:4#3/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:4#3/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:5:4#3/r9.claim: The handler must pronounce God’s name when releasing the dog; if omitted, the kill is unlawful unless the prey is found alive and slaughtered.
TABRISI:5:4#3/r9.anchor: ومن شرط في استباحة ما يقتله الكلب أن يكون صاحبه قد سمى عند إرساله فإذا لم يسم لم يجز له أكله

TABRISI:5:4#3/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:4#3/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:5:4#3/r10.claim: Life is established by movement of an eye, ear, or tail; the animal must then be slaughtered by cutting the windpipe and jugulars.
TABRISI:5:4#3/r10.anchor: وأدنى ما يدرك به ذكاته أن يجده تتحرك عينه أو أذنه أو ذنبه فتذكيته حينئذ بفري بالحلقوم والأوداج

TABRISI:5:4#3/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:4#3/r11.speaker: ابن عباس، الحسن، السدي
TABRISI:5:4#3/r11.claim: Ibn Abbas, al-Hasan, and al-Suddi say to pronounce God’s name before releasing the dog; the author calls this the stronger reading, rather than pronouncing it over slaughter.
TABRISI:5:4#3/r11.anchor: { واذكروا اسم الله عليه } أي قبل الإرسال عن ابن عباس والحسن والسدي

TABRISI:5:4#3/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:4#3/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:5:4#3/r12.claim: The command to pronounce God’s name is clear evidence that naming God is obligatory for game and slaughter.
TABRISI:5:4#3/r12.anchor: وهذا صريح في وجوب التسمية والقول الأول أصح

TABRISI:5:4#3/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:4#3/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:5:4#3/r13.claim: Piety here requires avoiding game caught by an untrained dog, not held for its owner, or taken without God’s name being invoked.
TABRISI:5:4#3/r13.anchor: التي منها أكل صيد الكلب غير المعلم أو ما لم يمسكه عليكم أو ما لم يذكر اسم الله عليه من الصيد والذبائح

THALABI:v4p18/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p18/r1.speaker: ابن عمر
THALABI:v4p18/r1.claim: Ibn ʿUmar reports that the Prophet loudly ordered dogs killed; people killed dogs encountered with a woman coming from Madina, and the Prophet prohibited their sale price.
THALABI:v4p18/r1.anchor: وقال ابن عمر: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول رافعا صوته

THALABI:v4p18/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p18/r2.speaker: أبو هريرة
THALABI:v4p18/r2.claim: Abū Hurayra reports the Prophet's prohibition on the price of dogs, a soothsayer's fee, and a prostitute's earnings.
THALABI:v4p18/r2.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

THALABI:v4p18/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p18/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p18/r3.claim: The Prophet also prohibited keeping dogs and ordered washing a vessel licked by one seven times, the first with soil.
THALABI:v4p18/r3.anchor: ونهى عن اقتنائها وإمساكها وأمر بغسل الإناء من ولوغها سبع مرات أولاهن بالتراب

THALABI:v4p18/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p18/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p18/r4.claim: After people asked what dog-caught prey remained lawful, the verse permitted useful dogs, forbade keeping useless ones, ordered harmful or rabid dogs killed, and spared harmless dogs.
THALABI:v4p18/r4.anchor: فسكت رسول الله فأنزل الله هذه الآية وأذن رسول الله في اقتناء الكلاب التي ينتفع بها

THALABI:v4p18/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p18/r5.speaker: عبد الله بن معقل
THALABI:v4p18/r5.claim: A report from ʿAbd Allāh b. Maʿqil says the Prophet ordered killing solid-black dogs and said keeping dogs except for crops, hunting, or livestock reduces the reward by one qirāṭ daily.
THALABI:v4p18/r5.anchor: وروى الحسن عن عبد الله بن معقل قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

THALABI:v4p18/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p18/r6.speaker: أبو هريرة
THALABI:v4p18/r6.claim: Saʿīd b. al-Musayyib transmits from Abū Hurayra that keeping a dog for other than hunting, livestock, or land costs two qirāṭs of reward daily.
THALABI:v4p18/r6.anchor: عن سعيد بن المسيب عن أبي هريرة عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

THALABI:v4p18/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p18/r7.speaker: عمرو بن عبيد
THALABI:v4p18/r7.claim: Asked why a nonworking dog reduces reward, ʿAmr b. ʿUbayd explains that it barks at guests and frightens petitioners.
THALABI:v4p18/r7.anchor: قال: خذها بحقها إنما ذلك لأنه ينبح على الضيف ويروع السائل

THALABI:v4p19/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p19/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p19/r1.claim: Generous Arabs disliked and condemned tethering dogs because dogs barked at guests and frightened petitioners, and they wanted to kill them.
THALABI:v4p19/r1.anchor: وكانت أسخياء العرب تبغض الكلاب لهذا المعنى وتذم من ربطه وهم بقتله

THALABI:v4p19/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p19/r2.speaker: بعض شعراء البصرة
THALABI:v4p19/r2.claim: An unnamed Basran poet jokes that the dogs at ʿAmmār's lodging nearly devoured the visitors, illustrating the social nuisance of barking dogs.
THALABI:v4p19/r2.anchor: أن بعض شعراء البصرة نزل بعمار فسمع لكلابه نبحا فأنشأ يقول

THALABI:v4p19/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p19/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
THALABI:v4p19/r3.claim: Saʿīd b. Jubayr says the verse was revealed about ʿAdī b. Ḥātim and Zayd al-Khayl, later named Zayd al-Khayr, who asked about hunting dogs and falcons.
THALABI:v4p19/r3.anchor: قال عطاء بن دينار عن سعيد بن جبير في هذه الآية قال

THALABI:v4p19/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p19/r4.speaker: عدي بن حاتم وزيد الخير
THALABI:v4p19/r4.claim: The two hunters asked about prey caught by their dogs and falcons: some animals could be slaughtered in time, while others died before they could be slaughtered, though carrion was forbidden.
THALABI:v4p19/r4.anchor: قالا: يا رسول الله إنا قوم نصيد الكلاب والبزاة

THALABI:v4p19/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p19/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p19/r5.claim: In the verse, الطيبات means lawful slaughtered animals, and ما علمتم means prey caught by trained hunting animals.
THALABI:v4p19/r5.anchor: فنزلت يسئلونك يا محمد ماذا أحل لهم قل: أحل لكم الطيبات يعني الذبائح التي أحلها الله

THALABI:v4p19/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p19/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p19/r6.claim: One view permits only prey reached in time for slaughter and forbids prey killed beyond reach; the author says this position is not acted upon.
THALABI:v4p19/r6.anchor: وما أدركت فما ذكاته فهو لك، وإلا فلا يطعم، وهذا غير معمول به

THALABI:v4p19/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p19/r7.speaker: سائر العلماء
THALABI:v4p19/r7.claim: Other scholars define lawful trained predators broadly as teachable hunting beasts and birds, including big cats, dogs, eagles, falcons, hawks, and saker falcons.
THALABI:v4p19/r7.anchor: وقال سائر العلماء: هي الكواسب من السباع والبهائم والطير مثل النمر والفهد والكلب والعقاب

THALABI:v4p19/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p19/r8.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p19/r8.claim: Predators are called jawāriḥ because they earn their owners' food from prey; the same root describes an earner supporting a family.
THALABI:v4p19/r8.anchor: فسميت جوارح لجرحها أربابها أقواتهم من الصيد أي كسبها

THALABI:v4p19/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p19/r9.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p19/r9.claim: The accusative مكلبين describes the state of hunting with trained dogs; taklīb means inciting or setting the animal onto prey.
THALABI:v4p19/r9.anchor: مكلبين منصوب على الحساب في المعنى وصيد ما علمتم من الجوارح مكلبين إلى هذه الحال

THALABI:v4p19/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p19/r10.speaker: الشاعر
THALABI:v4p19/r10.claim: An unnamed poet's phrase مكلب for a dawn hunter with a grey wolf-like hound supports the trained-hunter sense.
THALABI:v4p19/r10.anchor: قال الشاعر: باكره عند الصباح مكلب … أزل كسرحان القصيمة أغبر

THALABI:v4p19/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p19/r11.speaker: ابن مسعود وأبو زرين والحسن
THALABI:v4p19/r11.claim: Ibn Masʿūd, Abū Zurayn, and al-Ḥasan read مكلبين with a light lām, in the sense of training or urging the hunting animal.
THALABI:v4p19/r11.anchor: قرأ أبن مسعود وأبو زرين والحسن: مكلبين بتخفيف اللام على هذا المعنى

THALABI:v4p19/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p19/r12.speaker: الحسن والقتيبي
THALABI:v4p19/r12.claim: Al-Ḥasan and al-Qutaybī also derive the word from أكلب, meaning someone acquired many dogs; dogs are named because they are most common, while all trained predators are intended.
THALABI:v4p19/r12.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون من قولهم: أكلب الرجل، إذا كثرت كلابه

THALABI:v4p20/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p20/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p20/r1.claim: Training the hunting animals means teaching them the manners of hunting from the knowledge God has taught.
THALABI:v4p20/r1.anchor: تعلمونهن آداب الصيد مما علمكم الله أي من العلم الذي علمكم الله

THALABI:v4p20/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p20/r2.speaker: السدي
THALABI:v4p20/r2.claim: Al-Suddī reads من as meaning 'as': God taught that trained animals should not lie down on prey, bite, kill, or eat it.
THALABI:v4p20/r2.anchor: وقال السدي: من بمعنى الكاف، أي كما علمكم الله

THALABI:v4p20/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p20/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p20/r3.claim: The command to eat what the animals catch is paired with invoking God's name when releasing the animals or hunting beasts.
THALABI:v4p20/r3.anchor: فكلوا مما أمسكن عليكم واذكروا اسم الله عليه عند إرسال البهم والجوارح

THALABI:v4p20#2/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p20#2/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p20#2/r1.claim: A trained animal responds to release, holds prey without eating, answers its call, and does not flee; repeated performance establishes training.
THALABI:v4p20#2/r1.anchor: إذا أرسله صاحبه وأشلاه استشلى وإذا أخذ أمسك ولم يأكل

THALABI:v4p20#2/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p20#2/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p20#2/r2.claim: Prey held without being eaten is lawful; al-Shāfiʿī's more famous and stronger position forbids prey eaten by the animal because it kept the game for itself.
THALABI:v4p20#2/r2.anchor: فإذا أمسك الصيد ولم يأكل منه جاز أكله، وكان حلالا، فإن أكل منه، فللشافعي فيه قولان

THALABI:v4p20#2/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p20#2/r3.speaker: الحسن وطاوس والشعبي وعطاء والسدي
THALABI:v4p20#2/r3.claim: Al-Ḥasan, Ṭāwūs, al-Shaʿbī, ʿAṭāʾ, and al-Suddī share the position that prey eaten by the hunting animal is unlawful.
THALABI:v4p20#2/r3.anchor: وهذا قول الحسن وطاوس والشعبي وعطاء والسدي

THALABI:v4p20#2/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p20#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v4p20#2/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says game eaten by a released dog is carrion because the beast held it for itself and was not trained; he says to beat the dog and not eat the prey.
THALABI:v4p20#2/r4.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: إذا أرسلت الكلب فأكل من صيد فهي ميتة لا يحل أكله

THALABI:v4p20#2/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p20#2/r5.speaker: عدي بن حاتم
THALABI:v4p20#2/r5.claim: In a report from ʿAdī b. Ḥātim, the Prophet says to invoke God when releasing a dog, slaughter prey found alive, eat prey it killed without eating, and avoid prey it ate or that other dogs may have killed.
THALABI:v4p20#2/r5.anchor: يدل عليه ما روى الشعبي عن عدي بن حاتم أنه سأل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن الصيد

THALABI:v4p20#2/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p20#2/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v4p20#2/r6.claim: The same report says to invoke God when shooting an arrow, avoid an animal that died in water because its cause of death is uncertain, and permits eating it if found later with no arrow visible.
THALABI:v4p20#2/r6.anchor: وإذا رميت سهمك فاذكر اسم الله، فإن أدركته فكل، إلا أن تجده وقع في ماء فمات

THALABI:v4p20#2/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p20#2/r7.speaker: سلمان الفارسي وسعد بن أبي وقاص وابن عمر وأبو هريرة
THALABI:v4p20#2/r7.claim: The second Shāfiʿī position permits prey even when the trained animal eats; it is attributed to Salmān, Saʿd b. Abī Waqqāṣ, Ibn ʿUmar, and Abū Hurayra.
THALABI:v4p20#2/r7.anchor: وهو قول سلمان الفارسي، وسعد بن أبي وقاص، وابن عمر، وأبي هريرة

THALABI:v4p20#2/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p20#2/r8.speaker: سعد بن أبي وقاص
THALABI:v4p20#2/r8.claim: Saʿd says his fierce hunting dogs eat from their catch and that one may eat what remains, even if only half or two-thirds is left.
THALABI:v4p20#2/r8.anchor: قال حميد بن عبد الله وسعد ابن أبي وقاص: لنا كلاب ضواري يأكلن ويبقين

THALABI:v4p20#2/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p20#2/r9.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p20#2/r9.claim: The rule applies equally to trained birds and predatory beasts.
THALABI:v4p20#2/r9.anchor: ولا فرق في حمله على ما ذكرنا من الطيور والسباع المعلمة

THALABI:v4p20#2/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p20#2/r10.speaker: ثعلبة الخشني
THALABI:v4p20#2/r10.claim: Thaʿlaba al-Khushanī asks about arrows, trained dogs, and untrained dogs; the Prophet permits what an arrow or trained dog catches with God's name, while an untrained dog's catch is lawful only if reached and slaughtered.
THALABI:v4p20#2/r10.anchor: وروى أبو قلابة عن ثعلبة الخشني: أنه جاء إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: يا رسول الله إن أرضنا أرض صيد

THALABI:v4p21/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p21/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p21/r1.claim: The permitted good things include slaughtered animals; the food of Jews, Christians, and those who joined their religion before Muhammad's mission is lawful, unlike converts after it.
THALABI:v4p21/r1.anchor: اليوم أحل لكم الطيبات يعني الذبائح وطعام الذين أوتوا الكتاب حل لكم يعني ذبائح اليهود والنصارى

THALABI:v4p21/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p21/r2.speaker: ابن عمر
THALABI:v4p21/r2.claim: Ibn ʿUmar, as relayed by Rabīʿa, says not to eat Christian slaughter because Christians invoke Christ; he cites the prohibition on food over which God's name was not mentioned.
THALABI:v4p21/r2.anchor: فقال ربيعة: سمعت ابن عمر يقول: لا تأكلوا ذبائح النصارى، فإنهم يقولون: باسم المسيح

THALABI:v4p21/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p21/r3.speaker: أكثر العلماء
THALABI:v4p21/r3.claim: Most scholars permit a scripturalist's slaughter even when another name is invoked, treating the prohibition as directed at polytheists sacrificing to idols.
THALABI:v4p21/r3.anchor: والقول الثاني: إنه يجوز ذبيحتهم، الكتابي، وإن سمي غير الله فإن هذا مستثنى

THALABI:v4p21/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p21/r4.speaker: الشعبي وعطاء
THALABI:v4p21/r4.claim: Al-Shaʿbī and ʿAṭāʾ permit a Christian's slaughter when the Christian says 'in the name of Christ,' since God allowed their food and knows what they say.
THALABI:v4p21/r4.anchor: قال الشعبي وعطاء: في النصراني يذبح فيقول: باسم المسيح قالا: يحل

THALABI:v4p21/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p21/r5.speaker: الزهري ومكحول
THALABI:v4p21/r5.claim: Al-Zuhrī and Makḥūl say the slaughter of scripturalist worshippers and offerings made for their churches is lawful, citing this verse.
THALABI:v4p21/r5.anchor: وسأل الزهري ومكحول عن ذبائح عبدة أهل الكتاب

THALABI:v4p21/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p21/r6.speaker: الحسن والحرث العكلي
THALABI:v4p21/r6.claim: Al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥārith al-ʿAklī say not to eat if one hears a Jew or Christian name another than God, but to eat if absent; they regard such slaughter as disliked.
THALABI:v4p21/r6.anchor: وقال الحسن والحرث العكلي: ما كنت أسأله عن ذبحه فإنه أحل الله لنا طعامه

THALABI:v4p21/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p21/r7.speaker: علي
THALABI:v4p21/r7.claim: ʿAlī says Jews and Christians should not slaughter Muslims' sacrificial offerings; only a Muslim should slaughter the ritual sacrifice.

ASAD-NOTES:5:4#n12/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:5:4#n12/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:5:4#n12/r1.claim: Forbidden things are not among the good things of life, while anything not expressly forbidden is allowed.
ASAD-NOTES:5:4#n12/r1.anchor: what has been forbidden does not belong to the category of "the good things of life" (at-tayyibat)

ASAD-NOTES:5:4#n12/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:5:4#n12/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:5:4#n12/r2.claim: Asad says the Qur'an forbids only things or actions injurious physically, morally, or socially.
ASAD-NOTES:5:4#n12/r2.anchor: the Qur'an forbids only those things or actions which are injurious to man physically, morally or socially.

ASAD-NOTES:5:4#n13/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:5:4#n13/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:5:4#n13/r1.claim: Mukallib means trained like a hunting dog and applies to any trained hunting animal, including a hound, falcon, or cheetah.
ASAD-NOTES:5:4#n13/r1.anchor: The term mukailib signifies "trained like a [hunting) dog", and is applied to every animal used for hunting

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p259#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p259#2/r1.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p259#2/r1.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr says ʿAdī ibn Ḥātim and Zayd al-Khayl asked the Prophet about game caught by their dogs and falcons, since carrion was forbidden; this verse was revealed in response.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p259#2/r1.anchor: قال سعيد بن جبير: إن عدي بن حاتم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p259#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p259#2/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p259#2/r2.claim: Mādhā can be parsed as a single noun in the nominative, with uḥilla as its predicate; alternatively, mā alone is the noun and dhā is the predicate, with uḥilla as a relative clause, meaning what thing was made lawful.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p259#2/r2.anchor: وقوله تعالى: {ماذا} إن جعلته اسما فهو رفع بالابتداء وخبره (أحل)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p259#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p259#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p259#2/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses the permitted good things as all lawful things.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p259#2/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد من جميع الحلال

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p259#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p259#2/r4.speaker: أهل العلم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p259#2/r4.claim: Scholars say Arabs avoided many things they found repulsive and ate what they enjoyed; Allah permitted what they liked unless revelation prohibited it, including livestock, lizards, jerboas, and rabbits. They treat this as a broad rule: animals Arabs find pleasant are lawful and those they find repugnant are forbidden, in line with al-Aʿrāf 7:157.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p259#2/r4.anchor: قال أهل العلم: كانت العرب تستقذر أشياء كثيرة فلا تأكلها، وتستطيب أشياء فتأكلها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p259#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p259#2/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p259#2/r5.claim: Ṭayyib can mean pleasing or tasty; permitted lawful food is also called good by analogy because both tasty and lawful food are free of harm.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p259#2/r5.anchor: والطيب في اللغة: المستلذ، والحلال المأذون فيه، يسمى أيضا طيبا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p259#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p259#2/r6.speaker: مقاتل والكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p259#2/r6.claim: Muqātil and al-Kalbī interpret the good things as slaughtered animals.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p259#2/r6.anchor: وقال مقاتل والكلبي: المراد بالطيبات الذبائح

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p259#2/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p259#2/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p259#2/r7.claim: The author prefers the broad interpretation of all good lawful things because it covers more and is held by most scholars.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p259#2/r7.anchor: والقول الأول أولى؛ لأنه أعم في التحليل، وعليه أكثر العلماء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p262/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p262/r1.speaker: الزجاج وغيره
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p262/r1.claim: Al-Zajjāj and other scholars understand an omitted word, game: and [game] from trained hunting animals; the next clause about eating what they hold and the question about hunting support the ellipsis, a view shared by all semanticists.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p262/r1.anchor: قال الزجاج وغيره: يريد: وصيد ما علمتم من الجوارح، فحذف الصيد وهو مراد في الكلام

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p262/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p262/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p262/r2.claim: Alternatively, وما علمتم can start a new sentence whose predicate is eat what they hold, yielding sound wording without ellipsis.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p262/r2.anchor: ويجوز أن يقال: قوله تعالى: {وما علمتم} ابتداء كلام وخبره

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p262/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p262/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p262/r3.claim: Jawāriḥ are hunting birds and predatory beasts that acquire prey; the singular is jāriḥa, and a hunting dog counts as one because the root means to earn.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p262/r3.anchor: وأما الجوارح: فهي الكواسب من الطير والسباع ذوات الصيد، والواحدة جارحة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p262/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p262/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p262/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās through ʿAṭāʾ includes hunting birds, dogs, cheetahs, lynxes, raptors such as the falcon and hawk, eagles, and the zamaj; prey killed by these hunters is lawful.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p262/r4.anchor: قال ابن عباس في رواية عطاء: يريد الطير تصيد، والكلاب، والفهود

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p262/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p262/r5.speaker: مجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p262/r5.claim: Layth reports that Mujāhid counted falcons, hawks, cheetahs, and other hunting beasts among the jawāriḥ.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p262/r5.anchor: سئل مجاهد عن الصقر والبازي والفهد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p262/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p262/r6.speaker: ابن عمر والضحاك
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p262/r6.claim: Ibn ʿUmar and al-Ḍaḥḥāk restrict jawāriḥ to dogs and require live prey caught by other animals to be ritually slaughtered; a similar view is related from al-Suddī.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p262/r6.anchor: ابن عمر (¬7) والضحاك أنهما قالا: الجوارح الكلاب دون غيرها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p262/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p262/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p262/r7.claim: The author says the dog-only view is not acted upon.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p264/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p264/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p264/r1.claim: Mukallib is someone who trains dogs to catch game, and a hunter is called mukallib because he trains the dog; a poem illustrates the term.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p264/r1.anchor: المكلب: الذي يعلم الكلاب أخذ الصيد، ويقال للصائد مكلب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p264/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p264/r2.speaker: أهل المعاني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p264/r2.claim: Semanticists say mukallibīn does not prove that only dogs are permitted for hunting, just as calling someone a trainer does not limit the thing trained.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p264/r2.anchor: قال أهل المعاني: وليس في قوله: (مكلبين) دليل على أنه إنما أبيح صيد الكلاب خاصة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p264/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p264/r3.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p264/r3.claim: Al-Kalbī says the hunters train the animals to seek prey and not eat it, just as Allah taught people.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p264/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p264/r4.speaker: العلماء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p264/r4.claim: Scholars define a trained dog as one that obeys when released and urged on, holds rather than eats its catch, answers its call, and does not flee when approached; repeated behavior establishes training.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p264/r4.anchor: قال العلماء: وصفة الكلب المعلم الذي يحل صيده هو أن يكون إذا أرسله صاحبه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p264/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p264/r5.speaker: النحويون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p264/r5.claim: Grammarians take min in مما as partitive: only the meat, not offal or blood, is eaten.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p264/r5.anchor: دخلت (من) في قوله (مما) للتبعيض؛ لأنه إنما أحل أكل بعضه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p264/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p264/r6.speaker: الأخفش
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p264/r6.claim: Al-Akhfash says min is extra here, so the meaning is eat what the animals held.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p264/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p264/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p264/r7.claim: Another grammarian rejects the extra-min reading because min is only extra in negation and questions; in 2:271 it instead marks the source, meaning Allah covers deeds the people want hidden among their sins.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p264/r7.anchor: وقال غيره: هذا خطأ؛ لأن من لا تزاد في الواجب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p264/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p264/r8.speaker: العلماء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p264/r8.claim: If a trained dog wounds and kills prey that the hunter finds dead, it is lawful because the hunter's wound counts as slaughter; the same applies to other trained hunters, arrows, spears, and pointed shafts that wound.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p264/r8.anchor: قال العلماء: إذا كان الضاري وهو الكلب معلما كما وصفنا، ثم صاد صيدا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p264/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p264/r9.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p264/r9.claim: If a broadhead kills by its flat side without wounding and the prey is not caught alive for slaughter, it is forbidden.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p264/r9.anchor: فإن أصابه المعراض بعرضه (فقتله ولم تدرك (¬4)) ذكاته فهو حرام

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p264/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p264/r10.speaker: كثير من العلماء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p264/r10.claim: Many scholars forbid prey a dog smothers by pinning it down without a wound, but the author says analogy permits it because the dog held it for its owner; returning prey unharmed can better show training, which need not involve wounding.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p264/r10.anchor: لم يجز أكله عند كثير من العلماء، والقياس أنه حلال؛ لأنه مما أمسكه على صاحبه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p268/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p268/r1.speaker: الكلبي وغيره من المفسرين
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p268/r1.claim: Al-Kalbī and other exegetes say to mention Allah when releasing the hunting dogs.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p268/r1.anchor: يعني إذا أرسلتم الكلاب. قال الكلبي وغيره من المفسرين

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p268/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p268/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p268/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās through ʿAṭāʾ says to say Allah's name at release; forgetting does not prevent eating, and he connects the believer's and Muslim's names with Allah's names al-Muʾmin and al-Salām.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p268/r2.anchor: وقال ابن عباس في رواية عطاء: {واذكروا اسم الله عليه} إذا أطلقت

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p268/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p268/r3.speaker: الحسن
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p268/r3.claim: Al-Ḥasan permits eating when a believer forgets the basmala at release, since Allah's name is part of his religion, like the knife he uses if he forgets to name Allah at slaughter.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p268/r3.anchor: وقال الحسن: إذا أرسل المؤمن كلبه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p268/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p268/r4.speaker: العلماء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p268/r4.claim: Scholars say it is preferable to slaughter or release hunting animals in Allah's name; if the name is omitted, the meat remains lawful according to a prophetic report that a believer slaughters in Allah's name whether he names Him or not, explaining Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Ḥasan.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p268/r4.anchor: قال العلماء: الأولى الذبح علي اسم الله، وإرسال الجوارح على اسم الله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p268/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p268/r5.speaker: عائشة
