WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p268/r5.claim: ʿĀʾisha asked about game brought by Bedouins when it was unknown whether Allah's name had been said; the Prophet told them to say it themselves and eat.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p268/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p268/r6.speaker: أهل المعاني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p268/r6.claim: Semanticists say the pronoun in عليه refers to the act of releasing the animal, though release is not explicitly mentioned, because context makes it clear.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p268/r6.anchor: قال أهل المعاني: الهاء في قوله: (عليه) تعود إلى الإرسال

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:5:4/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:5:4/r1.speaker: عدي بن حاتم
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:5:4/r1.claim: Adi ibn Hatim asked the Prophet what hunting with dogs and falcons made lawful, since carrion was forbidden; this occasioned the verse.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:5:4/r1.anchor: سأل عدي بن حاتم رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال: إنا نصيد بالكلاب والبزاة

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:5:4/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:5:4/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:5:4/r2.claim: Good things means what Arabs regard as wholesome; this is the basic rule for determining lawful food.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:5:4/r2.anchor: يعين: ما تستطيبه العرب، وهذا هو الأصل في التحليل

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:5:4/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:5:4/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:5:4/r3.claim: Animals Arabs find wholesome, including monitor lizards, jerboas, and rabbits, are lawful, while what they find repugnant is forbidden.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:5:4/r3.anchor: فكل حيوان استطابته العرب، كالضباب، واليرابيع، والأرانب فهو حلال، وما استخبثته العرب فهو حرام

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:5:4/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:5:4/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:5:4/r4.claim: The trained hunting creatures are catchers among birds, dogs, and predatory beasts.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:5:4/r4.anchor: وهي الكواسب من الطير والكلاب والسباع

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:5:4/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:5:4/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:5:4/r5.claim: Mukallibin describes training the hunting animals to hunt.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:5:4/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:5:4/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:5:4/r6.claim: Teaching the animals means disciplining them to pursue prey.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:5:4/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:5:4/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:5:4/r7.claim: One may eat prey the trained animal kills if it does not eat from it; if it eats from the prey, it is apparently forbidden.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:5:4/r7.anchor: وإن قتلن إذا لم يأكلن منه، فإذا أكلن فالظاهر أنه حرام

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:5:4/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:5:4/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:5:4/r8.claim: God's name is mentioned when the hunting animals are released.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:5:4/r8.anchor: واذكروا اسم الله عليه } عند إرسال الجوارح

RAZI-FULL:v1p15#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p15#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p15#2/r1.claim: Razi says this sūra could yield ten thousand useful questions; he added the preface to show that such a number is attainable and not difficult to reach.
RAZI-FULL:v1p15#2/r1.anchor: هذه السورة الكريمة يمكن أن يستنبط من فوائدها ونفائسها عشرة آلاف مسألة فاستبعد هذا بعض الحساد

RAZI-FULL:v1p15#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p15#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p15#2/r2.claim: Seeking refuge in God means seeking protection from every prohibited matter, whether a matter of belief or an act of the limbs.
RAZI-FULL:v1p15#2/r2.anchor: المراد منه الاستعاذة بالله من جميع المنهيات والمحظورات

RAZI-FULL:v1p15#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p15#2/r3.speaker: النبي
RAZI-FULL:v1p15#2/r3.claim: A report Razi calls well known says the community will divide into seventy-three sects, all in the Fire except one; he gives no grading beyond calling it famous.
RAZI-FULL:v1p15#2/r3.anchor: في الخبر المشهور قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم ستفترق أمتي على ثلاث وسبعين فرقة كلهم في النار إلا فرقة واحدة

RAZI-FULL:v1p15#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p15#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p15#2/r4.claim: Razi takes the report to imply that the other seventy-two sects hold false doctrines across many questions: God's essence, attributes, rulings, acts and names, free will, justice, reward, afterlife, promise, status, and imamate.
RAZI-FULL:v1p15#2/r4.anchor: وهذا يدل على أن الاثنتين والسبعين موصوفون بالعقائد الفاسدة والمذاهب الباطلة

RAZI-FULL:v1p15#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p15#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p15#2/r5.claim: Because refuge from a thing requires knowing what it is and knowing its false or evil character, the formula encompasses ten thousand or more or fewer important issues.
RAZI-FULL:v1p15#2/r5.anchor: والاستعاذة من الشيء لا تمكن إلا بعد معرفة المستعاذ منه وإلا بعد معرفة كون ذلك الشيء باطلا وقبيحا

BAQILLANI:v1p200/r1.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p200/r1.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p200/r1.claim: The Qurʾān’s composition does not vary or break down; it has the highest model and excellence.
BAQILLANI:v1p200/r1.anchor: ونظم القرآن لا يتفاوت في شيء ولا يتباين في أمر ولا يختل في حال

BAQILLANI:v1p200/r2.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p200/r2.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p200/r2.claim: The hunting-and-food ruling combines wisdom, remarkable rhetorical movement, and concise choice, displaying inimitability even within one verse.
BAQILLANI:v1p200/r2.anchor: أنت تجد في هذه الآية من الحكمة والتصرف العجيب والنظم البارع الغريب

BAQILLANI:v1p200/r3.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p200/r3.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p200/r3.claim: The Qurʾān handles legal material, including the commands in 7:157 and inheritance passages, with concise eloquence and an arrangement no human can match.
BAQILLANI:v1p200/r3.anchor: أي بارع يقدر على جمع أحكام الفرائض في قدرها من الكلام ثم كيف يقدر على ما فيها من بديع النظم

BAQILLANI:v1p200/r4.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p200/r4.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p200/r4.claim: Passages of argument and monotheism, including the proof from the heavens and earth and declarations of divine unity, display the same inimitable composition.
BAQILLANI:v1p200/r4.anchor: لو كان فيهما آلهة إلا الله لفسدتا

BAQILLANI:v1p200/r5.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p200/r5.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p200/r5.claim: The oath passage about the ranks, divine unity, and guarded heaven integrates successive claims and imagery into a single eloquent sequence.
BAQILLANI:v1p200/r5.anchor: إن إلهكم لواحد رب السماوات والأرض وما بينهما

BURHAN:v1p159/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p159/r3.speaker: قيل
BURHAN:v1p159/r3.claim: It is said the hunting-animal verse concerns ʿAdi ibn Hatim, whose five dogs had proper names.
BURHAN:v1p159/r3.anchor: كان له كلاب [ خمسة ] قد سماها [ بأسماء ] أعلام

BURHAN:v2p222/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p222/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p222/r1.claim: The general ban on carrion is restricted by the trained hunting animal exception, which permits game killed in its mouth.
BURHAN:v2p222/r1.anchor: وهذا عام في جميع الميتات ثم خصة بقوله

BURHAN:v2p48/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p48/r1.speaker: أبو إسحاق الإسفرابيني
BURHAN:v2p48/r1.claim: When two verses conflict, al-Isfarāyīnī says to establish their chronology and treat the later as abrogating the earlier; if chronology is unknown, consensus on using one identifies the abrogating verse. He says no Qurʾanic pair lacks these indicators.

BURHAN:v2p48/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p48/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p48/r2.claim: One proposed priority test uses Meccan and Medinan classification as a chronology cue: exceptions are possible, but most Meccan verses preceded the Hijra, so the Medinan ruling is generally later for specification and priority.
BURHAN:v2p48/r2.anchor: وإن كان يجوز أن تكون المكية نزلت عليه صلى الله عليه وسلم بعد عوده إلى مكة والمدنية قبلها فيقدم الحكم بالآية المدنية

BURHAN:v2p48/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p48/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p48/r4.claim: The prohibition on killing game in the sanctuary is reconciled with the permissibility of trained hunting animals: game caught inside the sanctuary remains prohibited, while game caught outside and brought in alive is excepted.
BURHAN:v2p48/r4.anchor: فجعل النهي فيمن اصطاده في الحرم

BURHAN:v3p444/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p444/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p444/r7.claim: The verse about trained hunting animals is cited as another example in the list of tawriya, without a further gloss in this passage.

BURHAN:v4p47/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p47/r3.speaker: ابن مالك
BURHAN:v4p47/r3.claim: The source also uses ‘Say: lawful to you are the good things’ as a full verbal answer; when the final constituent is explicit, a verb is explicit, supporting an omitted verb in abbreviated answers.
BURHAN:v4p47/r3.anchor: ومما رجح به أيضا تقدير الفعل أنه حيث صرح بالجزء الأخير صرح بالفعل

BURHAN:v4p47/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p47/r4.speaker: ابن يعيش
BURHAN:v4p47/r4.claim: Ibn Yaʿīsh says an explicit verb is better, but the author rejects this: deletion is more common, and it makes a brief reply unambiguously an answer with a restrictive sense.
BURHAN:v4p47/r4.anchor: قال ابن يعيش التصريح بالفعل أجود وليس كما زعم بل الأكثر الحذف

BURHAN:v4p47/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p47/r5.speaker: شهاب الدين بن المرحل
BURHAN:v4p47/r5.claim: Ibn al-Muraḥḥal treats these replies as answering with wording different from the question for a rhetorical point, like the answer about lunar phases; the author says this analysis is questionable.
BURHAN:v4p47/r5.anchor: فكان الشيخ شهاب الدين بن المرحل رحمه الله يجعله من باب

ITQAN:v2p308/r13.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p308/r13.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p308/r13.claim: Al-jawarih includes dogs, cheetahs, falcons, and similar hunting animals.
ITQAN:v2p308/r13.anchor: ﴿ من الجوارح ﴾ الكلاب والفهود والصقور وأشباهها

ITQAN:v2p575#3/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p575#3/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p575#3/r1.claim: Answers generally match the question's sentence form; the verbal answers in 5:4 and 36:79 show that an omitted verb should be estimated before the stated answer.

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p293/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p293/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p293/r1.claim: Poets may independently share broad subjects such as praising courage, generosity, beauty, or a horse’s speed; this agreement is not borrowing.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p293/r1.anchor: أن يقصد كل واحد منهما وصف ممدوحه بالشجاعة والسخاء أو حسن الوجه والبهاء أو وصف فرسه بالسرعة

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p293/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p293/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p293/r2.claim: A poet may establish a quality through a familiar comparison, such as likening courage to a lion or generosity to a sea.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p293/r2.anchor: منها التشبيه بما يوجد هذا الوصف فيه على الوجه البليغ والغاية البعيدة كالتشبيه بالأسد وبالبحر

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p293/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p293/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p293/r3.claim: Poets also infer qualities from characteristic behavior: a composed, smiling warrior or a generous person welcoming petitioners cheerfully.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p293/r3.anchor: ومنها ذكر هيآت تدل على الصفة من حيث كانت لا تكون إلا فيمن له الصفة كوصف الرجل في حال الحرب بالابتسام

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p293/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p293/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p293/r4.claim: Al-Jurjani rejects treating shared praise topics as theft; such accusations mistake common premises, like bravery being praiseworthy, for one poet’s invention.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p293/r4.anchor: فأما الاتفاق في عموم الغرض فما لا يكون الاشتراك فيه داخلا في الأخذ والسرقة والاستمداد والاستعانة

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p293/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p293/r5.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p293/r5.claim: Shared ways of proving a trait, such as lion-courage or sea-generosity comparisons, are common knowledge embedded in reason and custom, regardless of era.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p293/r5.anchor: فإن كان مما اشتراك الناس في معرفته وكان مستقرا في العقول والعادات فإن حكم ذلك

DAMGHANI:v1p235/r2.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p235/r2.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p235/r2.claim: Sarīʿ al-ḥisāb can mean that the reckoning has arrived; the source gives a parallel in al-Baqara.
DAMGHANI:v1p235/r2.anchor: سريع يعني مجيء الحساب قوله سبحانه في سورة المائدة

DAMGHANI:v1p302/r1.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p302/r1.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p302/r1.claim: Al-ṭayyibāt can mean lawful things, including the crops and livestock the pre-Islamic Arabs used.
DAMGHANI:v1p302/r1.anchor: الطيبات الحلال وما كان لاهل الجاهلية من مواشي الحرث والانعام

DAMGHANI:v1p302/r6.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p302/r6.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p302/r6.claim: Al-ṭayyibāt can mean animals slaughtered as food and made lawful for people.
DAMGHANI:v1p302/r6.anchor: يسالونك ماذا احل لهم قل احل لكم الطيبات يعني الذبائح طيبة لهم

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p417/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p417/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p417/r1.claim: Ṭayyibāt is plural of ṭayyib, opposite to foul; it describes what pleases the self, including food and scent, and figuratively what is lawful.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p417/r1.anchor: الطيبات : جمع طيب . والطيب : ضد الخبيث . ويقال : كل ما يلذ للنفس طيب

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p417/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p417/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p417/r5.claim: The verse uses ṭayyibāt for slaughtered animals.

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r4#6/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r4#6/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r4#6/r2.claim: In al-Maida, God alone determines what is lawful and forbidden; rejecting any other legislating authority is part of rejecting shirk, so that issue receives emphasis.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r4#6/r2.anchor: والكلام في المائدة أيضاً على التحليل والتحريم ومَنْ بيدِه ذلك، ورفض أية جهة تُحلِّلُ وتُحَرِّم من غير الله فإن الله هو يحكم ما يريد.

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r4#6/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r4#6/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r4#6/r3.claim: Al-Anam says polytheists deliberately omit God’s name over some sacrifices, while al-Maida commands naming God over them; this supports foregrounding rejection of naming another.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r4#6/r3.anchor: فناسب ذلك تقديم بطلان ذكر غير الله.

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r4#6/r9.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r4#6/r9.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r4#6/r9.claim: The examples show the Quran’s wording and word order are intentional, with every expression placed for a contextual purpose and the Quran considered as a unified whole.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r4#6/r9.anchor: كلُّ لفظٍ فيه وُضِعَ وضعاً فنياً مقصوداً، وأنه لم يقدم لفظة على لفظة إلا لغرض يقتضيه السياق.

SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p57/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p57/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p57/r1.claim: The sūrah’s opening discussion of lawful and forbidden foods establishes that God alone legislates them and rejects any other authority claiming to do so.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p57/r1.anchor: والكلام في المائدة أيضاً على التحليل والتجريم ومن بيده ذلك، ورفض أية جهة تحلل وتحرم من غير الله

SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p58/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p58/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p58/r2.claim: The order also fits al-Māʾidah’s contrast between animals on which God’s name is omitted and its command to invoke God’s name over the game caught by trained animals.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p58/r2.anchor: فذكر في آية الأنعام أن المشركين لا يذكرون اسم الله على بعض ذبائحهم تعمداً

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p508/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p508/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p508/r1.claim: Al-Ma’idah discusses who has authority to declare things lawful or forbidden and rejects any authority besides God, who rules as He wills.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p508/r1.anchor: والكلام في المائدة أيضاً على التحليل والتجريم ومن بيده ذلك، ورفض أية جهة تحلل وتحرم من غير الله

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p509/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p509/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p509/r1.claim: Al-Ma’idah places “لغير الله” before “به” to foreground rejection of shirk; its prohibition of deliberate failure to name God and command to name Him over slaughter make this order apt.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p509/r1.anchor: ولذا قدمه في البطلان فقال (وَمَا أُهِلَّ لِغَيْرِ اللَّهِ بِهِ)

NASHR:v2p154/r9.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p154/r9.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p154/r9.claim: مما is joined except in al-Nisa and al-Rum; the verse’s مما أمسكن عليكم is an example, while al-Munafiqun is disputed.
NASHR:v2p154/r9.anchor: (ومما) كتب موصولا في غير النساء والروم نحو مما أمسكن عليكم

NASHR:v2p158/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p158/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p158/r1.claim: When codices differ in a letter’s spelling, the associated regional reading should follow that city’s codex: Medina for Nafiʿ and Abu Jaʿfar, Mecca for Ibn Kathir, Syria for Ibn Amir, Basra for Abu Amr and Yaqub, and Kufa for its readers.
NASHR:v2p158/r1.anchor: في مصاحف المدينة أن يجري ذلك في قراءة نافع وأبي جعفر

NASHR:v2p158/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p158/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p158/r2.claim: In stopping according to the rasm, “deletion” or “addition” means actual written omission or presence, not a merely estimated deletion or shape of hamza; the choice must reflect the reader’s case ending and hamza easing.
NASHR:v2p158/r2.anchor: إن الوقف على اتباع الرسم يكون باعتبار الأواخر من حذف وإثبات، وغيره إنما يعنون بذلك الحذف المحقق لا المقدر

NASHR:v2p158/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p158/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p158/r3.claim: If Hamza is eased at pause, readers using rasm follow its written yāʾ or wāw for rūm. Thus “ولؤلؤا” gets final alif only with accusative reading, and “عادا وثمودا” only when nunated despite the codices’ alif spelling.
NASHR:v2p158/r3.anchor: ومن وقف على اتباع الرسم في ذلك وكان من مذهبه تخفيف الهمز وقفا يقف بالروم بالياء وبالواو

NASHR:v2p158/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p158/r4.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p158/r4.claim: When two joined words are written together and the first ends in a consonant assimilated to the next, the doubled consonant is written once; for readers who use ghunnah before lām or rā, the preferred practice is to drop it in connected forms to honor the rasm.
NASHR:v2p158/r4.anchor: كل ما كتب موصولا من كلمتين وكان آخر الأولى منهما حرفا مدغما فإنه حذف إجماعا واكتفى بالحرف المدغم فيه

ALUSI-FULL:v1p10/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p10/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p10/r1.claim: Kalam can mean the act of speaking or the utterance produced by it; linguistically the word primarily names the product, whether much or little and literal or figurative, though al-Raḍī notes its use for the act.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p10/r1.anchor: ولفظ الكلام موضوع لغة لثاني قليلا كان أو كثيرا حقيقة كان أو حكما وقد يستعمل استعمال المصدر كما ذكره الرضي

ALUSI-FULL:v1p10/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p10/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p10/r2.claim: Each sense has a verbal and a mental form: verbal speech is the act of the tongue or the quality of audible sound; mental speech is the mind’s unexpressed act or its imagined, internally ordered words.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p10/r2.anchor: فعل الإنسان باللسان وما يساعده من المخارج

ALUSI-FULL:v1p10/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p10/r5.speaker: أم سلمة
ALUSI-FULL:v1p10/r5.claim: Al-Ṭabarānī reports from Umm Salama that a man asked the Prophet about an inward thought he feared would ruin his reward; the Prophet called it speech and said only a believer receives it.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p10/r5.anchor: ما رواه الطبراني عن أم سلمة أنها سمعت رسول الله

ALUSI-FULL:v1p10/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p10/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p10/r6.claim: A sacred hadith saying God remembers the servant who remembers Him inwardly supports mental speech in both its act and content senses, for servant and Lord, while their realities remain incomparable.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p10/r6.anchor: فإن ذكرني في نفسه ذكرته في نفسي الحديث وفيه دليل على أن للعبد كلاما نفسيا بالمعنيين

ALUSI-FULL:v1p10/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p10/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p10/r7.claim: God’s mental speech in its first sense is an eternal attribute opposed to an inner defect like muteness, not made of letters or words, and one in essence despite varied objects of relation.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p10/r7.anchor: صفة أزلية منافية للآفة الباطنية التي هي بمنزلة الخرس في التكلم الإنساني اللفظي ليس من جنس الحروف والألفاظ أصلا

ALUSI-FULL:v1p10/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p10/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p10/r8.claim: The relation of divine speech to a newly occurring object does not make the attribute itself temporal; the author accepts renewal only in the relation’s occurrence.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p10/r8.anchor: والتعلق من الأمور النسبية التي لا يضر تجددها وحدوث المتعلق
